review_title: Fantastic, efficient machine with some quirks
review_text:
I won't repeat everything that has been said in the other reviews in detail, but I agree that the performance and efficiency (water and power) of this machine are excellent. It's gentle on clothes, pretty quiet, and has lots of great options including the ability to delay the wash.

A couple of tips/caveats, however:
*The "auto-dry" feature is very convenient, but takes a lot longer than the "timed dry" feature. It will take roughly half the time using timed dry, which I believe uses higher heat.
*Setting it to run on a delay is great for having laundry dry and ready to fold when you come home, but you need to use powdered detergent (not liquid) if using this feature.
*Once drying is done and goes to "cool down" mode (which keeps it periodically tumbling to prevent wrinkles, you have to hit start, then wait several minutes before the door unlocks. This is to prevent kids from getting burned, but it's irritating.
*The biggest issue is that over time lint builds up inside the machine which restricts airflow and slows drying, since there's no real lint trap (the little one at the bottom doesn't really work). This happens especially if you wash/dry a lot of high-lint items like towels, and you'll notice that your clothes are taking longer and longer to dry. The good news is that it's not that hard to clean out, and doing so will restore the drying time of ~90 minutes for a full load. I have a step by step "how-to" guide with pictures here:

review_title: i love this machine, even though it's not perfect
review_text:
have been using my lg w/d combo for over a year now. i have a very small condo and lack of space, 220 power and venting were the deciding factors for me. i LOVE not having to take my laundry to the basement and worry about moving the laundry from the washer to the dryer. this machine has worked great for me.

i do more smaller loads now. usually 4-6 loads a week for just one person (and a cat). it rarely takes over 3 hours to wash and dry total and occasionally i choose to dry less time and line dry to finish. i never dry my jeans anyway. and yes, if i wash one towel, 2 wash cloths and a hand towel -- it is full. don't try to cram too much into this machine. it works a lot better with small loads.

i like the delay function so i can set it up in the morning and time it to be done when i get home from work.

things are more linty than a normal dryer. i got a lint roller. but my clothes come out a lot softer than the regular dryer because they're not baked to a crisp. it's a gentler dry.

it has different settings for "hand wash" "delicates" and "speed wash" in addition to normal etc.

i really like it. the only real annoyance i have with it, is that the door takes a really long time to unlock after a dry cycle, even after pushing the unlock button.

it is supposedly very water and energy efficient. i recommend the lg WM3431HW.

product_title: LG WM3431HW 24", 2.44 Cu. Ft. Washer/Dryer Combo (White)
review_text:
I've been wanting one of these for some time, and it was well worth the wait. This machine is perfect for me since I have limited space for it, and no outside vent for a conventional dryer. It is relatively straightforward to operate, turn it on, set the appropriate settings, and let it go. As the owner's manual suggests, I ran an empty load first to be sure all the operations worked as they should, and wash out the inside. (I suggest doing so, I could smell lubricants and such inside from the manufacturing process) Because the machine uses a direct drive system to turn the drum, it is surprisingly quiet. As most reviews state, the machine is not designed for a large family or extra heavy use. The first real load I ran consisted of a few towels. The second of a larger load of regular clothes. The towels took a total of about 3 hours from start to finish, which isn't that much longer than it would take with a conventional setup.

In all, I love this machine so far, it suits my space constraints well. The low noise means I can run it at night and it shouldn't wake me up in the middle of the night. The drum does spin very fast when it is washing and in the spin cycle, so there is a little vibration noise you can hear, but this shouldn't be a problem if it is on a level and sturdy surface. I will say that the vibration is less noticable than with my old regular washer. When drying, the top sides of the machine become hot, but not enough to burn, but be careful what you might put near it. Also because of the high spin speeds, I wouldn't recommend leaving anything on top of the unit. In all, I think it is a great value for the money. The higher price is justified by the convenience. I can't seem to find a matching pedistal which would raise it up a bit. Being a taller guy it is a bit of a stretch to get the clothing in and out.

review_title: Great Machine - unless you machine dry everything
review_text:
When looking for a new machine I was searching for a combo side loading unit. They're uncommon in the US but pretty much standard everywhere else (smaller houses I guess). Running the dryer is one of the most expensive appliances in most households (and pretty nasty for your carbon footprint) so having the ability to dry (for wet days or emergencies) but not using it routinely is a great fit for this machine. It's smart metering of water and heat depending upon what you put in it is really cool. It uses smart sensing for drying as well so the long cycle time is only really for full loads. (quick drying sheets or shirts can be done in 30 mins or less).

You will need to run more smaller loads than a large top loader but you'll still save money (plus a drum system is much kinder on your clothes than a top loaded paddle design).

review_text:
Seriously, did no one think beforehand that this is a bad design? To begin with, you can't put a second load into the washer while the other one is "drying," thereby extending the time you are using the electricity, the water, etc. From what I've read, it's normal to take 4-5 hours for this machine to do one small load? That's crazy too. Your clothes literally get imprisoned in the machine all afternoon. What if you only want to dry the clothes for 20 minutes, then hang them? I'm not sticking around long enough to figure that one out. I'm getting rid of this machine--don't care what it costs!

In addition, the child lock feature is ridiculous (you have to wait 2 minutes to even open the door after turning off the machine), especially if you do not have small children and I doubt most people with children would have a machine this tiny. It appears to be gurgling water in and out while it's supposedly drying, making noises so loud, it is impossible to think, let alone work. With the noises it is making, it absolutely has to be guzzling down water and we are in a drought. In addition, the dryer lets off so much heat too that it heats up the apartment and if you have air conditioning you have to turn that up to counteract the heat it is producing.

These energy-sucking appliances should be outlawed, or they should create something that is the opposite of Energy Star...Energy Sucker?!?

I think that LG should be brought up on charges for advertising that this is an "efficient" machine. Not time efficient, not energy efficient. Space efficient, maybe, but you're using the same square footage with the stackable units, just taking up more vertical space. Nothing good about this machine. Nothing. Nada.

If I could figure out how to give it 0 stars, I would!

product_title: LG WM3431HW 24", 2.44 Cu. Ft. Washer/Dryer Combo (White)
review_text:
I've had this machine since 2006, and I am in love with it. I live in a rental in NYC in a building without any laundry room. This means that prior to this machine, my husband and I had to gather our clothing, and walk 4 blocks to a public laundry mat. Not only is that inconvenient, but you're sharing machines with absolute strangers is not that sanitary and this really hit home when we were doing laundry and a homeless man came to wash his clothing in the machine next to us.

First thing I have to say is, this machine is NOT for everyone. If I had the option of having a regular side by side washer and dryer, I would not have purchased/liked this machine. The machine is small enough to fit anywhere. I have it set up between the sink and refrigerator. Since it is small enough to fit just about anywhere, this means that your loads are going to be smaller as well. Personally I don't have a problem with load size....instead of doing laundry once a week, I do laundry every other day or every two days during the week.

I think the first thing people need to understand about this machine is that it's a trial and error process. When you first start using it you'll have problems getting a load done as sometimes the machine is "unbalanced" and cannot spin. When that happened to me I used to stop the machine, and reload it to make sure that it was balanced (making sure to have some heavy items in the bottom, smaller items in between, a couple of more heavy items on the top). A normal cycle takes 58 minutes....my clothing comes out super clean. Sometimes when I am in a hurry I'll do the "speed wash" cycle, which only takes 30 minutes.

Sure laundry takes a little longer because it's an all in one unit, but I have NEVER had a load longer than 3 hours. This weekend I washed a complete queen size sheet set (fitted sheet, 2 pillow cases, and a sheet) and it took 2:30 hours from start to finish. Did it come out wrinkled??? Yes, but I personally don't care since it's my bedding. Was it dried when I pulled it out....YES!!! That I do care about. I read some of these reviews and I am amazed at the reasons people give it low rating (can't wash another load while drying...really? you didn't figure that one out before you brought it?) Is it a perfect machine...no, but for people without regular machine options I think it great.

Size of the loads....this is something else you have to play around with. When I first started using the machine, I had read that you should be careful with your load size, so I was making my loads really small. I just finished a load right now which included 8 shirts, 2 shorts, 1 long pajama pants, 3 underwear....the total time for this load, 2 hours (using speed wash, 30 minutes, and drying with timer set at 1:30 hour). My load was clean and dry. Taking your clothing out of the dryer is something else you have to get used to because the load will feel damp, but it's not. All you have to do is shake the condensation out (and I really do mean shake. What I do is when I pull it out of the machine, I shake it and set that piece of clothing on the back of the dining room chair. By the time I am done pulling everything out, all the clothing is dry and ready to be folded and put away.

Vibrations/Shaking...the machine is fairly quiet. The only thing that make a loud noise is when it's expelling water and even that is tolerable. I can watch tv in the other room and it doesn't bother me. When the machine spins, it spins very fast (which helps with making sure your clothing is almost dry by the time the wash is done) but this means that there will be some vibration. My floor is wood, and you don't really hear it. Now if I touch the counter or stove I can feel the vibration....but not hear it. My downstairs neighbor had never complained.

I've also read people complain about a musty smell inside the machine and I've never had an issue like that. I also make sure to take care of my machine. After I am done using it I let it cool off a bit (the time it take for me to put the clothing away). I take a piece of napkin and make sure to dry out the water that stays between the drum and rubber. After I am done with that, I do not close the machine but leave it open for a couple of hours. I also remove the detergent dispenser, rinse it, and leave it open as well so it dries out.

I have to admit that I have never cleaned out the inside of the machine for lint...but I plan to have my husband do it soon. I printed the instructions that I got from someone who reviewed the machine here. But even with all this time using it and not cleaning it properly, I really haven't had an issue. I bet when I clean it out my drying time is going to take even less.

In conclusion, if you live in an apartment where regular laundry hook-up is not available and are tired of going to public laundry mats or sharing machines, you should really consider buying this washer/dryer unit. But do so with the idea that it does not work the same as a regular dryer and therefore you need to adjust the way you do laundry.....but the advantages of having your own machine in the apartment far outweighs any negatives this machine may have. I wish I could hug whoever invented this machine :)

When you first start using it you'll have problems getting a load done as sometimes the machine is "unbalanced" and cannot spin. When that happened to me I used to stop the machine, and reload it to make sure that it was balanced (making sure to have some heavy items in the bottom, smaller items in between, a couple of more heavy items on the top). A normal cycle takes 58 minutes....my clothing comes out super clean. Sometimes when I am in a hurry I'll do the "speed wash" cycle, which only takes 30 minutes. Sure laundry takes a little longer because it's an all in one unit, but I have NEVER had a load longer than 3 hours. This weekend I washed a complete queen size sheet set (fitted sheet, 2 pillow cases, and a sheet) and it took 2:30 hours from start to finish. Did it come out wrinkled??? Yes, but I personally don't care since it's my bedding. Was it dried when I pulled it out....YES!!! That I do care about. I read some of these reviews and I am amazed at the reasons people give it low rating (can't wash another load while drying...really? you didn't figure that one out before you brought it?) Is it a perfect machine...no, but for people without regular machine options I think it great. Size of the loads....this is something else you have to play around with. When I first started using the machine, I had read that you should be careful with your load size, so I was making my loads really small. I just finished a load right now which included 8 shirts, 2 shorts, 1 long pajama pants, 3 underwear....the total time for this load, 2 hours (using speed wash, 30 minutes, and drying with timer set at 1:30 hour). My load was clean and dry. Taking your clothing out of the dryer is something else you have to get used to because the load will feel damp, but it's not. All you have to do is shake the condensation out (and I really do mean shake. What I do is when I pull it out of the machine, I shake it and set that piece of clothing on the back of the dining room chair. By the time I am done pulling everything out, all the clothing is dry and ready to be folded and put away. Vibrations/Shaking...the machine is fairly quiet. The only thing that make a loud noise is when it's expelling water and even that is tolerable. I can watch tv in the other room and it doesn't bother me. When the machine spins, it spins very fast (which helps with making sure your clothing is almost dry by the time the wash is done) but this means that there will be some vibration. My floor is wood, and you don't really hear it. Now if I touch the counter or stove I can feel the vibration....but not hear it. My downstairs neighbor had never complained. I've also read people complain about a musty smell inside the machine and I've never had an issue like that. I also make sure to take care of my machine. After I am done using it I let it cool off a bit (the time it take for me to put the clothing away). I take a piece of napkin and make sure to dry out the water that stays between the drum and rubber. After I am done with that, I do not close the machine but leave it open for a couple of hours. I also remove the detergent dispenser, rinse it, and leave it open as well so it dries out. I have to admit that I have never cleaned out the inside of the machine for lint...but I plan to have my husband do it soon. I printed the instructions that I got from someone who reviewed the machine here. But even with all this time using it and not cleaning it properly, I really haven't had an issue. I bet when I clean it out my drying time is going to take even less. In conclusion, if you live in an apartment where regular laundry hook-up is not available and are tired of going to public laundry mats or sharing machines, you should really consider buying this washer/dryer unit. But do so with the idea that it does not work the same as a regular dryer and therefore you need to adjust the way you do laundry.....but the advantages of having your own machine in the apartment far outweighs any negatives this machine may have. I wish I could hug whoever invented this machine :)

Super quiet.

Sometimes my pants get really wrinkled.
Some users have rated this with only one star simply for that reason. You just have to iron them.

product_title: LG WM3431HW 24", 2.44 Cu. Ft. Washer/Dryer Combo (White)
review_text:
Absolute, no-holds barred, incomparable, NIGHTMARE! I purchased this appliance about two years ago. Within the first six months (under a one-year warranty), it stopped drying. Service call. Rep doesn't fix dryer and breaks it further so now it won't even wash. Call new service company. After about four weeks of troubleshooting (I now know how Ed met his wife and takes his coffee), it finally gets repaired. A month later, it again stops drying. Service Call. Fixed. A month later, control board stops functioning. Service call. Replaced. A month later, it CATCHES ON FIRE. Service call. Fixed. It was about this time Ed the service tech suggested I contact LG about a replacement, as clearly this unit was defective. Unfortunately, I had such FAITH in a $1500 LG appliance that every time Ed came to fix it, I believed it was FINALLY fixed.

Fast forward a couple more months: The one-year warranty has now expired (I BEG you to get the five year), the control board blows a SECOND time. The board, however, is under a two year warranty. I call Ed, and this time - he insists I call LG and get a replacement. It has had way too many repairs and was obviously a lemon.

So, I called. After many transfers to finally talk to someone I thought was the "correct person," they asked that Ed fax over the work history and that I fax over my original purchase receipt. Within a couple of days Ed contacted me with a RETURN AUTHORIZATION NUMBER (w000t!!) LG had given him to give to me. I simply had to call to arrange the exchange. Well, I did call, and they said they could, indeed, begin the exchange process once they got a fax of my original purchase receipt (which they claim they did not receive the first time). I promptly faxed the receipt and waited for a reply, as per their instructions.

A few weeks passed (the Christmas holidays), and LG had not gotten back in touch like they assured me they would. To my dismay, when I called back in, I was told a "system upgrade" was done on their computer system and they no longer had ANY information on my account, the repairs, the return authorization number. NOTHING. So, I had to start over from the beginning, and - in the end - a decision was made that I could NOT make an exchange, that the repairs were NOT excessive, and my ONLY OPTION was to continue to have it serviced every 2-3 months. I gave up.

Now, the majority of the time, like now, it just sits, again broken, and unused. When purchasing this appliance (a $1,500 appliance - in my life I've only paid more for my car and my house ), I did not know I would have to budget $200-400 every few months for ongoing service. Not to mention $80 a month or so at the laundromat.

Saturday trusty Ed returned as now my dryer fan no longer works. He was a bit stumped and thought maybe the electrical harness needed to be replaced. When he called tech support, they actually had the audacity and ignorance to ask if he had "unplugged the unit and plugged it back in" to see if that would fix it. It was beyond insulting.

In all fairness, WHEN the machine works it does a fantastic job, and I truly wish I could recommend it. But, due to LG's woeful customer service, I could never, ever recommend this or any LG appliance to anyone I know and still be able to sleep at night.

UPDATE: 6/11/10 ~ So, LG finally conceded that, wow, ya, maybe we have serviced the heck out of your unit to no avail, and we SHOULD replace it. My faith in LG and humanity was momentarily restored! However, a new unit was delivered Monday. By Tuesday morning (as in, the NEXT day), I discovered that, while the "timed" dry was working, the "sensor dry" was not. I just called (and of course they had very little information from previous calls). My solution? I give up. Replace immediately or just give me a refund. Their solution? "We'll send a service tech." Here we go again...stay tuned! Maybe it will catch on fire one more time!

UPDATE: 2/11/13 ~ They never did fix the sensor dry, but I swear I'm NOT hard to please and was happy to live with just "timed" dry. It conked out completely about three weeks ago, though. Flooded my laundry room, won't drain; won't spin; won't dry. I contacted LG . They have yet to yet to get back to me.

product_title: LG WM3431HW 24", 2.44 Cu. Ft. Washer/Dryer Combo (White)
review_text:
We got this a year ago after LOTSA research. To begin with, although widely advertised, nobody seems to actually have it for delivery. So we ended up ordering it 4 - yes, FOUR, times from Home Depot (yes, they will get it for you, you have to ask and insist...). Home Depot's computer automatically deletes orders not filled within a certain time. The item was always back-ordered, so our order was inadvertently deleted the first three times. We didn't even know it the first time, until I called to inquire about the delay. After told what the story was, I made sure we kept up calling and renewing the inquiry to keep the order in the computer. Finally, after 5 months and 3 weeks (not quite half a year, you see...), it finally arrived outside our door. Outside, because nobody wanted to put it inside and risk having to install. Which really amounts to: nobody wanted to read instructions. Just as well. There is nothing to the installation of this. Plug in, put hoses where the hoses of regular washer go. Done. For an added level of complication, we installed it under the counter in the kitchen where the dishwasher was. Steps: slide out dishwasher (you may need to take a pre step, to remove the 'shoe cover'. Big F deal...), discard. Unpack W/D; unscrew shipping screw (keeps drum secure during transport); unfold cord; insert hose in hole and other end in floor or faucet hole (sewer outlet); connect water hose or hoses (you can choose to use both C & H or only C and let the washer warm/boil the water - waste of time and electricity... I connected both cold and hot, helped that I had the same hookup with dishwasher); plug cord; slide W/D under counter. For aesthetics and stability: put shoe cover back. Done! Proceed to wash clothes!

It washes perfectly! Total euro style wash! Hadn't seen whites so white since grandma's last wash across the pond. It doesn't take any more time than the other washers, if you set it according to time. I don't follow the preset 'programs', I just set the temp, spin, etc. I want. Our washes take: 55 min for sheets and towels, 34 min for anything else.

We do the same for drying - just set the time. Otherwise the clothes dry awfully much. Best part, the clothes are a tad humid/not quite damp, when taken out, just enough to stretch and fold and eliminate need for ironing. You can leave the dryer working and go away. Regardless of how long you will be gone, the dryer will not stop and let clothes sit and wrinkle. After finishing its cycle, it will continue spinning the clothes every so often to keep them from 'setting'. When you are ready to take the clothes out, you have to press the button to release the latch. The machine will not allow you to open for as long as the steam/heat is at dangerous temperature levels. After about 3 min the key icon turns off and you can take the clothes out.

Washes require a little planning because clothes will need to air for a little bit before ready to be used. So if you only have one pair of sheets and expect to wash them before your girlfriend arrives, this unit is not for you. Sheets/towels need to air out a little after they are out of the dryer, before used or folded. We wash these items on a Saturday or Sunday morning to have plenty of time before they are needed in the evening. Because of this detail, not having anything way too dry, there has been no shrinkage of any clothing (think cashmere...) since we started washing in the LG. Which in and of itself is worth the entire price of this unit!!!

I have recommended this to anyone who asked - and will continue doing so without any reservation! Go ahead, buy it and enjoy it!

4 years later: I keep LOVIN' this machine, now have two of these - Read about the new one. Although the same model number, it is a bit different:

LG still has it, but they have changed the electronics a bit, without changing the instructions... We bought a second one for another apartment and didn't have a separate function for drying, so it seemed that we had to set the drying at the beginning of the wash and do it all in one scoop. I hated that because I wash all my clothes together (using 'Color Catcher' to avoid mishaps) but I hang and air dry most wearables, while I use the dryer for sheets, towels, etc.

After pouring over reviews and comments, I found out that you CAN run the DRYer SEPARATELY. Just set the washer on 'Rinse and Spin' and then turn off the 'Rinse' button. The machine will spin the clothes to remove any water first and then will start the drying cycle. Don't consider this an extra spin, as the older machine which has the functions separate, starts the drying with a good spin to get rid of the access water first.

10 Years later: The first washing machine (pictured here) developed a knotting sound when spinning, most likely a faulty/broken bearing in the main tub. This is a very expensive fix, (quoted $600) and not one under warranty. But the WD still works just fine, except it is to loud to have in the main house. I swapped the loud one from my kitchen and put in the guest house. Since it is programmable, can be set to work while nobody would be around. -- The second WD was bought in 2011, only 7 years young, and still quiet.

product_title: LG WM3431HW 24", 2.44 Cu. Ft. Washer/Dryer Combo (White)
review_text:
i purchased this unit in february 2009. running a load from start to finish is very time consuming. depending on the size of the load it can take anywhere from 3 1/2 to 5+ hours. most of that time is due to the drying and "CD" or cool down cycle. clothes are never completely dry - they always feel slighty damp unless you do an extra "dry only" cycle.

it worked satisfactory until approximately may 2010. from then on when the washing cycle was finished and transitioned to the dry cycle it would run for 5 - 10 minutes at which point it would stop and say "CD". it has not dried a single article of anything since.

The icing on the cake is that the misery is not short lived, but takes 4-5 hours to do a single load.

product_title: LG WM3431HW 24", 2.44 Cu. Ft. Washer/Dryer Combo (White)
review_text:
This combo machine is an absolute last resort for anyone who does not have a way to vent a side by side or top/bottom combo machine.

PROS:
Looks good and will squeeze into most apartment or condo closets.
Has large timer display that counts down time left on cycle.
Uh - hmmm, that's about it for pros.

CONS:
Clothes will be damp at best for most loads. If you remove the clothes immediately while piping hot, the steam will dissipate and sheets or similar weighted items will dry if spread out. (I use a fan directed at the damp items to help finish off the drying process.) It is almost impossible to dry sweaters, towels and jeans. So, if you live in a climate where heavier clothes are the norm, you may want to take this into consideration.

Users will do better if they understand that you cannot employ the regular load washer/dryer mentality when using this machine. Mix the weight and size of the items - one sheet, two pillow cases, two bath towels and face cloths mixed in with a few gym socks or underwear.

It takes forever and a day to wash/dry one load. I've found that setting the cycle to wash and then opening the door even for a few minutes, THEN going back and starting the dry cycle cuts down the dry time considerably. Of course, this defeats the purpose of setting and forgetting a load to wash/dry un-tendered; but if you are a busy granny-nanny like me, it cuts down on hours of dry time. Plus, it's only an extra step and you still don't have to haul the load from the washer to the dryer in the process.

If you don't crack the door and let the moisture dissipate between loads, you may get this awful stench that is best remedied with a quick Chlorox rinse.

Lint accumulates around the rubber door seal and may re-deposit on the next load if not wiped down.

Our machine is less than two years old and has broken down completely once and at times will just shut down due to an uneven load, even with two equally weighted sheets. We will also get an arbitrary error message that can only be remedied by unplugging the machine or resetting the circuit.

Call me old fashioned, but I just can't be convinced that a few cups of water are able to get my grandson's cloth diapers cleaner than a couple of gallons in an energy efficient front loader or top loading machine.

review_title: Great machine 5 years in- but do your homework before you buy!
review_text:
This unit has been the perfect solution for our situation: an urban couple in a tiny apartment (who absolutely HATE the laundry-mat!!), with no basement access to setup a traditional washer /dryer pair.

Important note: if you like to dry all your clothes in the machine (i.e. not hang most of them up to air dry like us) you will NOT be happy with this condenser dryer. You can only dry a few items at a time, and it will take about an hour and a half. As well, the rubber gasket that seals the door will impart a slight odour to the dried items until it has been used a while. We don't use fabric softener or strong smelling detergent so your results may vary.

The last drawback is that it is pricey. However, we have owned it for 5 years, probably running it 5 days out of seven, and it has been rock solid, with only 1 self-repair needed. After 4 years of light use of the dryer function,the clothes started coming out damp. Googling the problem, I was able to easily take it apart and clean the accumulated lint out of the condenser tube with a long bottle washer (like a thick pipe cleaner). Voila- back to normal, and still perfect a year later.

Replacement parts seem to be reasonably priced from third party vendors to boot. If you're handy, you should be able to keep it running for a good long time.

product_title: LG WM3431HW 24", 2.44 Cu. Ft. Washer/Dryer Combo (White)
review_text:
This machine does not deserve even 1 star! I don't often write a scathing review, but after 3 years with this machine, it absolutely deserves it.

Let's talk about washing first - the LG designer that wrote the program for washing cycles has apparently never seen or used a washing machine before. The machine has all sorts of extra back-and-forth gyrations between cycles, and with fairly long pauses - enough so that it adds about 10 minutes to what should be the normal washing time. The drain pump is called for whether it's needed or not and this goes on constantly. But the absolute worst of the worst is the spin cycle. The machine will not do well at all with small loads, so don't even bother, but that's not the main issue. The machine cannot achieve any kind of a reasonable balance and makes several tries - the amount of time can exceed 20 minutes or even stop all together with a time-out error. In short, if the machine was a person, that person is terrified of spinning.

Next is doing the drying - the dryer spin does not tumble fast enough to remove wrinkles from permanent press stuff. There is no user accessible lint trap, so it gets trapped in the internal hot air ducts and eventually plugs them. These ducts need to be cleaned at least twice a year, otherwise it burns a hole into the composite plastic duct and the back half of the drum chamber, creating a severe fire hazard.

Fortunately, I purchased an extended warranty when I bought the machine. As of writing this review, repairs have exceeded the original price of the machine. Even the 10-year warrantied motor did not last more than 2 years before the bearings wore out. The front panel circuit has been replaced twice. The drum and drum chamber (2 halves) have been replaced. The most recent failure was the 110 VAC power supply filter and relay; it melted due to inadequate cooling and heat sinking. Currently, the pump sounds as if it is on its last legs. I only hope it goes out before my extended warranty ends because the machine has to be completely dismantled to replace it.

I bought this machine because I have always had good luck with LG appliances, and it truth, the quality of parts used in this machine is good. What destroys this machine is an extremely poor design. Washing and drying in the same unit calls for some pretty exotic design choices and are not met in this unit. The electronics need to be protected better from the intense internal heat generated during the drying cycle. As a matter of fact, it would be better to give up the condensation drying and just use a fan and heating element - the clothes might actually get dry.

At this point, you might be asking how much I use the machine - two medium-sized loads per week, and using the dryer on only one of them.

Do yourself a favor and pass on buying this machine - it is nothing but trouble due to poor design, especially considering its initial cost.

product_title: LG : WM2455HG 27 Front-Load XL Washer - Pearl Gray
review_title: No complaints on a great washer
review_text:
My wife and I bought this washer 3 months ago, along with its companion dryer the DLG5966g, for use in a new "kitchen laundry cubby" installation on a new ceramic tile floor. We had concerns about having a washer/dryer in our living area because of noise, but they have been totally unfounded. One room away from the living room and TV, we rarely even notice it working as it goes through its cycles. Our other concern was whether we would have problems with vibration and the washer wanting to "walk" during the extremely high speed spin cycle of these new front loaders. The first few loads put our minds to rest. Even at the highest spin speed the vibration is hardly noticeable. LG has done a great job engineering this unit. Note, however, that this washer needs to be on a solid floor (concrete or ceramic tile) to work properly. I wouldn't recommend installing it on a wood or laminate floor. We purchased the optional pedestals, which puts these at a great height for convenience and comfort. Built-in drawers, too. Very large capacity, and there are plenty of cycle choices and options, but not terribly complicated to operate. My wife says it does a much better job of cleaning the clothes than our old top loader, using much less water and HE detergent.

The only drawback so far is that a typical wash cycle takes about 90 minutes. If you're used to much less than that, and if it's a critical factor for you, consider another washer. We're not in that big of a hurry. It does have a "speed wash" cycle which can run a load through considerable faster if you find yourself in a hurry. My wife also uses the "extra rinse" option, which adds a few more minutes. Probably not necessary, but it's there if you want it.

The only reason that I didn't give this washer 5 stars is because we haven't owned it long enough to know if it will hold up well over the years. It's direct drive, which was one of the criteria that made me choose it over other models. I'm hoping that this will also add to the reliability. If it's continuing to work well in a few years then it definitely deserves a 5 star rating.

review_title: Great for Cleaning, Just be sure you have two ppl put it together
review_text:
Bought this washer/dryer from EnVive with free shipping. Took longer than expected to arrive. Once it arrived, the shippers dropped it off and left. Once they left we realized there was no electric plug nor an air vent for the back. Though it says its 4" standard for the back, we had to actually buy a second piece to make the standard air vent fit - an elbow piece of plastic (about $4 at Home Depot).
Be sure that you have a dolly handy, as well. There is a screw in the center on the bottom of the machine that you have to remove yourself - that's Step One in the instructions. Luckily, we just moved and had a dolly that holds up to 600lbs. No way we would have been able to lift it and not drop it without more people, otherwise.

review_text:
I purchased a Bosch washer (model WAS20160UC) and dryer (model WTV76100US) set in December 2011. This is the experience I have had with the Bosch appliances. It is a vented dryer, not the condensation model. This review is mostly about the dryer.

Pros: Stylish (witch makes no difference since the dryer is so poor)

Cons: This dryer takes very long to dry even small loads. It will get warm but not hot. A Bosch technician measured the temperature of the dryer at 122 degrees Fahrenheit. But, he informed me that this was normal for this dryer. In one test; two bath towels, two hand towels, and one facial towel were washed in the washer and rinsed on maximum spin to remove as much of the water as possible. It took the dryer 1hr. 20 min. to dry the load. After many phone calls and 3 or 4 service calls, they replaced the dryer. It performed as poorly as the first. So, I called an electrician to really find out what was going on. With freshly washed towels in the dryer, he observed the dryer drawing 10 amps (about the maximim rating) for 15 to 20 seconds. Then it went down to 5 amps for about about 30 seconds (he described it as half heat) then down to room temperature air coming out of the exhaust for another couple minutes. It repeats this cycle. At no time does the dryer actually get hot enough to remove the moisture from the load. It mostly just uses ambiant temperature air to dry the clothes. review_text: Like with all major purchases, I researched the heck out of this machine and its competitors. My biggest issue is the fact that I'm in a condo in a busy metro area, and there is simply no room for a full-sized washer (much to my chagrin).  I'd been using the original washer and dryer that came with the unit--which was built in 1989! I will say, to Whirlpool's credit, that both were still working great; it was just time to upgrade to something cleaner and more energy efficient, and hopefully with larger capacity.  This machine really fits the bill. My laundry comes out smelling much more fresh and simply feels cleaner.  I've followed the advice of other front-load owners and left the door and soap dispenser open after wash cycles to allow them air-dry, and have had no issues with the foul smell (probably mildew) that other owners have complained of with this type of unit. Its incredibly quiet, which in a small condo is a big deal! The wash cycle is fairly long (circa 1 hour), but that's not been an issue. The only thing I can't do is wash my comforters; I still have to take them to a friend's house, but I have yet to find a 24" washer that *can* handle an item that large. Highly recommended!

review_text: Complete piece of junk.  Everything the first reviewer says is true.  Not only that, but my Cabrio HE washer completely failed just outside of the 1 year warranty period.  The control board went bad during the wash cycle.  Estimated cost to repair is almost half of the cost of a new unit!  After doing a quick internet search, and realizing that this is a common problem, I decided that I am not giving Whirlpool one more dime of my money, EVER, since I will likely be in the same boat as I am now in the near future with this washer if I had it repaired!  So, a practically brand new unit is going to the dump, and I'm replacing it with a simple GE washer costing about the same cost of the estimated repair.  Oh, and get this, the Cabrio door locks when it's washing, and when the control board went out, and the washer died, the lid remained locked.  I had a full load of clothes in the washer when it died and could not get the clothes out without forcing the lid open with a crow bar.  There is no manual overide for the latch!  Why in the world does a top loading washer have to lock the lid down anyway!  The only way to get a FULL load of clothes out of the washer was to pay for the repair, or break the lock by forcing the door open.  Never, NEVER again, will I buy a Whirlpool brand product.  It seems that a significant number of other folks have experienced similar problems with this washer, so I am anxious to see if a class action law suit is in the near future!!!

review_text:
The Cabrio is okay only if you pre-spray dirty/stinky clothes, and use the PRE-Soak option on EVERY load of clothes. Using the Pre-Soak option increases your wash time significantly, but you have to do it...the adjitation is so poor your clothes DO NOT get clean otherwise.

The sheet/towel comment on previous reviews is true. They always ball up and the stuff that ends up inside the ball doesn't really get clean. In fact, I've pulled stuff out of the middle of that ball that is barely damp.

There is supposed to be a stabilizer built into the machine, but it doesn't always work and sometimes the machine seems like it is going to take off as it shakes, rattles and moves out of it's place. It gets really loud. So I don't like to wash sheets/towels unless I'm going to be home.

One pro with the top load verses the front load machine is you can stop the wash and add items if you forgot something (convenient with kids).

As of now, no problem with the mother board/electrical and have had it for 2- 2.5 years.

Not worth the money!!!

review_text:
I think some of the negative reviews have to do with some issues with the newer technology. Ours works great. This machine offers a good balance between efficiency and performance. If you are looking to buy a washing machine that just has good performance, the 6600 is probably better. A front-loader is also a good option if you have the space. But if you are concerned with water and energy usage, and need a top-loader for space, the only other model that comes close is the Fisher & Paykel Aquasmart. See[...]for the washer ratings. The 6700 is the #3 rated top-loader. The #2 is a Maytag that is essentially the same machine.

We love this thing and have not seen the problems listed. It gets our clothes cleaner and softer than our previous washers. I think if you are doing loads with 10+ pairs of jeans that you need to consider a front loader. For us, we only have 27" of depth in our utility closet and we wanted high efficiency (particularly with water) so this was the choice for us.

product_title: Frigidaire : FTF2140FS 27 Front-Load Washer - White
review_text:
When looking to replace my washing machine, I started out looking at the traditional top loaders. The cheap ones were around $300 and more standard quality ones around $400, and I saw some that were another $100 or more beyond that. When the salesman asked me about front load washers, I didn't give it much thought because they tend to be more pricey and out of my range. In fact, the first one he showed me was about $700. When I asked him what the cheaper ones cost, he showed me the Frigidaire FTF2140FS for $550, and seeing as they had $100 off deal, it was only slightly more than the standard top loader. So I took him up on the deal, ultimately paying $475 after tax, and so far I'm very happy with its performance.

I usually have two or three people who rent rooms in my house. The old washer took 40 gallons of water per load. The Frigidaire takes just 15 gallons! So right off the bat I'm going to be saving a lot on my water bill, as well as a few bucks on electricity as this washer takes less of that to operate, too.

The controls are pretty simple to figure out. Ten cycles, four temperature settings, you can set how fast you want the basket to spin, and there's a few extra options, too. Shut the door, hit start, and let it go. Just be sure to remember that you must use HE (High Efficiency) detergent.

The wash is very quiet and the spin dry sucks the water right out of the clothes. I can dry my stuff in half the time!

I did encounter one problem twice. When washing my bed sheets and blankets, I heard a beeping noise. The washer was stopped and I thought it was done, but it turns out my sheets were still soaked. I looked at the manual and apparently if the load in the washer basket becomes uneven, it won't spin (that's why it was beeping). So I just pushed the blankets a few times, shut the door, and on the cycle dial there's an option for Final Spin, which is just that, the final spin dry. So I selected that, hit start, and it worked both times. I haven't had that problem with any other load of laundry before or after that.

This was my first foray into the world of front load washers and so far I'm very pleased with the results! It's quiet, efficient, my clothes are clean and smell fresh, and most important of all to me, it isn't tearing my clothes like my old washer was. And for the price I got it at, it's a great value!

review_title: CANNOT ADJUST WATER LEVEL - Insufficient Water
review_text:
I had a Frigidaire front loader for 9 years that I loved. I replaced
it with this model. After the fact, I found out that the water level
could not be adjusted and it appeared that there was just enough water
to wet the clothes---someone told us that the new washers went from
40 gallons of water to 15 but I have not verified those figures. I
would always use the extra rinse and leave the door open after use
to prevent mold issues. Well after 18 months I noticed a mold smell.
There was NEVER a problem in the previous washer. I googled this
and found that it was a common problems in the new "energy saving"
(non-adjustable water level) front loaders. I talked with Frigidaire
and I will give them credit, they did replace the rubber gasket in the
door with a new one that has a mold inhibitor--at no charge even though
out of warranty. I will continue to buy Frigidaire but I will never
buy another front loader as long as there is not a water adjustment level.
I was told by an appliance salesman that in order to prevent mold issues
in these new energy (low water level) saving washers one must do the
following:
1. Only use warm water
2. Only use 2 tablespoons of soap if normal water
and just one tablespoon of soap if soft water
3. Always use extra rinse
4. Never use fabric softener
5. Leave the door and the soap tray open after use.

I now run the machine once with soap then run it again without any
soap to get the clothes clean and rinsed well. I will use it until
it breaks and then forget about buying another front loader.

I was told that the new TOP loaders have water levels that are
also NOT adjustable but that Speed Queen (made in USA) still makes one
that a person can adjust the level.

I bought my dryer a couple of years ago, and thought that only a one year warranty was a little shoddy, but never did I expect that the control panels in these dryers are like self-destructing "screw the customer" systems! The dryer started beeping one day while not even turned on, and displaying error code E68, the code for a stuck button. There are no buttons stuck, and upon researching it a bit, I found hundreds of other people online with the same exact problem. review_text:
We had no washer dryer at all, so we went out one sunny day and bought a washer dryer set from Sears, they were KENMORE, NEVER AGAIN!!!
Those machines were bought just before we had a massive influx of house guests and oh yeah, our wedding.
They were out of order for the majority of the time they were in the house, 20 days or so of function and then weeks of waiting for repair man, parts and repair.
So we were eventually given new machines!!

I chose BOSCH, a reliable forward thinking brand, I've had various bosch products before with no issues, ever.
Then these beastly machines!
We got the washer and the dryer.
The dryer is fine, does it's think no issues.

I've not seen a top loader for decades before I came out to the usa (from the UK, remember the twin tubs, lol).
So of course I wasn't going to get an agitator to ruin my clothes.
The BoSCH washer has near on caused mental illness via the sheer agonizing, infuriating consistency of it's inability to balance and spin.
There's no spin cycle of itself, so you have to go through a slow and harassing process of pushing buttons, waiting, pausing, manually repositioning, wringing out and starting the spin cycle again and again and oh it's 2-3am and I still have laundry to do.
I would be better off with my late Grandmother's old twin tub, agitator included!

I cannot bear to spend more time and money on the consumer end of buying new machines, but I can tell you I am 100% looking forward to moving as we'll not be bringing this B*st*rd machine with us!!
I doubt we've saved any water with all the re-cycling (not to be confused with recycling) that we have to do to get the clothes or sheets or whatever out spun!!

The machine doesn't smell, we've never left it off with the door shut, I prop a spray bottle or something in the door to stop it closing when passing.
No other front loader I've ever owned has stunk.

If yours does stink I suggest cleaning it. This usually involves the hottest cycle or a clean cycle and a bottle of machine cleaning Clorox.
I've done that twice in 4 years due to the filthy stuff that we've put in there.
Clothes are always very clean.
We use tide free and clear and occasionally fabric softner, while generally just use dryer balls.

I llove the features of the dryer that allow you to flat dry delicates and the air dry only (no heat) option, as I'm happy to leave a dryer on when I'm out of the house if there's no heat involved...to avoid a common cause of house fire.

I'll be putting a pulley in my new house as the laundry room ceiling is high enough...look it up, big $$$ saver on drying.

product_title: WED7500VW Electric Dryer with 3.8 cu. ft. Capacity, 11 Drying Cycles
review_text:
The first Whirlpool WED7500VW dryer I received was defective. The drum was mis-cast and couldn't make a revolution without scraping and catching clothes due to a large gap along one side of the drum. How something like that could be shipped, or even produced is amazing. Returning it was a little unnerving because everything had to go through all parties involved, the original point of purchase store, the subcontracted repair people from Whirlpool and Whirlpool itself. In the end, we were shipped a new dryer but we were also shipped a myriad of repair parts which we're told will be picked up from the side of our front steps (no pickup date or time can be given). It's been over a week and no one has come yet and it's tedious to keep bringing them in and out each day, not to mention the security risk.

Anyway, the new dryer actually works which is such a relief. On the other hand, it's way noisier than any previous dryer I've ever used. It has an unpleasant raspy sound and does only an adequate job drying. I need to shift the clothes to make sure everything dries evenly - more so than on other dryers I've had. So I would have given this dryer two stars except Whirlpool produced it in such a small 24"W package so I bumped it up to three stars. On the other hand, if I had it to do over again, I might look into a dryer from another manufacturer, even if it didn't end up matching my washer. I would caution people against buying either this dryer or the companion washer reconditioned or used. Quality is not awe inspiring.

review_title: Best washer/dryer we have ever owned!!!
review_text:
We purchased the matching dryer to go with this washer and they are fantastic! They are quiet, fast, and energy efficient. We purchased the drawer bases which give you more storage and raise the machines up waist level so you don't have to bend down when loading and unloading.

The only issue we had was with the brass "Y" included with the steam dryer for the cold water faucet. It leaked, but Samsung sent a replacement the next day!

We gave away an 8 year old set of Maytags that worked, but were both noisy...good ridence! These are so quiet and do a better job cleaning and drying our clothes than any set we have owned before. We have had GE, Kenmore, and Maytag. All good products, but these Samsung products are so far superior, it isn't even funny!

And don't let the "NASA" designed controls fool you, they are very easy to use with preprogrammed settings (e.g. whites, towels, perm press, etc.). And the steam in both the washer and dryer allow you to remove wrinkles and sanitize your clothes. This washer also has the ability to remove 99% of bacteria in cold water using silver ions.

Don't let our 5 star rating and the other person's 1 star rating make up your mind. We researched Consumer Reports and other web sites and read lots of consumer opinions before making our decision. Plus you get an energy credit on your taxes for purchasing these Samsung products!

One recommendation, purchase the extended warranty as these are high tech with digital controls. Ours are protected for 5 years along with a "lemon" warranty. If the other consumer who gave 1 star had purchased this, they could have already replaced the defective unit or got their money back. Although we are suspicious seeing that Samsung give a 1 year warranty and they claim they can't get Samsung to do anything about their washer...so do your research before writing off this product. We highly recommend this washer although it was the most expensive one we researched...worth every dollar!

review_text:
We have to prop open the door after washing to help prevent a mildew smell. Even with propping the door open, this this washer builds up a mildew smell over time. There are products on the market to help clean mildewy front loading washing machines, but they don't get out that sludge. review_title: Just plain awful--and SAMSUNG knows it!  STAY AWAY FROM SAMSUNG APPLIANCES
review_text:
We bought this set of stainless steel junk on clearance from Sears against my better judgement. But the salesman pushed it so hard, and they didn't have the pedestals for the Kenmore set we wanted, so we gave it a try. Big Freaking Mistake! By the way, the matching dryer is just as big a piece of junk as the washer, but I will stick to this horrid mildew generator for right now. By the way, I have posted other negative reviews on this junk, but you can't find them any more. I suspect foul play.

First: From the very first load of clothes we have washed with this machine, NOTHING gets clean unless you use the 3.5 hour sanitize-and-extra-rinse with twice the soap and twice the fabric softener. Ok for towels, but not for clothes. I have tried everything. We have never ever left the doors closed on this machine because we were warned about that being the source of mildew. The machine was professionally installed and then professionally repaired twice and then re-leveled professionally and every time the installer told us we hadn't leveled the machine properly. Since the machine is on a level tile floor in a fairly expensive house, I don't think leveling is the problem.

We use the required "He" (I think it means "Low Effectiveness" soap. Only name brand. We use tide washing machine cleaner about once a month. That stuff is expensive, and of course, it is only a "temp fix". Now, I am almost 50 years old and I have NEVER IN MY LIFE HAD TO WASH A WASHING MACHINE. I have also never had a washing machine that didn't work for at least 10 years. And I for sure never paid over $1K for a washing machine of any type, but they have all performed better than this one in every way.

God forbid you put two sheets into this pile at the same time. They will turn into a stinky ball of mildewed cloth that will never ever dry. Blankets...you're talking about blankets? HAHAHAHAHA. You see, this thing, which supposedly has "VRT" will pound itself into the tile if you let it go and it becomes out of balance. I swear, I have seen it get out of balance with a load of socks. God forbid you have a load of towels in it. And here's the funny part--at one point in time the technician that came out to service it (for one broken part or another during its all-too-short warranty) told us the best way to get the towels not to stink was to stuff the machine full! DO NOT ATTEMPT THIS AT HOME UNLESS YOU ARE A TRAINED WASHING MACHINE WRESTLER!!!

There is a poorly-designed plastic door near the bottom left-had corner of the front of the machine that has a piece of stainless glued to the front of it. The first time I opened the door, one of the plastic pins broke, so the door just sort of sits in place now. The reason I opened this little hatch was to gain access to the "filter" because on about the third load of clothes, the machine stopped and said to check the filter because the unit was not draining. So I broke into the door, then had to pull the pin out of the 1/4" drain hose, and then sit there for however long it takes to fill buckets with a soda straw, only to still get laundry water all over when I removed the filter which had--I swear--ONE piece of string in it. However, when I dutifully reassembled the unit, it started working again. Now when I get the "not draining" alert, I just drain a cup or so of water from the soda straw and that seems to get it going again.

The soap dispenser tray is a joke. It has always felt flimsy, and sometimes the soap doesn't seem to want to leave the dish (admittedly, this is too rare to be the cause of every load of clothes being stinky). Did I mention we have to leave this door open as well as the front door of the machine to try to keep the mildew stink from recurring as fast?

Now, I am not an appliance mechanic. However, I have spent my entire adult life repairing electromechanical things, including very complex aircraft radar systems. I own an engineering company. I design and document complex things, which includes developing technical (instruction) manuals. I spent 20 years plus in USAF aircraft systems maintenance. Suffice to say, I can not only fix stuff, but I do read the literature that comes with it and I am generally able to solve problems. I also know a pile of junk when I see it. The saddest part is, I personally know two other people who have had the same exact issues with Samsung's garbage. And from what I have read, it is only a matter of time before this machine breaks terminally (pump housing attached to drum falls apart). Also, I have had the same exact experience as others with "my cycle" not working. If anyone could make this machine work, or could find workarounds for the problems, I think I could. And I would share that knowledge with everyone I could because, hey, 2500 bucks for a washer and dryer is enough for you to try everything. But there is no solution here without replacing the garbage.

I was going to write about the dryer, but suffice to say that it doesn't dry anything in any mode other than repeatedly running the manual dry setting for an hour. And yes, I clean the @#$! filter every time. And yes, my vent is clear to the outside of the house. The dryer is just junk too. It is, though, professionally leveled.

product_title: Samsung : DV448AEP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Electric Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_text:
We purchased our set with a manufacturing date of 01.31.10.

I was a bit nervous about selecting these machines to purchase after reading a few complaints (overall, there weren't too many) about clothes not being cleaned, an occasional mechanics problem requiring resolution, noise, etc. and had decided the machines were either 'love it' or 'hate it.' I took the plunge anyhow and am so thrilled I did!

After owning the machines for a brief time, I can proclaim I'm definitely in the 'LOVE IT!' camp! Further, without wishing to offend anyone, I will even imply people who are in the 'hate it!' camp 1) perhaps have not read their instruction manuals thoroughly so they know how to properly use and care for their machines as well as understand their limitations, or 2) perhaps aren't using the machines properly. There seem to be some service / part replacement complaints from people, but those seem centered around models with earlier manufacturing dates than the set I own.

I have never been able to get my whites this clean without bleach or OxiClean or some other whitening agent, so I was truly impressed with the Silvercare feature (especially after wondering if it might be just hype and marketing). Silvercare really works, and works well! I can confidently sanitize things without worrying about using a great deal of resources other than cold water to do so, and ditching the bleach is a wonderful thing - I really don't think I'll need to use it anymore!

The steam features have already helped remove dirt and stains my last washer could never remove, leaving me quite impressed, and the refresh cycle on the dryer is a real boon when there isn't time to iron or quick-wash. I love being able to deep-steam more heavily soiled items like my son's soccer gear and have them come out looking pristine!

These machines are every bit as quiet as advertised - I can barely hear the washer (properly leveled) operating, and this allows me to do laundry at my convenience even at nighttime without disturbing the rest of the household. The dryer is dramatically quieter than my last one as well, and the lack of overall laundry noise is fantastic!!

I love the beauty of the machines - the polished understated glamor of the platinum set is fantastic. I'm very pleased to have them seen instead of feeling like I have to hide my washer and dryer from visitors who might enter the laundry room.

Although definitely not inexpensive, these machines are well worth the price considering the load of amazing features they utilize and the increased capacity of the washer and dryer drums. I'm very much looking forward to saving on our utility costs because of them! I would heartily recommend these beauties to my friends and family, and encourage anyone out there still on the fence to buy them with confidence!! I love them, and am confident if you read the manuals and use them properly you will too!!! =)

product_title: Samsung : DV448AEP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Electric Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_text:
There is a chronic design flaw with this dryer (which I've had for
18 months).

That flaw is the design of lint screen, which is installed vertically.
Yeah, exhaust flows through it and lint is caught, but when you remove
the screen, gravity causes the lint to fall off the screen and into
the chamber below the screen. Laden with moisture, the lint tends to
mat there. Lint also flows around the screen, which has no rubber
gasket to impede this. This design virtually guarantees that lint
will escape in great quantities to the duct line and (due to the
moisture content, especially with these steam dryers) line your
exhaust ducting.

This lint then has three 90-degree turns before it is expelled out the
vent on the back of the machine.

Have one of these? UNPLUG THE MACHINE, then take your exhaust
duct loose from your wall duct and see how much lint is matted
inside it. Pull the duct from the machine (this is easy) and
see how much lint is inside the machine.

Need to clean it out? Cleaning out under the lint screen is a pain.
Get a vacuum with a nozzle. The nozzle will likely not come close to
fitting down into that chamber. I got about 2' of 1/2" flexible
tubing and stuck one end into the vacuum nozzle and then I could
snake that down and clean the chamber out pretty well. This also
worked well cleaning out with the duct assembly pulled from the
machine.

You can also take the top off, which only means removing the two
inner screws (not all six screws) and then sliding it off. You
can vacuum that out. The control board is mounted here and
is easy to take it loose so you vacuum all the lint off of it.

I'd appreciate hearing from others on their experience with lint
buildup in these areas to see if you're having the same problem.
I'm figuring on needing to clean this expensive dryer out twice
a year. I pulled a plastic grocery bagful of lint out of
this thing.

We had Kenmore basic dryer for years before this and NEVER had
lint buildup ANYTHING like this. Ugh.

I took the dryer apart after find help on-line and discovered that the entire bottom of the dryer was filled with a 1/2" layer of lint in addition to burnt lint inside the heating element assembly and the assembly socket on the back of my the dryer. I suspect the lint leakage is coming from the thin foam wrapped around the end of the exhaust tube that slips into the blower housing. Unsure of how to remedy this other than metal tape if I can reach it. I sliced my finger open on a razor sharp cross bar near the bottom.  I had been exhausting my dryer in a dryer lint box and with a sock on the end. Both need to be cleaned often as they are covered in lint. I never hooked up the steam, fearing corrosion or other failure. Meanwhile, I am reinstalling the 4" metal duct under the house with a booster fan and slow bending right angle elbows for less restricted air flow. By the way, Samsung support is like talking to a wall. That's another story!

product_title: Samsung : DV448AEP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Electric Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_title: Lint can easily escape from the lint compartment -- and from the ...
review_text:
DO NOT BUY!!! --- MAJOR FIRE HAZARD!!!
The Samsung DV448AEP dryer is a poorly designed machine. Lint can easily escape from the lint compartment -- and from the poorly designed dryer drum -- and onto the bottom portion of the dryer where the electrical components, the heating element, and the motor are located. With a 12-month or less buildup of escaped lint a fire can occur - as did in our case five times. Four of the five times we called a repair tech referred by our warranty. The repair techs explained the lint buildup was the cause of the fires -- but - what they did not explain was the lint build up was due to the poorly designed lint compartment. Shocking! They're in the business of being able to detect poor design. And not one repair tech said - "Hey - major amounts of lint - like this - should not be located in this bottom area." It wasn't until our fifth fire - when we took the dryer apart ourselves that we discovered the design flaws. Any idiot can see where the lint is escaping. Why the machine was designed this way is beyond me. Why no one has contacted us about a recall -- or to tell us this machine is a fire hazard is beyond me. Why professional experienced repair techs did not know about this issue - or couldn't figure it out by looking at the machine is beyond me. Samsung should notify every consumer who has purchased this machine and offer a fix - or a newly redesigned dryer. You cannot tell me they don't know about this issue. Do not buy this machine. Or if you do. Don't go to sleep - or leave your house while it's operating - or you may wake up to - or come home to a burned down home. Good luck!
We purchased this machine 10/18/2009 - with four fire repairs over the first six years - the last fire in the seventh year of ownership.

product_title: Samsung : DV448AGP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Gas Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_title: Large Capacity Promises, Low Capacity Quality
review_text:
We purchased this unit within the last year hoping its large capacity would help to clear up the log jam in our laundry room and for a while it did just that.

Lately the thing stopped working and we discovered a series of nasty surpises: A fried electornic control board, a broken drive belt, one of the four rollars that supports the drum having separated from its bearing and gone walkabout, and a torn drum seal. All this after a bit more than 6 months' family use.

We also found that although we live in an urban area with a lot of appliance repair shops, there are relatively few who work on Samsungs (and the one we found missed most of the problems). Then we discovered that parts for this thing do not seem to be stocked cy local sources and have to be ordered from Samsung direct.

With an unresponsive repair shop and laundry piling up, I went to replace the drive belt myself, which is when I learned that the design of this thing is such that you have to disassemble most of the unit to get to the motor. Not easy or cheap (and not helped by the fact that this product is new enough that most of the guidance for replacing Samsung belts on line do not apply to this dryer).

The final touch: the "stainless steel" trim on the front is already showing rust spots (the trim on the companion washer is worse: it is simply covered in rust)

Bottom line: we have a unit that though less than a year old looks like it is 10 years old and acts like it is 15. What a lemon!

review_text: This dryer has been nothing but a total and complete hassle and waste of our money.  The dryer spins all of our sheets into a super tight little ball/roll and then shuts off.  Obviously, the entire middle of the roll is still wet, and we have to pull everything out, pull it apart, and then rearrange it when we put it back in the machine.  We have to do this 8-10 times per load.  I have called Samsung's customer service department a number of times.  The best suggestion they have has is to wash the sheets with wet, heavy towels.  Any person with any intelligence knows that you do not wash sheets and towels together as the lint and fluff from the towels will wreck your sheets.  Laundry 101.  That was the best suggestion they came up with.  When a tech was finally booked to come out, I got a call from Samsung's technical department and was told that the drum on the machine was too heavy and that it's a design flaw with the unit.  He said that they have had several people call with the same problem with this unit.  This was certainly in contrast to what the customer service agent said that I had previously spoken with.  He said he hadn't heard of any problems with this unit.  I explained this on my fifth call to the customer service department and was basically treated like I was stupid and had no idea how to do laundry properly.  I have NEVER had anything like this happen with any other dryer from any other manufacturer.  The machine is clearly a dud, and so is the so-called wonderful customer service provided by Samsung.  Stay away from SAMSUNG, and stay away from this unit in particular.

product_title: Samsung : WF328AAR 4.0 cu. ft. Front Load Washer - Tango Red
review_text:
I have had this washer for almost a year and a half and i'm completely in love with it. The capacity is absolutely amazing. You can pack it to the brim and it will clean everything thoroughly. I don't even pretreat stains anymore. The matching dryer is equally amazing as it will dry everything perfectly in no time. We bought the set knowing we would have to stack them (yes they are stackable if you buy the stacking kit) and we got the pedestals for free but we unfortunately had to store those under a bed until we moved. The high spin barely makes any noise and it does NOT walk across the floor like some of the other brands. The vibration reduction system works beautifully. In fact, when the spin cycle just starts you can see a little wiggle if you watch it but then it smooths out and your clothes come out with practically no water in them. I also absolutely love the silver care feature. This allows me to sanitize the washcloths that i use on my face without using a whole tank of hot water. It simply passes the water over silver plates to clean out the bacteria. I also love the delay start feature. If i don't want to wait up on a load to put it in the dryer i can just set it so that it will go off a couple hours before i wake up. That way the clothes don't set in the washer wet all night and smell musty in the morning.

I can't say enough good things about this washer. In fact, if my washer broke today i would buy it all over again. I've enjoyed using it so much.

product_title: LG : WM3988HWA 27 Steam Washer/Dryer Combo with 4.2 cu. ft. Capacity - DISCONTINUED
review_text:
We just got this unit yesterday, so have had it for a little over 24 hours now. We've washed about 4 loads of laundry so far, and we LOVE it!! Load #1 was a mix of jeans (4 pair), shirts, socks, & underwear, load #2 was a sheet set from a king size bed, load #3 was a blanket from a king size bed, and load #4 was about 6 pair of shorts. We also threw 3 wrinkled shirts in to try out the 20-minute steam cycle which removes wrinkles.

We've been having problems with our dryer vent. Our house was built in the early 1980's when they were using the flex plastic dryer vents. Due to the way our house is setup, it would have been some major construction and several thousand dollars to replace the dryer vent. We were having to run the dryer through 2 or 3 (sometimes more) cycles to get things thoroughly dry. This was making the electric bill higher than it should be. It also caused the heating element on the dryer to burn out and need to be replaced 3 times due to not being vented well. I did have the dryer vent cleaned out and it helped a little, but it still didn't work great. We had looked at the other LG combo units in the past, but didn't get one due to their small size and poor reviews. We decided to check them out again and found this new "full size" unit which had great reviews, so decided to take the plunge this time around.

It takes about 3 1/2 to 4 hours from start to finish to wash and dry a load in this LG, but that's not a big deal for us. You just start it up and let it do its thing. There are two people (including myself) in our home, so we don't normally have huge amounts of laundry to do. Instead of doing all the laundry one day a week, we've decided to do smaller loads a couple times a week. This new unit uses MUCH less water than our old washer, so the water bill should go down a little. Also, the electric bill should go down some since we won't be running a dryer two or three times per load. Another plus is that since it's just a single unit, we've put in shelving where the dryer used to be and now have a little more storage space!

The only drawback we've found so far is that there is no way to dry-only without washing. I would recommend that you thoroughly read the owner's manual before first use if you buy this unit. In our excitement to try it out, we ran the first load through without reading the manual and selected a cycle that washes only and doesn't dry. We then had to run the load through a wash cycle again to dry. The owner's manual has a chart in it that clearly shows what each of the cycles does and doesn't do. There are two or three cycles that will only wash and won't dry. Other than no option to dry without washing, I've found no drawbacks/problems with this unit and wish I would have bought it a long time ago.

This unit cost us much less (and no construction mess) than it would have cost to replace the dryer vent, and will end up saving us money on water and electricity. Thank you to LG for an awesome product!! We purchased from A.J. Madison which had the best price we could find anywhere, plus no tax (since we're not in NY) and free shipping!

UPDATE 10/18/08: I stand corrected! D.M. let me know that there is a dry-only option, and indeed there is! It's not listed anywhere at all in the owner's manual, so we weren't aware of how to do it. After you turn the unit on you have to press the Dry button BEFORE you turn the cycle selection knob, and it then puts the unit into dry-only mode. THANK YOU, D.M.!!! :-)

review_text:
I have this combo about 6 months now. Even though we live in a new home which has a perfect vent out, the main reason for buying this machine is to gain time and space (literally). We read through many reviews of the previous model and there were issues with the drying (wrinkles). Due to the fact that this machine has a larger capacity, this wrinkling have been greatly reduced. I have actually just one pants that is made of rough thick cotton and it's the only one that is clearly more wrinkled compared to using a separate (air) dryer. However, we found already ways to minimize it and that is to use the post-wash tumbling option (you can choose to let the machine tumble intermittendly when it's all done, to prevent wrinkling). This is a smart move from LG.

Apart from that, this machine is just the best, I wouldn't know why you want to buy a separate washer and dryer:
During the day we throw in cloth and usually we set the delay time as "switch-on around 3am" and the next morning you take the cloth out, ready to use, no more pain in remembering to put the cloth from washer to dryer.
The machine is also so quiet that you can indeed do the above, it's a simply a whisperer.
We are quite "green" so this machine is for us, the energy usage is so low compare to standard washers and dryers, mainly due to the condense drying system. Standard dryers are like a combination of many hairdryers and you know ho wmuch wattage they have.
Last but not least, you safe so much space by eliminating 1 machine (dryer).
Great machine!
