review_title: This family of 5 can't live without it....
review_text:
After waiting for a very long time because of the cost we decided to finally take the plunge on this 2 in 1 unit after a brick and mortar store offered price match and no-interest for 18 months. WE are so happy that we went for it! I don't know how we survived without it. Well actually we do know how we did... our 3rd bedroom had a minimum of 10 laundry bags waiting to go out. It was an endless and vicious cycle that never came to an end.

The washing performance of this unit is impeccable! We have been using it religiously since December 2008 and are in love. There are many different cycles that offer a myriad of water temps,soil levels, spin cycle speeds and drying time variations. We basically use the Cotton cycle for most of our wash and the cold/cold water option. This machine is so efficient and works wonderfully with nothing but cold water. It truly does remove stains! Since it is a front loader and energy efficient, then you MUST use HE liquid. We have used the Tide 2X HE and Wisk 3X HE; personally we love the Tide scent but the Wisk offers you more bang for your buck at this time because it is 3X concentrated.

I read and re-read the reviews posted on here and another site and found that the machine *MIGHT* be okay for our family of 5. We are very happy to report that the machine keeps the wash in check in our household and we honestly average 3 loads a week. It is my husband, myself, 6 year old, 5 year old (asthma sufferer) and 2 year old. The machine has a large 4.2 cubic foot capacity allowing for an extra large load at a time. As others have pointed out, your drying capacity is not 4.2 but rather half, or half of the load that you have originally placed in. It was a trial and error of a few loads to figure the drying aspect of this wonderful machine.

I also wash my King comforter with the Bulky/Large cycle. There is no dry cycle for this setting because it is for very large items that would otherwise not normally dry in a dryer. It does a wonderful job of washing our bedding and removing all of the excess water for hang drying on our closet door. That specific cycle is 54 minutes long.

What works for us is to not always drying the loads. We have set up a tension rod in our second bathroom shower area and air dry our clothes. We truly cram a lot of clothes in there and it does a great job each and every time. Within a couple of hours the clothes are fully dried and ready to put away. If we are just doing our second upkeep weekly load we usually just dry because it isn't as gigantic as our original load. The dryer DOES indeed work and makes everything toasty hot. For others who claim it doesn't, then their machine must have been overloaded or it may have been a very heavy, bulky item. The dryer runs on steam so it sprays small amounts of water on your clothes. YES, it does wet your clothes to dry them; not sure how it does it, but it does work! A cotton/normal (average) wash cycle with added 16 minute pre-wash cycle, high spin and more dry will take you about 4 hrs. Unless you are watching the machine, you will not notice the time.

Pros:
*Ventless system that is a great set up for apartment dwellers.

*Many wash cycles and water temp options that really clean clothes.

*Energy efficient... we haven't noticed a difference on our electric or water bill as of yet. Keep in mind we are washing in cold water.

*Convenience of just drying without washing if necessary. Just select DRY after turning the machine on and select time desired.

*Being able to PAUSE any time during the cycle to either, add, remove, relocate or just check on your items.

*Allergiene and Steam cycles remove allergens for those that have asthma sufferers or any allergies.

CONS:
*Extra Large capacity drum does wonderfully washing but will have to be cut in half for drying.

*The wonderful PAUSE feature that I constantly use has an 8 minute time out. Twice I would be in the middle of doing something and time out... I would unfortunately lose the whole cycle and have to start either from the beginning or somewhere near that. Not really a con, but an annoyance. The reality is that you can not do that at the laundromat so the feature is a GOD send at the end of the day. Many times, I have the kids bring me articles 5 mins later even though I was screaming at the top of my lungs to BRING ME EVERYTHING. That feature saved me.

*Our floors in the kitchen aren't rigid enough so at times on the extra high spin cycle we have shaking and vibrating througout the whole kitchen. The only remedy for this is to have good flooring. We are researching whether the stand can buffer some of the vibration.

So... my long review was trying to convince you to take a chance the way we did. Forget the negative reviews... they don't make sense. This is a great machine that will save you from the never-ending doom called, "LAUNDRY".

The unit plays tunes in response to starting, ending and errors, shows exactly what is being programmed on the illuminated display panel and displays a "door lock" message to eliminate damage from inappropriately trying to force the door open.
Overall, I love the unit.
Great job LG!

review_text:
After extensive research, we decided to take the plunge and invest a considerable amount of money in this machine. Our only regret is that we didn't do it sooner! It is amazing. Even our plumber, after he installed it, said "This is a beautiful machine!" --- and believe me, he has seen quite a few washers in his day. He plans to buy one for his own home. We live in NYC and our options were limited, both space-wise and in terms of venting. So that eliminated many choices that other people have. From reviews, which were mostly positive, I was afraid of low drying quality, low capacity, and possible odors since it is a front-loading machine. We have had ZERO problems with any of these. And I would disagree with the reviewer who said that this machine is not for a family of 4, 5 or 6. We are a family of 5 (two adults, 3 kids under 5) and this machine is perfect for us. I do loads about every other day, according to color/temperature, which are never that big anyway, so capacity is never a problem. However, when I have had to do larger loads, such as sheets and towels (for example, two towels and two sets of twin size sheets), everything comes out clean and dry with NO problem. The features are incredible, in terms of washing possiblilities and others such as pre-wash, steam, allergeine, and a wide range of drying cycles. The dryer will keep tumbling periodically even after it is finished in order to prevent wrinkles, which is great. Sometimes I prefer the clothes to be left slightly damp (I hate when normal dryers "bake" my clothes), and so sometimes they will be a bit wrinkled when they come out. This problem is very easily solved either by drying them a bit longer, or running the steam feature to eliminate wrinkles. It is so efficient that hardly any detergent (must be HE) needs to be used, and you will not notice a difference at all in energy or water bills (it runs on a 220 volt and is designed to use very little water. The amount of water needed for each cycle is tailored to fit the amount you need to wash by the machine).
I would recommend this to anyone who is interested in trying to reduce their carbon and water footprints---not just those with limited options, like us. It has a child lock, which really comes in handy with young kids. I also love the fact that I can program or delay a wash; often I put clothes in in the morning and they are washed and dried when I come home. Now they just need to make a machine to fold the clothes and put them away!!!
We have had no problem with mold or odors (I think because of the built-in dryer), no problems with capacity or with drying. I would highly recommend this washer dryer combo to anyone, regardless of their options or their family size. It's amazing and WELL WORTH the investment! Why have two, huge, bulky machines when just one will do?
THe only drawback I can think of, which is very small, is that, if I had separate machines, I would sometimes do two wash loads and then dry them together. Very minor inconvenience. I should also add that this washer/dryer is VERY kind and gentle to your clothes!

review_title: Runs like a TANK +tips for other owners
review_text:
I bought this washer/dryer heavily used and 8 years old in the local classifieds, intending to install it in my 133 year old house that had no proper washer/dryer hookups.
If you own one of these or are looking to grab one second hand, I hope my experiences will help you out.

I've had this unit for almost a year now and I've got to give LG some serious props, this thing is built like a TANK!
When I first bought this unit, the previous owner lied to me and said it worked fine. I assumed he was lying but bought it anyways since he only wanted $300 and I'm pretty good at fixing things.
When I got it home I found that it leaked like mad, didn't dry anything, and I would routinely come home to a flooded laundry room and the washer full of water with a drain error on the screen.

First, I looked into the flooding. That turned out to be caused by the extremely restrictive (it had crossed bars in the bottom) 1 inch drain on the old laundry sink it was draining into. Lint would get stuck in the bars in the drain, clogging it up and causing it to fill up. Once the sink was full it would flood every time the pump ran, then water would get sticker back into the washer eventually triggering the drain error.
The quick fix for this was putting in an over sink colander to catch the lint. The permanent fix was to replace the drain with a more open one. Now the lint (which there in very little of, BTW) drains just fine. This shouldn't be a problem if you have a standard washer drain.

Next was the leaking/not drying issue, which turned out to be the same problem.
The dryer on this works by blowing hot air thru a tall shaft running along the back right corner of the washer, then spraying a fine mist of cold water down the shaft. The cold water condenses the hot moisture which causes it to rain down the shaft to the bottom where it is pumped out by the drain pump.
The problem occurred when the mist sprayer was getting too much water, which sprayed out the top of the condenser shaft and leaked everywhere.
Where the cold water comes into the washer there is a manifold with 5 solenoid valves that send water to different parts of the washer. The valve for the mister has a flow restrictor press-fit into the manifold output. The flow restrictor had become dislodged and shot down the tube to the mister. I reinserted the flow restrictor and it quit leaking but it popped back out a few days later. I researched this issue and found that it is one of, if not the most common points of failure on this washer and LG recommends replacing the entire manifold when it fails ($90). I instead, reinserted the flow restrictor, drilled a 1/8 inch in front of it and slid a piece of brass rod into the hole to keep it in place. That fix will not only outlive the washer but probably me too. Since reengineering the manifold, the washer doesn't leak a drop and drys everything just fine.

Once everything was running well, I noticed that the washer want draining as fast as I thought it should have. This just turned out to be a worn drain pump which was only $50 (and in stock) at the local Sears. I consider this regular maintenance on an 8 year old washer.

Since giving it a little TLC, this washer runs like a champ. That said, here's some pointers to make your experience better:
1. Drying efficiency is largely based on heat dissipation. Don't put anything on top of the washer and get the pedestal if you can, it makes a difference in drying (and your back will thank you). Also, if you get the black version (or paint yours black) it will dissipate heat better due to black body radiation (yay science!).
2. To run a dry only cycle, turn on the washer, then, without turning the cycle selector, press the DRY button (once for normal, twice for more dry), then press the SPIN SPEED button once to remove the rinse/spin cycle.
3. Clean your washer once a week! I cannot overstate how much of a difference this makes to how well this thing washes and drys.
Here's how to properly clean your washer/dryer:
A. Turn on the washer then hold the EXTRA RINSE button for 3 seconds to select TUB CLEAN.
B. Removed any clothes that are in the washer.
C. Fill the bleach dispenser with bleach.
D. Start the cycle. It will run for 30 minutes.
E. Once the cleaning cycle finishes, use a towel to wipe down the inside of the door, the rubber sealing ring, and the tub itself. (Now is also a good time to clean up any spilled soap to keep it looking nice)
F. Open the little door on the bottom left of your washer.
G. Pull out the drain tube and remove it's plug to drain any remaining water into a bucket. Please note, this is only possible if you have the washer pedestal, otherwise the drain tube is right at floor level. If you don't have the pedestal, I recommend keeping your washer on a catch pan. They are cheap and can save you from a wet floor.
H. Unscrew the drain filter and empty it.
I. Reinsert the drain filter, ensuring the open end is facing up. It only really goes in one way but my roommate proved that it can be forced in wrong, then it won't seal and you end up with a flooded laundry room.
J. Put the plug back in the drain tube and snap it back into its holder.
K. Close the access door.

This it very useful if you don't have the pedestal as you can catch the remaining water by putting a towel under the drain filter when removing it.

review_title: Design flaw allows mold, trashes clothes, high upkeep
review_text: I have owned my WM3001 LG washer for 2 years. In the first year using powder detergent mold grew between the drums that could not be removed. Tub cleanse cycle, bleach, baking soda, hydrogen peroxide, Whirl Out, vinegar do not remove the mold from between the drums. The problem is the rubber door gasket that is pierced with 3 holes in the center bottom that allows water to infiltrate and collect between the drums so mold grows. Mold also collects in the manual drain tubing and filter. Irony of all ironies there is a sticker on the front saying "Certified asthma and allergy friendly. Meets ASP-WM-01:07 Standard of the Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America". Well, mold IS my asthma trigger and my toddler has eczema. Our clothes and towels smell moldy when wet. I contacted LG to address this and was told to fax my original sales receipt. Then they claimed never to have received it. So I emailed them a photo of the receipt and I was told I would be contacted by extended warranty service for a 1 time service call. I never was contacted again. Customer service is indeed negligible. Regardless this washer requires unacceptably high upkeep and it is so harsh on clothing and towels (unraveling them after 3 washes) that only the gentlest cycle can be used despite all the fancy options. Not what I paid for. Still looking for some satisfaction on this purchase.

product_title: Electrolux EIFLW55HMB Front Load Washer with IQ-Touch Controls Mediterranean Bluea
review_text:
This washer basin is huge - 4.7 holds everything and we have a family of 5. We almost bought the Kenmore Elite HE5T with steam but found out the regular units are 4.4 but the sale unit only available in "barolo red" was only 4.0 - big enough for most but size was our major factor in a new washer. So we gave up the steam and went with Electrolux. Electrolux does not make a steam washer, the steam dryer is in the wave touch model ($300 more apiece than the IQ touch). The main reason to me for steam is stain removal; not so much wrinkle removal, so IQ touch was fine. Apparently Electrolux and Bosch don't think steam in a washer is necessary; neither offer it. This washer/dryer is fantastic. I was concerned about the doors (as many are) but they are incredibly sturdy and you should have no trouble with them, I got used to the 'push' feature immediately. The tops of the units do scratch - we lined them with the rubber foam liners so we can use the surface area (you can get the wide at Lowe's in the tool section). Both are very quiet - washer spins so fast you won't believe it. I was also concerned about the extended wash time with front loaders but with the size of the bin I can almost double my loads. Also, Electrolux offers an 18 minute fast wash cycle. Dryer time is incredibly fast because clothes are almost dry when they come out of the washer - 20 minutes for drying in most cases.

UPDATE 6/3/11 - I checked back and saw the comments and Electrolux began offering a steam washer shortly after our purchase. Our Electrolux IQ Touch Washer and Dryer are still going strong and we love them. No issues whatsoever, and my teenagers do their own laundry all the time.

product_title: Electrolux : EWFLS70JTS 27 Front-Load Washer with 5.1 cu. ft. Capacity
review_text: I own the set, matching dryer. Yes, it's very quiet, you can sleep next to it and it won't make a sound to wake you. The clothes always come out clean and very dry for less dryer time which helps to keep clothes looking new and in good condition. You also save on electricity.  It's definitely a water saver, it uses only what it needs. The many settings are excellent for the many different needs we come across, comforters, baby clothes, delicates, etc. The machine does what they say it does! However it feels "cheap" for said brand and the price point.  The liquid laundry compartment feels wobbly, (I tested others at the store & they felt the same), the latch to keep the door closed is plastic (and part of the door so if it breaks and you are not under warranty it's $100 dollars for that little latch). The doors don't close as smoothly, or even come open on the gentle push as smoothly. The buttons aren't as sturdy as I'd like them to be. I've had the machine 2 years, and I would have expected it to hold up a lot better than it has. Yes, I do use it maybe 3 times a week, and 2 years is a long time but at this price point I was hoping to use it for at least 7 years. So to sum it up, I originally thought this machine would be like my BMW X5; rugged but classy, tough but luxurious... instead it feels like my old Camry, reliable but it started to rattle after those 200k miles. Happy washing.

product_title: Electrolux : EWFLS70JTS 27 Front-Load Washer with 5.1 cu. ft. Capacity
review_text:
I am a mother of four and wife to a filthy (and I mean that lovingly) farmer/rancher. I do a WHOLE LOT of laundry. I bought this washer over a year ago based on positive reviews by well-meaning people who only owned it for a week.

At first, this washer was okay. We were replacing a Whirpool front-loader after the control board went out after only two years. It was comparable to the much cheaper Whirpool. The large capacity was nice, as was the quick-wash cycle (though that was ONLY for very small loads). Yes, there are a lot of fancy cycle options and a neat dial and all kinds of gizmos, but the washer itself was just okay. I didn't notice it getting anything more or less clean than any other washer we've owned. I was never gaga over it, but it did the job.

Fast-forward a year. We came home from our vacation, and the washer wouldn't spin. My husband ran diagnostics, and either the control board (which costs half or more the price of a new washer) or a pressure sensor are out. NOBODY will come work on this machine. We have heard multiple excuses, but what it boils down to is, nobody will come out and touch an Electrolux. I called Electrolux myself and was told, respectfully, that since it was a couple of months out of warranty, I was on my own. My husband even offered to load the washer up and take it to someone, but nobody would even work on it that way!

So, now, I am doing laundry for six with a 1970s-model "spare" from the in-laws, researching new washers yet again while my pricey Electrolux sits in the garage strapped to a dolly. I would not recommend this brand, or this washer.

We also bought the matching dryer, and it is now taking an hour and a half to dry a load of jeans, so I expect we'll also be buying a new dryer soon. Lots of bells and whistles on this washer, just no durability.

product_title: Whirlpool : WTW5200VQ 27 Top-Load Washer with 3.5 cu. ft. Capacity White
review_text:
Bought this washer new. It is probably the noisiest washing machine I've ever heard and the most troublesome in 45 years of buying washing machines. With the feet properly adjusted, load balanced (and not overloaded), it dances all over the place, banging into the dryer, walls, etc. while spinning. Physically pressing down on the top quiets it down a lot and holds it in place. If you have the time and desire to do that, then you may be happy with this washer. Otherwise, look I suggest you find another make or model.

2 year update: After a year of service calls, the machine was judged to be not-repairable by the service organization and we received a refund under the extended warranty we had purchased from the selling store. If you insist on buying one of these, it would be a good idea to fully understand what happens when the service people are unable to find or fix the problem. Oh yes - the replacement washer (different brand) works just fine in the same location with the same washloads.

product_title: Whirlpool : WTW5200VQ 27 Top-Load Washer with 3.5 cu. ft. Capacity White
review_text:
As there is no need to repeat the positive comments made by the other 5-Star raters from this AND OTHER sites (with whom I totally agree), I'll just give a couple other comments/observations.

First, regarding the "noise": When I initially read these complaints - here and other sites (prior to purchase), I instantly thought, "Every washer I've ever owned makes that noise when the contents are very unevenly distributed". So I bought this model (based on the positive reviews); and I am s-o-o-o-o-o glad I did. Although NO washer I ever owned/used has been "SOUND-FREE" (SILENT), this one is quieter than ANY of the others - no "NOISE" - well, at least for the first 3- 4 days! Then there it was - a very LOUD THUMPING SOUND - "NOISE". This was my opportunity to test my theory. About 30 seconds or so earlier I had lifted the lid during the spin cycle; and apparently dislodged some items from their balanced positions. When I lifted the lid and saw that this, indeed, was the case, I simply rearranged the items (as with previous machines), closed the lid, and VOILA - problem resolved - back to quiet operation!!! Also, sometimes when tub is not centered, noise can occur - with ANY washer.

Second, I DO wish there was a TRULY HOT WATER option! This washer adjust water temp by alteranating hot with cool or warm to obtain what IT senses is the IDEAL temp for each load - based on the user's setting selections; however, I must admit that my "WHITES" DO get really clean. So I guess it's not a real issue!

SUMMARY: Not too fancy and/or expensive! Excellent basic washer (with some nice features - i.e. "extra rinse"cycle)! Does what it's suppose to do - gets laundry clean; and, does so superbly well! QUIET - WHEN BALANCED! I am extremely happy with this washer; and, would GLADLY recommend to my friends!!!

product_title: GE Profile DPVH890GJ 7.5 Cu. Ft. Capacity Gas Dryer with Multiple Dry Cycles, 5 Heat Selections,
review_text:
I bought this dryer along with the washer and pedestals. They look great and I like many of the features. The washer "talks" to the dryer and relays information based on the cycles you select so that all you need to do is throw your wet clothes in and it automatically sets the time for you. Sensor Dry is a nice feature as well. Relatively quiet units.

I bought them in March of 2009. The Smart Dispense system on the washer didn't work, so they had to send a technician out to replace a circuit board. Since then it's been trouble free....until now. The dryer drum stopped turning. I thought maybe the belt had snapped, so I was able to open the unit following some online instructions. Belt was broken, but it turns out the pully and the motor are also shot. 2.5 years old and we use it a few times a week (family of 5). Considering that I paid over $1000 for the dryer, you would imagine it would last much longer.

Now, GE wants to charge me $100 to come out and tell me what I already know - that the motor is dead. They said if that is indeed the case, they'd offer me $100 coupon to buy a new unit. If it comes to that, I'll probably simply get a Whirlpool and not worry about them matching or "talking to each other".

Lesson learned. Function > Form.

review_title: Great at first, then things go wrong
review_text:
I bought this dryer just over two years ago, along with the matching Samsung washing machine. For the first year and a half I was very satisfied with both: they looked great, they were quiet, and the washing machine doesn't use much energy. But then they both started making more and more noise. Things finally got to be too much just past the two year mark- when the warranty ended, of course.

Most recently, the dryer stopped working, and displays an error code ("HE") when I try to run it. Apparently I need a new heating element which I'll have to pay for, along with the service/labor expenses. Considering that I ponied up nearly $800 for this appliance just over two years ago, I'm less than thrilled about both the inconvenience of a breakdown and the bother/expense of getting it fixed.

Next time I'm going to look for something simple with a reputation for being a tank.

UPDATE: As it turns out, I was able to find online some very well-written instructions for how to fix this, and they include a source for the part: appliancepartspros dot com. (Check out shopping dot com, the instructions are in a review of the Samsung DV218AE.) The part arrived in two days, and I had it installed in half an hour. If you're somewhat confident as a do-it-yourselfer, this is not a difficult fix. I would, however, recommend replacing the entire heater duct assembly, not just a sensor or an element: it's a much easier operation, and you'll know that the heating element and the sensors are all brand new.

product_title: LG 3.5 CF WASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_text:
We bought a LG WM2010CW front loader washer in July 09 mainly to save water in our 17 year old country septic system. We had a still working 9 year old Maytag washer with a high capacity 45 gals per super wash and this new LG washer only takes 16 gals for the largest load (measured with the digital meter on our water softner). We are very satisfied so far after over a month using the new LG washer and also bought the matching dryer: with various dealer plus energy star [...] and selling our used older units for [...], the LG W/D combo only cost slightly [...] on sale including sales tax. Perhaps this Fall 2009 there will be US government "cash for clunkers" style additional [...] on new Energy Star washers, you may save another $50! We got ours on a special must by both washer & dryer for [...] total deal from a local appliance dealer.

This washer is very easy to use and gets the clothes as clean or cleaner then the old top loader Maytag that literally soaked them in water. It makes some strange noises and does take about 50% longer but they come out very dry on high spin (no noticable noise on a tile floor above a basement from that high spin either). Hopefully the JD Power top quality rating holds for us as my wife washes a LOT of clothes & towels so even with our kids gone it will get plenty of use. Only minor things to watch:

- Keep the door open an inch or so to dry out the rubber gasket. My wife occasionally wipes out the gashet and even the top detergent dispenser. You are supposed to drain and check the lower filter monthly. We just did and there was nothing there other than about a cup of water, so based on feedback from a friend with a front loader we may back off to a few times a year.

- If your house is like ours the old style W/D had the washer on the right and dryer on the left. All these front loaders seems to be reversed with the doors (not changeable on the washer) swinging so the washer should be on the left and dryer on the right. We have plenty of cord and hose to do that, however the dryer vent has to be re-drilled (through tile floor!) so we are trying it this way. We also skipped the ridiculously priced pedestals - bend at the knees and hang in there, it's not heavy stuff.

product_title: LG 3.5 CF WASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_text:
Growing exhausted from having to sit on and baby-sit my ancient never balanced top loader (no matter how scientific I loaded clothes) I decided it was time for a front loader. My primary objective was reducing shaking during spin cycles than reducing water usage. While there are models out there with VRT (Vibration reduction Technology) I was unwilling to pay the premium.
The spin cycle on a front loader differs from that of a top loader in a way that I had not expected. On a top loader the shaking is in a front/back side/side fashion making the machine walk when shaking and in my case making the machine join me in my office or the living room. A front loader on the other hand has a side/side Up/down shake. Though unbalanced loads are not as common the machine still has a vibration, and since the shake is Up/down this has a jack-hammer effect on the floor. So, on one hand the machine shakes far less than my old unit the shaking that remains propagates throughout the house more (crawl space). Anti-vibe pads did help allot later on (homemade from an unused 1/2" rubber mat). With that said the unit does not require me to baby-sit and with support under the floor or if placed on a slab shaking shouldn't be an issue.
VRT. My mother has a Samsung unit with VRT and it is noticeably better in terms of vibrations. Beyond that they both clean clothes just as well. Also, as advertised the unit is very quiet (except for the High speed spin cycle vibrations).

review_title: Efficient but be careful with small children
review_text:
We purchased this washer 2 months ago because the new GE washer that came with our home was aweful and we got tired of calling service to fix it and getting the run around.

This washer is amazing in that it spins the clothes so they're practically dry before you need to dry them. (Maybe our other washer was just that awful, but this seems amazing!)

One time water did come out of the front door but I figured out I had loaded it too full (a twin comforter and a bit of clothes). I have had no problem since then, just didn't give enough room for water to move around that time.

The front loading idea was new to us and we didn't really think about the issue in regards to our kids pushing the beeping buttons. We were relieved that you can turn the beeping off if you want to and that there is a child lock on the buttons so the kids can't push them in a cycle. The PROBLEM IS there is no child lock for when the machine is OFF! Our son likes to go and fiddle with it and turns it on and then plays with the buttons. So, while he can't mess with the washer during the cycle he can before and after. :P Fortunately we can just shut the laundry room door, but even so, it's something we have to watch out for so keep this in mind if you'll have kids around.

review_text:
I wish I were happier with this unit but it doesn't do what I want it to do. I live in the North so my cold water is quite cold. Also the washer is in the basement (60ºF) and there is about 20' of pipe filled with 60º water before any real hot water reaches the washer. This machine starts by squirting cold water into the machine--even for the so-called Hot wash which is preset to be something like 105º. So because of the very low water usage, enough hot water water can not be added to get it up to speed, besides which I want actual hot wash not 105º. The warm is preset to 95º but because of my situation it only reaches 75º. I tried using the Hot wash setting to get warm and it still did not get above body temp and then it only has a cold rinse which is pure tap cold which in Montana is just too cold to rinse properly.

As a note, to test the water temp, I let it fill and start washing and actually used a thermometer to test the water in the tub. Likewise for the rinse temp. I know you can't tell anything by what temp is running into the machine at a given moment.

If you are happy with tepid and cold temperatures, or maybe you live in Texas, this is a great washer. I have had another front loader which worked fine and I found out belatedly these were the reasons:
1. My other house had radiant floor heat so the machine was pre-warmed to room temp
2. machine was on main floor
3. laundry room was in center of house and h/w heater was in there, making it the warmest room in the house
4. brand new H/W heater
5. washer very close to H/W heater

The LG repairman told me I needed to get a model with built-in heater, but after I researched what the preset temps are, I know I would still not be happy. I think I am going to get the amana 7200 which has a true Hot wash (straight hot out of the tap although it will be lessened by the cold water in the pipes). The amana preset warm is higher than the LG and I am waiting to find out how it fills (does it start with hot or cold water?). I also have a call in to my plumber about inserting a valve to increase the temp of my incoming cold.

This has taken many hours of research and I am longing for the old days! So many features but not what I want and need! All I really want is about 105º wash and 75º rinse. Ideally (and my previous washer did this) I would also like a 75º/75º setting for wool. My other washer, which I regret leaving in the house I sold, had TWO warm/warm settings--one with a wash temp boost, one without. I set the un-boosted warm to be tepid; in the boost setting, it let in more hot water. It worked great for my needs. I rarely use a true hot wash, but when you need it--because of diapers, sickness, lice, whatever--you need it.

Aside from the temp. issue, I think this is a great washer. It has cycles that I want and is easy to use. It's kind of noisy in the beginning beacuse it starts and stops as it senses the load. One drawback is it doesn't save a favorite setting, so if you don't like the defaults on a cycle, you will have to push a few buttons each time.

product_title: LG 3.5 CF WASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_text:
We purchased this appliance Mid-Yr. 2010 to replace a top loader. Our 15Y old high end Kchn.Aid T/Ldr. would more than likely have kept on chugging along..however I attempted to wash a "Q" size quilt/comforter. Once wet...just became extremely heavy & finished off the thing. Rather than repair an old app., we purch. new. Found a terrific deal at Sears on a seemingly "last model on sales floor" of this type. Cost 350.+/- (200.00+ off reg). After researching these LG Frnt-LD washers.., alt. brands etc..including Samsung, Kenmore & others as well; we decided to purchase the LG. (Our 2007 LG 15,000BTU AC is a charm thus far)
As for the washer- After 6 months of daily usage we have no major complaints. The appliance works very well. Cycle choices & adjustments are helpful. Advises on "time remaining", chirps when finished and more. However to get the most out of the washer...brief the manual.
While reading reviews from others for this model some make note of issues with drainage or smells...but I haven't noticed anything actually worth mentioning. For the smell issue my wife occasionally either opens the door a tad for an hour..or a quick wipe around the inside door/seal. (On the same plane as emptying the crumb tray for the toaster) As for the drainage & vibrating pipe issues, we don't hav'em. Possible our plumbing application is configured where no pipe-vibes occur & the drainage door at bottom/front is never a problem.
So,while tomorrow may add new thoughts on this item...we are completely satisfied with it's operation/performance to date.
I believe that prior to the initial manuf. warr. expiring, we will purchase an extended warr. (mostly to cover the Digital/Dig. Operation/Readouts etc.)
One feature that could be re-designed is the LED readout. Though no issues, it could be expanded to show actual gallons consumed upon completion of any given cycle type...or even specific H2O temperature during cycles...or other certain "go-green" type data../Other brands may already incorporate this..i don't know.
Would recommend this appliance. VG op's & also a VG value as few brands average 2+ X the price...for features that might not be "absolutely" necessary. Why go over the top ?

If we get an average of 12-15YR or (*20,000 HOURS) of service from the unit...all the better.
It gets replaced despite it's condition at that time for newer technology.

May update review...once appliance sees 1yr+ usage.

review_text:
I love my washer and dryer. I do 2-3 loads a week and I usually use the normal setting so I just push 2 buttons to get it started If you like to customize it doesn't remember your settings so you would need to push the settings you want to change each time you do a load. This doesn't bother me at all but if you do a lot of loads and don't like the preset settings it might be a bit annoying.

I use way less detergent than the recommended dose on the side of the box (basically half!) and my clothes are always perfectly clean.

This is a front loader so the cycles do take longer than the upright machines. About an hour or more for a normal cycle. I stuff my loads full so I'm not in a hurry to do another one and I find they are almost dry when you pull them out due to the excellent spin it's not a big deal to leave them in the washer for a few hours.

The finished sound is a nice bell sound and you can turn it off, plus it has a child lock and a self cleaning cycle.

It does get moist inside, I leave the door open after a load so it drys out inside. If you leave it shut after a load it does smell a bit. Plus, I do have to clean where the rubber gasket is around the opening of the washer as it gets hair and gunk built up from your dirty clothes. Not a big deal but a filter there would be nice. I paid $799 for the pair, so I am very happy with them!

review_text:
I purchased this machine in March of 2010. I was looking to replace my 11 year GE washer, that still worked, but I wanted a new efficient machine for my new home. I did a lot of research on this LG washer before purchasing it. I based my purchase solely on (at the time) the MANY glowing reviews, the 10 year manufacture warranty, my history with OTHER LG products, and the great price I was able to negotiate. I loved it from first use and had ZERO issues with it........ until this week!
I noticed that it got VERY loud during a normal load in the last week or so. No codes were lit & not an "un-balanced" sound either, nothing sounded "off", just louder. Now fast forward to today......A very loud and sudden clinking in the spin cycle and the machine/drum seizes up?! The drum is immobile at this point. The clothes are wet but no water in the tub. After referring to LG's 800 number- they let me know it is OUT of warranty! After speaking to many others throughout the company I finally told me that if it WAS a motor issue that I would be covered for the parts-not the LABOR? Wow? So, long story short-After speaking with 3 different repair men (they ALL agreed from my description of events)IT will be a very Labor intense fix! At $350.00-$450.00 and they will not guarantee that it will not happen again? Apparently it has a "SPIDER" type mechanism that will corrode and disintegrate with some water types? According to the local repairmen I spoke with, this is happening frequently in my area! How many others are going through this?? I AM kicking myself that I did not get the extended warranty!! WHO KNEW this would happen after only 2.5 years? I will NOT be buying another LG! I am going back to my Tried and TRUE GE machines. At least if they break, I can afford to fix it and wont have to SCRAP it!!!!! DO NOT BUY this machine unless you have the money to replace it every few years!!

review_text:
A couple weeks ago we got our LG WM2101 washer and matching dryer.

I'm very happy with the dryer. It determines accurately when the load is dry without baking the clothes.

Unfortunately, the washer is another story. In the hot setting the temperature is regulated to a barely luke warm 95F. We thought the machine was broken and got a replacement. Same temperature! Then we called LG and had a technician come out. He determined everything is normal. LG says the range is 80 to 100F for the hot cycle, according to the technician who was sent to repair it. That is "warm" at best. BTW, this is not because our hot water supply isn't hot enough. The machine pumps in a lot of cold water to regulate it at 95F. I haven't seen any comments or reviews on this aspect. It seems most people don't check how hot their laundry is washed. I prefer 140F (60C) for hot.

The machine also has a sanitize cycle which is promised to achieve 158F. However, that cycle takes about 1 hour 45 minutes. Not really practical, nor energy efficient.

Sadly, we'll have to return the product and look for another manufacturer. Hard to believe LG can sell so many washers considering this issue!

I went to sears and they didn't have the model I had settled on - they directed me to this one. More checking of reviews ensued. I ended up buying this from Sears. On sale, + 5% off for using my sears account plus no financing for a year it was a reasonable deal. $665.00.

My husband did the pick up and installation and that was easy. (Don't forget to take out the shipping bolts!)

There were two things that stood out right away when we ran our first few loads -

1) The clothes were WAY cleaner than they had been in our top loader. I mean, seriously, I don't even know how to describe it. Just, wow, I didn't know a washing machine could get things so clean.

2) The dryer time was cut in half or better. A load of towels will dry in 20 minutes on the permanent press setting! AWESOME!

On the down side the cycle times are a little longer - Averaging just under an hour. The sanitize cycle is 1hr40-min. One reviewer had a complaint about water temperature. I have no idea how hot the water gets and will never have the energy to figure it out. I'm happy enough just seeing how clean everything is. Dish towels run in the sanitize cycle came out smelling clean. Yay!

The machine has a speed wash that will complete in just under 30 minutes. How cool is that? If you are behind on your laundry and just need to get some loads through you can have loads going through every half hour and you don't have to wait for the dryer because the clothes are spun dry so well their dry time is short.

The only real down side is that it is a myth to think you are now free to wash bulky things like king comforters. The load won't balance to spin and so the machine just keeps trying to balance it but it can't. However, I think it will work to wash the bulky items and stand by for the spin cycle. Just pull the clean comforter out and air dry it. (or squeeze it out yourself and put it in the dryer.

We debated on the 179.00 for an extended warranty. Based on the 10 year motor warranty and 3 year drum warranty we're skipping the extended warranty. I'll check back here if that turns out to have been a terrible mistake.

product_title: LG WM2101HW 27 Front-Load Washer 4.0 cu. ft. Capacity, 8 Wash Cycles - White
review_text:
I was tired of the old washer leaking all over my floor. The things that attracted me to this washer were the efficiency, the quietness, the high speed spin (dryer clothes), the direct drive motor (no mechanical gears etc.) and the sump to catch the water it does spill. Also It doesn't have a seal in the bottom of the tub to spring a leak, there is no bottom of the tub.
My experiences so far (only had it a while) are very good. No water on the floor. The sump drain only gets about a quart or less of water after a few loads. It is very quiet, though you do hear it at times. It is insanely simple to use. It may look complicated, but it isn't. You just dump your clothes in and your detergent in the reservoir, select the type of cycle you want with the knob. and push the go button. Now it will display a lot of lights in columns showing what options are default for the chosen cycle, if you want to change any of these you can use the buttons below the lights to toggle through the choices for that option before hitting go, but the defaults will get you through. It does get your clothes clean and it does get them quite a bit dryer. Also we set ours on our concrete slab floor and haven't had one iota of trouble with shaking at any time.

Still the thing is new and we haven't had it long, but we're very happy now.

review_text:
Unfortunetly I had my washer break and had to go get a new one all in one day because we live in a very small town and had only that day to get to the city so I had no time to read reviews. I'm a huge review reader so this was very hard for me. I used the online feature on my phone to look while we shopped, but still not the same. So needless to say I was very skepticle and tried my best to compare a few washers and dryers at a few different stores.
I'm very glad to say that after a few weeks, I am nowhere near dissapointed and had I had the time to review I probably would have bought these anyway. The morning after we bought these and before I unpacked them I did read as much as I could and I only got more excited. (We also bought the matching dryer) I take a LOT of pride in my laundry, and thought I was pretty good at it already. Our top loader was about 9 years old and it did just fine so I wasn't even in the market. My laundry is so clean and even more fluffy now and it smells amazing! I can actually smell the fabric softner better and it's evenly dispensed so not oily looking stains on the darks. I think I have washed everything in my house 3 times ;O) just for fun. My poor little kids are lucky to have clothes on them because I'm constantly looking for things to throw in the wash! I think the hot water setting and internal heater work just fine because the glass gets all steamy, however my hot water heater is on the other side of the wall from the washer so it doesn't have far to travel. I can see with the spurts of water how it wouldn't travel a whole house well and stay hot and that seemed to be some peoples complaint. Fortunetly I don't have that problem. I have also never expected complete silence from a washer and dryer... get a sound proof room if you need it that bad... it's laundry! As others have wrote... the water filling is louder than the rest of the cycle but I can't believe how little water it uses. The spurts come from the fact that this thing is so smart it measures just the right amount of water for each load! Think of the money I'm saving! And then to top it off my dryer is super "smart" too... it knows when the clothes are dry on the sensor dry and adjusts the time to it. The only problem I have had with that is not really a problem.. the sensor can't always tell when a blanket is still damp on the inside so it will lessen the time... I just adjust the blanket and use the timed dry setting instead of the sensor....
I hope this product still remains wonderful for years... it also has a ten year motor warranty on the washer! And I super LOVE all the "bells and whistles" AKA all the different choices I have for my differnt types of loads to include the time delay setting... cause lets face it... not all loads of laundry are the same!

review_text:
I bought this washer about 15 months ago. The motor failed just over a year; the rotor contains a plastic piece that connects to and turns the tub. The worst part of this ordeal is to deal with their services. The rotor is supposed to be warrantied for 10 years. However, the service person told me that the warranty was voided because I attempted to repair myself. Since I can't wait for two weeks for their "official" repair person to come to visit (I'm living in Austin, Texas; a decent sided city, not a remote village), I did end up fixing the machine myself, and having to pay for purchasing the rotor. My request to have the part reimbursed was repeatedly refused. The reason given is that they don't ship parts to customers directly. If so, why do they claim the 10 year warranty? It's so frustrating to deal with customer support whose only job is say NO if they can. I'm so surprised that LG doesn't care about customer satisfaction at all. I'll really think twice because I buy any LG again.

review_text:
I chose the LG WM2101 HW due to Consumer Reports rating. I ordered the optional pedestal and extended service plan from Home Depot also. I have owned the unit for one month and have no complaints. The unit was placed in my basement which has a cement floor so vibration is not an issue. The unit does "thump" a little when first it starts to spin, but then quiets down. The washer does not use as much water as my twenty year old Maytag top loader, but gets the clothes clean gently. I purchased the optional pedestal. It works well,but is too expensive.

I was concerned about the mildew issue mentioned on this site and others. At the end of laundry day, I wipe down the door, gasket and soap tray. I leave the front door and the soap dispenser tray open when the unit is not being used. So far, no odors.

Update... 14 months now I have owned this washer. Still is OK. There has been a few times the washer did not spin the water out of the load. I think the problem was an unbalanced small load. I've found out that it is best to do full loads ,if you can. My water bill has dropped $20.00 a month.

product_title: LG : DLE2101W 27 Electric Dryer with 7.3 cu. ft. Capacity White
review_text:
It took a while to choose which dryer to get to go along with our LG SteamWasher (dryer purchased at Sears, washer purchased at Best Buy). We didn't feel the need for the matching steam dryer, since we have that feature with our washer. It slightly mismatches the SteamWasher, yet it doesn't "stand out" as a sore thumb. The control panel is different and the metal rim on the dryer has a bit more of a gloss finish than the SteamWasher (since they are different model designs). This isn't an issue for us, since the washer and dryer aren't on display in the kitchen area, and they are in a separate laundry room.

Other dryers I've owned before this one: Kenmore, Whirlpool and Amana (all large - super large capacity).

Household: 2 adults, 1 teen, 3 very furry Siberian Huskies as (indoor) family members.

Concerns: removing as much fur as possible, keeping clothing & linens in top condition, ability to do large loads, low noise, and perform for everyday use.

I don't LOVE the dryer like I do the SteamWasher, but I do like this dryer quite a bit. Yet, I have never loved any dryer that I've had. My main issue has been that some loads may take an extra cycle or two to completely dry. --This occurs with very large loads though. With other dryers, I've had to also run an extra drying cycle (with these type of loads; especially towels, comforters, pillows & stuffed toys). Much of this is most likely a learning curve, that I still need to work on, since I am new to front load washers & still playing with different spin settings.

--

Some "issues" I've read about LG electric dryers and my experience...

Lint screen - "lint screen falling appart?" My lint screen is very sturdy & I have had no issues at all with it falling apart anywhere...it is well made.

Dryer drum - "drum cracking?" I've had absolutely no signs of even minute cracking, & my dryer has gone through as many as 6+ loads in one day or 1-2 loads daily...high temp setting gets used as well. The drum isn't all metal (it's stainless steel main drum with rubber type "hands") , but it appears well made and sturdy. Our machine is also well balanced.

Dryer Sheets - "can't use dryer sheets due to it messing with sensor?" I use dryer sheets and have had no issues. One thing I have noticed though, I don't need as many dryer sheets as I use to use. Even with very large loads, 1 dryer sheet does the trick with keeping clothes static free.

Drying - "even small loads need an extra cycle?" For small loads, I have had no issues. Even larger loads of just sheets dry in one cycle. --With just making sure items are taken out of washer individually; checking so they aren't tangled or balled up (like what I'd do with any dryer)& this ensures less chance of wrinkling too. Larger loads and heavier materials, these do take a while longer to dry (extra 1-2 cycles, depending on how wet the items come out of washer too). Again, I am also learning my new front load washer spin cycles too.

--

With having Siberian Huskies, clothing and bedding can get quite furry (and their fur is super fly away soft!); even with regular vacuuming & husky grooming. This dryer picks up a LOT of the fur, that our washer misses (and the washer does get a good amount, and better than a top load) and sends it to the lint filter screen. This is very nice, and our LG dryer works a lot better with removing fur than any of my previous dryers. A typical small to average/normal load will be virtually fur free. Larger loads will have a little more fur, but still much, much less than our other dryers would perform.

The Cycles: 4 Sensor Dry (cotton/towels, normal, perm.press, delicates) and 4 Manual Dry (speed dry, freshen up, air dry, time dry). The 4 sensor dry cycles offer wrinkle care and damp dry options (with also ability to adjust dry level); while manual dry cycles offer the options of more time/less time and wrinkle care (as well as, the ability to adjust temperature settings & dry time).

Other features: child lock option, custom settings program option

LED digital display shows: settings, estimated drying time (and true time for manual dry settings), options & status message

Overall, this is a very nice dryer, easy to use, performs well for this family's needs and helps our clothing/linens stay in great condition. I haven't had any issues with wrinkles or any damages to clothing, linens, bedding or even stuffed toys. It's definitely not noisey while running & the beeper is loud enough for us to hear within the house (on low setting)...it plays a tune instead of an annoying BUZZ (which is another nice feature, and beeper can be disabled).

review_title: Great appliance after 6 months.... and one year update
review_text:
I own a bed and breakfast and do between 3-10 loads per day. I have been working this machine like a beast for 6 months and have been satisfied with my laundry.

I will say that the cycles are a lot longer than I was used to with my top loader. Still, I think that is only to be expected given the small amount of water used. To get my sheets whitest white I use the special white cycle. You can also use a sanitize cycle for items like towels and bathmats. All of the cycles leave the items a bit twisted into knots, but if you shake them out before putting the items into the dryer they are fine. I also frequently use the extra rinse cycle if I am concerned about a packed load which may have some residue. Which brings me to the point of SIZE of load. I have stuffed 3 rooms' worth of laundry in one load-- sheets with 4 pillow cases each, and towel sets for two people. I can't believe how much laundry I can do in one load and and how white and clean they get.

It is important to use only the recommended amount of soap. I became heavy-handed with the soap and the experienced a system shut-down due to too much soap.

I think the washer looks great-- very space-aged and clean looking. I have the units stacked, which I didn't think was possible with such large appliances.

I also think the washer runs fairly quietly. The only time I ever hear it is when the spin cycle kicks in.

Both the washer and the dryer were expensive units but seem to be worth the money when it comes to heavy use and clean laundry.

I've now been using the units for over a year. They still clean and dry great. I only have one complaint, and it is kind of a big one. I started to notice that some of my sheets were torn-- some after only one wash. This kept happening, and happening. I finally discovered the culprit. The "peg" which starts the machine when the door closes is a metal fin which sits right in the middle of the area where your clothes inevitably get dragged over. The peg is just raw metal, no plastic coating, no soft, rounded corners. I actually had to take a (freshly torn) sheet off the peg. I am just stumped as to why this peg couldn't be coated with something protective. Now that I know the issue exists, I can be more careful removing clothes from the dryer.

review_title: Unsuitable for more than one person.
review_text:
I purchased a Bosch washer (model WAS20160UC) and dryer (model WTV76100US) set in December 2011. This is the experience I have had with the Bosch appliances. It is a vented dryer, not the condensation model. This review is mostly about the dryer.

Pros: Stylish (witch makes no difference since the dryer is so poor)

Cons: This dryer takes very long to dry even small loads. It will get warm but not hot. A Bosch technician measured the temperature of the dryer at 122 degrees Fahrenheit. But, he informed me that this was normal for this dryer. In one test; two bath towels, two hand towels, and one facial towel were washed in the washer and rinsed on maximum spin to remove as much of the water as possible. It took the dryer 1hr. 20 min. to dry the load. After many phone calls and 3 or 4 service calls, they replaced the dryer. It performed as poorly as the first. So, I called an electrician to really find out what was going on. With freshly washed towels in the dryer, he observed the dryer drawing 10 amps (about the maximim rating) for 15 to 20 seconds. Then it went down to 5 amps for about about 30 seconds (he described it as half heat) then down to room temperature air coming out of the exhaust for another couple minutes. It repeats this cycle. At no time does the dryer actually get hot enough to remove the moisture from the load. It mostly just uses ambiant temperature air to dry the clothes. If touch the clothes in the middle of the load, they mearly feel slightly warm. While it is not practical for most people to use a clothes line, I think it would be just as effective as this dryer.

The thing that bugs me the most about this whole debacle is this: Both Bosch and the appliance store had the attitude that I should just accept the poor performance because it is a European design. I heard many excuses defending an appliance that I truly believe they KNOW does not perform as it should.

If you buy a coffee maker, do you expect it to make coffee in about 15 minutes? If you buy a blender, do you expect it to blend what you put in it? Well, when you buy a DRYER, you kind of expect it to actively dry.

In fairness, this washer/dryer set may be suitable for a single person who does small loads of laundry. You can expect a small load to take 60 minutes to wash and 80 minutes to dry. So you are right around 3.5 to 4 hours for two small loads.

Update: The appliance store has taken back the Bosch washer and dryer. I have replaced them with a GE unitized washer/dryer (model GTUP240EWH) This dryer completely dried the same load in 30 minutes.

I hope this review is helpful for you.

product_title: Bosch WTV76100USAxxis 3.9 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Electric Dryer
review_text:
Like its matching washer, we purchased this stackable dryer to fit a small laundry closet in our 1BR vacation condo.

Pro: It is attractive, vents out back or side, and install was easy. The stainless drum is nice and the lint filter is easy to clean out.

Cons: It does NOT dry the clothes quickly. It gets warm, occassionally moderately warm (never hot), but then it does not stay warm for long. So a small load of towels takes a couple hours and still come out damp dry. Just not enough energy going in to remove the latent heat (i.e., not hot enough to dry the clothes in a reasonable time). Bosch says this unit uses "higher flow rate at a lower temperature," and I completely understand their intent, but it just doesn't seem to move enough moisture regardless of their claim.

Well, we have only had the unit a couple months and have yet to get a dry load.

Machine uses moisture sensors (near the lint filter). Repairman could not tell me if these have any control over heat level or just used to indicate level of dryness to turn machine off. There is good flow out the vent, so if it isn't the flow rate then it must be energy level. Repairman says - "normal" , but it was close to lunchtime. Or maybe it really is just a poor Bosch design.

This machine is a disappointment. Stay away from Bosch.

One year later. Still dries very slowly. But we have learned to keep the loads small (two bath towels, one hand towel, a couple wash cloths and bath mat take about 1.5 hours to dry). We also learned that the cotton, very dry setting is the only setting that works well. Lint filter fills up fast, so empty after each load.

review_title: Love our little bosch washer and dryer!
review_text: We built a little cottage on the water to replace our river house after it was destroyed by Hurricane Katrina.  Got the plans from the Lowe's website in August 2008 and built the little 700 sq ft cottage we now live in. Because of the dimensions, we were very limited in what kind of appliances we could put in.  The Bosch washer/dryer set stacked together exactly perfectly in the very small closet we had downstairs.  They remind me a lot of the washer and dryers you run across if you spend much time traveling in Europe or the Middle East.  Because of the cost of utilities overseas, these systems are designed to be extremely energy efficient.  They're also the quietest systems we've ever owned...they need to be, because not only are they in a tiny house, they're stacked in the closet immediately outside of our bedroom.  We never have trouble sleeping while they're running, as long as we're not washing or drying something like dog collars with a lot of metal parts.  They are unique for an American to use...unlike the dryer I grew up that just blasts heat non-stop, this system will take longer to dry your clothes, but that's not necessarily a bad thing.  It uses a little more gentle heat, and rather than running continuously, it runs silently for a few minutes, stops to let the heat it's built up continue to dry the clothes without motion for a few minutes, then runs again.  That's what makes it so energy efficient.  We've had ours for about four and a half years and have done nothing other than clean the filter with each load.  The only downside I've found with it is that we'd like to buy a new lint filter because the filter light is starting to stay on, and the bosch website is fairly useless for providing detail on how to purchase what I would assume would be the most often touched/highest wear and tear part.  You can find every single nut/bolt/spring on this device on the bosch website, but you apparently can't buy the filter there...that seems like more than a minor oversight.  Anyway, I would rate the dryer a five star for our situation.  I'd give the washing machine a four star, primarily because no matter how much you clean the gasket on the door, it develops large mildew spots quickly if you don't dry out the gasket, and if you ever decide to take the gasket off to try to clean it more, you need an SEC football offensive lineman to help you get the spring that holds the gasket in place BACK on to the machine.  Other than that, it's actually fairly easy to service a lot of the things yourself, and I've never thought highly of my ability to work on appliances.  We're building a bigger house now and we're going to go all Bosch on that one as well, although we'll look at getting a larger Bosch washer/dryer if they make them...but if it comes down to it, I'd buy the exact same ones again.

product_title: GE WHRE5550KWW 27 4.1 cu. ft. Top-Load Washer - White
review_text:
First, let me say that historically I've never bought G.E. appliances---especially laundry appliances. My youthful years spent working at Sears as an appliance delivery/installation technician (1986-1991) showed me more than a fair share of fairly new but recently deceased G.E. washers. I remember one customer who had only had hers about a year (and was obviously rich enough to simply buy another rather than repair it). I know that all of this was nearly 15 to 20 years ago and much can change with a company's quality (remember when Maytag appliances were still good and Hyundai cars were horrible?), still, it kept me away from G.E. washers for many years. Ironically, G.E. has built for many years probably the best line of refrigerators and ranges in the industry.

If you're reading this review then it's obvious that you know a thing or two about washers. I don't really need to go into the hows and whys, but I'd like to focus this review on what is unique about this washer.

1. Stainless steel tub!!! Hey, I'm a fool for a stainless steel tub, although I can't really say that they are any better than others. Remember the cool Speed Queens and their once-patented stainless steel tubs?

2. Lack of agitator/"Hydrowave." One benefit of front loading washers is that they can wash more clothes, yet get them cleaner and treat them more gently than a top loading washer with an agitator. Well, this machine is still a top loader but lacks an agitator---at least what we know as an agitator. I suppose the little "nub" in the middle of the tub is the agitator. At any rate, this machine employs what G.E. calls its "Hydrowave" system. Most likely, this is yet another industry buzzword.

3. Super capacity! According to the manual, this has a capacity of 4.1 cubic feet. That's big! Other "super capacity" washers are usually around 3.5 cubic feet. This extra capacity is achieved, of course, by the lack of the traditional agitator.

4. Quiet! In terms of quietness, this machine is what I'll call "library quiet." It really is wonderful not to hear the "clunka clunka" from the Maytag piece of garbage it replaced! It sits perfectly still like a good little church boy during the spin cycle.

5. Drier clothes. No, this is not a one-in-all machine like I've seen in motor homes and Parisian apartments, but this thing gets clothes drier after the spin cycle than any washer I've ever known. Drier clothes after washing means less time in the dryer and, ultimately, less energy consumed.

6. Options. In addition to the multiple cycles and settings on this machine, two extra "bells and whistles" that may prove handy are the "Extra Rinse" option and/or the "Extra Spin" option. I've not used them yet, but certainly see the benefit.

***** WORD TO THE WISE ***** Do not overfill your washing machine! 4.1 cubic feet doesn't mean that you can force 50 pounds of dirty laundry into the maw of this appliance---or any other washer. Nothing shortens the lifespan of a washing machine more than overfilling the machine, yet almost everyone does it. The rule is to fill it no more than halfway from the bottom of the tub. If fact, this washer only fills slightly more than halfway on "Super" capacity. This is probably the reason some reviewers have complained that the machine left some articles of laundry dry in their machine.

review_text:
I've had this pair for about 3 years and use it often. I'm not happy with it for multiple reasons. It does smell, I wipe it down, leave the door open...everything. If I do not use the washer cleaners available (throw it in alone and it will clean the inside) my clothes smell as if I've left them in the washer for days. It has a ring just inside the door, where the dirty water goes in, I always find smaller items stuck in there...really gross to pull out wet soppy socks (or worse) knowing they have served as a filter for the rinse! The high spin is nice, but it essentially glues my clothes around the washer tub, so I have to pull them out, then they turn into this big "chain" of semi-wet clothes. I have to attempt to keep the chain together as I feed it into the dryer, but usually they start to break apart and fall all over the ground. So I've tried to pull them out, and break them apart from the "chain" so I can shake them a bit, to avoid the wrinkles--nope, wont work--still fall all over the ground. I do not notice the clothes being any cleaner...and most of the time they smell worse than when I put them in (unless I drown them in fabric softer to hide the musty smell). The clothes do come out of the washer fairly dry, but the irony is that I put them into the dryer for the 55minute HIGH cycle and usually many items are STILL damp!!?? Socks, jeans etc...I always have to add another 15minute quick dry, sometimes I'll have to do that twice. It's just not saving me any time, seems to be taking MORE energy--at least for me.
I also hate that I start a load, and if I walk through the house to find a "last minute item" I can't open the door and toss it in (it's locked and filling with water). I think I'd rather go back to the top loader.

review_text: I have had my washer and dryer set for only a month and although I know that isn't very long to test out an appliance that should work well for years to come I've already run into some issues. review_title: If I could give it ZERO stars, I would!
review_text:
Let me start by saying that because of my experience, I will never again buy ANYTHING with the Frigidaire or Electrolux name attached to it. NEVER. I bought my dryer a couple of years ago, and thought that only a one year warranty was a little shoddy, but never did I expect that the control panels in these dryers are like self-destructing "screw the customer" systems! The dryer started beeping one day while not even turned on, and displaying error code E68, the code for a stuck button. There are no buttons stuck, and upon researching it a bit, I found hundreds of other people online with the same exact problem. The control panel shorts out after 2-3 years and will cause the dryer to think a button is being held down and won't run. Nothing is wrong with the mechanics, it's all just this stupid electronic panel. As I, and the hundreds of other people with these dryers, have found out, Frigidaire absolutely refuses to replace the faulty control panel unless you pay ~$200.00 plus the cost of a service person to come put it in if you don't know how to do it yourself!

They KNOW that they are selling dryers with defective control panels, yet hide behind their wimpy one year warranty as a way to milk a ton of extra cash out of their customers. Where is the recall, Frigidaire??? Hopefully the Better Business Bureau will care to urge them toward resolving this. In the meantime, I recommend that you DO NOT BUY THIS DRYER, OR ANY OTHER FRIGIDAIRE PRODUCT! THEY ARE SCAM ARTISTS!!!

review_text:
There is a design flaw with the new whirlpool duet washing machines. There is a small space between the boot (rubber piece that goes around the machine) and the drum (what spins the clothes) and clothes get caught in between the two pieces. This rips the cloths and tears the boot leaving rubber all in your cloths and washing machine.

I had 2 repairman come out who had no clue what was causing it and just kept telling me I had a good machine. After this happening 5 times and 5 calls to whirlpool with no change in there tune I contacted Lowe's, the company I bought it from 4 months earlier. Thankfully Lowe's took the machine back allowing me to choose another one (diff brand) which I love.

2 things to consider when your buying a front loader. 1. make sure there's no space between the boot and the drum. 2. get one that the drum tilts back slightly to keep the clothes from falling forward and running along the boot.

product_title: Bosch : WTVC3500UC 27 Vision 300 Series Gas Dryer - White
review_text:
Hooray!!! A dryer at last!

What I like:
*The inside is nice, high quality stainless steel.
*When I use the timed standard cycle, the towels are dry and fluffy.
*The window allows my kitty to watch the spinning textiles.
*The interior light illuminates beautifully when you open the door and goes off a few seconds after you close the door. This is so nice. No sock is left behind!
*The large interior allows me to easily dry quilts, blankets and bedspreads.

What I don't like:
*The end cycle signal is SOOOO annoying!!!! When your dryer finishes it will beep, loudly
beep beep....beep beeep...
beep beep....beeep beeep

and then after a few minutes the drum is activated and starts your load tossing about for 20-30 seconds then stops and begins the whole annoying beeping sequence again...this goes on until you turn the bloody thing off.

I miss the old dryer system model that defaulted to 'off' at the end of a drying cycle, buzzed once and was done with it.

If you put a load of laundry in your dryer, right before bedtime...unless you are deaf or sleep with earplugs or have your laundry in the west wing of your large castle, you will be compelled to get up and silence that beeping beast!

*Lint filter sensitivity: the dryer will stop and start beeping at you midcycle until you check and empty the lint filter (which sometimes has hardly any lint in it). This is annoying. Again, I miss the old 70's dryers that just ran and ran until their cycle ended, regardless of their full, half full, or near empty filter.

*The moisture sensor cycles are another waste of energy in my opinion. I do not use this feature unless I want my laundry to be slightly damp at the conclusion of the drying cycle.

The moisture sensor cycles also beep beep in the noisy end of cycle pattern mentioned earlier. This hardly conserves energy in my opinion. It seems like they could have left this end of cycle siren and spin feature out of the schematic.

Overall I am happy.

but:
It would be nice if we had an easy to access dial to adjust the loudness of the system signal.
I also wish we could push a button to turn on/off the moistere and lint sensor settings. This would keep our machine spinning regardless of the faulty sensors.

Alas, No more hanging towels like Wilma Flintstone, to dry over the tar pits!!! I like this dryer much more than the clothes line!

product_title: Bosch : WTVC3500UC 27 Vision 300 Series Gas Dryer - White
review_title: I agree with prior review on many points as well; overall very happy
review_text:
I purchased this dryer (along with the matching 300 vision series washer) two weeks ago at PC Richard's for $699 (free delivery) and am so far very happy. It works well and like the previous reviewer, I don't use all the different settings (the later model series like the 500 and 800 have even more settings, like steam cleaning, wrinkle reduction which adds a few shots of steam to the dryer etc.)...I just want my clothes dried quickly and without scorching them.
And this machine does what it says. I fill the dryer up about half full and the load dries in 30 minutes; clothes are nice and warm when they come out, not scorching hot, and they are dry but not wrinkled.

(Note to the previous reviewer (Davina), the 300 series dryer should let you turn off the annoying beeping alarm by depressing the two top buttons (the Econo-dry button and the other button right next to it) at the same time).

I have to agree with Davina that the lint screen is WAY too sensitive. The beep went off twice the first time I used the dryer (I had it set at cotton/regular dry) and it stopped the dryer until I pulled out the lint screen to clean it (I admit, the first time it went off, there was lint in the screen, but it went off again 10 minutes later with no lint). The folks at Bosch recommend that you don't use dryer sheets (which I wasn't) because the residue sometimes sticks to the sensor and that you makes sure the lint screen holder is free of dirt before you run the dryer. I haven't used the dryer enough to see if my "cleaning" the lint screen holder (by blowing in it) fixed this problem or not, but I did about 5 loads and it lint alarm hadn't gone off again (granted, for the first load, I set the dryer on the dampness-sensor settings; for the last four loads I simply set it up to dry for 40 minutes and the lint alarm didn't go off. That's fine for me.

So overall, I'm really happy with the dryer. It dries quickly and efficiently (by the way, my old dryer was electric and it ATE electricity; I'm looking forward to getting my next ConEd bill to see how much money I'm saving on this gas dryer).
