product_title: Front load steam washer, Wave-touch controls, White
review_text:
It's a great machine but you can save four hundred bucks by buying an IQ-Touch instead. There is nothing a Wave-Touch can do that an IQ-Touch can not. The Wave-Touch has 4 distinguishing features over the IQ:

1. The Wave spins at 1350 vs. the IQ's 1200 rpm. No big deal. I don't think there's any practical difference in the amount of water extracted that will make a real dent in the drying time.

2. The Wave has an "Active Wear" cycle. It's not something you'd ever miss if your machine did not have it in the first place. You can use the IQ's "Casual wear" cycle instead, which differs from the Active Wear cycle by only 5 minutes.

3. The Wave's options are hidden in tedious to use menus and submenus, instead of the IQ's simple to use buttons. Buttons win here because you can see at a glance what options are active, especially useful for the next time you use the washer. With the Wave-Touch's menu style you'll be forced to scroll through the menus to see what options have been selected.

4. Wave-Touch has 3 favorites memory buttons vs. one favortie for the IQ-Touch. I have yet to find this feature useful. When one is useless to me, having 3 doesn't make it any better.

Construction-wise the two machines are otherwise identical.

Conclusion: The Wave costs $300 to $400 more than the IQ and delivers the same level of performance as the IQ. The Wave is for people who have money to burn. Okay, with a bit of sheepishness I have to admit I did buy a Wave instead of an IQ.

Now, let me review the Wave with steam function, since that's the one I actually bought.

The machine is exceedingly quiet when washing. The only real noise comes during the spin cycles.

As for vibration, make sure you balance the machine using a good quality level and follow the leveling instructions. Read the manual and it's imperative that the shipping bolts be removed per the instructions before using the machine!!! My house has a crawl space. My laundry room is on the first floor, where the washer would be perfectly capable of transmitting vibration if it was not leveled properly. So far it's been very smooth, in fact much smoother than my previous top-loader, with hardly much of any vibration. Keep in mind that every load is different and each load has its own vibration and noise characteristics. Some loads will be vibration free, other loads with a very unbalanced load (pillows and comforters, for example) will have some vibration. If it vibrates at all it's almost always during the spin up and spin down phase of the spin cycle. Once it actually gets into the spin cycle, there is usually little vibration.

This washer is quite ingenious in fighting vibration by ramping up to full spin speed in incremental stages. During the first stage, it slowly rotates the wet load counterclock-wise to test for balance, and also to pump out water. If it detects even the slightest hint of an unbalanced load, it will stop and reverse direction, i.e. spin clockwise, at the same slow rpm to let the clothes to shuffle in the drum. After a few seconds of this clockwise spin, it reverses direction again, i.e. counter-clockwise again, it then tests for balance again. If it again detects a poor balance, it will keep on doing this reversing direction routine until it redistributes the load evenly. When it's finally satisfied that the balance is good, it will then launch into high spin speeds in several stages. Frequently, after it has launched into a higher speed, it detects unacceptable vibration. It will instantly abort the spin and perform the shuffling routine again and again until it gets the balance right. It's not uncommon for it to go back and forth many times for as long as 5 minutes to find the sweet spot. As more water is progressively pumped out and the load becoming progressively lighter and better balanced, it will proceed to the next higher speed, finally maxing out at 1350 rpm, during the last 2 minutes of the spin cycle.

As for the steam feature, I've yet to find definitive evidence that it's the steam itself that gets the dirt out. The steam cycle essentially adds 20 minutes of wash time to any wash cycle using either warm water or hot water. Maybe it's the extra 20 minutes of washing in warm water in the steam cycle that does the trick. It's hard to tell.

It washes loose clothing very well while using little water. By "loose clothing," I mean items that are somewhat small and that will wet easily and shrink in volume as they are wetted. Items with these characteristics can freely tumble around one another inside the drum, as long as the machine is not overloaded. However when it comes to washing bulky big loads, such as pillows and synthetic fiber comforters, synthetic fiber bedspreads, etc., its miserliness in water use is its biggest flaw. With these bulky items, the water level is woefully inadequate to thoroughly wet the interior mass. And because they are synthetic fiber items, they don't shrink much in volume even when wetted, so they don't have much room to rotate inside the drum. The same side of the pillow or comforter then faces the drum and the center side doesn't ever get enough water. So, the side facing the drum surface gets cleaned but the center side doens't get cleaned. I bought this washer specifically to wash big bulky items such as pillows and synthetic fiber comforters, so it's a bit disappointing that it doesn't clean these items well. The way to get around this problem is to pause the machine after it's finished filling, and add water on your own either through the door or through the detergent tray. It works. Adding about 1 to 2 gallons of hot water fixes the problem.

I still love the washer, but only wish it had a "bulky items" selection which would allow it to have more water during the wash cycle. I believe this problem with washing bulky items is endemic to all high effiency front load washers and not just Electrolux. The real wish is to allow a separate button to vary the water level, like that found on my old Kenmore top-loader, but I don't think we'll ever see that water level selection switch on these high efficiency washers. I think the Electrolux designers' hands were tied by the stringent Federal energy efficiency standards.

So far it's been very smooth, in fact much smoother than my previous top-loader, with hardly much of any vibration. Keep in mind that every load is different and each load has its own vibration and noise characteristics. Some loads will be vibration free, other loads with a very unbalanced load (pillows and comforters, for example) will have some vibration. If it vibrates at all it's almost always during the spin up and spin down phase of the spin cycle. Once it actually gets into the spin cycle, there is usually little vibration.

This washer is quite ingenious in fighting vibration by ramping up to full spin speed in incremental stages. During the first stage, it slowly rotates the wet load counterclock-wise to test for balance, and also to pump out water. If it detects even the slightest hint of an unbalanced load, it will stop and reverse direction, i.e. spin clockwise, at the same slow rpm to let the clothes to reshuffle in the drum. After a few seconds of this clockwise spin, it reverses direction again, i.e. counter-clockwise again, it then tests for balance again. If it again detects a poor balance, it will keep on doing this reversing direction routine until it redistributes the load evenly. When it's finally satisfied that the balance is good, it will then launch into high spin speeds in several stages. Frequently, after it has launched into a higher speed, it detects unacceptable vibration. It will instantly abort the spin and perform the shuffling routine again and again until it gets the balance right. It's not uncommon for it to go back and forth many times for as long as 5 minutes to find the sweet spot. As more water is progressively pumped out and the load becoming progressively lighter and better balanced, it will proceed to the next higher speed, finally maxing out at 1350 rpm, during the last 2 minutes of the spin cycle.

As for the steam feature, I've yet to find definitive evidence that it's the steam itself that gets the dirt out. The steam cycle essentially adds 20 minutes of wash time to any wash cycle using either warm water or hot water. Maybe it's the extra 20 minutes of washing in warm water in the steam cycle that does the trick. It's hard to tell.

It washes loose clothing very well while using little water. By "loose clothing," I mean items that are somewhat small and that will wet easily and shrink in volume as they are wetted. Items with these characteristics can freely tumble around one another inside the drum, as long as the machine is not overloaded. However when it comes to washing bulky big loads, such as pillows and synthetic fiber comforters, synthetic fiber bedspreads, etc., its miserliness in water use is its biggest flaw. With these bulky items, the water level is woefully inadequate to thoroughly wet the interior mass. And because they are synthetic fiber items, they don't shrink much in volume even when wetted, so they don't have much room to rotate inside the drum. The same side of the pillow or comforter then faces the drum and the center side doesn't ever get enough water. So, the side facing the drum surface gets cleaned but the center side doens't get cleaned. I bought this washer specifically to wash big bulky items such as pillows and synthetic fiber comforters, so it's a bit disappointing that it doesn't clean these items well. The way to get around this problem is to pause the machine after it's finished filling, and add water on your own either through the door or through the detergent tray. It works. Adding about 1 to 2 gallons of hot water fixes the problem.

I still love the washer, but only wish it had a "bulky items" selection which would allow it to have more water during the wash cycle. I believe this problem with washing bulky items is endemic to all high effiency front load washers and not just Electrolux. The real wish is to allow a separate button to vary the water level, like that found on my old Kenmore top-loader, but I don't think we'll ever see that water level selection switch on these high efficiency washers. I think the Electrolux designers' hands were tied by the stringent Federal energy efficiency standards.

review_text:
Hi there. Firstly, the WM2501HVA is the same as the WM2501HWA with the only difference being the Graphite Steel color vs White. Big deal. In a lot of places, you'll pay $50 more just for the Graphite Steel color! WTF? Price for fashion I guess. I'll pass. I bought the white one and accompanying DLGX2502W after a couple of months researching steam washers/dryers(gas) reviews and prices on the interwebs and in person at the usual cast of brick-and-mortar retailers (Best Buy, Home Depot, Lowes, PC Richards, Amazon, Sears, etc.). I kept looking for great value in the duet (a.k.a., great reviews combined with a great sale).

I finally decided on this LG set and wound up buying from somewhere other than Amazon (BB) for $$509.99 (washer) and $569.49 (dryer) + after "instant" 15% advertised discount, plus $69.00 delivery and NYS tax for a grand total of $1,245.27 - all inclusive. The delivery came quickly and the delivery guys were very nice, very quick and very professional. I would have liked stainless steel but I wasn't about to pay hundreds more for aesthetics - eh...

On to the review...

The Good: Price! Value! Techno-wizardry interface, boops, beeps. I've never experienced such clean clothes from a single wash or any machine outside professional dry cleaners!!! Fantastic device in terms of cleanliness. Even my dress shirts that I either scrub excessively at the collar with stain removers normally before washing (and still don't get completely clean) came out spotless on wash #1 (with steam)! Wow. All the clothes have great, great smell - very different from my old clunky traditional top-loader. Very quiet cycle. Lots of features available at the push of a button. Certain programs disable certain options in an effort to not ruin certain types of clothing - nice. Lots of temp options unlike old ones where you're sometimes limited to certain temp combinations.

The Bad: Techno-wizardry interface, boops, beeps (takes some getting used to). It's not like the old-school turn 1 knob, select large-med-small, hot-cold and push to start. My wife was daunted at first but now she's happy with the setup. The wash time takes significantly longer than a "standard" top-loader - 15 - 20 minutes more maybe. Add steam, and you're looking at over an hour - yikes. I can live with it as long as my clothes keep getting super clean like they have been. A bit taller than normal machine but whatever.

In the end, I would HIGHLY recommend this product for anyone looking for a new washer. I have no clue why you would (and could easily) spend double on a steam setup. All the stores have the $1200 washers front and center at their displays - no thanks. I would have ranked this 5 stars except for the longish washing cycle times.

Enjoy...

review_text:
After our cheap-o washing machine and dryer broke down, we decided to make a Black Friday purchase and get both the dryer and washing machines from Best Buy. review_text:
We're a family of 3; with also 3 very furry Siberian Huskies. A large capacity washing machine was important for us. With moving last year, we chose to leave old Amana washer/dryer set behind and purchase new. Before the Amana set, we had Whirlpool. After much research and reading several reviews, we decided that the LG front load SteamWasher fit our needs. I was originally looking into the red and metalic colors, but they were $100-300 more. Best Buy had the white color on sale, about 6 months ago, so we chose to go with white.

I love this washing machine! Clothes come out much cleaner, & whites come out much brighter. The steam feature is really nice as well; whether you want to freshen up your clothes, use allergen control or sanitize. The bells and whistles to this washer provide just about everything anyone would need. Cycles include: *Steam Fresh, *Allergeine, *Sanitary, *Bulky/Large, *Cotton/Normal, *Perm.Press (*these first 6, all have steam feature; first 2 are exclusively a steam cycle), Delicates, Hand Wash/Whool and Speed Wash. Other features I enjoy are: steam, extra rinse/tub clean, stain cycle & water plus. I also like how I can adjust preference on: spin speed, soil level, water temp (all important for me). Not to mention, the beeper is not the standard loud and annoying beep most washers have...it plays a tune. Other useful options and features include: Delay Wash, Pre-Wash, Child Lock, and the option to turn Spinsense and Beeper on or off.

Clothes do take a little longer to wash (depending also on what settings you use) than most top load washers, but clothes come out cleaner, less soap is needed and less water is used. At first, I was concerned about the less water, since with a top load, using more water seemed to clean the clothes better. This is not an issue at all with LG SteamWasher. Most importantly, none of our clothes, linens, pillows or huskies' plush squeek toys come out torn or damaged, from washing! --We've had all too many items torn and warn down from top load washer's agitators.

Overall, this washer meets all of this family's needs. It's very quiet, very well balanced, has more warranty coverage than any other top load washer we've viewed, and it's a nice looking machine. I have nothing negative to say about it, even after 6+ months.

review_text:
Just got one of these a couple of days ago (not from Amazon, got an excellent deal elsewhere), to replace a Samsung front-loader.

I liked the interface and the SilverCare in the Samsung, but it didn't clean particularly well, and man did it beat the heck out of my clothes. This one is just a night-and-day difference in terms of cleaning power. I have an older white bathrobe that was starting to get pretty dingy-looking out of the Samsung. Even one trip through the LG brightened it up a ton, and a second trip through has made it look almost new again. I haven't even tried the steam cycle yet! Two runs on Sanitary (for the extra-hot water), and wow, what a difference. Same detergent, similar cycle times, but MUCH better results on the LG.

Don't know yet about clothes wear on this model, but Consumer Reports gives other LGs high marks for gentleness, so I'm expecting this to be good, too.

It's important to always dry off the seal and the inside of the door when you're finished with a front loader, and you're supposed to leave the door ajar to let the inside dry. This unit has a cool little stop that keeps the door slightly open, but holds it in place magnetically, so it won't swing any wider. I always left a towel in the door of the Samsung to keep it from sealing tight, and I won't have to do that with this unit. This tiny little feature makes me unreasonably happy.

If you're a laundry nerd (yes, they do exist :) ), be aware that there's no Favorite Cycle setting. If the built-ins aren't right for what you want, you'll always have to manually modify a cycle to do what you need. Doesn't bother me -- judging from the results I'm seeing, that machine knows a lot more about cleaning clothes than I do, so I just set the dial and push the button. One annoyance: the dial responds slowly. It doesn't matter how fast you spin it. The machine waits for the beep to finish each time it switches to a new setting, so you can't just crank it over to the right spot. You have to live through all the beeps in between. Mild grr.

As others are saying, it looks like this washer may be a little higher-maintenance than most; there's a drain filter on the lower front left that you're supposed to clean about once a month. The manual makes it sound pretty easy, but it is something to have to think about. For the results I'm seeing, I don't mind.

My only real complaint is that dial. LG, if you're reading this, modify your UI to let people spin it faster.

Can't speak yet to reliability or wear on clothes, but purely on the basis of cleaning performance, I'm really, really impressed.

We will be contacting LG shortly to complain, however based on other reviews I have seen in terms of customer service with LG, I have very low hope that LG will make good on this.  This will probably be my last LG purchase!!

product_title: Electrolux EIFLS55IIW 4.2 cu. ft. Front Load Steam Washer - IQ-Touch Control Island White
review_text:
Amazon says authors shouldn't review books.
But they didn't say anything about authors not being able to review whitegoods.

I'm an author. I'm also a feminist and I love my new washing machine.
The alternative - washing everything by hand - doesn't bear thinking about. How would I write The Next Amazing Novel (TM) if I was stuck in the laundry all day?

Ever wonder how Tolstoy wrote such massive books like War and Peace and Anna Karennina? I bet he never had to do laundry in his life.

Mind you, on the first day when this little love came home, I did sit in the laundry all day.
It was mesmerising. Clothes tumbling left. Stop. Clothes tumbling right. Oh the giddy majesty of it all.
1000rpm for the spin cycle. That's some serious torque right there.

But it's the "jetstream" fountain of sudsy wonderfulness splitter-splattering onto the clothes, making them all wet, that makes this washer so special.
Reminding me that I desperately needed to pee. You know, like at the end of that movie Titanic, when you've been sitting there for nearly three hours and your bladder is going to explode, and all you're looking at is water? Cold, icerbergy water that makes you want to pee!

That.

So, if I may advise anyone about to buy one of these fabulous products, don't sit there watching it all day.
You won't get any writing done, and you'll need to pee.

(I recently bought a 7kg Electrolux frontloading washing machine. Not this exact model, but one very much like it. And I really do love it.)

review_title: Jingle your clothes dry in style!
review_text:
I bought this dryer with the matching [[ASIN:B003044XOC LG : WM2050CW 27in Front Load Washer, 4.0 cu. ft. Capacity - White]] washer (see my LG WM2050CW washer review). This is our first electric dryer from LG and we are happy to say that just like the matching pair of washing machine LG WM2050CW the DLE2050W 7.1 cu ft capacity electric Dryer is an excellent dryer appliance!

It is very easy to operate and has sensors (Sensor Dry System) and automatically adjusts the drying time for clothes which in my humble opinion eliminates the guess work one needs to do with respect to drying times for clothes. This saves a lot of money in electricity bills.

It has manual controls for timed drying cycles if you are not happy with the sensor based drying cycle. It boasts 5 Temperature Levels of High, Medium High, Medium, Low & Ultra Low and also another Wrinkle Care Cycle to Periodically tumble-dry clothes without heat to reduce wrinkles.

Product dimensions are (WxHxD) 27"x38 3/4"x30" (51" with door open) The machine is very well built and made in Korea and in my opinion should last many years!

PROS

[+] 7.1 Cu ft is large enough for most households
[+] Reasonably quick drying time (40-45 mins) for regular load of clothes
[+] Plethora of automated options for desired fabric care
[+] User friendly control panel which also has child lock
[+] Fairly large lint screen filter to capture lint.
[+] We like the musical jingle at the end of a cycle rather than a loud buzzer!

CONS

[-] Needs 3-wire (30AMP) 220V AC power cord to be purchased extra
[-] Needs a semi-rigid dryer duct to be purchased extra depending on installation location
[-] Does not include stand for drying shoes

Make sure that you level the Dryer properly for optimal operation, the included feet leveling screws may need tweaking to match the washing machine's height level.

If you have already bought the excellent energy saving washing machine model [[ASIN:B003044XOC LG : WM2050CW 27in Front Load Washer, 4.0 cu. ft. Capacity - White]] add this to complete your laundry pair - Highly recommended!

review_title: Nice dryer but use with caution
review_text:
We bought one of these dryers in late 2011, and loved it: looks and works great.

Then we moved in 2013, and after installing the dryer in the new house, the lint inside the dryer housing ignited. Some of the lint must have shifted during the move, moving closer to the gas heater source. Luckily, the fire didn't cause major damage. review_text: I love this washer. I paid about $650 including delivery and 7% sales tax. This is my second front-loader. Do not be afraid of front-loaders. My first one was a Whirlpool Duet, probably cost about $1000 in 2003 and worked well for about 6.5 years -- so that's disappointing -- sounded like a bearing was broken and that costs a few hundred to repair so I figured I was better off buying new. This LG is so much better than my old Whirlpool. I'm guessing the front loader technology has gotten better since then. The LG has very little shaking and vibration, it is very quiet. The biggest concern with front loaders is the moldy smell, I have used my LG now for one month and no smell. I did occasionally get the moldy smell in my old Whirlpool and some mildewy stuff around the rubber part surrounding the washer opening which I wiped down occasionally, but so far nothing in the LG. The LG has simpler lines on the rubber thing so it looks like less nooks and crannies for water and mildew to accumulate plus it has drain holes so the water can drain away. Also, I learned with my Whirlpool front loader and I do this with my LG and you should do this with all front-loaders-- you must leave the washer door open all the time, leave the soap dispenser drawer open all the time, and never let wet clothes sit in the washer, move them to the dryer right away. I do at least a couple loads a week in hot water and use oxi-clean powder on a couple loads a week. In the Whirlpool, I found that the Tide product for cleaning the mold smell didn't help that much, I found that Oxi-clean a couple times a week does a better job. I usu do an extra rinse on all cycles and the cotton cycle takes about 65 minutes and extra soil cycle might take 90 minutes or so, so the cycles are longer than top loaders. I use only HE detergent for front-loaders and I use only the amount recommended by LG -- not the amt recommended by the detergent company. The LG has a user-friendly display panel, and the soap dispenser is clearly marked for correct levels of soap. This LG plays a cute little song when it's done rather than an annoying beep. It spins the laundry really dry, so the dryer cycle can be shorter. I washed a king size down comforter in my LG using the bulky cycle, no problem.  I just love this machine.

and just summarize by saying you won't find a better high efficiency washer for
your money than the LG WM2050.

review_title: Beware of  "noisy door syndrome"  with this LG model
review_text:
This is my first front loader and I have generally been pleased. I was aware of front-loading issues like musty drums and moldy seals from the experiences of others. I leave the door open, wipe down the seal occasionally, clean the detergent bay and do my best to remember to clean the bottom drain.
The real annoyance has been the noise from the front door. The washer is on a solid floor and while the unit itself does not vibrate, both the door and door latch do. The noise travels throughout the house and you certainly cannot be on the phone while the washer goes through its spin cycle. The vibration did not start until after 500th load. The washer was close to its one-year anniversary when the rattle started and it just kept getting louder. I put in a service call and the service person the came was very professional and thorough in looking the machine over. He said that the noisy rattling door did not hinder the performance of the machine and repairs would not be eligible under the warrantee. As far as exactly what was wrong he could only speculate that the rubber seal on the door was "relaxed" or "broken in" to a point where the seal was not pushing as strongly against the door resulting in some "play" that allows the door to rattle (loudly).
While this noisy machine may not be considered defective it sure is a irritating. There is no way to run a load of wash at night without waking the entire house and you can forget about watching television when the spin cycle kicks into high gear.
Too bad.

review_title: Good features and performance, poor reliability
review_text:
I have owned this unit for approximately 3.5 years with light use (~4 loads/week). I have been happy with the features and performance, except that the door seal builds up gunk and odors if not cleaned regularly. Also, laundry will mildew if left in the machine for more than a couple of hours after the end of the cycle. From my limited research, these seemed like common problems with front loaders back in 2010, so I wasn't concerned. The other problem I've encountered is that the detergent dispenser drawer seems poorly designed, because if you attempt to fill the bleach compartment, bleach spills out down the front of the machine. I'm not sure if I have a faulty dispenser, but I hardly ever use bleach, so I haven't bothered to fix this problem. FWIW, I have not seen some problems others have had, such as water spilling from the door seal drain and loud noises during spin cycles.

I would have recommended this machine until yesterday, when the unit suddenly started spewing water from underneath the top cover. Lots of water. Luckily, I was nearby and noticed it in time to shut it down and unplug it before much damage was done. It's out of warranty, so I removed the top cover and quickly discovered a massive hole in the rubber hose that connects the cold supply line to the main wash detergent dispenser. The OEM replacement hoses are absurdly expensive and appear to be poor quality seam-welded construction - lo and behold, the rupture occurred on the seam. I just went to the hardware store and got a 6' length of braided reinforced hose to replace all 4 of the inner hoses for about $5. That should fix the problem, but if I hadn't been standing right there, the water leak could have easily shorted various electrical connections inside the machine and started a fire. Major safety hazard.

review_title: Worst Washing Machine Ever - Just Horrible
review_text:
I've used Maytags most of my life. Our wonderful Maytag Neptune front loader was ruined by storm damage and could not be replaced: Maytag is out of business. So we went for a Whirlpool.

One reason we picked this was that the Duet is one of the few washers that had (I thought) rational wash settings. Most of the brands now have cycles called "Baby", "Jeans", "White", etc. What are those supposed to mean?? Really, in the stores are whole rows of machines with a "Baby" wash cycle. How long do they expect people to have an infant? What is a "jeans" setting anyway? White is a color, not a cycle, people! Does a white throw rug get the same temperature and treatment as a white bra? I would hope not. Whatever happened to "Delicate", "Hand Wash", "Heavy Duty", "Wool", "Perm Press", etc?

So, onto this Whirlpool Duet SteamFresh Premium lemon. First off, what's the point of a 4.x cubic foot basket if it unbalances and dies all the time?? It can't handle one more sock than the smaller models, so right off the bat save your money and go for a smaller washer. The Neptune was 3+ cu ft and could easily wash a queen comforter and set of sheets. This Duet stops and starts and can hardly make it through just a comforter, no matter what setting I choose. The Neptune would re-asses loads, toss back and forth if it thought the load was unstable. The Duet grinds to a halt if a feather is out of place.

The washing selections on the Duet are lies. "Active Wear"? My active wear is sweats: the Duet stops dead. Apparently, my "active wear" is "bulky" or "heavy duty" or whatever. If I only put underwear in the active cycle the Duet spins them into pulp. And you are doomed if you ever mix cloth weights: want to put some underwear in with pants or sweaters? Error. Or, even better, it doesn't toss well enough to clean anything. Heavy stuff just sits there and light stuff gets ground to dust.

And now I have a perpetual F20 or F21 error code and I see online that I have to disassemble the case, root around for some internal filter, grab a bucket to catch a couple gallons of water, then dig into the guts to clear some drain filter. Are they really TRYING to make business for repairmen? WHO PUTS AN INTERNAL FILTER IN A WASHING MACHINE??

Other issues: The Duet runs the drain before it starts a cycle to "empty the basin". It ALWAYS has water in it. It's in the book. It never, never is empty. That seems like a recipe for disaster. It smells funny, musty even, if you don't use it for a week. The fabric softener cup is miniscule and will dump it's load at random points in the wash cycle. Most often when I close the door at the start. AND the book tells you to dilute softener first. WHY have a massive basket if it can only use a couple tablespoons of softener? You also do not have full control over cycle and temperatures. Some will allow warm water rinse, others will not. WHY??

It is such and unfair market where Maytag's Neptune recall put a great company out of business, and a venal, uncaring company like Whirlpool can sell $1200 washers with a 12 month warranty that fail at an alarming rate. Just researching the latest problems with this horrible Duet makes me feel for the people who had $1000 repair bills 13 months in. We've had the Duet Premium for about 18 months and I really, really regret buying it. I should have taken my chances on one of the other name brands with the stupid "Baby" cycle, or even just gone for a generic brand at half the price.

review_text:
We have has the machines for about 3 years. Both the dryer and the washer are still functioning well. My major problems are as follows. While they may not be a deal breaker for you, something to think about..

1. The time that it tells you on the washer it takes to complete the load is SO Wrong all the time! Takes longer than the 50 min it tells us (usually 1:10 minutes) TOO LONG.

2. Washer - everyone in the house (4 of us) use the washer and each of us has at least once (for me countless times and why I am writing this) where you press the start button and you think it's started, only to come back an hour later to find dry unwashed clothes. (We have learned to wait the 30- 60 seconds for it to start and actually drop water into the washer, then it's confirmed that it's started)

3. I do not like to have the washer door open so that it can "air out" the moldy smell.

4. Probably not a big deal to many, but there are too many choices and not all combos can be picked. For example the super hot setting can only be used on the 2 hr cycle called sanitize.

5. Sometimes (not only when it could be overloaded, which I doubt) the spin cycle does not remove all the water. So okay, I'll run the spin cycle, except it's a rinse and spin cycle.

The dryer also has timing issues. I get it can not tell the exact amount of moisture in a load, but the estimated time left is crazy! I have sat and waited for 10 minutes when it tells me there are 2 minutes remaining. I have also had many occassions where it does not even come close to being dry but stops the machine... Once again there are too many choices and the combos I would like to make, I can't.

review_title: Beware, Whirlpool shares design with Kenmore & Maytag!
review_text:
We "invested" in the set (Washer & Dryer), the wife was thrilled with the operation and efficiency. A few months after the warranty expired, the washer started making a slight knocking sound during the high-speed spin. It slowly got worse until it was so bad it was scaring the kids and shaking baskets of laundry off the top of the machine.

Being a Mechanical Engineer & mechanic that specializes in rotating equipment, I investigated. Apparently the main shaft seal that protects the bearings from splashing water doesn't do much protecting. My rear (smaller) bearing was junk and I bought a repair kit to replace the bearings. Turns out Whirlpool had a change in their production run and the seal, bearings and another seal my on-line vendor thought was correct were all wrong. They were stumped, and apparently Whirlpool / Kenmore / Maytag are also stumped because they can't build a machine that doesn't destroy bearings after 18 months of service. It is obvious that they know there is a seal problem as the modification to the design they tried on my model didn't work either.

Guys, IF you try this repair yourself, be prepared for disappointment. Even though you tried to save the $600+ to keep this $1,000+ machine running more than 2 years, IT WILL NOT LAST! Try the stainless steel permanently sealed bearings from SKF to buy more time.

I can understand having a faulting product every once and a while. They took care of it immediately and I was happy. Then about 6 months into using the unit it stopped working again. This time Lowes would not take care of it so we called whirlpool. They sent out a tech and they determined that there was a sensor that had not been installed correctly. The screw had worked loose and it was an easy fix. Took him less then 15 min to put it back in correctly. It worked great again for the last few months until about 8 weeks ago. During the spin cycles it got louder and louder. Then about 2 weeks ago it sounded like there was gravel in the machine. We called whirlpool again and they sent out the tech. He took one look and said that it was the bearings. He then told us that they are having this problem a lot and that he would suggest getting the extended warranty because it will happen again. Whirlpool sent out the parts which arrived in 3 large boxes 1 week for delivery. We now have the washer fixed again with a new drum, bearings, etc. We are trying to decide what to do with this unit. Do we try and sell it off to some poor sap and get a new one? That does not sound very ethical. We will probably buy 1 year of extended warranty and see how it goes and begin saving our money for a new one, again. I will never buy another whirlpool product again! If you know you have a problem be a good enough company to fix the issue.

review_text: I purchase one of these based on CR reviews.  Wrong move!  Within 2 months it sounded like a jet taking off. I was told that is normal.  At about 10 months it started making a banging noise. Called customer 'service'.  Was told that apparently I had not properly used the machine. Seriously!?  I live alone and do 4 loads of laundry a week. I take large blankets and comforters to a laundromat even though the machine is advertised as being able to handle large loads.  I called back every other day for 2 weeks.  I finally managed to get a supervisor who said they would allow an authorized repair service to determine if it should be covered under warranty. I was told that I bought it at Sears so I had to call Sears to get a repairman to look at it.  First available appointment was when the machine was 11 months and 2 weeks old.  Repairman came out and said both tubs needed to be replaced but it was covered under warranty.  He said he would order the parts. A week later I called because no parts had been received and I had not heard from them.  No parts had been ordered.  Another appointment was made when the washer was 12 months and one week old for another repairman to see what needed to be ordered.  More contacts with Whirlpool customer 'service'.  Finally got a supervisor's name to go with the assurance that repairs would be covered under warranty.  Since Sears repairmen had messed up, I pitched a fit with Sears until I received an email from Sears stating repairs would be covered under their warranty even if Whirlpool did not cover the repairs.  The parts arrived (3 huge boxes).  The repairman arrived only to announce the incorrect parts had been sent.  2 weeks later, the parts finally arrived and were installed a week later.  Sears and Whirlpool customer 'service' reps where rude and obnoxious every time I called.  They acted like I ordered the incorrect parts myself!  They even argued with me about who ordered the parts and demanded that I pay for the shipping.  I refused to pay for the shipping. I sent a letter to the CEOs of Sears and Whirlpool and received a response from Sears saying the repairs and shipping were covered under the Sears warranty.  It should not have taken 2 months without a washer, hours on the phone and internet, and untold aggravation to get the machine repaired.

product_title: Whirlpool WFW9750WL
review_title: So far So Good. The Wife Loves it.
review_text:
Going on a year with this unit. Installing it was not too bad, but if you don't have a very solid floor (2X10 joists with tile or simply concrete) you will find that the vibration with a large load can be pretty intimidating to say the least. I leveled the unit perfectly, and with no load the washer spins incredibly smooth at max rpm. With a smaller load, spin cycles aren't bad at high speeds. With large loads, watch out. I have 2X10's, and I added 2X6s to strengthen them. I also added a support under the crawl near where the washer is to prevent any bounce in the floor. I don't yet have tile, so I put a 3/4 inch piece of plywood under the washer and dryer for now. It's as good as it's gonna get on a wood floor. Once I put in cement board and tile I'll remove the 3/4 plywood and all should be fine.

Once installed the unit looks great and works wonderfully for my wife and I. She uses it more than I do, and with two young children it gets used nearly daily. I'm not holding my breath, but so far there have been no problems.

We ALWAYS take out the soap dispenser and leave the door open after washing. Zero problems with smells using HE detergent. To be on the safe side I do use the afresh cleaning tablets once every few months.

Hint: Use just enough detergent (HE seems to work best so far) to get the job done and let the thing dry out between washings.

Clothes come out very clean every time, and that is without using the steam cycle very often. Whites are white!

We'll see how this unit holds up. Whirlpool has sold tens of thousands and one can find a few dozen terrible reviews. A few dozen out of thousands is probably a good bet. Of course Whirlpool is not alone with bad reviews. When shopping for a washer and dryer I could not find a brand that didn't have negative reviews so I rolled the dice.

The matching steam dryer has also been great, and the steam cycle to touch up clothes before going out does work pretty good depending on the material. The dryer capacity is great.

Despite the size of the machine one cannot fully load it and expect it to get the job done. If it is too full the clothes simply cannot move around enough to get thoroughly clean. Don't overload it!

I'm not expecting it to last as long as an old fashioned mechanical timer top loader, but if I get a couple of years out of it before I have to repair it myself I won't mind. If when the time comes I need to get a part to repair it and the part is hundreds of dollars I'll be disappointed! Time will tell.

So far we love it and the dryer. The spin cycle can be crazy with a heavy load. Clothes come out clean. It's easy to use. It does hold a lot of clothing.

Update: December 3, 2012. No mechanical or electrical problems with the unit. We have also not had any smell problems as reported by some users on many makes and models of front load machines. We ALWAYS leave the door open and take out the soap dispenser after washing clothes to let everything dry out. When using powder oxidizer, we do notice a build-up of oxidizer under the soap dispenser, which is a minor hassle to clean. Other than that, the wife is still very happy with the machine. I'd still recommend and purchase this unit again. The matching steam dryer has also been a great product.

review_title: If I could give it a lower rating, I would
review_text:
We purchased our washer at Lowes in March, 2011. It was working great, I was happy over all, though I was a bit annoyed at the exaggerated advertising that this washer will hold 16 pair of jeans (5-6 is more like it). On September 11, the rubber boot pulled completely out of place and the wire wrapped around clothing and ruined them. I called the Service Center at Whirlpool and had them come out. They were out within a week. The repairman said that he would have to replace the boot and the part would take 2 weeks to get in. I was without a washer for 3 weeks at this point. They came and repaired it, and within a month it started leaking again. This time the boot was still in tact. We call the service center at whirlpool again, a week later a new company comes out and they declare it has the same issue - a leaking boot. They order the part and it takes 2 weeks to get in and installed. Again, we are without a washing machine for 3 weeks. A few weeks pass and I run a self cleaning cycle and the machine starts leaking yet a third time! I get on the phone with Whirlpool and demand a new machine. They refuse and tell me they are 'honoring the warranty and standing by their product by sending out a repair service'. The Service center tells me there is no one else to talk to - no case manager, no manager, no one at all higher up and the only way to get a new machine is to have a service repairman declare the machine is unrepairable. Yet a third company comes out and fixes some minor issues saying that's been the problem all along. They say they ran a self cleaning cycle and it was great - no leaks. They leave and that night I do laundry. The first load I run I know something is horribly wrong. It smells like burnt rubber. When the cycle finishes, I open the door and am greeted with rubber grit all over my clothing. They smell awful. I run the load again, thinking perhaps the grit was left from the service call. The smell during the second load worsens. When the load finishes, the grit is gone, but the smell is horrible. I dry the clothes, thinking I'd rewash them after the smell was gone from the washer. I run a self cleaning cycle with Affresh. Not 2 minutes into the cycle and the machine leaks all over. AGAIN. I call whirlpool the next morning and the soonest they can have someone out to fix it is a WEEK later!

Whirlpool by far has the WORST customer service I've ever dealt with. If you don't believe me, check out their facebook page. It is littered with people just like me. So far, Whirlpool refuses to replace my machine, and I continue to be a working mom of 3 kids who can't do laundry. Unacceptable, Whirlpool. My husband and I have missed 6 days of work waiting on repair service calls and our machine has yet to be fixed. We did the math, and at this point, we are out enough money it would have been cheaper to just purchase a new machine rather than miss so much work and do laundry at a laundromat.

Buyer don't just beware, RUN far away from Whirlpool and their products.

review_title: Don't Buy Whirlpool!!! The Duet Washer WFW9150WW is Garbage!
review_text:
Purchased new in July 2010. Brought home, plugged in and water spewed all over my laundry room from the soap dispenser. Called Sears, they sent a technician out who said Whirlpool had the hoses incorrectly assembled. He re-arranged where the hoses were run and our machine seemed to work properly.

We watch it filling with water...barely has any water. The water NEVER reaches anywhere near the rim like the commercial washers at the laundromat. (I went and checked them out, because our clothes did not seem to be getting cleaned.) I've only used Tide HE and our clothes are not coming out clean. During, "Add a Garment", I often wait until the water stops and toss in another 1.5 gallon bucket of water. This seems to help some, but doesn't alleviate the problem. (After I began doing this, I commented to a sales lady at Sears that our machine does not clean clothes well. She said she had the same one and had to add water during the "Add A Garment" stage to get her clothes clean. I told her that is what we had been doing!)

I often have to do a load 2-3 times...especially if Jeans. Stains easily transfer from one set of clothing to another...many items have been ruined. This would never have happened with the top-loader we had had for 18 years! Stains that would have come out with our old machine barely get wet with this one. We were able to load more clothes in our top-loader, also!

While under warranty, I called Whirlpool and told the rep that our clothes did not come out clean. My husband will be wearing a shirt and an hour later start wondering what smells...and realizes that it is his shirt. How gross! The rep said that even though the machine was under warranty, if a service tech came out and couldn't "find anything wrong" with the machine, we would be responsible for the $129 service call. After reading all the other negative reviews about Whirlpool online, we told her, "No, thanks!" Because their technicians would claim they all only use a little water and were working properly.

My husband ended up taking the machine apart and found that it was only adding 1.5 gallons of water for a full load of clothes! No wonder it doesn't clean well...it barely gets the clothes wet. We're still trying to decide if we are going to purchase a new front loader (NEVER WHIRLPOOL, ever again!) Or go back to a top loader...that you can at least allow clothes to soak in, when needed. The soak cycle on this front-loader is a joke when it barely gets the items wet.

Save your money, your time, and your disposition by purchasing from another manufacturer. My mother's LG works Great...maybe we'll change to that.

review_title: Good thing I got extended warranty
review_text:
I bought this from a Fred's Appliance (Spokane) and they have their own extended warranty - and they they are great; the machine is a lemon.
The machine is on visit 3 from Fred's.

I had a Kenmore 417.43142200 prior, its paired to a 628.9468213 dryer - still works fine.
It was a top rated model (CR) that was made by Frigidaire (GM), and in 3-ish years a badly corroded aluminum basket and bearing lead me to the descision to dump it.
I can fix these things, and I was prepared to, but I found out the repair components were made the same way and expensive.
I did extensive research on the matter, and learned that in this case, the Amazon reviews were more useful then the CR ratings - which are model specific only for new machines.
Overall, Kenmore is still good.

I e-mailed CR and explained their reviews failed me entirely, and in fact they still showed the unit as recommended, when I could see a YouTube explaining its fatal problem.
So its restoration didn't pencil-out.

The Whirlpool looked similar - so the issue of a non-matching pair was ameliorated.
I was happy...for a while. I had the same leak issue others had, and in fairness we aren't that kind to machines in this house.
I could hardly believe it when I read my receipt for the purchase date, I bought the extended warranty - never have before on a major appliance.
The second issue was done while I was on the road - I don't really know what was fixed.
Now it won't go through a cycle, for the 3rd inning.

That now about $275 worth of trips, but "free" to me, and we may hit 400 tommorow.
Right now I can here it beeping an error message, leading me to make this charitable act.

Before I got this unit I knew the risk.
I called a local repair shop I have used for 30 yrs.
I asked him is this normal (The Kenmore)? He mumbled out 4-5 years is normal.
We talked about the old Maytag that went 20 years, the Whirlpools that went 10, but were easy to fix.
He warned the Maytags are made by Whirlpool now (still a pretty good brand I thought, he didn't confirm.)
I asked what he'd buy, he said "LG makes a good machine, Samsung..."
I said, you'd think American industry would learn their lesson (cars), you mean were doing this again with appliances?

I went to Sears first, with my paper work, before I got this Whirlpool, they might make a deal...?
Well, no, but, I found they now private label Samsung and LG as Kenmore.
So they moved on, as I should have.

The Extended will probably get me through to a reasonable service life for the dryer.
If I'm not unemployed, I'll pick up a new set of LG's in 2-3 years.
If I am unemployed then, I won't be for long, I can fix these lousy machines 50hrs a week, and buy a dented pair of LG's.
I can't imagine how i might feel if I were out of work in my 20's, maybe springing for a new machine for my wife and kids, and getting this.

I belong to the American Society of Quality: I know much of this isn't due to our American labor as much as bean-counter management
Toyota can take our labor, at least the non-union variety, and make a Tundra in Kentucky that's perfect (no issues at 100K).
A US Camry (no issues at 180K), from Japan I had three Corollas, (no issue's at 180, 185K, but one, I bought used, had a problem at 150K).
We got a Lexus, no issues at 80K so far, that's a Japanese labor product, it appears to be perfect.
So 6 Toyota products, 10000 parts, and one $1400 repair -and I can't but a good domestic washing machine in two trys?

Most of those recalls in 2009 and such, were due to American parts from Toyota's plan to become more American, and on the American made units from there upstream suppliers.
Still, a Toyota made in Kentucky beats most American cars, however in terms of essentials, I think the quality issues with domestic cars tend to be minor.
I got my mom into a Focus, because used Toyota's were overpriced at the time - seems the a good car and well engineered.
That Ford engineering came out of: Ford EU....

I'm really glad Whirlpool doesn't make cars.

Maybe LG will have a US plant in a few years, so I can "buy American" - sort of.
That's my plan.

Pros - it is space saving, is gentle on clothes (more gentle than TL models with agitator) and looks nice

It came with the house I bought, but I would never buy anything like this again. I dislike it sufficiently that I am considering removing it to get back some of my cabinet space and going to the launderette.

review_title: Great machine, but a couple of minor flaws.
review_text:
I live in a small apartment and bought this machine to save space. Being ventless, it takes a long time to dry clothes, but I knew that when I bought it. I put a new load in each night after work, and as long as the laundry is done 24 hours later by the next night, I'm happy. It has lots of settings and, being ventless, plugs into a standard outlet and drains into the sink.

I bought the LG because I read on many different consumer sites that the other competing machines (like the Haier) have a lot of breakdowns and problems. The Haier is less expensive than the LG, but you get what you pay for.

But there's a couple of flaws. For one, if you wash too few items, it becomes unbalanced and stops. Sometimes, I just want to wash a couple of towels, and come home the next night to find that it's signaling an unbalanced load and didn't finish the load.

The bigger complaint is that the sensor that it has to tell when the load is dry and to stop the dry cycle doesn't work. I've had the repairman out a couple of times, and told me that the machine is working according to spec. So I use the timed dry setting instead of the automatic dry. But the problem there is that the maximum dry time it can be set to is 2 and a half hours, and that's not long enough. So my clothes are always slightly damp coming out if it. But the machine dries fine; it just needs more time to dry. If only the dry time could be set to 4 hours or so, my clothes would be perfectly dry the next day and the machine would be perfect.

review_text:
We ordered this unit on the last day of 2010 and it was delivered 24 January 2011. We've now been using it for about three weeks.
It's just the two of us in our household with no kids.
We found this unit because we were struggling with venting arrangements for a conventional dryer. This is ventless. And ventless means that you are not exhausting warm air from inside your home to the outside causing it to be replaced with cold air (in winter) that has to be heated.
We love the combined washer+dryer. Our laundry room is quite small and we did not want to lose any space unnecessarily.

--The lint mostly goes down the drain except for a trap that you have to clean out occasionally. And wipe down the door seal regularly. This is less troublesome than cleaning out a dryer lint trap each load. And no risk of fire from accumulated, trapped lint in the exhaust duct.
--We also love the fact it requires only an ordinary 120VAC power circuit. No 220VAC `pigtails' and plug configuration to figure out.
--And you just put in dirty laundry and the next time you open the unit door it is clean and `ready to go'. No need to transfer heavy, soggy laundry from washer to dryer.
We did read and comply with the directions about `similar lint' laundry items. For example, don't mix bath towels (high lint producing) with nylon underwear (zero lint producing). This seems to serve us well.
--The unit seems very quiet to us. It does not `act' as the typical power-sucking washer and dryer running continuously for lengthy periods of time. It operates briefly, then pauses. Then again. This may be disconcerting to some (like our cat) but does not bother us in the least. We know this is necessary to save energy while cleaning effectively. The unit seems easy to use. The pre-sets are easy.
--To know if the laundry is `dry', reach in and pull out a `sample' item. The air inside the unit may feel `damp'. Disregard this feeling of the dampness of the air inside the unit. When you remove the sample item and note that it dries nearly instantly as you give it a gentle shake, then you know the cycle is sufficiently long. This is often well before the machine says the cycle is complete. It is true that the dry cycle for bath towels is longer than for a conventional high-energy consumption machine. Remember that you are only putting the energy coming thru an ordinary 120VAC circuit into the unit. We think that is a good energy trade-off, tho. The unit is Energy Star-compliant and we got a $180 tax credit from State of Oregon because of its high efficiency ratings.

This unit seems ideal for small apartments, condos, and where venting is a problem.
This is a larger capacity unit than most `combined' units. Nice!
Cost of this unit may seem to be a disadvantage but don't forget to include the cost of pedestals (typically $150-200 each) for front-loader washer and dryer, plus extended warranty for each. When all was summed, our cost was about the same for a single unit as for the high efficiency separate front loader washer and front loader dryer. We did not choose to include a pedestal for this unit because we put laundry in dry and take it out dry -- no transfer from washer-to-dryer.
This unit may not necessarily be optimal for a large family with children if you have multiple loads `back-to-back' and need a washing cycle to be running simultaneously with a drying cycle of another laundry load.
And if you are wedded to the idea of your laundry coming out of a dryer `toasty' and radiating heat (and willing to pay the energy cost), you may want to think about whether this unit is the right choice. This dry method seems ideal for no-iron outcomes.
Only time will tell whether the unit is reliable but we have no reason to believe that the `combined unit' configuration will be a factor in that outcome. The motor does have a 10-year warranty. Will any service tech be mystified by the unit if repairs are needed? One financial feature we liked is that the extended warranty we purchased cost us for one unit rather than purchasing one warranty for the washer and a separate warranty for a dryer.
The guys that brought it did not leave the drum security bolts that are to be removed from the unit when it is `in place' for use, but kept and replaced before the unit it moved to a different home (to avoid transit damage to the drum suspension system). We had to get them to return the bolts. And we don't know if they removed the bolts in the proper order prescribed in the manual. Otherwise the deliver guys were very friendly and helpful.

review_text:
I've traded up from a super crappy thin-twin stackable washer and dryer set, and let me tell you, it's one of the best things I've ever done. I read tons of reviews before I settled on this washer. One of the major complaints that most people talk about is how long it takes to dry, but I've found that it doesn't take any longer than a regular set, unless you're one of those people who sits and waits for the dryer to buzz. Personally, I stick my laundry in and forget about it for a few hours, and when I'm ready to think about it again...poof!...it's all clean. One other thing people talked about was that they didn't feel like their clothes were dry when they took them out. Because of the way the dryer works, there is steam left over at the end of the cycle. Once the dryer cools (it locks you out until the tub is cool enough to touch to keep you from getting burned) you take our your clothes, give them a quick shake, and they go from a little damp feeling to warm and dry. It's like a little miracle every time you do laundry.

I've had to get used to the way the machine sounds. It's not a constant hum, but a series of on and off cycles. I assume it's because it's supper energy efficient and its only drawing power when it needs to turn.

That's another really awesome thing about this machine...it runs on a regular outlet plug. Also the "Direct Drive" motor turns the tub directly, instead of through a series of belts, which means you'll never have to worry about replacing them.

Oh and another thing!!!! I had a shirt that I wore outside to do heavy gardening and yard work. It's been stained and dirty for more than a year, no matter how many times I've washed it. One trip through this new washer and it's as good as new! I use "Charlie's Soap" which is HE compatible, and only use 2/3's of a scoop. So little soap for such clean clothes!!!

I've only had the washer a few weeks, but so far so good. I"m really pleased.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_title: Great unit, a few quirks, but below are the work-arounds!
review_text:
Cost of Operation

-Not sure as to the amount of water it uses (water is included in my rent)
-Using my [[ASIN:B000RGF29Q P3 International P4460 Kill A Watt EZ Electricity Usage Monitor]], and running a half full drum of clothes through a wash and dry cycle, it cost me $0.21. That's 21 cents at an estimated 12.2 cents per KWh. The entire cycle went through 1.72KWh.

Design/Size/Installation

-I had a very tight space to put this machine in, and it should be noted that the listed dimensions are the maximum values. The machine's front is 29 inches from the rear, and the circular knob on the front is what adds the extra .75". They do recommend that you have about 4 inches behind the machine for the hoses and stuff.

-I installed the machine by myself. It was very easy and it comes with a few sets of (the same) installation instructions so it's hard to go wrong. Make sure you remove the shipping bolts and retain them if you have to move the machine later. It is worth noting that if you have to tip the machine, as I had to, to remove the shipping foam from the bottom, LG tells you to tip it on its side, not on the front or rear (I am guessing to protect the drum). Having a second person to help move the unit would definitely make it easier, but if you note in the pictures I uploaded, LG added nice hand grips to the side to aid in moving the unit.

-The unit comes with all hoses, etc, necessary to connect the unit.

-The design is very nice. Although it stays in a closet, it is a very aesthetically pleasing unit. The LED readout is nice, and the buttons are big and clear. The chrome door is a nice touch as well.

Operation/Tips I've Learned

-There are a ton of different wash and dry settings on this machine, and I am sure you can read about them elsewhere, so I will focus on the quirks that you may encounter (that I have encountered) as you operate the machine.

-The machine plays a little tune when you start it up and a load finishes. (Warning: The tune may get stuck in your head if you do a lot of laundry.)

-If drying on the automatic setting I have noticed that when it gets down to "6 minutes remaining" it will stay there for 5, 10 maybe 15 minutes, before counting down. So if you see a 6 on an automatic dry cycle don't wait around for it thinking it will finish soon.

-The clothes come out dry despite feeling damp when you immediately open the door. The dampness is just in the drum itself, not in the clothes (unless you wash something heavy).

-When washing a queen comforter in the machine, we noticed some soap still on the inside after the dry cycle and we pulled it out. To combat this, I would recommend after the initial wash cycle of a bulky item, remove the item, move it around, and run another rinse/spin cycle (which is an option)
-Although you can do a wash/dry cycle at the same time, I like to do a wash only cycle (on extra high spin) then put a few dryer sheets on then go to a dry only cycle.

-There is a certain smell about the new materials in the machine, expect this smell in your clothes for a few washes. I would keep the door open once you install it to maybe dissipate the smell more quickly.

-After a dry cycle, the LED readout will say "Cd" which I am assuming stands for cool down or clothes done. The door to the dryer will remain locked and you will not be able to remove the items inside. If you wait for it to go away on its own, it takes a few hours. (I let it do it on its own once to see). The way to get around this is so just simply spin the silver knob once "Cd" is displayed. A few seconds later the door will unlock. It is nice to know though that while "Cd" is on, the machine will still rotate your clothes every so often to avoid wrinkles. Good thinking LG.

-I usually fill the drum about half way for every load. You can wash a full drum of clothes but then it says in the manual to remove half of the clothes for the dry cycle. After I wash a half drum of clothes and do the automatic dry, it has never taken more than an hour and a half to dry the load. Combined with the 49 minute normal cotton wash cycle, you are looking at about 2.5 hours or so to do a half load of laundry (washed and dried).

Final Thoughts

Overall this is a great machine if you are looking for a single unit that can wash and dry a full load of laundry while presenting you with the limitation of a smaller apartment, a non vented area, or an area without a 240V outlet. We experienced all three conditions and this was the best unit we could find to meet our needs. The full size drum is a rarity for this type of machine, and its worth should not be overlooked. The clothes come out clean and (after the first few uses, see my tip above) fresh. You will not be disappointed in this machine.

review_text:
We bought our LG all-in-one from US Appliance in March 2009 (don't think it was available on Amazon at that time) and got a 2 year extended warranty from Assurance along with it (on top of the one year mfg warranty). Long story short, several warranty repairs were needed after the mfg warranty ran out, including broken internal drain hoses, pressure regulators and sensors, and finally the motor went bad. Assurance refused to cover the last motor repair saying it was our fault and not an equipment defect.
Turns out the ventless dryer design does not have a lint screen, and with extended use the lint can accumulate in the drive motor, causing it to fail. I am still fighting with the Assurance extended warranty company on that issue, since even the repairman stated there was no way we could have either intentionally caused the problem (as per Assurance's bogus claim) or avoided it by operating it differently. US Appliance even went to bat for us until Assurance stopped answering their calls! LG customer service was no help at all, siding with Assurance's point of view.
Bottom line is this machine is best for light use only, until LG makes its design more rugged. And make sure to ALWAYS get the extended warranty.

review_text:
After seeing so many less than great experiences, I thought I should share mine.

I bought this model in the summer 2010 (about a year ago at the time of writing this). After researching all different kinds of units, I decided to give this one a go. None were remotely local, so I had to order blindly online. I was stationed in Germany, so I was aware of such units since they are pretty common place there and I had a friend that lived in a small high-rise place in Chicago that had this kind of washer/dryer (albeit, it was smaller, much older and didn't quite do the best job). I was a little concerned by some of the reviews I saw for this model, but decided to try due to being just one unit and the energy usage.

Right from the start I had great results. There was a learning curve though for using a unit like this. You MUST be open to it being different from what you probably grew up with and not try to cram it into that old way of thinking. How it works is completely different -- at least the drying side -- from all the conventional washers and dryers so many are familiar with. You will probably be disappointed, for whatever reason, if you don't take this into consideration.

That being said, I find it cleans clothes very well and dries clothes pretty darn well for using so little energy. On average, my loads take about two hours to wash AND dry. I don't think I've ever had a load go as long as three hours even. I do the auto cycles that calculate how long to wash and dry. I fill the drum usually about 3/4 full. If you cram it full to the point nothing care move, it will not clean or dry as well. THIS ISN'T AN OLD-FASHION UPRIGHT AGITATOR! You can't expect that really from new front loaders either. They just don't work that way.

As for drying, if you open it as soon as it finishes (it has an auto cool-down feature that will tumble it periodically until the temp drops) it will appear that the clothes are damp. As I've found though, when you pull something out, it's dry to the touch within several seconds of pulling it out. I find if you open the door and leave it be for about a minute or two, it's not so bad. It's pretty steamy due to the nature of how it dries. Sometimes with jeans, it takes a little longer, but I lay them out on the unit or on something else while I fold other things first and they are usually good to go by the time I get to them. I don't really complain even if something does need more time to dry -- which isn't that often -- die to what I get overall. You have to remember this thing doesn't have a heating element like on many stoves that cooks your clothes dry essentially. It also doesn't produce lent anywhere near on the same levels as a conventional dryers. Just think about how much lent that ends up in your lent trap each time. That's from your clothes. This shortens the life of your fabrics. Every couple of weeks, I clean the wet collection tray deal and it produces a tiny fraction of what the conventionals do. Also when I got it, I was living temporarily on the Mississippi Guld Coast. So for it to dry as well as it did then, I figured it wouldn't be an issue in dry Montana--which it isn't.

I don't find it to be that loud either from all the different kinds of units I've ever used--which is dozens. It's just different, so I take it some notice it more. I certainly wouldn't call it loud.

Just read the manual and you shouldn't have any problems. Everyone that's seen mine in action, wishes they had one or hadn't bought what they had. If you're going to spend $1,000 on two units, I say spend a little more and get something like this. Shop around. The place I bought it for had free shipping and I bought it for around $1,300. You should made up the extra money spent in the first year of use. I recommend these to everyone and would buy again without hesitation.

My pros:
only one unit (saves space and not having to switch loads between two different units)
uses only 110V
no vent needed
uses A LOT less energy
auto sensing for cleaning times
can program to have a load finished when get home from work or being out or just when you have time to deal with it.
easy to use technology (for me)

My Cons:
None I can think of. I guess I could say I can't tell how wore out my stuff is by the amount of lent is left in the lent trap of a dryer. I've ran into loads being a little damp with conventional heating element dryers that "sense" when the load is dry, so for much greater energy saving and easier on my clothes, it more than evens out.
Would be handy if it was lighter? She's a heavy machine.

If you have any questions, leave a comment and hopefully I'll get it in time. I LOVE THIS THING and so does my girlfriend!

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text:
I did not buy this combo at Amazon. I found it cheaper with free shipping somewhere else. I have also noticed that most of the "bad" reviews came from people who had had it for a while and had some electronic or mechanical problems. These problems are actually to be expected. This is a complex machine, and it is difficult to service! It is one of the VERY FEW appliances where I RECOMMEND buying an extended warranty! A five-year (4 yrs extended) program is available from various sellers for about $140-180. LG's extended warranty is much costlier ~$350 for the same length (and therefore not recommended!).

Another problem is with people who haven't done their research but bought this machine even though they had other options. This machine is for people who have very limited space, no capability to vent and no 240V. For those who meet these requirements, this combo is FANTASTIC! There is no better solution (so far).

I refuse to give this combo 5 stars though. There are too many limitations and compromises that had to be made. If one wants to dry, then one cannot fill the drum more than 50-60% of capacity. A full load will simply not dry. The ventless drying uses a cold water line to a radiator, which condenses the steam from the hot clothes. This process is not too efficient, a bit noisy, and takes more than 3 hrs to dry a 1/2 load.
The lint from the process stays mainly in the clothes. Some get flushed in the drain and some get trapped in a filter located on the lower left corner. The manual recommends cleaning the filter every 2 weeks or so.

Thus, to a family that has many loads, I recommend washing every day, instead of having a "laundry day" that so many people seem to have. Those people that can run a vent should consider buying a separate dryer. It does the job much faster, and also more efficiently.

This machine is doing what it was designed for within its limitations. It is not a cure all, but for those of us who meet the requirements for buying this machine, THIS IS BY FAR THE BEST OPTION.

A side benefit of the ventless system is that in the winter, the heat that this combo produces will help in keeping the condo/apt warm. Even in the summer when the heat makes the a/c works harder, it is not a zero sum game. A vented dryer removes copious amounts of air to the outside, and this air is needed to be replaced, so the a/c will also work harder, though not quite as hard as with a ventless system.

And this brings me to my biggest concern. The radiator is located in the upper front right of the machine. When it is in dry mode, the spot becomes quite hot. Not hot enough to give someone a burn, but if the combo is in a closed space, I am afraid that it can cause a fire if a combustible item is left on top. I urge LG to install an insulating material over the radiator, attached to the top panel.

I have tried to publish my review on LG's website, but for some reason, it broke some of their rules even though I gave this combo a positive review. :(

05/16/12
I have had the combo now for a year and would like to expand on the lint problem that I encountered during that time. The lint assembles around the boot (rubber gasket around the tub). One needs to constantly remove the lint that accumulates there. If one does not do it, the lint will accumulate in the inner hoses and will clog the pump. LG recommends running the "clean" cycle with liquid bleach once a month (depends on number of uses per month). I recommend using this cycle WITHOUT bleach. Liquid bleach will harm the spider (the thing that holds the tub in place - a major repair if it needs replacement), which is made of aluminum. I recommend using bleach every 5-6 months. It is enough to clear the inner hoses and infrequent enough not to harm the spider too much.

I have gotten used to removing lint from my clothes all the time. There is really no solution to the excess lint :( , but that's life. :)

4/20/14
The machine is now almost 3 years old, and so far so good. I had no problems whatsoever. I assume that it is because I only have 2 loads/week on average. I cannot stress more strongly how important it is to clear the lint from the bellow. I work for a service company, and there are so many front load washers who get their drain pump clogged and the owners have to call for a repair that could have easily been avoided if they bothered to clean the lint at the end of the day.

I had to have a machine replaced a little over a year ago (same identical machine) due to the same problem but the service company could never figure this out and LG did not suggest this fix. The tech said this is the most common problem on these machines and that he sees a large number of service calls due to this.

IF you buy, you MUST buy a service warranty!

I purchased it online (not from Amazon)AND received a free 4 year extension to the warranty. Thank goodness for that extended warranty! I have been through pumps, motors, hoses, and more. Five service calls and many hours lost of my life. My warranty ran out a few months ago and guess what...it is making all sorts of noises and giving me error codes left and right. I now know way more than I need to know about this washer. I am a teacher and engineer and this is the next take it apart project for fifth graders in the Makers' Lab! The concept is solid, the implementation very poor. From motor placement, filter screen systems, etc. I won't go into the details, but suffice it to say it is a pain to deal with. I may have it working as a washer only now and am in the hunt for a good dryer.

I use Amazon for tons and love 'em...where are all the reviews on appliances?? Don't trust the manufacturer sites or even some online resellers. They censor their reviews. In all the years I have spent with Amazon, they do not censor.

By the way, my wife hates the fact we switched to this from a traditional washer dryer setup. Everything is always wrinkled and still damp. We purchased a steamer to hang the clothes and steam them...what a pain. Wash them then dry them and pull them out right when dryer finishes...perfect. Albeit, not as economical, but come on...five repairs?? Pffffft.

Update: 12/25/2011
Yup, have nothing better to do between hold'em and cooking the prime rib...
The washer is about to give up the ghost as well. Here is a link to a website with consumer complaints about LG washers: [...]

I am going to look a the Miele and Bosch units...users on the above site seem to have had good experiences...

Update: 2/5/2012
About four weeks ago the washer was on its final breaths. I decided to dive deep and learned about all sorts of horrible lint that builds up in the lines in the washer. Lint that accumulated above the pumps and caused them to fail due to stress. I did not know the strange noise was coming from a pump until I slid the washer on its side and did exploratory surgery. What I found is below. Know that the washer has had multiple issues with the pump and I believe it is due to the design and inability to easily access the location where the lint is accumulated.

There is easy access from the bottom and back of the washer. The back has a panel with four screws and the bottom has no panel at all. The large hose (3-4") coming from the soap dispenser down to the 'basin' under the washer is the problem child.
