review_title: Stay away from Whirlpool Cabrio... didn't last 3 years
review_text: We relied on consumer reports as the primary source for a recommendation on this washer.  Just under two years old, it started making a noise, which suddenly went away.  Then one day the machine would not spin and drain, and we could not decipher the error code into anything useful. I turned the machine over to find that the drive belt was half-on/half off the pulley on the drive motor.  This caused the belt to ride against the belt guard and wear right through it.  I removed the belt and determined that the cause of the problem was that the large pulley on the drum was loose.  For some reason the nut which holds that pulley on was slightly loose, causing the pulley to wobble.  Not sure why they didn't use some loctite on that nut.  I put everything back together and tightened the nut.  No problems and I checked it a month later, everything was still good.  Fast forward to last week, when the machine was not yet 3 years old.  Same thing, washer would not spin and drain.  Tipped machine over to find that the belt had fallen off, the drum pulley was again loose.  But this time the belt had damaged the pulley on the motor.  I figured, no problem, just order a new pulley.  Well you can buy just the pulley on the drum, but the pulley on the motor is part of the motor, it cannot be ordered by itself.  The cheapest I could find the motor online was $250.  We decided to cut our loses and buy a new machine.  We will NEVER buy another whirlpool appliance (or anyone else's by the same manufacturer, i.e. maytag).  Our last kenmore washer lasted 23 years.  Oh but it had an agitator and wasn't listed as "HE" (High Efficiency), so I suppose the environmentalists would get the dry heaves thinking about the impact of that washer on the environment.  But it was useful for 23 years.  Now this "HIgh Efficiency" whirlpool is headed for the recycling pile.  Sorry, I think this hurts the environment more than an appliance which just works year after year.  Yep, they took a design that worked and now we have energy/water efficient washers that don't last very long and are so expensive to repair that the solution is to just buy a new one.

review_text:
I had done months and months of research before deciding that the 5.2 cubic feet Whirlpool Cabrio would be our next washing machine. I knew I wanted a large capacity machine for our family of eight, and I also discovered that I preferred a top loader for many, many reasons. I hesitantly decided to go with the top-load HE, and ultimately the Cabrio, despite mixed reviews online.

First of all, it is a super quiet machine! I live in a very small house with the laundry just off the kitchen, and I can never even tell if it is on or not without looking. It holds and washes approximately three times as much as my old agitator washer did. It can literally handle at least 12 pairs of kids' play jeans with no problem. Everything comes out clean, fresh, and spun almost dry (if that is the spin speed I select). I do have to pay attention to the types of materials (denim? towels? sheets?) going into a load, the cycle I select, detergent and additives I use I truly feel the science and thought behind doing each load is totally worth it to save so much time, energy, and resources in the process!

It also works quite amazingly for my cloth diapers, even with hard water and then just as well after we added a water softener. I do a quick wash on cold with all natural, diaper-safe additive specially formulated for my hard water. Then I run a cycle with HOT water on the towels setting (because it uses the most water), a small amount of diaper detergent, and highest speed spin cycle with an extra rinse selected. Finally, I run one more quick wash cycle on cold with no detergent in place of an extra rinse. Yes, that takes a lot of time, but it uses no more water than a traditional agitator machine would in filling the basin all the way up several times. Once a month, I soak/strip all of my diapers in the "wash machine with affresh" cycle and Funk Rock soak.

I have and will continue to recommend this machine to friends, especially those with a lot of laundry to do. It has cut my time doing laundry in half or more! It also easily washes king sized comforters or a load of 15 full sized towels. It did have a slight learning curve for me to figure out what loads need liquid (oil-based stains), and what loads need powder (organic stains). I also know which loads will need a boost of oxiclean. But after reading the manual and paying attention to how my clothes look before putting them in the dryer, I have got to say that I have got a system that works for our house and everything is clean and fresh and done in half the time!

review_text:
Although this washer is now listed is "no longer available" on Amazon, I am writing this review in support of those folks who will happen upon it from other sources. I am pretty easy to please and actually don't think I've ever written a 1 star review on Amazon, so that's saying something about this piece of junk.

I bought this washer in Nov 2012, at first I was happy with it. I didn't have any issues with it not getting our clothes clean (like previous reviewers have mentioned), although when washing big loads I sometimes used the Bulk Load to allow more water into the bin. I do hate the lid lock feature, the main reason I didn't purchase a front load is because I often find things after I've started the load and want to add in. Waiting for the lid to unlock is annoying.

The main reason for my 1 star review, is that this POS quit working after 18 months. Of course it only carries a 12 month warranty, and of course I didn't purchase extended (nor is it covered by our current home warranty). At first I thought it was something simple like a clog from a small sock so my husband tore it apart and found no clogs. We spiraled from there; probably should have called a repairman from the beginning but we didn't. We talked online with a service tech and got a diagnosis of "bad control board", which, after researching, is a REALLY common problem with the Cabrio. After purchasing two control boards, a motor, a lid lock and an attenuator this junk still is not working. The local company that we bought the control board from told us their techs are always complaining about the Cabrios. So, we are actually going to buy a used washer. Lesson learned, just because it has more lights and buttons and fancy things like "Affresh", doesn't make it better. I'm going back to an old school washer that just has turn dials and no electronic control board. Don't care if it's not HE, either.

review_title: Wake up people! What did you expect?
review_text:
People, come on. This is NOT a bad washer. First of all, the selling point of this and similar HE (High Efficiency) washers is that they use unconventional and cost-saving cleaning methods. In other words, these HE washers are nothing like what your mother or grandfather is used to. From my experience with this washer so far, it cleans clothing remarkably well considering the little water it uses. Because it's designed to use less water than normal washers, it periodically dispenses water over the spinning clothes instead of conventionally having them drenched in water. This method allows for a much lower level of water in the drum, thereby saving the operator some money. Due to the lack of an agitator, it's allowed to spin at a higher RPM than agitator-based washers without roughing up clothes. In other words, the faster spin means a bigger centrifugal force to "launch" away dirty water outwards. In my opinion, the washplate and faster RPM makes up for the agitator to a respectable degree. However, some people may miss the ole agitator despite its roughness.

DO NOT confuse this with dirt and think that your HE washer is a dud. However, a good dryer will suck that excess lint right out.

review_text: We have WTW5700 for several months.  After reading all negative comments and knowing ourselves, we had decided to buy the model with glass lid, so we could observe the process, and see for ourselves, how the washing is done.  It does take a change of mind to accept high efficiency washers.  After studying the high efficiency washing process I have to say that it makes more sense than traditional machines.  How was washing done in old times?  By soaking clothes in water (as in traditional models, where clothes are floating in deep soapy water), or by rubbing it on the board (as high efficiency machines do)?  I cannot say that the washer is perfect, but if correct type of detergent is used, and the machine is properly loaded, the clothes come out clean.  However, if you cannot break the paradigm, and you cannot accept the process with very little water, you may be disappointed and be better off with the traditional models.

I'd do that anyway with a machine with so many working parts, but figured I'd throw this into the review in case someone else experiences it or knows if this is ok/dangerous.

review_title: Yes, this HE washer is amazing technology
review_text:
I've read about as many reviews on the Cabrio line that I could, and still went ahead with buying one myself (WTW5700XW3), plus the matching Cabrio dryer. Instead of just being a cheerleader or basher...I'd like to just dive in and list some observations about what I see when I wash clothes in my Cabrio and then contrast it with what I read in all the negative reviews. You can be the judge on what you think.

First off, this Cabrio doesn't just shut off in the middle of a load. It actually pauses to let gravity drain the load for a minute or two and also does water level checks. Yes, it sounds like the washer just died; falling completely silent. Yes, your traditional washer doesn't do this. Yes, there seems to be a lot more logic in this machine making decisions for you along the way to optimize the washing process. In the end....it will continue on just fine, if you let it...

In the beginning cycle where it does the sensor stage to determine the load, you would think the sensor stage is done after a few brief spins with no water. I thought the same, but the sensor cycle is a little longer. The washer runs for a couple minutes with just a little water added, but it's STILL part of the sensing cycle (note the light hasn't changed to the wash cycle yet). The clothes are actually absorbing the first dump of water as the machine tosses them around. The washer will pause again and then add additional water after it has checked how much the clothes have absorbed. Of course, the water level will never be above the clothes like a traditional washer, since the clothes need to press against the bottom washer plate to be moved around. This is also the part that most are getting hung up on, or can't accept. If you watch closely between the clothes, you will see a level of water under the clothes. The clothes will churn out, under (into the water/detergent brine mix), and the back up the center.

The clothes actually do move throughout the washer from center to outside in a donut fashion, it's just in slow motion. If you are used to a traditional washers, where the clothes slush around gallons of water in a fairly fast pattern, then you will need to re-adjust your brain for how this HE process works......and yes.....it does work!

Now for big sheets/towels/blankets/etc.. the "bulky" setting is the one you want. It'll use much more water, but it will also allow the large items to churn in the wash cycle correctly. Using the Bulky cycle is next to worthless for regular loads, because the wash plate at the bottom will not come in contact with the clothes and move them correctly. It's tempting to set all your regular loads to Bulky to satisfy your old cravings for gallons of water sloshing around, but that is not how an HE washer works. Do that, and you will be frustrated (hence the gobs of negative reviews).

My favorite cycles are "quick wash" and "normal". Quick wash is really useful if you just have lightly soiled clothes. Let's say something like the clothes wore to an office, verses construction work. The cycle is pretty much identical to the Normal cycle, but runs about a one half hour only. The Normal cycle handles most everything else, plus whites. The washer has a whites setting, but then it burns hot water and runs a longer than normal cycle. If your whites are in hurting condition, then by all means go for the whites setting. For me, my whites are not in that much of a need for aggressive cleaning.

I have thrown just about every type of clothes at this washer (work, play, blankets, towels, sheets, etc...) and it has performed flawlessly. The clothes are clean! The water usage is low. The washer is reliable with no baby-sitting/re-balancing of the cycles required so far. Since my model of Cabrio (5700) has the glass lid, I can see the clothes churn several times down and around the drum; coming back up the center every 2-3 minutes. All clothes are cycling through the water/detergent brine several times. I have seen nothing that is left bobbing on top totally dry at the end of the cycle, like some other comments have said. Dryer time is also reduced significantly because the washer does such an excellent job on the spin cycle to remove most of the water from the clothes. The clothes come out of my dryer with no wrinkles. I can understand what folks are seeing when they take the clothes damp, to almost dry, out of the HE washer. The clothes will dry just fine in the dryer with the wrinkles gone. Again, folks with traditional washers might be used to their clothes being a lot wetter coming out of the washer; but I never found that to be a feature/benefit.

In conclusion, I don't fault the consumer as much as the companies that have designed these HE washers. They have obviously dropped the ball on educating the public about what really is going on with these machines. Just saying they use less water, and the water line will be below your clothes doesn't cut it. You make a new technology HE washer, and then the consumer sees it stop at times for minutes thinking it died, then not explaining the details of the cycles and what it's accomplishing (sensor technology? tell the consumer more about how it does this and the fill lines, the flow of the clothes, etc...), and then these companies just tell you it makes different sounds you not used to and all is fine??? ....well....to me this paradigm shift is like we're going from horse-n-buggy technology to gas powered automobile technology with these HE washers .....and the folks using them are still looking for the ropes to giddy-up.

I would highly recommend this HE washer to anyone that wants to significantly reduce their water consumption and have clean clothes. My water costs were high. This HE Cabrio washer put a significant dent in the water consumption. Now, if you can't get your head around what's going on inside these HE washers and agree with how they work, then stick with what you know. Buy a traditional washing machine that fills the bucket full of gallons of water, and be at ease with your decision. As for me, I look forward to doing laundry every time with my Cabrio, and the savings it brings.

UPDATE 1/25/2017: Well, it's been a few years and the washer is still going strong. Enjoy using it just as much as the first year. Only repair I had to make was a shift actuator module [[ASIN:B00DM8KQ2Y Whirlpool W10006355 Actuator]] that prevented it from spinning. This occurred about 3 years into having the washer. The part cost me about $30 on Amazon and replacing it only took removing a couple screws to replace it. About 10 minutes of work. Other than that one repair, it's been rock solid. Clothes still come out clean and everything functions just perfect.

UPDATE: 12/7/2018: Still going strong. Everything working great.

I have a Whirlpool Cabrio washer. WTW5700WZ0

review_title: If I could give this washer a -100, I would.
review_text: This machines is without a doubt the poorest excuse for a washer I've ever experienced.  For a full load, it says it will take 74 minutes to run with hot water. That might be true if it washed efficiently without any issues.  Unfortunately, that is seldom the case.  1) the clothes, or sheets, or towels bunch up on one side of the tub which puts it out of balance thereby either stopping or freezing the cycle in whatever stage it happens to be; 2) When unbalanced, it doesn't spin fast enough to wring out the load and you open your freshly wet clothes to find out they are still full of water; 3) it doesn't get the soap out of the clothes.  When it rinses the clothes, the tub slowly spins while wetting the "washed" clothes while the tub fills up again.  Then the SHORT agitator tries to get the clothes to move for the water to effectively reach everything.  Unfortunately all that happens is the clothes stay piled on top of each other not allowing water to flow freely through all the materials.  The soap gathers on top of the water and stays there while the tub drains, leaving all the visible soap on top of the clothes. 3) I have found that it's impossible for me to wash more than 1 sheet at a time, and even then, the material twists and bunches up on itself.  Of course the tub becomes unbalanced and all the things mentioned above happen.  I always have to stop the machine between the wash and rinse cycles to untangle the item and lay it evenly and flat on the bottom of the tub.  By the time the spin cycle comes around, the same things happen.  Most times, I have to either run an extra rinse and spin cycle or an extra drain and spin cycle - or both. Sometimes it takes me between 2 and 3 hours to wash one load with this agitator, not to mention again the additional problems.  The fact that Whirlpool unleashed this sub-standard product on the public disgusts me.  Remember the good old days when you could wash an entire load in 30 minutes with a machine that has a tall agitator?  Well, that won't ever happen with this machine. DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT!!!!  YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED!!!

Seeing as how users have had multiple repair problems, if this thing breaks down on me, I'm just going to replace it and it won't be with another Cabrio.

review_title: Worst I've ever owned. Incredibly bad. Zero stars.
review_text:
If I could give this a "0" stars, I would. It's hard to pick the most infuriating feature of this product, so here they all are:

I am all for eco-responsibility, but Whirlpool has taken this too far in order to get its "energy star" rating. The Cabrio doesn't get your clothes clean, and therefore, doesn't perform its only function.

The temperature settings are all wrong: "tap cold" --whatever that is--is cold. "Cold" is cold. "Cool" is cold, "Warm" is cold. "Hot" is hot. So either you boil your clothes or you wash everything in cold.

I find is really annoying to have a machine 'sense' how dirty my clothes are. The machine controls the water level, the temperature, and the 'oomph' of the wash and rinse cycles. With this washer you have no real control--Whirlpool has made all the choices for you. You have no choice about the rinse temperature you want, and if you want to choose another option, such as "soak" or "rinse and spin," you can only do that with cold water. You can't choose to wash your 'delicates' in 'warm' water, only in--you guessed it--cold.

The cool, sleek new profile is curved on the top, instead of flat, which means that if your dryer is next to the washer, you can't fold clothes and place them on top of the washer: they slide off. What was Whirlpool thinking? Don't buy this unless you have a separate folding table in your laundry room.

Whirlpool wants me to periodically 'clean' this thing with a product called "affresh" which is advertised prominently on the front of the washer.

Last but not least, you aren't allowed to just quickly throw one more thing into the load--a forgotten sock, for instance: you pause the thing and wait for 45 seconds while it makes up its mind to unlock itself before you're permitted to open the lid. I don't have time for this.

Cabrio has an extra rinse feature, and a 'clean boost' feature--whatever that is--and also an 'eco-boost' feature--whatever that is. None of these is explained well in the literature that comes with the product, so I believe these features are antagonists: eco-boost probably means colder water with a shorter wash-and-rinse, and less oomph in the wash and spin cycles.

I plan to unload this thing at the earliest possible opportunity--as soon as I can afford a different machine. Thank God I held onto my dryer instead of buying the companion to the washer.

review_text: I shopped for a washer for several months (a couple of years ago)before settling on the Whirlpool Cabrio after reading some good reviews and the sales pitch about how well it does with large loads of clothes. I can live with it and the reduced/multiple loads, but really wish I had seen more negative reviews before purchasing this rather expensive machine.  The water saver feature may be attractive to some but for those who want clean clothes...CABRIO WASHER SHOPPERS BEWARE!!

review_text:
I thought that I'd treat myself to a "fancy" washer and dryer set. My previous set had been a top-loader with agitator, your basic three-speed secondhand model from a used appliance store, and it served me well over 5 years. I was so excited to upgrade to something nicer. Boy, was I ever fooled!
For starters, the spin cycle sounds like a freight train is running through the house. It's by far the loudest washer I've ever heard. The normal cycle runs for more than 90 minutes, I've timed it. The clothes get damp at best, so they aren't really washed at all - there isn't any water in the tub for them to agitate in, and the agitator sounds like it's lurching its way to a slow death. I hate the lid lock - really, my kids are smart enough to not climb into a washer. It's been about a year and the washer is completely messed up now. It won't run the cycles as stated, and it won't spin at all in time with the cycle. The stupid chimes will signal that the washer is off but the washer remains running. I've even unplugged it completely and the washer still indicated it was on for 5 minutes. Above all, I not only didn't save any money on our water bill, but our usage has actually increased.
The companion dryer sucks just as much, I have to run each load 3 times on 70 minutes each due to the washer barely, if at all, spinning out the clothes. Luckily, tax time is just around the corner and this hunk of junk will be taken straight to the metals recycling center. I'll be gladly going back to a basic three-speed Roper.

review_title: unreliable; expensive to repair because major assemblies have to be replaced
review_text:
This is by far the least reliable major appliance I have ever owned. In 6 years of ownership and light-to-moderate use, I have spent about $200 on repair / replacement parts, including the suspension system, the lid lock, the gear case, the rotating seal, and the drain pump. Fortunately I do my own work and know how to shop around for parts -- otherwise, I would have spent far more than the original purchase price on parts and labor. Making matters more frustrating, I have been sent the wrong part twice, by two different vendors, including Sears Appliance Parts. Fortunately, both vendors were gracious about accepting my return, but were unable to supply the correct part.

Particularly frustrating is the lack of repairability of the major components. Bad main bearing? Replace the entire gear case, at somewhere around $150. Bad teflon stops on the suspension rods? Replace the entire rod, at $50 for a set of four.

To put things in perspective, this replaced a 19-year-old Maytag that finally rusted out, but which required only a new lid switch under heavier use, with our two sons still living at home. In turn, it had replaced a GE we had bought used and kept for well over 10 years.

product_title: Whirlpool WED5600XW Cabrio 7.4 Cu. Ft. White Electric Front Load Dryer
review_title: annoying in many ways, just ok at drying
review_text:
The most complimentary thing I can say about this dryer is that I don't hate it as much as I've hated 'advanced energy-efficient' appliances I've had before. My #1 complaint is, tho they may be energy saving & groovily computerized, they don't actually do what they're supposed to do very well, i.e. dry clothes (or get them clean). That said, this dryer is slightly better than the previous brand new dryer we had.

If you leave the settings at their default --and you have to re-set them every single time you do a load if you want to use any other setting (more about this in a sec)-- you get clothes so damp you either must then hang them up to finish drying (which sorta defeats the main purpose of having an actual clothes 'dryer'), or put them away & end up with closet or drawer full of mold & mildew.

So, you have to change the heat settings. Every time. Every. Single. Time. If you even pause it too long you have to re-do them all time; the cycle setting at least is a knob you turn. The default setting is medium heat, no cycle signal or "Wrinkle Shield" (which you would definitely need if you use the Med heat setting, or aren't poised to yank the clothes out the instant the dryer is done). Med heat doesn't dry anything but the smallest, flimsiest cloth. You have to punch thru "Low" & "Air Dry" to get to "High." I'm honking on about this because tho most people don't have serious pain problems with hands/wrists, it's a literal (for me) & figurative pain to have to re-punch the 'touch' setting(s). They don't set with a touch either; you have to mash them with a good bit of force.

& then there's the noise; perhaps to really show how robotically computerized & futuristic the thing is, you get an incredibly loud & annoying electronic "bee boop bop beep baboobareep!" medley of tones every time you turn the thing on, a different set of screaming electro-tones when you turn it off, & other random boopy noises at other times --& you cannot turn them off. It doesn't matter whether the cycle signal is on or off; the stupid thing has to let you (& half the neighborhood) know whenever you or it does anything. I've hunted around to try & disconnect the frigging speaker so I could do laundry when the rest of the house is sleeping, but so far no luck.

If I sound l like a dinosaurian Luddite, I am a bit of one. But I do embrace lots of up-to-date things, especially if they're good for the environment/use less energy. However, I firmly believe something that proclaims itself to be 'energy efficient' & GREEN should still do what it's designed to do without you having to use it twice, or twice as long. And that computerized things shouldn't shatter the quiet with screaming electronic tones just to prove how compu-groovy-modern they are.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW7300XW 27 5 cu. Ft Top-Load Washer - White
review_text:
I've had my WTW7300XW for about 3 months now.

It does a fine job of washing, with everything coming out clean. Delicates seem to be treated gently.

Wrinkling is perhaps a little more noticeable than my old washer. No matter the washer I use I always use a low spin speed for my clothes so I don't know how faster speeds affect wrinkling. From the get-go I discovered that even on the lower spin speeds, this washer does a great job of ejecting the water from the laundry, while still being gentle on delicates. So it has never occurred to me to use a high spin speed.

I also never ever use my dryer, preferring to just line-dry all my laundry and take my clothes to a laundromat for pressing.

My two peeves:

1. It often goes out of balance with loads of towels, say 3-4 towels along with a few hand towels or washcloths. I'm a single guy and I tend to wash smaller loads. I don't know how it would work with a larger load like I would expect a larger family might normally wash.

2. The stupid lock feature prevents me from adjusting my hot & cold water valves to get the water temperature in the ballpark. With my old washer I could adjust them while it was filling with water. This was necessary because with the cold open all the way, it was just way too much cold water for a warm wash. So I would need to dial it down. It it baffling that we are prevented from opening the lid when the washer is filling with water. I've never ever heard of a person being injured while a washer is filling with water. This is beyond stupid. I do close the valves after each use. I understand that this washer adjusts temperature automatically, but I don't think it can compensate for the wacky water valves I have.

I must edit this review. After more than a year with the thing I have to now say this is the worst purchase I have ever made. This washer is pure junk. Stay away.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW7300XW 27 5 cu. Ft Top-Load Washer - White
review_text:
We purchased this washer and matching dryer after our 9-year-old washer that was already bouncing all over for a couple of years had the sensor go and over-filled spilling water all over our floor (which it had ripped the vinyl previously, so water got under and had to have the floor replaced).

I read several reviews, but found it was just like when I wanted to purchase a new mattress. Nothing really got an awesome review. People either loved it or hated it, so I knew I couldn't go by reviews alone. There was a great sale on the items when we needed them, and we talked at length to the salesman. So glad we purchased them and didn't listen to the negative reviews!

It may be that the people who didn't like them are used to high efficiency washers and just want more bells and whistles. We were going from a 9-year-old machine that ruined our floor and bounced all over when it frequently became imbalanced, to this wonderful new machine. We love that it barely uses any water compared to the old machine. Love the different settings. It knows what is best for different loads and I don't have to think about it. It has a great capacity. What would've taken me two loads can now be done in one. Someone complained that it has longer wash cycles. The whites are a really long cycle, but it makes sense, since they usually need more sanitizing being your sensitive articles (underwear). I don't mind that some cycles are longer when I get the equivalent of two loads at one time.

To me, some people are just highly critical. I love these machines. They do the job well and I really don't need more bells and
whistles. Capacity is important to me, and they do a great job with that too. And another good thing that the salesman noted, they are made in the USA (I believe in Ohio). So if you do have trouble, it will be a lot easier than dealing with a manufacturer whose parts are out of the country.

review_text: It is 5 years old now. Started hearing a new noise, like a scraping noise. A few days later, error code 51 appeared.  Had a tech in. He found that the single 1/4" hex bolt on the bottom of the motor assembly was loose. He tightened it. Ran a short cycle with no load. No error code. He leaves and I start a full regular colors load. 10 minutes into the cycle and error 51  appears again. The tech returns. He removes the motor rotor  that the 1/4" hex bolt holds onto the motor assembly. Magnets around the rotor have scratches. Obviously when the bolt came loose, the rotor then was wobbly. That wobbly rotor ruined the stator and motor assembly. $530 for the part! Apparently this 1/4" hex bolt is not glued on. It comes loose and destroys the motor. The tech also said this model  often has the main bearing fail. Water gets into the bearing and it rusts! review_title: Awful Awful Dryer - DO NOT BUY
review_text:
If I could give this dryer negative starts I would. We bought it in May 2011 from a big box store and the drum cracked about 2.5 years later, outside of warranty just like everyone else writing a review. The sound of cracking metal is so loud when it operates that we keep the door shut and it still sounds like a construction zone. It's pretty embarrassing to operate when you have company over. Also, don't try and watch TV while its on because you won't be able to hear it. I read all the reviews and comments and saw no one was getting anywhere with Samsung so I didn't even bother going down that road. The quality on this thing is pathetic. I know its not the top of the line model but I expected it to last a bit longer.

We made do with it for a while and placed aluminum heat resistant duct tape over the crack as best as possible from the inside of the drum. It really only bought us time....the crack in the drum steadily got bigger, ripped through my tape job, and turned into a sharp jagged metal hole that cuts our clothes. So tonight we did more research on the issue and found that a replacement drum can be purchased for about $250, if you can find it in stock. The dryer only cost us ~$400 so that seemed like a waste of money. Instead we found a very nice youtube video on how to disassemble the dryer and get the drum out. Check out [...]. The video is actually on how to replace the heat element but you only need to watch far enough to get the drum out. It's very detailed and if you are decently handy with tools and machinery it's a doable task. Once you have the drum out you can put more aluminum tape on it from BOTH sides of the drum. Also the drum is reversable so once you repair it don't put the same broken side in just the way you got it out. Ours broke in the rear so when we put it back in after repairs we put the broken side in the front by the dryer door. From there just reverse your steps in putting it back together. Watch the video again if needed. We tested it after it was re-assembled and it works much quieter again. This is hardly a permanent fix and is only delaying the inevitable that we'll have to buy a new dryer soon. You can bet your lunch money it won't be a Samsung.

We own alot of other Samsung electronics and I don't understand how they can make the best TV's and fail miserably at dryers. Just do yourself a favor and don't buy this POS.

review_text:

I called customer service and was quickly told that is "normal", that the "metal changes color due to heat", and that "no black would get on the clothes". I felt my concern was quickly dismissed since the customer service rep promptly then said "thank you. and if you have any other questions to call back", and then she hung up after directing me to a survey. Having done some research and seeing a law suit from 2014 for this very issue that has caused burned clothes and resulted in home fires, leaves me just a bit concerned. I used to run the dryer at night and even when we've left the home. I will no longer feel comfortable doing that.. Again, the dryer works very well. But the burn marks internally on the back of the machine are a big concern to me.

we just built a house (a horrible experience!!!) and needed all new appliances. I read some older bad reviews and I hope (HOPE) that all the old issues are corrected. This machine is great and fingers crossed it will continue to be awesome.

product_title: Electrolux EWFLS70JIW 27 5.1 cu. Ft. Front-Load Washer - Island White
review_text:
I literally put 2 laundry basket full of clothes in this thing, and it cleaned them all, without a problem!
I don't know what the other review is talking about, I guess they just got 1 of the bad ones out of the bunch.
We have had nothing but happiness with this washer.
I literally sat and watched this thing do 2 loads, because it's so awesome to look at your clothes being washed with a bright white light illuminating everything.

I am not an engineering genius, I am only 23 years old and I installed this by myself, connected the hoses, leveled it front to back, side to side and it passed the install cycle within 5 minutes!
After that I did 3 loads in 1 day, BIG loads, and the washer still kicks butt.

THE BEST THING ABOUT THIS WASHER?
It has an OUT-OF-BALANCE sensor, so when the Spin part of the cycle starts, you will see the washer spin moderately to see if it is balanced, if it's not, it will come to a stop and repeat, until it finds the perfect balance, and then it goes to its 1400 RPM AWESOMENESS!!! This is the best thing any company could do to increase the longevity of their washers... I had a Maytag top loader whose suspension bars bent because I washed a comforter and it was out of balance and it decided to spin to its top speed. When I read about this Spin Balancing Sensor, I was SOLD.

Also, it has a deep clean + sanitize setting which is NSF(National Science Foundation) certified to kill 99.9% of bacteria!
What more could you ask for?
I have a little one on the way, and this was just the icing on the cake for me!
I knew I had to have this awesome washer.

It also has an Allergen option, which is NSF certified to kill 95% of Dustmites and remove 95% of pet dander!
I am allergic to cats and dogs, so this was a great addition for me, incase I visit someone who has them, I can come home, wash my clothes and know that my Electrolux Washer will keep me safe from the pet dander!
AMAZING.

P.S. The Department of Energy changed the way they measure the Cubic Feet of washers and dryers, so if you go to Electrolux, you will see that they have updated their size for this model to 4.42 cu Ft.
That may sound like a huge disappointment, but the largest front loaders on the market are 4.5 cu Ft. so they were all doing what Electrolux was doing, which was measuring from the Door to the end of the drum, now the measure from the Lip of the drum to the end of the drum!

This washer makes laundry fun... which I never thought was possible.
It is so silent you can't even hear it, until it gets to the spin cycle where it is moderately loud, but barely vibrates (if you leveled it great)!

I hope my review helps you in your decision!

review_text:
The number of cycles, and options per cycle, are just staggering. At first, it's even confusing, since there are so many.

You select the cycles with the main central dial. From left to right, the cycles are: Favorites specialty, Deep clean sanitize, Heavy duty, Whitest white, Colors, Normal, Casual, Active wear, Fast wash, Delicate, Hand wash, Rinse & spin.

Then in the LCD window, you get the water temperature (7 levels), the spin speed (6 levels), the soil level (6 levels) and several other options that include: Add steam, Eco friendly, Allergen, Extended fresh, Shrink guard, Add more water, Stain pretreat, Fresh rinse, Extra spin, Pre wash, Warm rinse, Delay start.

But that is not all. When you select the Favorites specialty cycle, there are even more cycles available from the LCD window. There are two options displayed in the LCD window under the Favorites specialty cycle: My Favorites and Specialty cycles. product_title: Whirlpool WED4900XW
review_title: Hair and lint stay on clothes and in dryer
review_text:
We just bought this dryer about 2 weeks ago and for the most part I agree with the positive points mentioned in the other reviews: dryness sensor works well, 'wrinkle guard' feature is great, I like the pull down door. Overall a good inexpensive dryer.

But I am giving a three star rating due to my extreme disappointment regarding the lint filter. One of the reviewers points out that she has never seen the filter overloaded with lint. This is exactly the problem - the lint stays in the dryer and on the clothes!

This may be partly due to the fact that the fins on the inside of the drum are plastic, instead of metal. I find lots of lint and hair clinging to the plastic from static. It's possible using softener sheets in the dryer would eliminate the problem, but I don't like using chemical sheets and never had to with my old dryer.

I have several cats and the lint filter on my old GE dryer was always packed with cat hair and I even would use the dryer to de-fur stuff from time to time.

After using the new dryer a few times I was surprised to see how little cat hair was captured in the filter, so I inspected the drum, and lo and behold, the interior of the dryer was full of hair and fuzz! Now I know to clean it after a load, but what a pain, and there is still lots of cat hair left on clothes after drying. Not good!

The lint filter was below the door in my old unit - I wonder if the position of the filter in this machine makes it less effective. I really don't like the fact it is on top of the dryer - I tend to leave things on the dryer and it's a bother to move everything to clean the filter. Although the way this thing filters, I only have to clean it every 3rd to 6th load.

Luckily we are going to convert to gas soon, so I will be able to replace this dryer with another model. Any recommendations for good dryers (and washers) for pet owners?

review_title: Good "old school" clothes dryer; could do better at getting lint off clothes
review_text:
After reading hundreds of complaints in regards to front load washers and dryers reliability, not to mention price, my wife and I decided to stay "old school" with the traditional steel top load washer and flip-down-front-load dryer. As we recently moved, our old dryer was gas and the new house had no provisions or cheap way to retrofit the electric-only hookup. In addition, I wanted to keep the same style as the washer because I'm anal retentive about things matching. This dryer was the closest thing that would match our washer (the dark grey paint color has lightened on the new models). So far, I've found it to heat and dry the clothes better than any previous electric dryer I've ever used (owned or laundromat). The only complaint is that it doesn't seem to get all the lint like our Whirlpool gas dryer did - maybe its because this is a slightly larger capacity. However, it's an inconvenience, as small as it may be, and should be noted (as someone else has). Another gripe, but we purchased knowing that it didn't have the feature is the inability to use a drying rack.

Please note that with any electric dryer, you'll need to purchase and install an electrical cord that matches your house hookup and a dryer vent hose if you don't already have one.

review_title: Follow the directions and it's a great washer!!
review_text:
This washer is NOT the typical top loader agitator style washing machine. READ THE FURNISHED MANUAL AND FOLLOW THE DIRECTIONS!!!

We purchased this washer as part of a matched set along with the GE electric dryer [[ASIN:B0046MH7RC GE GTDN500EMWS 27" Electric Dryer with 7.0 cu. ft. Capacity, Multiple Drying Cycles, 4 Heat Selections, Sensor Dry, Wrinkle Care, Stainless Steel Drum and Quiet-by-Design Performance]]. We are VERY happy with this washer dryer set as a matched pair!

My list of points to keep in mind with this washer after our initial experiences:

1. READ THE FURNISHED MANUAL!!! And read plenty of reviews first!!
2. ALWAYS USE LIQUID HE DETERGENT for HIGH EFFICIENCY Washers!! Use anything else such as high sudsing powder detergent (is that really a word??) and you are likely to experience problems such as white detergent scum on the clothes!
3. Always add the appropriate amount of LIQUID HE DETERGENT, start the washer to begin water flow, then load and run as usual. (At least during our initial learning experience we used a small magnet to keep the switch activated so we can do this with the lid open - caution do NOT do this if you have cats, children or other small pets or absolutely anything else that can become harmed while the machine is running!!)
4. Do NOT expect to be able to add more clothes once the water level is set ie once the machine is running. The first time I tried this and restarted the washer it drained ALL the detergent water out first, then replenished the water level. Therefore my newly added liquid HE detergent was on TOP of the clothes, not down in the water where it belongs. LESSON LEARNED: just because it's a top loader, don't expect to add more clothes once the machine is running, same as a front loading washing machine more clothes cannot be added later once the machine is running and has water up on the seal of the door. (I called the GE answer center, they report once START is pushed clothes cannot be added to the washer at all since the auto-water-level sensing is the first aspect that completes.)
5. Noise level - this machine is a different technology than the old style agitator top loaders therefore makes a completely different sound when running and pauses during the cycle. It is not LOUDER than our old Amana, just different.
6. Balance - So far we have no experienced any balance issues, just be sure to load the wash AROUND the nubby "agitator", not on top of the agitator (same concept as a typical washer where you would NOT load clothes on top of the agitator either so on this machine just think of it as a shorter agitator!)
7. This washer has a stainless steel drum. This is a PLUS for dying clothes (I love to tie dye! - but I'm not certain this particular washer would be useful for dying clothes I will update once we try dying some items.)
8. Due to concerns with soap residue from ANY and ALL washers, we have always used the extra rinse (even with our old washer) and the extra spin (simply set the selector dial in between both). With this high efficiency unit we will be conserving more water than the typical household as this will save water on THREE fills, not just the typical two. If you are like us and have always used the extra rinse cycle, you will also experience further water use reduction.

As we have only washed a few loads and are still in the learning curve I will update this review in a few weeks once we have more experience.

Happy Washing!!

PS I gave this washer a FOUR star review simply due to trepidation over the learning curve on how to successfully load and run this washer - it simply is a different technology. If this machine proves itself over time I will likely upgrade this to a full FIVE star review. I could not give this washer five stars at this time since it is requiring a learning period which again is simply due to a different technology than the old standard agitator washers - and I somehow would feel better if there was an option to add MORE water... sometimes the amount of water just appears to be so low.. yet so far all the clothes are coming out perfectly clean.

GE Parts: 1-800-GE-Cares
GE Answer Center: 1-800-626-2000 Option 3 (Questions about operation, etc)

UPDATE Dec 2011: I have upgraded this washer to five stars since it has been functioning flawlessly and continues to prove itself worthy. If you "cheat" like us and use a magnet to cause the machine to run with the lid up, for whatever reason it often won't finish the final spin cycle. Stop using a magnet, close the door and the washer will continue to work flawlessly! ;-)

product_title: GE GTWN5050MWS
review_text:
We bought this for our Mom who is in her 80's, so simple and efficient operation was important. It was advertised as being quiet, and the spin cycle is amazingly unobtrusive, but it screeches during another part the cycle, which alarmed Mom at first because it sounded like it was having mechanical difficulty (i.e. not the sound of a smoothly operating appliance). Having to go out and buy a special type of detergent was also a thumbs-down (although I understand the reasoning behind it). People may have their distinct favorite brand after several decades of doing laundry, or they may want to use coupons or buy detergent on sale if on a limited income and not be obligated to a higher priced item.

One day I came over to did the laundry for Mom. I am fascinated with new technology so I peeked inside the tub mid-cycle trying to see how the odd-looking agitator worked. I was surprised to see barely any water in the tub, and the clothes on top were out of the water. I thought maybe I had forgotten to change the Load Size setting from small to large when I put in the load. Guess what? No setting for load size--it automatically fills so you can't add more water even if you wanted to. Then I noticed actually printed on the machine "It is normal for some of the load to be above the water level". Hello. Last time I checked, you actually have to have clothes IN the water for them to get WASHED and eventually, clean. The machine is advertised as high-volume capacity but what good is that when you can't fill the water up to that capacity? The concept is that the agitator will eventually rotate the clothes on top down into the water, and push the others out of the water. So, I get it, you use only half the amount of water necessary by making the clothes take turns getting in and out of their bath. But....are you really getting the clothes clean swishing them around in half the water, which is twice as dirty? And the clothes are getting washed only half the time that you think they are, because half the time they are waiting their turn to get rotated in?

At the end of the cycle, there was just a little bit of detergent residue (using the high efficiency detergent) but the clothes still had dog hair on them. I had to redo the load which of course, negated the energy star effects for both water and electricity. Maybe if you never check the laundry afterward and just throw it into the dryer, you'll land up with more lint because the extra stuff got blown out instead of washed out. I understand you might not get everything out if you have tons of dog hair in there but it's not like she owns a kennel or anything, she has one little 15 pound dog. I have 3 dogs and my Kenmore (that actually uses enough water to wash the load) gets everything fabulously clean. So I think this is an example of a company being so excited about their new technology that they put it into production right away so they could be the first on the market, but actually thought it was not important to test it thoroughly first. What were they thinking? Truthfully, I wouldn't even get this machine it it were at the Goodwill.

product_title: Samsung DV520AGW
review_text:
We bought this dryer (Platinum/Stainless Steel color) DV520AGPwith the matching washer when my local store had it on sale, about half off Samsung list price.

The washer/dryer combo has been great. They do a good job of washing and drying. The dryer has left my close a bit damp but it's due to the cloths/sheets getting twisted and wrapped up, any dryer would do that and my old dryer did that. The middle of the heap is still a bit damp.

My biggest complaint was that the dryer was making a loud buzzing noise while running after a couple months of owning it. It seemed like every time it was heating it made the noise. I called Samsung about it and was told that it was normal operation but it seemed to loud and too frequent. After some discussions, it was agreed to send a repair person to look at it.

The repair man came and ordered a new gas valve and would come back 2 weeks later to install. I received a call out of the blue from Samsung support to talk about my repair ticket and they told me the noise was normal operation behavior. I went to the dryer and had them listen, they stated it was normal. I asked about the repair call, they stated he shouldn't do any repair. I asked how do I return the dryer because if it's this loud I don't want it. They told me to work with my local store for that. This made me quite upset that they are trying to tell me that this faulty unit was working as expected.

Regardless, the gas valve was shipped to me and the repair man came anyway. Supposedly, once the repair person is called, it's out of Samsung's hands, thankfully! He took 15min to replace the gas valve and the loud buzz went away. He stated it was definitely a gas valve struggling to work properly. He felt there will be a recall on gas valves soon from what he has been seeing. Thankfully this happened within my year warranty.

So, if your gas dryer is buzzing really loud through out the cycle, it could be a bad gas valve.

Shame on Samsung for trying to pass this off as "normal operation".

Otherwise, I'm pretty happy with the product and would recommend people to buy, just watch for the bad gas valve.

review_title: Does not rinse well, rough on delicate clothes
review_text:
I have high expectations for a washer because I use cloth diapers on my children. I was extremely happy with my previous traditional Kenmore Elite which did a fabulous job of getting diapers and clothes clean. When the agitator quit working the repair job was going to be a few hundred dollars less than new, so we thought we'd go with new. I wish I had spent the money on the repair.

I did lots of research and felt the GE was the best of old school and new. I wanted a top loader to be able to soak, but I did not want a locking lid. I wanted an agitator and I also wanted to be able to control the water level and the temperature. Despite the HE components like auto sense load and auto temp, this machine still lets you choose the water level so I thought I made the best choice. I also thought it was a great price compared to the new fancy machines with all the bells and whistles that I don't need in order to do a simple task like laundry.

When it was installed and I washed my first load, I was pleasantly surprised at how quiet it was. After a few loads however, it started making a bad squeaking sound that I knew was not normal. The big blue home improvment store that we bought it from was excellent about coming to replace it quickly. I could have chosen another machine, but I still felt this one had all the features that I wanted so I just got another one.

After a few more loads I had to figure out how to make the machine do what I really wanted it to do. Because of new government restrictions, hot is barely tepid. To get the machine to fill with all hot water from the water heater without getting diluted by cold water, I have to leave the lid up. The downside to this is if I forget to put the lid down, the load never starts. I've gotten use to it, but everyone once in awhile I forget long enough that the water cools down and I have to start all over. It's ridiculous to me. Hot should mean hot. I HAVE to wash diapers on hot and their version of hot is completely unacceptable.

To get the water level I want, I have to set the dial one to two loads above what I think it is. Large is really more like medium so if I fill the tub up with clothes, I have to select super to get as much water as I want. Don't change the dial while it's filling up because then the tub empties all the water and starts all over. Sort of defeats the water saving feature if you ask me.

So all of this was inconvenient and maybe annoying, but if it was cleaning clothes then I figured I could live with it. Wrong again. I was use to basic food or playground stains coming out with a little pre-treatment or something. Not with this machine. I have to put something through at least twice and I'm still not sure that the stain will come out. I've also had items like gym clothes that come out still smelling like sweat or a mixture of detergent and sweat. Yeah, gross.

It also cannot handle delicates. With my previous machine I could put in items that said hand wash and they would came out clean and in good shape. This machine leaves holes at the seam line in clothes that say to wash on gentle despite chosing the delicate cycle. I've also noticed that many of my kitchen towels and bath towels are starting to shred at the ends. Granted I've had some of these towels for years but I find it odd they ALL starting fraying after we got this machine.

The final straw with this machine is that it does not rinse well. My kids are not overly sensitive to detergents, but I've noticed that they have been scratching or are otherwise irriated after we've had this machine. I've noticed a difference for myself too. The biggest tell-tell sign is with diapers. It is very important that diapers are rinsed well so that leftover detergent doesn't irritate baby's skin potentially leading to a rash. Even when using the second rinse feature, or the fabric softener option, diapers are NEVER rinsed well. I can smell the detergent when I pull them out. And yes, I am using HE detergent. I've tried powders and liquids and the results are the same. I can run a load of diapers without new detergent and suds will float to the top of the water. To get my diapers as clean as they should be I have to run at least 3 hot loads while manually scooping out the suds. Consequently, I have grown to loathe this machine.

Now that we are expecting a third child I MUST have a machine that can handle cloth diapers. With three little ones, I will not have time to babysit this machine and scoop out suds. My wish list is still the same so the search continues. If you need a machine to do some heavy duty cleaning, keep looking. This machine can only handle ligth weight laundry and even then I'm not sure I would recommend it.

review_text:
This washer does a great job cleaning clothing and running quietly, while offering many settings to choose from. But I am the type of person who likes to run a regular cycle, then before it rinses, change the cycle to gentle and throw in a few items that need to be gently washed. If you do this with this 4250 model, it will drain out all your soapy water (wasting it) and then begin refilling your machine for a totally new cycle- your gentle cycle. I have spoken with GE technicians and repairmen to verify this and have been told, "You cannot change the cycle once it has begun."

If you like to have the option of changing the cycle, check out the 18, 180, and 2800 models.

Another caveat, if you open the lid a few times too many during agitation, to add a few items say that you found laying around, the machine usually will drain all your water and end the cycle. What gives with that? How is this efficient? I was told to use the "pause" button each time I want to interrupt the cycle to add laundry, but I was also told "you shouldn't be interrupting the cycle once it begins." Seems there are sensors (as opposed to 'mechanical' workings) that have a mind of their own. These sensors are set to end the cycle when there are too many interruptions.

I prefer managing my machine myself, but if you are the type that likes to load it up and leave it, then go for it, bkz this machine does a great job, runs quietly, and has lots of options for cycles!

My less than 9 MONTH OLD Haier Super Plus Capacity Encore Washer broke down on

Karen said that if she couldn't find someone to repair the washer, she would start the process of MAYBE replacing the DEFECTIVE WASHER with a new one because she would have to get that approved. These empty promises change with every breath.
I am greatly surprised that Amazon would do any kind of business with this type of company. I have bought many things from Amazon and have been very pleased with the accurate descriptions of the items and the quality. I'll still do my Christmas shopping at Amazon, but I'm spreading the word about Haier.
I wish someone had told me that the Haier Warranty is worthless, and Haier will not honor their own warranty.

review_title: Great Washer, but with an Engineering Flaw
review_text:
I bought this unit 2-3 years ago and am very pleased with the thoroughness of the wash and how gentle it is on my clothes. It is relatively quiet, and without the agitator I have an easier time washing large items like sheets and duvet covers.
However, the reason I dropped this down to two stars is because I have been fighting a poorly designed drain pump since we purchased this washer. In the first year of ownership I had the unit serviced twice, under warranty, for a faulty drain pump. I had no issue with their warranty services since I was within their coverage area.
Now, I am outside the warranty period and am having to replace the drain pump again! I called Haier and there is no recall and nothing they will do for an issue that is clearly an engineering flaw. I am ordering a new pump ($40) and will install it myself this time around, but I will not buy another Haier washer when I replace this one.
All in all, plus two stars for being an effective washer but minus three for ongoing drain pump issues. I expect I will be replacing that drain pump once every year or so until I replace the unit.

product_title: GE GFWH2405LMS
review_text:
Have had the GE 'Adora' front load washing machine for 5 years, and it has been one headache after another. The biggest problem, not counting everything on it rusting out, is the door seal, or 'boot'. Not only does this leak water, the design is so poor it allows socks, colorfast sheets, washcloths and the like to slip around the seal, and make their way to the pump suction. This in turn clogs the filter, does not allow the pump to pump out, leaves you with a washer drum full of both water, and soaking wet clothes, and the only remedy to clear the clog is to remove the filter cover, and, thanks to the miracle of gravity, all that water in the drum pours out the filter basket, and there you are, trying to catch it in a funnel and bucket arrangement, and trying to either swap out one bucket for another when it fills up before it runs all over your floor, or screwing the filter cover back on, which often results in a garden sprayer effect, causing water to go inside the bottom of the machine, and getting everything under the washer soaked. (sorry for the run on sentence, but if you do this just one time, you'll understand.)
If you have the pedestal, as I do, this constantly is filling with water, making it useless for storing anything but rubber duckies.
Even on it's best days, the pump fails to pump to the height in the specifications, making this washer unsuitable for most basement applications.
The washer rarely is able to crank itself up to full spin speed. I've tried running smaller and smaller loads, and that only seems to alleviate the problem somewhat. Not a lot of sense having a 'high capacity' washer if you can only fill it about 1/4 full.
To add isult to injury, this week, after discovering a flooded floor, found that the door seal is full of holes, rips, and tears and is leaking like a seive. I know I could take this piece o' junk apart, and replace the seal, but it just isn't worth the trouble, since all the same problems are still going to exist.
In short, run away from GE Adora.

review_title: Hey, I think I figured out how to fix this POS...
review_text:
I recently moved into an apartment with this dryer, and like many other reviewers, I found it was completely worthless. According to the manual, this thing is actually designed to NOT completely dry clothes, since that supposedly damages them. However, I prefer my clothes to be mildew-free, so here's what I did to get this thing to properly dry my clothes:

-Stop trying to clean the sensors with vinegar. It's a complete waste of time--use the vinegar to clean your coffee maker or espresso machine instead.
- Next, open the panel below and to the left of the door and remove the plastic drawer-looking thing after twisting the two tabs on the corners. You won't be needing this thing anymore, but place it on top of the dryer or someplace nearby so it doesn't get lost/discarded. Someone else who wants their clothes to smell like mildew may want this at a later date....
- Next, don't close that panel door if you want to do laundry. Obviously, you can close it between loads, but you will always run the dryer with this panel open. If your dryer is in a closet with a door, carefully make sure the closet door closes without slamming into the dryer panel door when it is open. My unit is in a very small area and the closet door wouldn't close without hitting the panel door, so I cut a piece of string to a very specific length and then knotted it to make a loop so the panel door is open at about a 30 degree angle when looped around the panel latch and either of the metal pieces that make up the locking mechanism in the dryer door. This may take some trial and error, and you can do it anyway you want, but the panel door absolutely needs to be open when you're doing laundry. If you have a closet door, I'm just guessing you want that closet door to be closed, but obviously that is up to you.

- Next, take out the lint screen, remove any lint, and wash it with hot water and shake it off to dry. Even if it looks clean, it may not be, so rinse it with hot water.

- This next step is optional, but I found it severely reduced the "filter" light warnings I was getting. Turn the lint screen over and notice the screen mesh covers the hinged area in the base of it. Take a razor blade and cut through the screen at the base (i.e., between the plastic along the hinged base). This may not look like a big deal, but it will dramatically increase the airflow through the lint screen while still allowing the lint screen to function and collect lint. Again, this part is optional (and it does permanently modify the lint screen), but I found it significantly reduced the number of times that the filter idiot light comes on.

- For regular maintenance, I only wash the lint screen with hot water and shake it out to dry when the filter light comes on. I think the mesh is so fine that it gets clogged by stuff that's hard to see, so don't trust your eyes. When the filter light comes on, take out the lint screen, remove any lint, wash it off with hot water, and shake it to dry. Also, I used to rinse off the metal condenser thing in the drawer behind the open panel, but I don't think that matters, so I don't even do that any more, but if you run into any problems, you may want to rinse that off as well.

- Lastly, I always use the Regular/Cotton--Extra Dry setting, with the "Low Heat" push-button option selected. Unfortunately, it can take an hour or more, but it always dries my clothes that way. The clock is never right--it starts at 2:37 but then updates continuously and I'd say it takes about an hour or so, I haven't tried a lot of the other settings, but they may work as well.

Hope this helps. Feel free to add your experience/comments/thoughts/ tips below.

review_title: good product but beware the poor factory warranty service
review_text:
Purchased the matching washer and gas dryer in December 2009 at the local Home Depot. All this time (now is November 2011) I have used them only for basic washing drying of cotton based laundry and both units worked great until 4 weeks ago. I cannot comment on the fancy new features because I have never used them.
Four weeks ago I open the dryer and strong smell of burned electric wires comes out. The shirts are shredded with large holes as if burned by the iron. Inside the dryer, the stainless steel drum is covered with a blue/gray film that cannot be washed away with a wet cloth. Oh well, stuff happens and that is why I purchased the 4-year extended warranty
And that is where the problem starts. The current warranty provider is A&E Factory service and that is where the problems start: nobody picks up the phone at the other end. After a few days of unsuccessful calling I drive to the Home Depot and they dial the same number but this time somebody actually answers. Coincidence? You be the judge when that happens to you!!!!. Of course the next available appointment is a week away, technician shows up, sees the damaged drum, can't find the cause but nevertheless orders a replacement drum. Another week goes by and the replacement drum is at my house. Service technician shows up a few days later and upon opening the package finds that the new drum is crushed and therefore unusable. Not a problem! He orders a new one to be delivered immediately and promises to come back when the replacement to the replacement is back. The replacement drum does arrive 3 days later but the technician forgot(!!!) to make the appointment in his busy schedule. Now I am waiting for the next appointment a week from today. And the only thing I know is that he will replace the drum not fix the problem that caused the original drum to burn my clothes. Which of course begs the question: How many more drum replacements are there in the future before (if ever) the actual problem is identified?
So let me draw a line, $2500 invested in washer-dryer and extended service plan, $300 worth of damaged shirts, one month of tracking to the nearest Laundromat. And the ordeal is not over yet.
Do you think it is worth your pretty cash? I thought so 2 years ago but the factory service from A&E is definitely a deal breaker.
Next time I will just buy the cheapest washer-dryer machines and never again buy the extended service plan. When they break down just take them to the curbside and get new ones. It's got to be better than this.

product_title: GE DCCH480EKWW 24 Ventless Condenser Electric Dryer with 4.0 cu. ft. Capacity
review_text:
I've owned this dryer for about a month now and am very happy with it. I spent months researching and hemming and hawing about buying a condenser dryer to replace my traditional dryer. I purchased a condo year ago and despite it being sold as having a washer/dryer hook-up, I learned that the dryer was venting into the condo and I had to use a bucket system in order to keep the lint from floating around my house. Running the dryer was miserable, but I couldn't find a condenser dryer that had decent reviews so I held off on buying one.

Finally, I got fed up with the bucket system and gave this GE a chance despite the lack of reviews. I couldn't be happier with this dryer. I was expecting the worst, but this dryer turns out to be great.

Drying clothes takes longer than a traditional dryer, but this dryer is definitely able to get clothes completely dry. I would estimate a large load takes about 2 hours to dry completely. Usually, the dryer stops before the clothes are completely dryer. Then, I switch to a manual setting to give it an extra 20-40 minutes of dry time. The clothes come out completely dry using that method.

The dryer has a bunch of settings and it's simple to select which ones you want to use. The link trap is large and works well. I have this dryer connected to my washer's drain, so the condensate goes down the drain, but you can set it up so the water goes into a tub that can be emptied into a sink.

This dryer is smaller than most vented dryers, but it works for me. It can fit a king sheet set, but not a king sized quilt.

I purchased this dryer with the matching washer (WCVH48). I'm also happy with the washing machine. With a condenser dryer, if you have an older washer, you'll likely want to replace it since the spin speed of the washer is important in drying times. The matching GE washer spins at up to 1400 RPM. This whisks a lot of the moisture out of the clothes before they even reach the dryer. When washing delicates, I set the spin speed lower, but do fewer clothes in a load, otherwise the dryer has a difficult time getting everything dry.

The dryer does emit dry, tepid air into the house. Unlike other condenser dryers I read reviews for, this one doesn't release hot air into the home, so it can be used year round.

Overall, I love this dryer and am so happy I made the switch from a traditional dryer. If you need a condenser dryer, this one seems to be great. However, just be aware of what you're getting when you buy one of these dryers. If you have the option for venting outside, I think a traditional dryer would be better, but if you don't have that option, this GE is an excellent choice.

review_title: It works, but total pain to work around "smart" sensors, stick to timed dry
review_text:
The dryer does eventually get clothes dry but you have to use timed dry. So all of the whiz bang programs are completely worthless.

I moved into a new building with new appliances so I am the first user. The dryer has been in use for 3 weeks as of this review.

The accompanying washer is also wretched.

When you chose a drying program, say "cotton" it pops up the temperature, adjustable, and the dryness sensor, NOT adjustable. It also shows you expected time to complete the cycle. Using a cotton example, the machine states high temp, dry for wetness sensor, and time 1:20. So, imagine my surprise when I came back to the dryer in 45 minutes to find the load "done."

The clothes are not dripping, but no one in their right mind could call them anything other than damp - imagine 15 minutes walking to work in a light but steady summer rain . . . without an umbrella. You aren't quite dripping, but you are definitely damp.

So not only had the sensor shut off the dryer before time elapsed, but it wasn't even accurately sensing dryness. Boo.

If you try to run the cotton cycle again, it will shut off even faster. Damp is what this dryer considers dry. Poorly designed. The clothes are entirely too wet to fold and put away. They would need another few hours to open air dry. Never mind that the point of a machine dryer is to erase the need for open air drying....

None of the programs seem to allow you to override the wetness sensor. Stick to timed dry.

product_title: LG WM2350HWC
review_text:
I purchased this washer (less than 2 weeks ago) at a major discount home improvement center, along with the matching dryer, and they comp'ed the pedestals (to match another discount electronics store). I've always had good experiences with LG before, so chose it over a Whirlpool/Maytag similarly priced.

I wish I hadn't. The washer doesn't use anywhere near enough water to carry the dirt out of the clothes. Using the "water plus" feature doesn't add much more. In fact, at the end of the prewash cycle with "water plus" turned on, and a full load of jeans, sweat shirts, wear guard work pants and tee-shirts (work clothes), some of the items weren't even wet yet. The "Load Sense" indicated the load was only three-quarters full, even though nothing else would have fit in the washer. Stopping the washer and re-starting it sensed the extra weight of the somewhat wet clothes, so the second pass "load sensed" as full. But the clothes still came out dirty at the end of the 2 hour and 20 minute wash with pre-wash and "water plus".

Also, you can't use "water plus" and program any extra rinses. Setting one cancels the other. So if you want the extra water, you have to run a wash, then run a "rinse and spin" cycle after the wash finishes.

I called to complain, and they did send a tech out in two days, good turn around time. But the first thing he did was fill the washer on a Large/Bulk load instead of normal clothes. The manual indicates Large/Bulk is for things like pillows, bedspreads, comforters, slip covers, etc., not normal clothes. Also, the spin and water temps available on that cycle are restricted. So by the time he tried to test for my original problem (dry clothes at the end of pre-wash), the clothes were already wet. When he called LG to find out about the "water plus" cancelling the extra rinse, and vice-versa, they said that was what it is supposed to do.

Will I return it? Probably not. Will I buy another LG appliance. Definitely NOT.

UPDATE: After two service calls, the second one from another company, it still doesn't completely wet full loads by the end of the pre-wash. And it usually "weighs" a full load as only being three-quarters (load sensing). The second service company did replace the water level sensor, as they agreed it doesn't take on enough water. But that only raised the water level about an inch, still not anywhere near enough to wet the clothes at the center of the washer. I don't expect water up the door like a laundromat, but I do expect the water to at least fill the bottom of the drum. Never again will I buy an LG appliance, and with their attitude about (NOT) making this right, I probably won't buy their electronics again either.

product_title: LG WM2350HWC
review_title: A front-loader is nothing like a top-loader...however, the LG is great!!
review_text:
Its a washing machine, nothing magical. I love it. Quiet, and it washes my clothes like it is supposed to do. User-friendly and moderately priced as well.

First of all, you have to educate yourself about front-loader washing machines. They are designed to NOT fill up with water like old top-loaders do. That is why they are more water efficient. Top-loaders filled up with water and cleaned clothes by agitating; front-loaders filled up with just enough water, and the clothes rub against themselves (friction, like you would do hand-washing) to clean.

Second, you MUST leave the door open so it can air out. As with anything where water will be sitting, mold and mildew will soon follow. If you see reviews about people's clothing smelling like that, its because they 1) probably shut the door immediately and do not allow the water (hot or cold) to air out. They also probably never clean the rubber seal, and underneath the seal, around the door.

Third, there is a valve/hose that has to be drained out every other wash cycle, as well as a filter/catch-all that needs to be checked frequently ,too (for coins, earrings ect). If you do not drain the house often, the water will get backed up and that is not good.

If you aren't willing to take on the extra work, don't buy a front loader. If you think that leaving the door open so the washing machine can air is hazardous, buy a top-loader. While some negative reviews are serious issues, a lot of people are just lazy and don't use common sense. If you think you might be interested in a front-loader, ask people you know if they have one, how they like it, what brand they have, ect. A lot of stores also have return policies, so if you are not satisfied with the washing machine you can return it.
