product_title: Whirlpool WET3300XQ 8.4 Cu. Ft. White Electric Washer/Dryer Combo
review_text:
I took delivery of mine (from a local dealer) on December 31st of 2014. The FIRST one was delivered the previous Friday, that one's washer did not work at all. Yes, it was brand new. The second one works, but don't buy one until you read this entire review.

The washer is a failed attempt at saving water. I have no clue how any engineer or marketing team could be this stupid, but I have a feeling the WET3300 is not the only dud out there - since it uses the same pressure switch as many other models, and it is the pressure switch (and how it is configured in the WET3300) that makes this washer so awful in performance.

The washer, when set to "LARGE LOAD" will only fill with 6.5 inches of water. If you load this thing like a normal top loader, it it not going to perform well. Running small loads, it works fine - but read on.

The rinse cycle is horribly designed. On the "LARGE LOAD" setting, the tub fills with only 3.5 inches of water. This means the rinse is not complete (I have read reviews where people said they had to rinse twice with one of these, I see what they mean.) But there seems to be a way around this - liquid fabric softener, with so little water, will stain your clothing. So, for those who use liquid softener, Whirlpool put a switch on the control panel. By leaving the Fabric Softener switch on, the system fills to 6.5 inches on rinse!

If you only load the machine tub 1/2 full, run the machine on "Large Load" setting, and run with the Fabric Softener switch on at all times, you will likely be happy with this machine. Doing this, the machine is effective in doing one thing: Saving space. IT does not save water because you can't load the machine very much - but it DOES save space. If you have a family, htis is not the machine for you! A single person (like me) or maybe a couple can get by with it - but you will never wash blankets or large items in this machine.

If you really want to save water, but a front loader - they do the job of saving water AND cleaning clothing very well. The top loader, let's face it, is on it's way out. As I said before, the pressure switch in this machine is the same as many others -so either it is employed differently in other machines (likely) or else all new top loaders are junk. I simply don't know.

review_text: We bought this dryer after first asking for the next model down, the DV330AEW.  This one, the DV331AEW, has "steam technology," which is really just a water connection that allows a fine mist spray into the hot dryer.  Having tried it, I must say it really works.  I have plain cotton shirts that wrinkle a lot, and have always needed thorough ironing after being thru a dryer.  Using the "Refresh" cycle, 15 minutes with a small water (steam) spray, all I had to do was touch-up iron the collars & pockets.  In addition, there is a 90 minute "wrinkle prevent" option that tumbles clothes every few minutes and keeps lots of wrinkles from setting in.  Installation is easy, but still a few comments.  The dryer specification says it is 38.6 inches tall.  (We bought the one without the booster drawer underneath.) Really, with its plastic feet, it is 40 inches.  No big deal?  It was for me, as we had already built a counter that had exactly 38.65 inches clear, so I removed the big plastic feet and put a square of 1/4 inch plywood under each corner.  Samsung furnishes water hoses and a wye fitting to get cold water from the washing machine faucet.  It would have worked OK, but to reduce the clutter, I ran an extra water faucet from the crawl space and up behind the dryer.  The dryer's lint filter is well-designed and has all rounded corners to avoid catching clothes, which had been a real problem with our old dryer.  It also has a door over its lower half, which avoids spilling lint while removing to empty it.  By the way, as many people have already learned, some shopping around gets better prices: the vendor I bought dryer from was asking $859.00

When I hear the inevitable thump thump thump of the created wad of fabric, I go shake it out again only to hear it wad up again. Woe to me if I am not right there to monitor. I found a mega wad of several items of clothing yesterday, wound so tightly that I could barely get them unwound. This after the inevitable wad of sheets that I didn't have the time to monitor because, I don't know, I have a life with kids and dogs?? This dryer takes forever to dry laundry. First of all, the sensor dryer doesn't work. It's not a very smart machine. I totally regret retiring our old Whirlpool dryer (which still worked, and dried clothes VERY well compared to this one, but my husband wanted a newer-looking dryer to match our new washer).

review_text:
Either they have the incorrect picture or incorrect model listed here. I own a Whirlpool WTW4910XQ(0) and I can state they do not match up. See my customer Pic.

The following review is a copy from my review at at C o s t c o w e b s i t e where I paid about 1/2 the price listed here.

I would like to address the one comment by a reviewer who wrote that he/she was unable to add cloths after the machine was started. Unless I have a newer model, I am able to on mine by pressing the START button. Whatever cycle the machine is in it stops and unlocks the lid. Press the start button again and proceeds on the cycle it was in. Press and hold the Start button for three seconds, and it cancels whatever cycle it is in.
Now to the details. The group of switches on the far left is the Load size, ranging from EX Small-Small-Med-Large and Super. Next is the Temperature control which has the settings of Cold-Cool-Warm and Hot. On the right of that group is this odd Fabric Softener On or Off with the option of an Extra Rinse . Fabric softener is dispensed from inside the agitator
The large dial to the far right is the washing cycle with Normal Heavy-Regular and Light and Casual Normal -Regular and Light.
Two interesting features also on the Dial is the Drain & Spin and a Rinse & Spin.
Drain and Spin is for thick items like comforters and towels than you may want to remove excess water before you place in the dryer. There is no water used in this function
The Rinse and Spin is a great option for me if you have pet hair or sand in your laundry and want it to go through an extra rinse cycle.
Now my machine has two options that are now displayed or mentioned in the manual and that is a Soak cycle and a Super Wash.

Laundry tip # 1: To retain the color of newly purchased clothes add 1 cup white distilled vinegar in the agitator (the fabric softener dispenser) and set to RINSE & SPIN or do what I do and save an old 1 gallon milk jug add 1/2 cup vinegar and fill the jug with cool water. Place the new dry garment(s) in the washer, pour the vinegar-water solution over garment(s) and set washer to DRAIN & SPIN.

Laundry tip # 2: Do you ever get those dark oil-grease stains that are almost impossible to remove from Laundry? Purchase a can of liquid lighter fluid and pour a small amount on the stain, enough to cover and wash as usual. I can almost guarantee those stains will come out.

The only complaints I have with this model is that there is no detergent dispenser. The manual just calls for you to dump the detergent in first then add then add your laundry. Second complaint is the small tub. Smaller than my last washer.
Over all I am fairly pleased with my machine . It cleans sufficiently; I would purchase again.

Update: I have two corduroy shirts that are a lint magnet. I put them both in the washer and ran the Rinse-Spin cycle. Most of the lint was removed (about 95%). Nice option to use.

Other uses for White distilled vinegar in laundry.

Prevent lint from clinging to clothes by adding 1/2 cup white distilled vinegar to the wash cycle.

To remove soap residue that makes black clothes look dull use white distilled vinegar in your final rinse.

Get stained white socks and dingy dishcloths white again. Add 1 cup white distilled vinegar to a large pot of water, bring it to a rolling boil and drop in the articles. Let soak overnight.

Some stains on clothing and linens can be soaked out using equal parts milk and white distilled vinegar.

Before washing a mustard stain, dab with white distilled vinegar.

Attack spaghetti, barbecue, or ketchup stains with a white distilled vinegar and water solution.

Remove perspiration odor and stains on clothing, as well as those left by deodorants, by spraying full-strength white distilled vinegar on underarm and collar areas before tossing them into the washing machine.

Forgot that you left wet laundry in the machine and it now smells moldy? Pour a few cups of white distilled vinegar in the machine and wash the clothes in hot water. Then run a normal cycle with detergent.

Remove smoky odors from clothes by filling the bathtub with very hot water and 1 cup white distilled vinegar. Hang the garments above the steaming water and shut the door so the steam can penetrate the fibers.

Keep the steam iron clean and in good working order by getting rid of mineral deposits in steam vents and spray nozzles. Fill the water chamber with a solution of equal parts white distilled vinegar and distilled water. Set it in an upright position and let it steam for about 5 minutes. When the iron is cool, rinse the tank with water, refill and shake water through the vents onto an old cloth. Test before using.

Remove scorch marks from an iron by rubbing it with a warmed-up solution of equal parts white distilled vinegar and salt. If that doesn't work, use a cloth dampened with full-strength white distilled vinegar.

Remove musky smells from cotton clothes by sprinkling them lightly with white distilled vinegar and then pressing them.

Get water and salt stains off shoes and boots by wiping them down with a solution of equal parts white distilled vinegar and water.

Give patent leather shoes and bags a better shine by wiping them down with white distilled vinegar.

Get cleaner laundry! Add about 1/4 cup white distilled vinegar to the last rinse. The acid in white distilled vinegar is too mild to harm fabrics, yet strong enough to dissolve the alkalies in soaps and detergents. Besides removing soap, white distilled vinegar prevents yellowing, acts as a fabric softener and static cling reducer, and attacks mold and mildew.

Note: I don't like to use conventional liquid fabric softener because of the buildup on the inside of the machine; plus it makes my clothes feel gummy. I use vinegar in the fabric softener dispenser and it really makes my clothes soft. Also I like Ecos all natural laundry detergent

Eliminate manufacturing chemicals from new clothes by adding 1/2 cup white distilled vinegar to the water.

Remove soap scum and clean the hoses of your washing machine with white distilled vinegar. Periodically run the machine with only a cup of white distilled vinegar in it--nothing else added to the wash cycle.

Bring out bright colors by adding 1/2 cup white distilled vinegar to the rinse cycle.

Fluff up wool or acrylic sweaters (hand- or machine-washed) and rid them of soap smell with 1/2 cup white distilled vinegar in the last rinse water.

Get rid of the tiny holes left along the hemline when you take out the hem of any garment by moistening a cloth with white distilled vinegar, placing it under the fabric and ironing.

product_title: Samsung DV520AGW
review_text:
We bought this dryer (Platinum/Stainless Steel color) DV520AGP with the matching washer when my local store had it on sale, about half off Samsung list price.

The washer/dryer combo has been great. They do a good job of washing and drying. The dryer has left my close a bit damp but it's due to the cloths/sheets getting twisted and wrapped up, any dryer would do that and my old dryer did that. The middle of the heap is still a bit damp.

My biggest complaint was that the dryer was making a loud buzzing noise while running after a couple months of owning it. It seemed like every time it was heating it made the noise. I called Samsung about it and was told that it was normal operation but it seemed to loud and too frequent. After some discussions, it was agreed to send a repair person to look at it.

The repair man came and ordered a new gas valve and would come back 2 weeks later to install. I received a call out of the blue from Samsung support to talk about my repair ticket and they told me the noise was normal operation behavior. I went to the dryer and had them listen, they stated it was normal. I asked about the repair call, they stated he shouldn't do any repair. I asked how do I return the dryer because if it's this loud I don't want it. They told me to work with my local store for that. This made me quite upset that they are trying to tell me that this faulty unit was working as expected.

Regardless, the gas valve was shipped to me and the repair man came anyway. Supposedly, once the repair person is called, it's out of Samsung's hands, thankfully! He took 15min to replace the gas valve and the loud buzz went away. He stated it was definitely a gas valve struggling to work properly. He felt there will be a recall on gas valves soon from what he has been seeing. Thankfully this happened within my year warranty.

So, if your gas dryer is buzzing really loud through out the cycle, it could be a bad gas valve.

Shame on Samsung for trying to pass this off as "normal operation".

Otherwise, I'm pretty happy with the product and would recommend people to buy, just watch for the bad gas valve.

product_title: LG SteamDryer Series DLEX2450R 27 Front-Load Electric Dryer 7.3 cu. ft. Capacity - Red
review_text:
I purchased the LG 2040 steam washer and dryer in combination, and could not be happier! Prior to this, we owned an old whirlpool agitator washer and drier, which worked great, but after 14 years, were starting to have some issues. In researching washers and dryers, we decided to go with the steam versions due to their excellent ability to wash more efficiently, reduce wrinkles in clothing, and reduce allergens. However, never having had any experience with the steam option on washers and dryers, we were not really sure what to expect. Well, after using them for about three week now, we are very happy with the results!

I must say, the steam option in a dryer is a must have feature, at least for my family. I was not at all sure that would be the case before buying this machine, but it has proved its worth to me. You can add steam to normal drying cycles to reduce static or improve ironing conditions by removing wrinkles. Bottom line, this feature works, and works well. Importantly, with the LG model, water is added to a reservoir on the top left panel before the cycle begins. This is very convenient, and doesn't require a separate water line hookup like other steam dryer models do. I am currently in the process of learning how to properly steam dry my dress shirts to minimize ironing and reduce the dry cleaning bill - so far with really good results. This dryer also has a steam fresh cycle for already dry materials in need of a good de-wrinkling and refreshment. The steam sanitary cycle works great for already dried clothing or other items that cannot be washed, but could use a good sanitation. The rack works great on sweater and shoes. There are lots of features, and I am still trying to figure them all out.

The dryer, whether using steam or normal drying procedures, is fantastic! We've had tremendous results, and our clothing has never felt fresher. The machine is overall very quiet and smooth. It will take lots of experimentation, which can be quite fun actually, to understand all the features of this dryer. Highly recommended!

However, never having had any experience with the steam option on washers and dryers, we were not really sure what to expect. Well, after using them for about three week now, we are very happy with the results!

The steam option on the washer (which can be difficult to fully appreciate) definitely has benefits. The primary benefit is the ability to reduce allergens on the "Allergene" setting. It is great to know that items are getting thoroughly sanitized in the wash. Steam also reduces the amount of water being used (which is already quite low in the front-loading machine). Finally, don't worry about steam shrinking the clothes. Basically, the steam comes from above, while there is cooler water in the bottom where the clothes are located. The steam gives a deeper penetration with superior cleaning, while the cooler water keeps your fabric protected. It also minimizes wrinkling problems by softening the fabric. We've had excellent results in experimenting with the steam washer option.

Another feature we love in the washer is the load sensing capability. In this process, which takes about one minute at the beginning of the cycle, the washer spins a couple of times, judging the weight of your load (the material must be dry for this to work properly), and estimating how much detergent you should use. Bottom line, this will save you lots of money on the HE detergent required for these machines. Most loads, which look like full loads due to their volume, actually only require a half measure of detergent. The machine lets you know exactly how much to put into the load before beginning the cycle. This is a genius feature!

The washer, whether using steam or normal washing procedures, is fantastic! We've had tremendous results, and our clothing has never felt cleaner and fresher. One note: the machine does wobble a bit in the spin cycle, but is overall very quiet and smooth. It will take lots of experimentation, which can be quite fun actually, to understand all the features of this washer. Highly recommended!

review_title: Failed after a year and a half
review_text:
Note that the following is regarding FAFW3577KW1, a previous iteration of this model; perhaps the current model has improved.

My tiny 1970s-construction laundry closet isn't deep enough for most current models, so (not wanting to remove the closet door) I had limited choices at my local dealer in 2011...basically, this was it. The installers had a terrible time stacking the corresponding dryer on top of this washer and installing the set in my closet, so I hoped it would last many years. I read the manual, followed all the instructions, and took good care of it. Since it's just me, I do wash once a week at most.

However, about a year and a half after installation, the washer started beeping. It wasn't even in use! All its lights (including the panel and interior light) were flashing on and off too. Was it possessed? To get the beeping and flashing to stop, I had to unplug the machine.

The Electrolux warranty is one year (they've got it down to a science), and the repair was for 2/3 what the washer cost. Fortunately, I'd used VISA (which covers an extra year for repairs). Electrolux agreed to cover the parts, so the untimely problem mostly cost me time and headache.

The local Authorized Service Center guys (Bay Appliance Repair, yay!) replaced the control panel and said this machine breaks down all the time. (They suggested I sell the set and get a better one, like Whirlpool Duet--which I already knew wouldn't fit in my closet, as it's what the dealer originally sold me).

Jumping forward to the first pandemic year, 2020, another issue cropped up with this washer. Troubleshooting indicated the door lock. I bought a generic door lock assembly on Amazon (about $6), watched a video on the repair, and had my friend (by phone!) walk me through fixing it. It worked! So, while some learned to make sourdough, I learned to be a handy-person!

It's now December 2021, and I can happily report that the door lock is still operational. (Time to learn how to make sourdough.) The washer control panel is still going strong too. Do they build the originals of these things with parts from the Rejects bin or what?

One other thing I've noticed with this washer (which may be common to modern washers) is that the delicate cycle leaves the load somewhat waterlogged. I run a spin cycle afterward, and that does the trick. This probably nixes much of the benefit of the delicate cycle, but hang drying takes less time that way. I suppose I could use the normal cycle on cold instead of running two cycles. Whatever.

I'd rather have spent twice as much for something that's not crap but isn't ENORMOUS. I'm aware of the European models like Bosch, but the capacity is smaller. If anyone knows of a reliable normal-capacity (US) set that's 29-and-3/4" deep or less, I'm open to suggestions.

review_title: Still love this washer a year later
review_text:
It is now May 2014 and I've now had the washer for a year of hard family use, and am still absolutely loving this washer. Highly recommend. (Maybe the other reviewer here who leaves change in his clothes...maybe that is what eventually broke the glass door of his washer?)

Anyway, here is what I wrote in May 2013:

This is my new washer. It is an HE front-loader, and since I didn't buy the optional pedestal (too expensive!), the washer requires only the same space as a conventional top-loader washing machine. Perfect.

It is my first front loader, and is easy to use, just a quick perusal of the instructions in the manual, and I was washing my first load. The machine is so quiet, I went down in the basement a few times just to make sure it was running, because I could not hear it from upstairs! (The horrible, awful GE machine that it replaced sounded like a broken jet airplane when it ran.) This beautiful Frigidaire washer doesn't even vibrate. It's so sturdy and stable.

I saved the best for last: it cleans beautifully! Even in our hard well water, clothes look and smell clean, bright and fresh, even the half-dirty clothes that hadn't been getting clean, not really clean, with my old washer. The appliance dealer told me use just a tablespoon of HE detergent, no more, and that is what I do. Works great. A bottle of Tide lasts more than a month of daily or twice daily loads.

As a side note: there are several reviews here bringing the star rating of this washer down, and it's misleading people looking for decent reviews. At least one of the reviews is for a DRYER! One is for a different model! So, don't go by the average star rating on this, read the individual reviews on this product and the other washers you are considering.

Recommendation: Yes, two thumbs up for this beautiful, quiet and efficient washer.

product_title: LG WM3550HWCA
review_text:
Pros:
--As of Feb 2012, this is the most efficient large capacity consumer washing machine according to the EPA. Google 'EPA washing machine' to see their website.
--This unit costs $10 a year to operate!!!
--Gets clothes really clean. I use the ultra efficient 'tap cold' setting every time and I haven't had a problem yet getting out tough stains (like blood)
--The steam mode is a nice bonus feature I think, but I don't really use it very often. But when i do, it's on a blanket on a cold day, and it's refreshing.
--The aller-genie mode (get it? as in allergy-fighting mode) does sheets very nicely, and I notice a real difference from my old washer
--Each load takes 1/2 the detergent I would normally use with my old top-loader.
--According to Consumer Reports, LG is the most reliable washing machine brand, and we haven't had any problems yet in last couple of months we've owned this machine.
--Easy install, setup, and operation. I'm not good with electronics, but it's easy even for me.
--Auto balance will determine the size of the load so you don't have to. It weighs it, which is interesting to watch!

Cons:
--Expensive.
--This is my first-front loader, and I hate that I must wipe the front rubber seal after each use. I have tenants who live in my house, so I worry that they'll forget to follow instructions and I'll have mold some day.
--Some wash modes take a long time! A full 'heavy' soiled load takes about 1.5 hrs.
--There is such a thing as too many options; there are 10 different wash modes! It can get a little overwhelming, but luckily 'normal/cotton' seems to work for just about everything
--As with all high efficiency washers, it's recommended that you use the special HE washing detergent, but I refuse to pay extra for my washing solution. Just use less of the normal detergent (so this is actually a positive if you ignore the advice).

I was hesitant to buy this washer as it's not very common and I could only find one review online. The more expensive LG 3875 seems to be far more common here in the USA, but there are 2 reasons why this model is better:

(1) Cheaper and
(2) More efficient

I was not disappointed. It has not leaked or otherwise malfunctioned. I love this machine, it makes washing fun, and I high recommend it!

review_title: Don't waste your money on LG washers
review_text:
Don't buy LG.
We bought the top of the line LG front load washer a few years ago. It was great for a year, and then the problems started. We've had repair people in several times and repairs are always a hassle because all LG parts must be ordered from CA.
The smell started the second year, and it has been a continual problem. You may hear about wiping the door seal, using different detergent, and other solutions, but we've tried them all, as well as products to eliminate the smell. The only reliable solution is to use the bottom drain line located inside a small compartment on the front of the washer after every load. Yes, the small door that is not mentioned in the manual contains a drain line, and we drain the left over water into a small bucket after each wash.
Our clothes don't smell, but this process is absurd. We've contacted LG, but it's a waste of time. The only thing they haven't told me yet is their washer is better than washing clothes on a rock near a river.
Our washer is now 5 years old, and the bearings are bad. My wife called the repairman and the estimate is over $500. I am thrilled, I can now throw out this piece of junk and buy something that works. I struggled to throw out a $1500 washer that worked, but it's an easy decision to toss it now. Good bye LG.
Once again, don't buy LG products until they learn how to build reliable products and develop some customer service.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW8200YW Cabrio 4.6 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
The "Ides of March" (well, one day later) is a perfect time to warn anyone considering the purchase of this washer about the multitude of problems it will introduce into your laundry routine (which you can read about in reviews of other Whirlpool Cabrio models on Amazon and elsewhere). But here is a quick summary, which should be all you need to run screaming from this machine: 1) Clothing wrinkled like aluminum foil that has been balled up and opened (If you prefer to hang the majority of your clothes like I do, you'll want to get your iron ready); 2) Items coming out of the washer with dirt and stains remaining, as well as with lint and even, possibly, small holes (like the one in a fleece blanket I washed on the "delicate" cycle, or the one in my daughter's shirt that I made the mistake of washing on "normal," even though that is the appropriate setting for a sturdy cotton fabric; 3) Cycles that take at least an hour on average (so forget squeezing in a load before heading out the door or to bed); 4) The need to carefully load your clothes "doughnut style" around a washplate without letting any fall into the center; 5) A moldy smell that can develop if you don't run a special cleaning cycle every month or so--or, as I've heard, even if you do; 6) Operational problems and poor customer service from Whirlpool.

I can't comment on the last two items personally, since I am one of the people the reviewer above refers to, who fortunately replaced my disappointing Cabrio with a Speed Queen, the only fully mechanical, American-made (to last!) washer left on the market. (Speed Queen's main competitor used to be Maytag, until they were bought by none other than a company that begins with W.) My Speed Queen AWN412 is a complete 180 degrees from the Cabrio in every way. It looks and sounds like my grandmother's circa 1960 washer (complete with simple dials and a pull knob) and it functions like it, too, washing clothes thoroughly, without undue wrinkling and in half the time the Cabrio would take. Just beautiful.

Like my fellow reviewer said, don't be fooled by appearances and a fancy platinum panel of electronic buttons that are far more likely to malfunction--or the quiet, high tech noise that belies new but unimproved technology. It doesn't matter what your washer looks like--just that it cleans your clothes well. If you can't stand the traditional sounds of an agitator churning away, just turn up some music or sing Hallelujah that you don't have a high efficiency washer attempting to spin the dirt off your clothes at warp speeds. The bottom line, as I learned the hard way (and paid for, with a steep 20% restocking fee from a local appliance dealer--despite being oversold on the Cabrio), is that you simply need a tub full of water and an agitator to clean clothes properly (and there are multiple settings on the Speed Queen so that you can match that water level to your load size).

The government regulations that led to this new "green," low-water technology may be well-intentioned, but they are nonetheless misguided. As much as liked my previous Maytag, it died after 7 years--which is probably longer than I would have gotten out of the Cabrio. So to echo what a Speed Queen reviewer wrote on Amazon, the savings on energy and water with high efficiency washers is completely negated by the energy from manufacturing plants polluting our environment as they create appliances that break so quickly and end up in landfills. Not to mention having to rewash clothes that aren't clean, doubling the amount of water/energy use, and having to prematurely replace clothes that are destroyed. Or the increased use of your dryer--and iron--to remove wrinkles. Or the need for toxic cleaning agents to prevent mold (which undercuts the use of natural and organic products). So, it turns out, "high efficiency" does not equal "green" when it comes to washing machines, and it certainly doesn't equal "effective."

To those who are in the market for a new washer, do yourself a favor and pass on the flashy HE models. And to those who are stuck with one--Good Luck and God Speed (Queen)!

review_text: I am very dissatisfied with the Whirlpool Cabrio washer.  The water level stays so low that the cleaning is only mediocre and the rinsing is terrible.  Even using an extra rinse cycle, my dark cottons come out with streaks and splashes of white, from the detergent, and look unsightly.  These streaks have to be sponged off by hand with a wet towel or they will still be visible after drying the clothes.  I have tried different detergents--both powder and liquid, as well as different brands.  I have tried different spin speeds and water temperatures.  I have called Whirlpool as well Lowes, where we purchased the machine, and neither offered any helpful advice.  The Whirlpool rep agreed that my machine's performance is unacceptable but offered no remedy and would not transfer me to any higher employee to speak to.  To me, this says that Whirlpool does not stand behind its products, and if a product does not perform well, that's the buyer's problem.  I will not be buying any other products from Whirlpool, including the dryer that would have matched this washer.  In addition to the washing and rinsing problem, the laundry comes out of the washer very wrinkled and hardly wet, due to the high spin speed.  The idea is that this saves energy by reducing drying time.  The purpose is defeated, however, when you have to dampen the clothes before drying, in order to get some of the wrinkles out.  I would strongly advise any potential buyers to steer clear of this machine and all Whirlpool products in general.

review_title: Great looking machine, abysmal quality and customer service
review_text:
Poor quality and even worse customer service. I purchased the machine in Feb. 2012, and while the machine worked well at first, the quality of the components used showed through after two years. The spin cycle began to develop a loud noise, which increased over time, until I put a service call in. I did some research on the side and suspected a bad bearing, based on the noise. The tech diagnosed it as that and explained that the repair was to replace the inner tub, at $440 including parts, labor, and service call. For a machine that cost $1000 (MSRP), you'd expect better.

I then called Whirlpool customer service to discuss the problem. The woman I spoke with on the phone was rude and generally condescending. When I asked why there were countless reports of Cabrio stator drive washers with bearing failures, and why there were bearing replacement kits available for 2009 model Cabrio units, she had no answer. A bearing, most likely supplied by a low bidder, is unacceptable. The conversation ended when I told her I'd avoid buying any of their products in the future, since they don't stand behind them after the warranty. Her suggestion: buy a service plan. Ridiculous! At the end, I was told she'd note my frustration in my file, and to have a good day, then hung up on me.

Long story short, spend your money elsewhere on a machine worth the price tag, not this (or any) Cabrio machine. In the future, I'll look at an LG or Samsung appliance long before Whirlpool for ANYTHING I need in the future.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW8600YW Cabrio 4.6 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
Update 2021: We're still using it.

2010: We bought this washer on clearance at Lowe's. It had been marked down to $699.99 over MLK weekend, but we got an additional 10% off since they'd sold all except the floor model. For $629.37, we think it was a good deal. We know repairs to Cabrio washers are expensive, so we opted for a SquareTrade 5-year warranty; we got a great deal on that, too, since they sent me an email for 40% off a warranty purchase.

The first thing we washed was a fairly heavy, generously-sized, king comforter. We used the bulky setting. It washed up *great*. We were amazed it didn't need any kind of re-adjustment in the drum during its cycle. My next load was comprised of various clothes, a mixed load. I'd say there was well over a laundry basket's worth. I did them on the recommended setting and they, too, washed up very well. All the clothes cycled through the agitation cycle and everything smelled fresh. On the whites setting, I washed a very large load of towels and threw in our plastic shower curtain liner. At one point, I did have to pause the load and redistribute the shower curtain liner since it had formed a mushroom top over the linens. Once I did that, the wash continued without incident. We had a Frigidaire frontloader the last 9 years and this was the first time a shower curtain liner came out spotlessly clean. That impressed me, given what we were used to.

You definitely have to follow the manufacturer's directions on how to load the tub and what cycles to use. We're pleased with the washer. The only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 is the propensity for the mushroom top. I'd read this can happen with this style of washer and I've seen it myself on two loads now. The other was a thin, but heavy king bedspread.

review_text: I purchased this washer and dryer combo a few years ago and loved it at first.  It still does a very good job of cleaning clothes and I love that I can get a queen size comforter in it.  I'm only 5" 1" and I do have to stand on my tip toes to reach the bottom of the washer to retrieve washed items.  This machine loads differently from a traditional washer so you have to follow the loading instructions for it to work well.  I don't usually buy extended warranties but I did on this item because of all the electronics.  Right before the warranty expired, the machine started making a LOT of noise during the spin cycles.  I kid you not, it sounds as if a supersonic jet is taking off.  Prior to this, the machine was so quiet I had to have the alarm on to tell when the load was complete.  Since the machine was actually not leaking and would do what it was supposed to do, the company would not honor the warranty!  Whirlpool told me that it definately should not be so loud.  I have a friend whose Cabrio washer did the same thing after about a year.  My repairman told me that he wasn't sure what the problem was but that he couldn't guarantee that it wouldn't continue even after he took it apart to fix it.  The technology is so new that repairmen aren't as familiar with it as they are with older technology.  So, I live with the noise.  I wouldn't buy this washer again.

review_title: Very poor performance and customer service
review_text: I am very dissatisfied with the Whirlpool Cabrio washer.  The water level stays so low that the cleaning is only mediocre and the rinsing is terrible.  Even using an extra rinse cycle, my dark cottons come out with streaks and splashes of white, from the detergent, and look unsightly.  These streaks have to be sponged off by hand with a wet towel or they will still be visible after drying the clothes.  I have tried different detergents--both powder and liquid, as well as different brands.  I have tried different spin speeds and water temperatures.  I have called Whirlpool as well Lowes, where we purchased the machine, and neither offered any helpful advice.  The Whirlpool rep agreed that my machine's performance is unacceptable but offered no remedy and would not transfer me to any higher employee to speak to.  To me, this says that Whirlpool does not stand behind its products, and if a product does not perform well, that's the buyer's problem.  I will not be buying any other products from Whirlpool, including the dryer that would have matched this washer.  In addition to the washing and rinsing problem, the laundry comes out of the washer very wrinkled and hardly wet, due to the high spin speed.  The idea is that this saves energy by reducing drying time.  The purpose is defeated, however, when you have to dampen the clothes before drying, in order to get some of the wrinkles out.  I would strongly advise any potential buyers to steer clear of this machine and all Whirlpool products in general.

review_text:
11 Reasons NOT to buy this washing machine:
1. You cannot soak clothes in hot water. When I need to soak clothes, it is because a child had an accident during the night or there is a stain - both of these options MUST have hot water to soak the clothes in, but this washer will not allow you to do that.
2. The water it does allow your clothes to soak in (only cold or warm), is not actually soaking your clothes in a tub of water. It gets the clothes partially wet and they sit there damp, not wet. What good this actually does for cleaning clothes, I have yet to figure out.
3. Your clothes will never be clean unless you choose the "Heavy" option. I have no idea why it has other options, they are useless.
4. The heavy option takes 90 minutes to wash a load of clothes, no matter how big or small the load is. 90 minutes? I find this absolutely ridiculous.
5. We were told by the salesman that the washer could determine the size of the load and would adjust itself accordingly. Yep, it sure does - 90 minutes for extra small or extra large load - it adjusts itself by doing nothing.
6. Many times after washing a load of clothes, they do not smell good at all. Therefore, the load has to be washed again. Yep 90 + 90 means that load of clothes just took you 3 hours to wash!
7. You have to wash the machine, empty, too! You have to buy special cleaning supplies for this as well. They are not cheap either. This also takes 90 minutes.
8. A regular machine like the old ones that you can turn the water on to fill up the tub gets your clothes MUCH cleaner - those machines are cheaper, too!
9. I tried for months to find something good with this machine - I can find nothing!
10. It is MUCH more expensive than the regular washers. You will be MUCH better off to get the cheaper model that is NOT a Whirlpool He.
11. Emailing the company about your problems will get you nowhere. I asked them to trade me for the regular kind - it would be a loss on my part, since I have the most expensive machine. They wouldn't do it - They know it's a piece of junk, too!

product_title: Whirlpool WTW8800YW Cabrio 4.6 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
I purchased this washer in January 2010 and was initially happy with the way it cleaned and I liked the top loader without an agitator so it could handle bulky items. The first year was great and the high speed spin cycle got the clothes almost dry so that very little time was spent in the matching gas dryer.
January 2011 was my first service call, a week after the manufacturers warrantee expired. Fortunately for me the day I purchased it the unit was on sale for $100 less than I was expecting to pay and I was talked into the extended 4 year warrantee for $79. I don't usually purchase these warrantees but did this time because it was lower than my budgeted total cost. Best money I have ever spent! The January 2011 service call was a covered item, a control board part that cost around $250. Since then we have had several service calls, another replaced control board, other misc. parts I don't know and several weeks ago it started getting the dreaded UL (unbalanced load) code on a regular basis, to the point a load would have to be rinsed at least 3 times before it would cycle thru to the end and finally it wouldn't do the final rinse with a constant UL code. I ran the washer with nothing in it because the warrantee company said it wasn't a warrantee issue but I didn't know how to load the machine I've had for almost 4 years. I still got the UL code so another call to the service center to schedule an appointment. Based on this information they diagnosed the problem, ordered parts and scheduled an appointment a couple of weeks out. Service tech comes and it's not the problem diagnosed over the phone but a major bearing, the motor and other expensive parts. Again at least it's not costing me money, but I will be without a washing machine for almost a month before this worthless POS is working again. It's less than 4 years old and it's been one of the worst appliances I have owned; the service tech told me that major appliance like this have a 5 year life span these days, not what I would expect from a $1,000 item and I didn't even get close to that without major problems, in fact I made it only to 53 weeks.
We had constant problems with an oversudsings error code, using the HE detergent; LD - long drain issues where the unit would shut down and not drain properly and UL codes over the years. Advice from service techs always seemed to be a problem other than the manufacturer design and quality, one tech said the LD issue and oversudsing was the HE detergent we were using (not a bargain no name brand but a leading company) the next tech said the current brand we switched to was the issue and recommended the original detergent we had been using. Is someone kidding! When we had LD - long drain issues - there would be a definite foul odor from the machine that didn't make you feel good about putting normal soiled clothes in a cleaning machine that smelled so foul.
I will not spend any of my money on servicing this machine and the next issue will be the last one I deal with. Nor can I recommend anyone purchase it, at any price this washing machine is not worth the aggravation of a poor design, with a good concept, and obviously poor quality. I'm not sure I'll buy another Whirlpool product.

Update - Jan 2014 - When the service tech came out with the replacement parts from Whirlpool the replacement part was broken and the machine couldn't be fixed again. Another delay and reordering of the part, this time the service company promised me that they would inspect the part prior to having a tech come to my house. They did and the second part from Whirlpool was broken also. It's bad enough to have a broken appliance, but to have two defective replacement parts sent was the last straw. I have a new non-Whirlpool washing machine. The first month has been good and I did purchase an extended warrantee. Other brand names from the same parent company of Whirlpool include Maytag, KitchenAid, and I understand also they manufactures for the Sears Kenmore line so they were all excluded from being purchased.

review_title: This machine failed from day 1 and died 5 years later
review_text: I brought this machine 5 years ago because of the recommendations from Consumer Reports. I wish I had been able to read these reviews on Amazon first and avoided this mistake. This "washing" machine failed in the most basic way- It does NOT clean clothes. I followed all instructions and was told, "That's just the way HE machines are." In addition, the clothes got so tangled, I had to remove dozens of tight knots which ruined my clothes. It does not clean moisture-wicking workout clothes because of its design (non-effective agitation and low water) so they came out stinky. My all-black clothes loads came out streaked with white lint. I used an extra rinse to no avail. The machine is very noisy and the cycles take too long. The locking mechanism is wonky and began to fail to release. Finally, I got the dreaded F51 warning on the dash to call for repairs. I had no interest in extending my pain any further. I replaced it today with a Speed Queen. In my first Speed Queen load, the machine actually removed food stains from my tablecloth, something my Cabrio couldn't do. For the thousands of people who purchased this shoddy appliance, Whirlpool owes us all a heartfelt apology and a refund. I want my $900 back for 5 years of dirty clothes. I will never ever, ever buy another appliance from Whirlpool.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW8800YW Cabrio 4.6 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
This product was supposed to take advantage of using less water and at the same time be a top-loading washer. Front loading washers use gravity to assist in washing and circulating the water through the clothing. The engineers of this product "hoped" that their use of a small center "agitator" would "swish" the soapy water through the clothing, and also allow the clothes basket to "wobble" thereby assisting in water movement.

Nice try.

It didn't work. No even close. The water is engineered not to even cover the clothes. The clothing sits in a basket of barely moving water, and only the bottom of the clothing gets wet. They tried to mask this defect by an extreme spin cycle, which squeezed every last bit of water out of the clothing. Most of the very long process is spinning.

It is true that the clothing comes out very well spun, but still dirty. According to Whirlpool, you are not supposed to wash sheets at the same time as other clothing. That is correct. If you try, the sheets gather up the clothing into a snug cocoon, and the agitator batters the cocoon on the side of the agitator for 50 minutes. When it starts to spin, as you guessed, it is an unbalanced load, and must be dissected apart.

If you try to wash a comforter or blanket, they will sit, not even covered with water, almost unmoving in the tub. You might just as well put your laundry into a large tub in the back yard and just let it sit. Oh yes, and don't cover it with water, either. On the plus side, it uses very little water. But it doesn't wash your clothes either.

Obviously I don't like this machine. I kept it a week and paid a restocking fee of 90 dollars (gladly) to get rid of it. I am still buying a Whirlpool front loader. I guess I am crazy, but it is labeled a "Maytag."

I guess you could say that this was a disaster. I wish I had read more reviews before I bought it. Don't buy this machine, unless you just want to soak your unmoving clothes in a tub of water that doesn't even cover a half of it. If it were possible to not give this even one star, I would do it.

Garbage.

review_title: Anyone Want My Piece of Junk Washer??
review_text:
We have had this machine for about three years and it has been an absolute nightmare. I am thinking about giving it away on Craigslist. There have been so many problems it is starting to be a joke around our house. Here's what happened:

1. The spin cycle stopped working before our warranty was up. Whirlpool got us in contact with a repairman who literally had no idea how to fix the machine. He had to come back four times and it still did not work, so my husband had to take the whole thing apart to fix himself. That was two years ago, and the spin cycle stopped working twice since then; I literally just ordered another part because something else went on it. If you purchase this machine do not be surprised if your clothes start coming out sopping wet; based on other reviews I have read this sounds like this is a common problem!

2. You cannot overload in any sense of the word. The first time I put a "normal" amount of clothes in the machine, the washer bounced around so much it made a hole in the catch pan under the washer. We have a second floor laundry, so the water leaked out and water started dripping down onto the first floor ceiling. We had to rip down the entire ceiling and put up new sheetrock. This actually happened twice; the second time Mr. Clueless Repairman didn't tighten the water hose and it came loose and water went all over inside of the walls. So far we have spent about $2000 just repairing our ceiling and repainting.

3. It takes forever to wash. If you wash any large items like a comforter you have to put on a "bulky" setting. It takes over an hour to wash! I thought this was supposed to be energy efficient! We literally have saved no money on water or energy since purchasing this machine.

We called Whirpool to complain about the quality and issues we have had with this machine. Do you know what their response was? "I am sorry, sometimes machines break". Instead of spending $1000 for this washing machine, how about I give you mine for FREE! I can't get rid of this thing soon enough!

I don't feel that there is truly a gentle cycle on this machine. Take my advice and that of many others and DO NOT BUY THIS MACHINE!  If I cold, I would rate it ZERO.

review_text:
I don't understand all the negative reviews here. When I bought my Cabrio about 5 1/2 years ago, it was one of the highest rated machines by Consumer Reports. I don't always agree with or go by their ratings in some things, and they can overlook problems, but they seem to have a pretty good testing system for washing machines. As mentioned, I've had it about 5 1/2 years, and I have not had a single repair problem, although I only need to do laundry about once a week. I usually use it set on Normal, but I may try Casual now, as one reviewer mentioned it gives it more water. However too little water has not been a problem. I have a white machine with a clear top, so I have watched the mechanism in action as it's washing clothes, and even in the Normal setting it does wet and rotate clothes in the wash. At first I didn't realize it needed HE detergent, but no harm was done and once I switched to HE detergent the clothes seemed even cleaner, about as clean as with an old Kenmore with a traditional agitator used in my previous residence. It seems like the agitation used in cabrio is gentler on the clothes, from observation of the action and perceived wear to my garments. More recently I started adding non-chlorine bleach (hydrogen peroxide). I always run the extra rinse cycle, just to make sure the detergent is rinsed out completely--I did that with my previous machine and would do that no matter what machine I used.

I thought the washer may have been eating some socks, as I was missing about 4 or 5 mates, but I recently found several, including one long-lost one, so it wasn't the machine. I don't know if most modern machines have this, but I like the load balancing mechanism--I assume that's what it is--which gives the load a few spins at first, stops the drum short, and a balancing weight slides into position. If there are too many clothes, at some point in the wash cycle the machine stops, drains the water, shuts itself off and gives its shut-off beeps. The LCD screen reads oL, which means overload, so you need to take out one or more pieces of clothes and start the wash over with more detergent (it shuts off before the bleach is added, so that doesn't need to be replenished). This only happened for the first time in the last year, and only a few times.

I think most of the problems people have with the machine (I can't speak to repair problems, as I've never had any), is that they are not used to the agitation mechanism and wash action, expecting it to fill the tub, and don't understand it. When Consumer Reports did one of their wash tests, which is to leave the clothes in the washer, for a period of days, I think, to see if any mold or odors developed, the Cabrio did fine in that regard, an indication it was thoroughly cleaning the clothes, and I have never experienced any odors in machine.

PS My model, being from 2009, may be a little different than the ones reviewed here, as someone mentioned a Sanitize setting, which mine doesn't have, but I believe it's basically the same model, 4.6 cu. ft., stainless steel drum, clear top, etc.

PPS it's now January 16, 2016, 11 months after I wrote this review, and the problem with the overload shutting the machine down and having to remove a garment, which is not fully spun dry, is happening almost every time now, and I'm not putting any more close in that I did before this started happening about two years ago. Researching the problem it seems this is a known issue, probably related to either corrosion or rust on the driveshaft, or the nut on the bottom which holds the assembly together becoming loose and falling off--this assembly is usually designed with the nut of the top to avoid this problem. It could also be a control panel or sensor problem.

review_title: Very poor machine - Extremely loud, doesn’t rinse properly, and it leaks!
review_text:
I bought the GE Unitized Spacemaker Model GTUN275GMWW six months ago to replace an older GE unitized model. I was pleased with the previous model and used it for several years, so I didn’t hesitate to buy the latest GE model when it broke. Unfortunately, the new model is very different from my old model. The new machine has been a clunker since the day it was installed! It’s extremely loud, it does not rinse properly, and now it’s leaking water and black soot from the bottom on the machine.

I’ve been washing clothes for almost 30 years, and I’ve used many different washing machines. This is the only one I have any complaints about. It is truly the worst home investment I’ve ever made.

I contacted GE Appliance Service and scheduled a service appointment. When the repair technician removed the front of the machine, he immediately saw that the machine is leaking and is rusted out. To fix it, he needs to fully disassemble and rebuild the washer, including the transmission, tub seal, bearings, tub assembly, tub ring, inner and outer basket, and probably other parts. This is a new machine, only 6 months old!

Given my experience, I do not recommend this machine. Following is a more detailed description of the problems:

1) The washer leaks – Water and black residue (looks similar to black dirt when it dries on the floor) are leaking from the bottom of the washer on the left-hand side.

2) The washer is extremely noisy – My neighbors can hear it spinning from outside of my condo unit, even when they are a full flight downstairs. It sounds like a train roaring down the tracks! The noise interferes with phone calls and TV, and it definitely doesn't make me popular with my neighbors!

3) The washer does rinse properly – With just two regularly-sized bath towels in the washer, the washer will not rinse properly. Even after running it through an extra 2 - 3 full wash/rinse cycles without soap (which takes a lot of time and wastes energy!) there are a lot of suds left in the water and there are suds on the sides of the tub after it spins. To wash towels, I have to skim out the soapy water by hand. I currently use high-efficiency (HE) laundry detergent, but the problem occurs with both HE and traditional laundry detergents. As for the question of whether I'm using too much soap, I’ve reduced the amount of soap and it didn't resolve the problem. Also, I've been washing clothes for almost 30 years, and I've never had this problem with another washer, so I don’t believe the problem is related to too much soap; the problem is with the machine and the way it rinses.

product_title: LG DLEX3470VSteamDryer 7.3 Cu. Ft. Graphite Steel Stackable With Steam Cycle Electric Dryer
review_title: Never. Again. It's a lemon, and LG has sour customer service.
review_text:
Run. That's all I can say. Run as fast as you can from LG. Mine was not an Amazon purchase but I feel obliged to help others make an informed decision, and all I can offer is my own personal experience with this product and manufacturer.

Purchased this dryer 11/02/13, with matching washer WM3470HVA.

The "steam fresh" and "steam sanitary" cycles stopped working. I got an "Ie2" error message. But at least it dried clothes. LG customer service said that either I'd have to A) "preheat" the drum for 5 minutes (which pardon me if I'm wrong, but doesn't that defeat the purpose of having an HE machine?) or B) select the "big" setting for those two cycles and just can't use the other two garment settings. Then they told me that the current cold weather is causing this issue and I should wait until it's warm outside before calling to complain again. I insisted that I was getting the error message when it was over 70 degrees out. I live in Atlanta. I'm wondering, according to LG, do people in colder climates just have to live with error messages 6 months out of the year if that's the case?

I insisted on a service call. They obliged. BTW, the service tech has been extremely sympathetic and professional. I get the feeling he's genuinely embarrassed by LG products and customer service. His first service call didn't fix it. So he ordered replacement parts and scheduled another visit a few days later. That still didn't fix it. He said my only recourse at this point was to call LG and see what they could work out with me.

I called customer service and remained calm, but the person on the other end ("Tish") was smacking gum or food in my ear and proceeded to read a prepared statement about the cold weather causing these issues. I got frustrated and told her that's unacceptable, that a $1000 machine should work top to bottom no matter what, especially 3 months old. And it isn't like I live in Siberia. I live in Atlanta. She got condescending with me (something I've read is not unusual for LG customer service reps). I was still calm, until....she said I was getting upset for nothing. So 2-1/2 hours on the phone with customer service, missed two days of work for service calls, and to her it's "nothing." Not only that, she said there was nothing they could do, and there was nothing they were going to do. She said it was my problem. I have cut out a lot of the terrible exchanges between me and LG. Suffice it to say every call but one was this bad or worse, and nobody wanted to help. By the way, this thing is under warranty until 11/02/14.

Today it just stopped drying altogether. Oh it will turn on. It just won't heat up. Ever. Called customer "service" and have a new error message, "H5." I now have a THIRD service call in a couple of days.

I'm out $1000, have had this less than three months, and the headaches have only just begun. I pray the washer keeps working.

Bottom line: Don't do like I did. Do your homework. Read up on reliability of dryers by all manufacturers, and please take into account how customers are treated AFTER the sale closes and issues arise. If you don't believe me, you can look up something called customer service score board and LG. Read for yourself the nightmares. Look them up in the better business bureau of Huntsville Alabama. I can assure you I'm not alone.

For your sake, don't make yourself their next victim.

UPDATE: 5/6/14

If you google LG TE2 error, you'll find a video of someone who fixed the issue with a $5 part from Lowes/Home Depot. LG never knew about this, or if they did they aren't owning up to the dryer not functioning properly. That small, inexpensive part (dryer vent valve) fixed the problems I've had with this blasted machine. However, despite it working fine now, LG customer service proved to be such a horrific, maddening, traumatizing experience that I'd sooner lock myself in this very dryer and go over Niagara Falls in it than ever speak to them again.

review_title: An incredible upgrade from a top-loader
review_text:
I LOVE this washing machine. Seriously. I finally dumped an 18-year-old noisy top-loader for this sleek new digital wonder and couldn't be happier. To address some of the complaints I've read on this model, first, you don't have to clean any filter daily or after every load. There IS a water pump filter on the lower left corner of the machine which is LG recommends you clean monthly, depending on use. I've checked the filter twice in a month and haven't seen any build up yet. Second, the machine does its best to balance an awkward load of heavy wet items in the spin cycle. If it starts to spin and is too off-balance, it will give up, try to readjust the items with some low-speed spins, and try again. The machine WILL vibrate some as it first starts spinning and the clothes are heavy with water. As the clothes start to lose their water, the spin will even out and become nearly vibration free. Regardless, it is MUCH quieter than my old top-loader.

I actually checked the noise level with a dB meter and compared them to what my old machine used to put out. My old "Lady Kenmore" top-loader would top-out at about 80 dBs, usually during the wash and spin cycles. The LG WM2250C tops-out at 50 dB, while injecting water into the wash drum, or during the first part of an awkwardly balanced spin cycle. As a reference, 50 dB is about the same noise level you'd get in a busy park or face-to-face conversation with someone. I also installed two "water hammer" arrestors on the water inlets for about $15 total from your local hardware store which "cushion" the water column in your pipes as the fast acting valves used in these types of clothes washers inject water into the wash drum. Without the water hammer arrestors, the valves switching on and off (they do so a dozen times during a wash cycle) might produce a loud thud in your water pipes, which is annoying and could cause damage to your plumbing. The water hammer arrestors reduced the noise level during the water injection another 5 dB, making the loudest part of this washing machine an off-balance spin cycle.

The clothes coming out of this washer are incredible. There is much less odor in the clothes from residual soap residue because the rinse cycle is much more efficient and the washer needs much less detergent than a top-loader to start with. Also, the high speed spin option gets the clothes so dry they need significantly less time in the dryer, increasing your utility savings. After drying, all my clothes and bedsheets and even towels feel softer and more supple, with less detergent smell. I am extremely happy with this. The washer also has a handy magnetic door holder which keeps the door semi-closed and out of the way while allowing air to move in and out, preventing mold or mildew growth.

The few drawbacks I can think of are a longer wash cycle (normal cycle with normal soil level takes about 45 minutes) and the fact that you can't open the door at all during the cycle - unless you unplug the washer. I found the silly electronic chimes that the washing machine plays at the beginning and end of the cycle to be annoying, but it was easy to permanently turn them off. Overall, anyone graduating from an old, noisy, inefficient top-loader to this sleek digital wonder will be extremely pleased.

review_text: Beware looking at reviews on LG.com.  They rejected this review, would not post it, and only accept 4 to 5 star, glowing reviews.  I've had my LG washer 5 months.  This is my first front load machine so I don't know if all machines are like this, but every few washes you're supposed to drain excess water out of a drain plug.  If you forget, you'll get a code when enough water is built up and the machine won't run, which happened to me when I set it, walked upstairs and went back expecting to take the wash out only to find out it hadn't been washing.  You need to unscrew this plastic plug out of a small rubber hose and I can see over time this will be the first thing that goes on the machine from constantly manipulating it in and out.  During the initial fill of water, there is a knocking of pipes and although we got 2 water arresters, one on the pipes from the furnace and one behind the washer, there is still a knocking sound for several minutes and I worry what this is doing long-term to my pipes.  I've seen this knocking issue in other reviews.  You also need to wipe down the rubber gasket after each wash to prevent mold and mildew; not a big deal but combined with having to drain this tube, I would consider this a high maintenance machine.  Would rather just "set it and forget it" like the old-fashioned washers and not a bunch of electronic gizmos.  The clothes are not wringing wet when they come out and I have two points of view on that.  Is it because the spin cycle is so good it wrings the water out, or is it because not enough water is going in during the cycle to adequately clean the clothes?  I can't complain about the cleanliness though.  It does a good job of cleaning.  It replaced a Cabrio that lasted only 6 years so hopefully I get more mileage out of this one or I'll go back to the old fill-the-tub kind.  Would I recommend it?  Only if you know up front the high maintenance aspect and can deal with that.

product_title: LG WM2250CW3.5 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
Let me start off by saying this washer is really, really good at cleaning clothes. I've never had whites so white, or towels so fresh, as this thing provides. It's easy to use, and has a pretty big capacity drum, so a weeks worth of my laundry would fit in one load. Amazing.
However, there are a couple things about this washer that drive me absolutely insane. I'm not sure if it's just my particular machine, but here are a few issues I've had:
1) After a few months of use, the washer became very noisy. Not the pump or motor, but the suspension. It would creak and squeak at any change of motion (eg. when the drum switches rotational direction). I opened the washer up and found that the shock absorbers in this machine are completely plastic, and were the cause of the noise. LG had a tech come out and was unable to validate my concerns, even though I told him what I thought it was. He said the suspension wouldn't be a problem unless there was a vibration or balance problem. Which brings me to item #2.

2) This washer is terrible with vibration and balance. Even though it has the "true balance" system, it takes forever to balance loads, and sometimes when it spins you can hear the drum vibrating so badly that it shakes the floors (in a one-story home). Oh, and that causes the suspension and cabinet to be noisy as well, so not only do I have a vibration problem, but it squeaks, squeals, and creaks for the duration of the spin cycle sometimes. Keep in mind my washer has been completely level since day one (validated by LG tech) and this still happens. Replaced the shock absorbers, and while it's not as noisy, the balance problem remains.

3) The stainless steel drum, while corrosion resistant, is stupidly thin, and susceptible to dents/dings. I threw a dog collar and leash in the washer (something I've been able to do with family members FL washers of competing brands with no problems), and the drum got dinged up in many places. Noticeably dinged - it looks terrible. I mean, come on, it can't handle a dog leash and collar mixed with regular clothes?

4) After about a year of use, the motor started getting super loud on spin cycles. It's normally no quiet soul, but now it sounds like a giant vacuum with a high-pitched noise at speed. In addition, the pump has developed a relatively severe rattling sound at startup, which kind of worries me. I take perfect care of this machine, cleaning the pump filter religiously every 20 loads. It should not be doing this.

5) The steel top cabinet for the washer was formed incorrectly from the factory. It is visibly tweaked and is not flat on top. Not dents, but a result of the top being manufactured incorrectly or being the incorrect size.

6) The washer sometimes does not turn on. It takes unplugging and re-inserting the power cord to get it to respond if that happens. I hope it's not a sign of bigger issues with the control board.

As much as I like this washer, and as well as it washes clothes, I'm not going to be buying another one of this brand in the future. All these little things (the noises and electronic quirks) make the washer an annoyance to use. Other people seem to have had great luck with this machine, so I'm not sure if it's the fact that my machine is made in China (this model is manufactured in both South Korea and China) or what, but it definitely has been a less than stellar experience with this washer.

review_title: Both were advertised as excellent machines. While I fully realized they were not ...
review_text: I am writing this review after trying so hard to resolve the issue I was having with my LG washer and dryer. I purchased the matching LG 2250 washer and dryer at the end of 2013. Both were advertised as excellent machines. While I fully realized they were not the top of the line LG machines I was hopeful that they would be longlasting and do a comparable job as the 12 year old whirlpool machines I was replacing. The machines looked beautiful and I chose to purchase the pedastal companions which were outrageously expensive in my opinion. Regardless, I did this because I found the machines too low for comfortable use and it certainly completed the "look". What I found was that the washer was mediocre at best. It never fully cleaned the clothes regardless of settings. In addition, I found the "tub" of the 2250 series incredibly small. Although said to be efficient I ended up doing several loads rather than one large load because the machine couldn't handle the extra clothing. When I tried to do too much laundry at one time the results were horrible. I used high efficiency detergent with the hope that might have resolved some of the issues. It did not. Regardless of the quality of laundry, the most annoying and disgusting aspect of these front loading machines was the awful smell that came from the machines. I called LG numerous times and they told me about cleaning the tub with a special cycle, leaving the door open, cleaning the rubber gasket, etc. I did all of these things over and over. What it came down to is that a front loading machine pools water and the gasket gets mold build up on it. This is unlike top loading machines. Did I mention the dryer would hardly dry anything unless I ran it for more than an hour regardless of the amount of clothes. I checked and rechecked to make sure I had a clear outlet to the roof. review_text:
We've only had this, and its matching dryer, for a couple of months, but so far we love it. Writing this review is almost difficult because it's so easy to use and works so well that I hardly think about it. We always have the TurboWash feature on, and loads are done so quickly that we are often surprised when we hear the end-of-cycle buzzer. There are plenty of cycles and options, so I never find myself wondering whether my clothes are being washed with the right settings. The wash capacity is great--sometimes we start sorting out items from a basket of laundry for the first load, only to realize that the entire basket fits, with room to spare.

The only downside, if it is one, is that water sometimes pools in the ring around the door. We had a front-loader before that had the same problem, so we just left the door open after each load to allow it to dry out. LG thought about this problem, and added a little magnetic plunger on the bottom of the door. It's a little hard to explain, but it basically makes it easy to prop the door open after each load, just enough to allow it to ventilate. From the outside, it's hard to tell it's even propped open, and it provides little enough resistance that you don't notice when you actually intend to close the door.

review_title: Buy only if you love ironing. The end-of-cycle signal sounds like a child's ...
review_text:
Buy only if you love ironing. The end-of-cycle signal sounds like a child's toy and is so feeble, even on its loudest setting, that you can't hear it unless you're in the same room and there is no other noise. Furthermore, when the cycle is done, the dryer just stops, rather than continuing to tumble so that the clothes won't wrinkle. There is "wrinkle care" option that is supposed to keep the drum tumbling for a little while when the cycle is over, but it only turns the drum a quarter-turn once every minute, not enough to stop the wrinkles from setting in. Even worse, the "wrinkle-care" setting inexplicably disables the end-of-cycle signal completely. If you don't want to iron, you basically need to pull up a chair next to the dryer and sit there the whole time.

The dryer also has a special cycle to take the wrinkles out of a dry garment using steam. It shoots steam into the drum alright, but also plenty of liquid water along with it. So when the cycle is over, your shirt will be wrinkle-free but will have one sopping wet sleeve, for example.

It's pretty clear that LG doesn't have a clue about how laundry appliances are actually used. Avoid this brand.

review_title: A fix for the water leak.
review_text:
I’m responding to the review by Mumofmany as air vent was the leaking problem. Thank you Mumofmany!
I bought the same front load LG washer back in 2013. The leaking has been an intermittent problem since then.
I’ve had an LG service tech out to look who said not to fill the detergent higher than the normal fill line. We were sure to fill below that line and still had leaking issues that leaked on our 2nd story laundry room.
I bought the washer and dryer at Home Depot and they couldn’t help me either.
I literally saw water and foam coming out of the air vent in back of the washer toward the end of the wash cycle which is the rinse and spin cycle.

First, I removed the rubber gasket around the mushroom fitting in the air vent but that didn’t do the trick. I put the rubber gasket back.

I bought a 1-1/4” Electrical locknut to secure the connector. I connected the air vent hose to a threaded end of the 1-1/4” pvc plumbing connector to the washer. product_title: LG DLEX5170WSteamDryer 7.3 Cu. Ft. White With Steam Cycle Electric Dryer
review_text:
After my old dryer went I wanted something more reliable, and one with a stainless steel drum such as this dryer right here.

It dries your clothes quickly, but you cannot rely on the timer for when your clothes will be done. The more heavy stuff like thick blankets will have to be done twice, but that's to be expected in a dryer.

The iron function works nicely, and honestly and I have not noticed a single wrinkle in my clothes. I even completely forgot about the iron up until this review. What I don't like is I cannot use two functions at the same time, such as iron and reduce static. For a 'smarter dryer' I would think they would at least allow that much.

The dryer plays a musical tune when you turn it on, and plays another when it's done. It's not really that loud where you can hear it from far away. You will just need to time your loads. If you have bad hearing then I highly doubt you will hear it at all.

The dryer also has this weird alert that says 'Check Filter' even if it's clean. Just ignore the warning and check it before each dry. The warning comes up even if the filter is clean. You can turn the knob to make it go away.

Overall, it's a nice dryer. Also, don't let the picture mislead you... The drum don't actually light up like that with the door closed. :)

My dryer unit ARRIVED defective, and made a very loud hammering noise and vibrations upon cold start from the moment it was turned on for the first time. The vendor I purchased the unit had me contact LG warranty service, or I had to pay for the return shipping in upwards of $300-500 - please note that it seems most online vendors have a similar policy when dealing with an LG defect. The only feasible replacement option was to go through LG warranty service, and LG sent out local warranty technicians three times (one appointment a no show) who could not determine the cause of the problem after taking the unit apart completely several times. The last tech sent out called LG tech support, and they assumed that the problem was with a worn turbine, rubber bushing and a washer that'll need to be replaced. If that doesn't work, they may replace the entire dryer drum that could be dented although it doesn't look dented at all???  wow - how is that a brand new dryer unit was shipped with WORN parts? Doesn't LG QA their appliances before shipping new products? The bottom line is that LG customer support is horrible and full of attitude, and they're completely adamant about their policy that unless a unit is deemed "unrepairable" by their own tech line, you'll get many warranty service visits and parts replacements even with a brand new unit. At one point, they even noted that my dryer noise is normal until I sent them another set of videos to prove otherwise. I've had my dryer for less than 30 days, but it is full of scratches (from the clumsy techs) and I completely regret purchasing it online. Even if the unit noise gets fixed with further parts replacements, the appliance has already suffered quite of bit of strain on its body/motor that probably reduced its lifespan. Do yourself a favor and get it from your local appliance store, and know that LG customer service is rated 547 to 25, a whopping 96% negatively reviewed under Customer Service Scoreboard. I am completely disappointed with LG, and I'll stay away from the brand.

review_text: When we decided to upgrade our washer I scoured the internet looking at review after review for all different brands and types. Immediately I realized that front loaders were out. Why should you have to perform extra cleaning to your washer so it doesn't smell like mildew? Overall this washer is more energy efficient than my old one due to more clothes washed at one time, less water usage and shorter wash times. I also bought the matching dryer which is going strong as well. To sum it all up, for the price compared to many other smaller, stinky, inferior washers I am completely satisfied with my choice.
