product_title: LG WT5070CWWave 4.7 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
Okay, I tried posting this review on LG's website and it was rejected...go figure:

I had this machine installed a week ago, and I've had nothing but problems from day 1. I HATE IT AND WANT MY OLD MACHINE BACK! The salesman is convinced we got a faulty unit because he says this is his top seller and the best machine on the market. He is going to replace it without even sending a tech out. I get another one Friday. I don't have high hopes. But, this is the route to be taken before I can get something else.

Here is what I'm seeing (in no particular order):

1. Unbalanced loads - I've seen the drum knocking HARD on all four walls of the washer and the washer visibly moving across my concrete floor. The washer did not stop, I ran in and shut it off before it could error out. I'm not sure how long it was going to go before it stopped, but I didn't want to find out. I've had issues with this washing jeans and bedding.

2. Water HOG on bulky/bedding, towels and perm press cycles - my tub filled to the rim with water on each load. Loads tend to get unbalanced when the tub is full and the machines remedy for an unbalanced load is to fill the tub and try to balance again. This is rarely successful, especially on the bulky cycle, which tends to wad up the blanket into a ball. Also, pausing the cycle to add a garment seems to override the load size sensing feature and the tub fills to the max. I'm not 100% sure this is what is happening, but it is my best guess at this point. I think this is why the tub filled on the towels and perm press cycle, but I haven't had a chance to try those cycles again.

3. Bleach dispenser doesn't always empty - a cycle ended with it completely full of water. It remained full for another complete cycle and then emptied in the last 5 minutes of the spin cycle. Thankfully, I wasn't using bleach for the first load, or I would have had some ruined clothes.

4. 20 minute spin cycles - I watched a load on the normal cycle spin for 20 minutes??? Really?

5. Waveforce - what waveforce? I have yet to see the washer perform this function like what was shown in the store demo. Oh, and the waveforce functionality is only available on the normal and heavy duty cycles.

6. Clothes don't circulate in the washer. I have watched the same clothes sit on the top of the load the entire wash cycle and rub against the tub wall, completely dry. They do eventually get wet in the rinse cycle, but I don't see how this can be considered "clean". Saw this with a garment bag too. The garment bag remained on top the entire cycle, so only one side of the items was exposed to the friction that is supposed to clean the clothes.

7. The bulky/bedding cycle is in no way efficient, this cycle overrides the load size sensing feature and automatically fills the tub to maximum. I see a huge water bill in my future as I do wash a lot of bedding. The recommendation is to only wash one blanket at a time, so this will really use a lot of water. Also, this does a terrible job washing pillows. I followed the instructions in the manual and washed two queen sized pillows on the bulky cycle. The washer filled to the max and left my pillows floating on the top like a couple of marshmallows in hot chocolate, pressing on the glass lid. When the machine started to swish, I could see that since the pillows were floating so high, they were going to hit on the metal water tray and I was going to have either a ripped pillow, or broken machine. So, I stopped the machine and manually pressed out all the air from the pillows.

8. There is a sticker on the front warning NOT to wash any water-proof or water-resistant clothing in the washer even if the label says it is machine washable. I contacted LG about this and asked if this included things like jackets, snow pants, rain gear, and mattress pads (not the ones with the vinyl back). They essentially gave me a generic response saying the machine can trap bubbles of water during the spin cycle and this can cause serious damage to the washer...WHAT???? Now the salesmen says I should be able to wash that kind of stuff??? I have a feeling this has to do with the recall on the older model.

I don't see how there can be so many positive reviews on this machine. My fears are this machine is operating as designed.

I don't see how there can be so many positive reviews on this machine. My fears are this machine is operating as designed.

review_title: The money I paid was good, but this washer is not.
review_text:
Washer tries to wash a full load of laundry in 3.5" of water. Clothes cannot move about in that little water so they come out with some areas clean and others not. Company says "Oh, it's high efficiency. That's the way it's supposed to work!" The "impeller" (its alternative to an agitator)severely twists and knots clothes, an extra step is needed to untie them prior to tossing washing in the dryer. The washer is placarded against washing any waterproof items, so no shower curtains, no GoreTex rain gear, no shoes, no rubber-backed carpets. If clothes aren't evenly distributed at the end of any cycle prior to spinning, the washer will repeatedly refill with water and agitate again trying to even the load (not so high efficiency). If it can't even the load, it will simply shut down and fail to finish the load. Nice surprise when you come in expecting your wash to be done and you have to start it over. I want my money back and I want a machine that does what it says it will do. I did due diligence and this machine was highly rated, but it is inherently defective. Don't buy it. As you read reviews for it, notice the length of time people have had it before they review. The good reviews are mostly from new owners, the bad ones from folks who've used it a while. It is not just this machine, most of the new HE machines are receiving similar feedback. I have had very few disappointments with a major purchase in my life, but this one is near the top. They took my money and gave me dirty clothes.

So... I was able to return this machine for a refund. I bought a simple Whirlpool machine that lets me set the load size, wash temp, and cycle strength manually. Both it and its companion dryer cost a little less than one-half the cost of this washer and its companion dryer. The Whirlpool should last long enough for the makers of HE machines to work out the bugs and in the meantime, I have $1,000 back.

review_text:

And starting just recently, the spin cycle will run and run for minutes even though the machine says it has 1 minute left to go.

We're calling LG service -- again. This was a very expensive machine to purchase. We're very disappointed. Hope they will make good on the original promise.

review_title: So far so good, but what does this button do
review_text:
I have had this washer for 3 months and have not had the problems some others have experienced, and I hope I never do. It cleans well but is cryptic as to what some of the settings are. "Cold" setting will mix hot and cold to come to a temp around 65.

The "Cotton" cycle uses very little water and this can be not so good for clothes that wrinkle easily. It seems like this is very aggressive and clean clothes very well however.

The "Towels" and "Perm Press" cycles seem to be good all around cycles ans use reasonable amounts of water.

The "Wool" is actually the delicate/handwash cycle.

If I figure out anymore about this washer or have any issues, I will update this post.

review_title: By far the WORST Washer I have ever used
review_text:
This is by far the worst washing machine I have ever used. I have actually watched the wash cycle (through the cool top glass) on several settings, and I can say this with certainty. There is never enough water in the barrel to adequately wash the clothes to get clean. As the tub is washing and thrusting the clothes around, only the clothes on the bottom are even being hit by water. The clothes on the top 2/3 are not even getting wet or hitting the water. Now, another complaint I have is that the clothes come out extremely tangled...all of the time, thus very wrinkled. What does this mean for me...well...for every load of laundry that I wash I have to remember to go into my laundry room about 5-10 minutes after the load has started and push the 'water plus' button at least 2 times in order to feel comfortable that my family's clothing is actually getting washed.
I realize this is an energy efficient machine, but clothes have to be washed in water to get clean. In this washing machine, without adding additional water as I mentioned above, the bulk of the load would not get washed in water. Terrible product, I wish I could get my money back and find another brand.

product_title: LG WT5070CWWave 4.7 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
Probably the worst purchase we’ve made in a long time. We've had this washer for over two months, which is long enough to form an opinion and get to know it. The washer does a great job cleaning clothes and its washing load is larger than our dryer capacity; something we didn’t think about! It was top rated in Consumer Reports. However, as many others have complained on other sites, this washer goes out of balance very easily -- too easily! (Its physically level side-to-side, front-to-back. I checked it three times!) The worst part is there is no audible alarm to tell you the washer has stopped washing! The first you’ll know something went wrong is when you go to do second load and discover the first is not done.

The washer will try to rebalance several times. This entails filling the basket with water and agitating then flushing the water and trying again. This process can happen many times before it gives up completely. This totally defeats the water saving benefits for which one would buy a high efficiency washer!

It seems counter intuitive, but the larger the load the less the chance of going out of balance. The problem seems more common with smaller loads of somewhat dissimilar items. Let’s say you’re washing bed sheets and find a cotton towel you missed when washing all the towels. You add the bath towel to the sheets. That one cotton bath towel will hold more water than the permanent press sheets. When spin time comes, the washer will go out of balance. One pair of jeans with some permanent press casual shirts - forget it.

Even with similar items it sometimes has trouble. I got called out of town on short notice and needed to run a very small load of underwear and socks. Much to my dismay the washer got out of balance because the clothes didn’t evenly distribute around the tub. Frustrating.

I gave the lowest marks for value since a washer that doesn't run to completion 1 out of 10 washes is not meeting my needs and therefore of low value and a continuous irritation. I can’t recommend this washer.

review_title: do not buy! will not clean your clothes
review_text:
We bought this based on the high ratings less than a month ago. I was reluctant to buy LG since it was a washing machine and LG isnt normally the first or even 2nd manufacturer you would think of for washers. We previously had a front-load GEwasher which kept breaking, so no more GE for me.
After installation, we did several loads of clothes. The first loads didn't come out smelling clean at all with just the tide pod, as they had in our old washer, so I decided to add detergent in the dispenser in addn to the tide pod. Ok, now better/cleaner smell, but for some reason, any residue/particles/lint from any previous washed load remains in the washer, then sticks all over thr next load.Very odd.

Then came the white load.
I had a pack of brand new socks. Pulled a couple pairs out, wore them, they got a bit dirty on the bottom from the tile floors. Washed my whites. NO STAINS OR DIRT CAME OUT!! the whites, including my socks, ended up looking just as dirty as when they went in the washer! I did pre-treat one item where my toddler pooped on it, and have since washed it 3x, each time pre-treating in same spot without drying it after, and the poop stain still will not come out using this machine. At first, I thought, clearly I am missing something...so, I read the not-helpful manual. It recommended using the pre-soak button when putting detergent in the pre-soak compartment, which it did not show a picture of, so I figured it must be the same as the detergent dispenser. Trying that still did not get any stains or dirt out.
So, don't be stupid like me and waste your $$$ on a product originally known for cell phones. Buy a highly-rated product from a company who has been making washers for years. Dont buy this one.

review_title: NOT A GOOD WASHER - PROGRAMMING FLAWS
review_text: The washer was delivered on a Saturday and we did our first load of laundry within an hour.  On the very first load the washer filled to the top of the drum with water on the rinse cycle.  We didn't think this was normal so on our second load of wash an hour later the washer filled to the top of the drum on the wash cycle!!  We did a couple more loads of laundry the next few days and the machine was doing the same thing.  I called for service...the service tech came out and said "there was a loose wire" and that he fixed it.  I asked him to stick around for a bit to watch what happens but he was in a big hurry to leave.  We did two morre loads of wash that afternoon and the same thing was happening.  We sent the first unit back and had the exact model delivered about a week later (thinking we got the one-in-a-thousand lemon)...the second washer is doing the exact same thing...over-filling the tub which is using about 40% more water than our old "inefficient" washer.  Also, we noticed that if you use the PAUSE option to unlock the lid for whatever reason during the wash cycle (let's say you want to add something or you want to untangle the clothes) it messes up the water level sensor and the tub will fill all the way to the top.  Sometimes it fills up completely all on it's own (when washing sheets or towels) but using the PAUSE function during the wash cycle will guarantee a full tub of wasted water...and with the clothes floating around in 35 gallons of water in a washer with no agitator the clothes just...well...float around and don't get washed.  Most loads we are having to PAUSE the wash cycle so that we can hand-agitate the cloths just to make sure they are getting cleaned because they are floating on the top of a full drum of water.  The washer will be going back and we will be trying a different brand in a HE top-load before going back to the more efficient "low-efficiency" version.

I am seriously considering deducting the review down to 2 stars

product_title: LG WT5070CWWave 4.7 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
Purchased this at Home Depot about 2 years ago because I loved how it looked. I also liked the extra large capacity.

I use this machine to run 2-3 loads every week. Sometimes 2 load and sometimes 3, depending on my load. I haven't had any mold or odor problems and I haven't noticed any lack of water. If anything, I think it puts in more water than it should because the machine rotates the dry load to sense how big it is. Problem is that rotating the dry load makes the load higher in certain areas, which is why I think I get more water than needed.

As for how well the machine cleans, I don't have any complaints. My clothes come out clean.

There are 3 issues though:
(1) there is always water in the bleach reservoir, which is annoying. After reading a review, I think I know how to clean it out now.
(2) the agitating motion really twists your clothes toghether. It's a struggle getting the clothes out of the dryer because they are all tangled together. This means it's really heavy to take it out as one huge clump. Or, you have to really work at untangling items. I'm good about putting my stuff into washer bags so I haven't had any issues with knit items stretching out.
(3) Lint and other gunk collect along the top rim. I'm not sure how to clean that out because the tub clean cycle definitely doesn't do it.

review_title: Drying sensors are a joke, and clothes don't "toss" properly
review_text:
Now that I've finished bashing the matching washer, it's time to turn my attention to the faults of this dryer.

First of all, the so-called "sensor" is a joke. Don't even bother using them; just experiment with whatever Timed Dry setting does the job for you. When I first got the dryer I set it to Casual, which on my former Duet came out to 36 minutes. Worked fine for a load consisting of one queen sheet set (top and bottom sheets + two pillowcases). Casual setting for the same load in this dryer was "supposedly" dry in 20 minutes (What the..???!!?). Naturally everything was still wet.

Speaking of Timed Dry, this machine does NOT let you choose the amount of minutes that you want! There are only pre-sets, and the only useful (ha) ones are 25 mins and 40 mins. Hello???? My old Duet let me set the exact number of minutes, which usually ended up being 37 for 95% of the laundry that I do. But this machine basically forces to you run it for 40, even if your laundry would be perfectly dry in 35 or 37 minutes.

Ours is stacked on top of the matching washer. Although the pair is absolutely level, the clothes "congregate" at the front door and continually wipe against it during the entire dry cycle. What's up with that??? When I complained to Electrolux they told me that my unit must be perfectly level. Well, my 18" spirit level says that it is. Then they said that this happens with "oversized loads". A pair of queen sheets plus 2 pillowcases is "oversized" for this machine? Seriously?????

Honestly I don't know which is worse, this dryer or its matching washer. They are both a huge disappointment and annoyance. My only hope is that I will have sold this house before either of them breaks or the second-year warranty expires.

product_title: LG WM3470HVATurboWash 4.0 Cu. Ft. Graphite Steel Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: I think Amazon reviewers are being a little hard on this washer
review_text:
I bought this washer a few days ago. I absolutely LOVE it. It's quiet (except for some vibration and "jet engine" noises when the spin cycle is getting revved up, which is a common issue with ALL front loaders which spin 1200 RPM or faster) when washing and rinsing - I can literally hardly hear it at all, and it's right outside my bedroom door in the hallway.

I did a TON of research and settled on this washer as the best compromise of price (in my case on sale for $800), capacity, features, and "Brand Reliability." LG scores well with reliability, although there are some horror stories about some of their top-load washers (see the videos on the #1 ranked video web site - search "LG washer exploding".) Samsung and LG are about head-to-head in reliability and features, although in technology, Samsung might be a bit ahead - they have a washer now with an 8" touch screen which handles all functions and is wi-fi enabled. But it's also about $300-$500 more expensive than this LG WM3470HWA washer.

This is one of the top-rated models according to a well-known consumer testing agency. It also scores well on websites which sell a lot of appliances - you can search for the results yourself.

The washing experience is great. Tons of options when it comes to choosing what cycles to use for which clothes. The 4.0 cubic feet rating means it can wash a LOT of clothes in one load. It has the TurboWash feature which can get a load finished in about 25 minutes, if the soil level is not too bad and you are in a hurry. The 1200 RPM spin speed means many clothes come out virtually DRY. Polyester polo shirts? Practically dry. I washed a thin blanket and it went straight from the washer right onto my bed - just slightly damp.

You want to be cautious if you have this on a second-level-or-higher wooden floor, as the spin cycle can get noisy for people below. There are rubber "vibration reduction feet" you can buy on this website if you need them. On a lower-level concrete floor, you'll be fine.

One other common issue with this washer seems to be "water hammer" problems. With older plumbing, or higher water pressure than normal, this washer might cause your pipes to "bang" or make noises when it fires it's internal water jets during the wash cycle. This can be easily solved with $20 worth of "water hammer arrestors" which can be purchased at most hardware stores, and also here on Amazon. I bought myself a pair of them, since my apartment complex is "older" and I just wanted to make sure this problem did not bother either myself or the neighbors. So far, I have heard NO pipe sounds with the arrestors installed. The go on at the back of the washer, between the water hose and the washer. You can web search and find all this information.

I did buy a 5-yr extended warranty to cover myself in case of problems, but the warranty was very inexpensive. The motor is warrantied by LG for 10 years, the stainless steel tub for lifetime, and all else for 1 year.

I'm only giving this washer 4 stars because of the potential for water hammer noise and the fact that it might not be perfect for laundry rooms on the second floor or above which have wooden floors. As far as performance and how much I love it, 5 stars for sure !!!

product_title: LG WM3470HVATurboWash 4.0 Cu. Ft. Graphite Steel Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Good features, but it will leak eventually.
review_text:
You can read all of the good stuff I wrote when I first bought this below. After five years of light use it started leaking. If you call the LG support line the system will ask you if the unit is leaking (hint: a lot of these units must be leaking). They instruct you to run the tub-clean feature three times consecutively. If you buy an LG front load washer, run the tub clean once a month or it will build up debris that will eventually cause it to leak. Also, I have to replace my unit because it will never complete a towel spin- stops dead and reports unbalanced every time. Service people cannot determine why. My recommendation: Buy a Samsung instead.

One of the first things that impressed me was the load sensing feature. This is not your grandma's washer. The drum is direct drive, so it responds immediately to the electronic instructions it is given. You will see the load turn once clockwise, immediately reverse direction and turn counter-clockwise, and so on as it tests the weight of your load to help it determine how long to run and how much water to use.

This is very efficient- it is not like the old school laundrymat washers that fill with water. You will probably not see any water at all through the transparent door, but your clothes will get clean. I love the fact that you have so many choices. For example, if you want to use cold water your clothes will get just as clean as with warm or hot: the machine just runs it through more cycles.

I was very impressed when I pulled out my first load. I was prepared to heave out the heavy wet towels (as with my conventional top loader) only to discover they were practically dry!

Fairly quiet and smooth running. Just make sure you level the thing and take out the shipping bolts. Oh, and dry the seal with a towel after every use and leave the door open to let things dry out- I hear that front loaders are prone to mold growth if you don't.

review_title: Serious Dissapointment - You think you're buying the Mercedes of washers and you get a Ford Pinto product and service
review_text: I purchased this washer and the corresponding dryer 2 years ago while expecting my first child.  We decided to go with the creme-de-la-crem of washers knowing there would be a lot of laundry in our future.  For the last two years, we have mysteriously had water leaking from below which a technician could never diagnose why.  It was not consistent and enough water to cause major concern so we ignored the problem.  Then last week, when starting a load of laundry in the morning the washer simply died.  It gets absolutely zero power and will not turn on.  I had a non-LG technician come out to look at it and told me the main control board was dead and the cost to fix, a whopping $550 with parts and labor.  I was astonished that a 2 year old washer that was purchased for over $1K required this kind of cost to get it working again.  I decided to contact LG to see what they could do for me.  I never submit reviews but after my experience with this machine and LG as a company, felt compelled to save other people the trouble and recommend they do not buy one.  Their customer service is some of the worst I've ever experienced.  In order to have the machine fixed for $350 through them, I have to get serviced by one of their providers they are contracted with.  They have scheduled, missed appointments and my washer has been broken for a week now with no one to come until 3 days from now (if they actually show this time).  LG has given me the run around, transferred me so many times and no one helps.  We now have a 6 month old baby in addition to our 2 year old and have not been able to do laundry for a week.  I can not even explain the frustration.  I hope if my review even deters one person from buying an LG that I have done a good deed.  Best of luck shopping!

product_title: LG WT5070CWWave 4.7 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
I bought the predecessor to this machine just before it was discontinued a little over a year ago.

Pros:
Get's clothes clean.
We have not had a "smell issue" like we did with the front load washing machine that we "upgraded" from.

Cons:
1. It does have a large capacity - but you cannot necessarily use it because when you fill it - it ties all the clothes together.
2. You cannot wash clothes that are in anyway delicate as it will rip tiny holes into them.
3. My biggest concern - the center cap in the bottom of the tub is made out of plastic. The cap is attached with three tongues that snap into a lip. The fact that the company made this out of plastic is probably the most irritating and poorly thought out design I could ever imagine. If they are not going to put a modicum of thought - what else have they screwed up. After a little over a year - one of the tongues broke off. I bought some underwater welding putty and fixed it. It ran for a month and another one broke off which I repaired the same way. Seeing the writing on the wall - I repaired it and reinforced the remaining one. It ran fine for a month - and broke off just above my reinforcement.

You cannot run the machine without the cap. If you do - the exposed hardware cuts into your clothes. I have called the company - they will not stand behind their product and replace it.

When I pay top dollar which I'm willing to do - I expect quality.

I used to purchase all LG appliances and 55 tv. No more. I just bought a 32 cu/in fridge by Samsung and a Kitchenaid dishwasher. Two sales LG lost because they lost my faith in the quality of their product. We'll see how these companies play out.

Update: They tried to make me get a service call so that they could send a tech out to snap in a cap for me. I rejected the suggestion. Finally they referred me to a parts distributor. Found out from the parts distributor that this is a common problem and that it happens with their front load washing machines too. They fully agreed with me that this is a huge indicator of poor quality. I ordered two so that I can get through another couple years without calling for another "Pulsator Cap".

Good job LG.

review_title: Only owned 1 month, but are very pleased so far.
review_text:
We bought this washer (and its matching dryer) to replace an 11-year old Kenmore (with center post agitator). Our immediate observations have been:
1) The machine is taller than the the one it replaced, by about a couple of inches.
2) It runs very quiet. Most of the time, we can't even tell it's running (except for the spin cycle, which does have a soft-whine that can be heard outside the laundry room).
3) The wash cycle is fascinating. We watched the entirety of the first load we ran through it, from start to finish, through the see-thru lid. It's amazing how well it cleans clothes with a minimal amount of water.
4) We washed the large comforter from our bed. I don't think that comforter has been this clean in years. Same is true for the electric blanket we washed next.
5) The cycle times are a little long. What took 39 minutes in the Kenmore, now takes a little over an hour in the LG.
6) The high-speed spin does a nice job of water extraction. It is also almost vibration-free, once it gets up to speed.
7) The end-of-cycle signal is a catchy tune (not a bell or buzzer), but it is not very loud (even on the loudest setting), so it's hard to hear if you are not within earshot. (The dryer also plays the exact same end-of-cycle tune; I'd have appreciated something different, so we can tell which one is shutting off.)
8) My wife believes that the laundry is coming out smelling fresher from this washer, as opposed to the old one. I haven't noticed this myself, but my wife is more sensitive to smells than I am.
The bottom line is that the clothes are coming out clean, with no damage that we can tell, while using a minimal amount of water. With the much larger tub, my wife does larger and fewer loads. After 1-month of usage, we have so far been very pleased, and have not regretted the purchase.

review_title: Very easily goes out of balance during spin cycle and will tear holes in clothes and towels
review_text:
I bought this washing machine from Home Depot 3 months ago. At first, the washing machine was very quiet and operated without any problems and just in the last 3 weeks I have been having trouble with it going out of balance during the rapid spin cycle. Sometimes I have to re-arrange the laundry several times before it can finish spinning. I would not recommend leaving this washing machine unattended because of it going out of balance. I have been doing laundry for 40 years and I have never had a washing machine this sensitive during the spin cycle. Otherwise, I like this machine because of the large capacity and the ability to control the water level and temperature.
April 19, 2013-After owning this washing machine for about 9 months, I have experienced another problem. It will tear holes in items that are allowed to agitate for very long. I don't know how it is happening but I have washed new sweat shirts and pants just once and they come out with little holes in the material that turn into big holes with repeated washing. I now put clothes into zippered laundry bags to protect them and that seems to work, although it is a hassle. The washing machine mysteriously completes all spin cycles without going out of balance. It somehow corrected itself of that problem. Doing laundry with this washing machine requires a watchful eye. I definitely would say avoid this washer!!

review_text:
This is my first experience with GE products. My parents only bought Sears products during my childhood and for 23 years I have owned Sears Kenmore models, Samsung, and Whirlpool appliances.

This is my second GE washing machine in the past 6 months, and it is definitely another huge dud.

Can you say never again! I originally purchased the GE 3.6 DOE CU. FT. Model GTWN4250MWS (White) stainless interior no agitator bar with matching dryer for $1520.00.

It simply did not wash even a small load (see my review on this model). I washed one t-shirt in the machine and it came out dirtier than when I put it in--I kid you not.

I showed it to the GE tech who serviced the machine, and of course he could not say anything even when he saw it with his own eyes.

To appease me, GE offered me choices. Replace the machines with new machines within a similar price range, or upgrade and pay hundreds of dollars more for their top of the line models.

I chose the match and they replaced the other machines with the GE Washer Model #GTWN2800DOWW, and a matching dryer.

Well folks, apparently GE knows very well they're selling a mechanical mess. The load switch on this particular model gets stuck in position and floods your house--ask me how I know.

I have new construction and it is good I was paranoid and bought flood insurance, and I have a home warantee.

The reset switch is suppose to automatically switch back by itself, but as the tech stated, "Sometimes it gets struck in position and overfills and over flows."

He also found that I needed a replacement part in the machine so we made an appointment for him to return on the Tuesday, and he never showed.

As soon as I get my tax return, I am selling these two buckets to a second hand appliance shop with full disclosure, and upgrading to Samsung or Kenmore.

review_text:
The way to appreciate this machine is to use a High Efficiency top loader for a year like we did. Unless you wash in an area with water rationing do NOT buy an HE machine. After struggling with ridiculous low water levels I put a 12 lb weight in the tub of our new Kenmore top loading HE machine to test the "auto adjusting" water level for a really large load and we only got 8" of water. There is no soak capability because there is not enough water. A NORMAL load only gets 3" of water and that won't even cover the clothing. If you complain about stains, the sales men say you aren't using the right soap and if you tell them you are using the right soap they say there is a lawsuit with your brand. We bought this GE model and gave that machine away.
If you have heavily soiled clothes like a mechanic, wash children's clothing, are interested in washing diapers or work with any body fluid contact this is the machine for you. You have control of the water level, wash time, you can soak with bleach. If the laundry doesn't come out to your liking it is probably YOUR fault with the settings. It is quiet, reasonably priced and the laundry looks and smells clean.

review_text: GE exchanged our HE(High Efficiency) washer GTWN4250DOWS we had recently bought for this model, GTWN2800DWW. The so called High Efficiency model was anything but as it refused to fill the tub more than 7 inches even for extra large loads and even after 4 separate service GE calls.  This is because of the UNIVERSALLY hated "Precise Fill" feature apparently imposed on most manufacturers in an effort to save water. But instead, in many cases it WASTES water as the poor housewife/househusband must wash twice or ADD SEVERAL PALES OF WATER BY HAND. review_title: Free at Last from the Throes of HE Machines - Clean Clothes and No More Stink
review_text:
This basic machine is sold by the big box retailers also with only a change of a couple of letters so they have some sense of exclusivity. For all practical purposes they are the same. GE offers one of the largest 3.9 cu ft conventional washers now available. The offer an HE model, an EnergyStar model with agitator, and they offer the nonEnergyStar conventional machine which actually has some more desirable features than the more expensive brethren.

This machine has been the beginning of a new and better life at our house.

We installed a new LOW efficiency clothes washer with as big a tub as we could find and all mechanical dials -no electronics - complete with manual temperature controls and with no electronic override on hot cycles which often tempers even HOT cycles to only 110 deg F washes. Our still-youthful, very large deluxe main brand HE washer has been relegated to basement storage -after draining all the stagnant water out of it which HE machines cling to in between washes..

You may read that this model is noisy - it is not. It is quieter than our old HE, which also played a symphony depending upon the stage of the cycle - very irritating. So unless you have your washing machine installed in the den right next to the TV, you may not even know it's working.

Does it fill the tub? Oh my - on LARGE load setting it fills to within a couple of inches of the top of tub-very satisfying.

Is hot water really HOT?-yep, just like it comes out of the heater. Likewise, warm is warm, cold is cold. How about that?

We had already decided we wanted a very large machine, so a 3.9 cu ft was the one for us. Over the last six months our family has bought three GE 3.9 cu ft machines. One was an EnergyStar rated for a rental property. No complaints from the tenant on that one. My son-in-law spoke highly of this nonEnergyStar model. He had replaced a deluxe HE machine which smelled and needed sanitizer regularly, whose pump broke down three times, and which yielded dry, unwashed clothes sometimes on the BIG wash cycle. The dirty little secret (not so secret anymore) about HE machines is that most of that large stainless steel drum goes basically unused on the wash cycle, therefore the big numbers for size are misleading....and they hold onto significant amounts of old rinse water in name of efficiency which sits and festers waiting for your next load of unmentionables Remember that the next time you wash clothes contaminated with lawn and garden chemicals, oil and gasoline or other work related substances.

So, I was leaning toward the GE 3.9 EnergyStar Model. Then, I met a lady at Lowe's who was trading hers back in after a few weeks. To Lowe's credit they were allowing her to do so. She said that the agitator only turns very little, that it would not fill very much with water and the water never reached a high temperature on HOT cycles.

Some research told me that she was right on two out of three counts. A GE spokesman wrote online in a reply to similar complaints that the EnergyStar machine tempers hot water to a maximum of 110 deg. F. One can culture bacteria at 110! GE also says that some of the same models may have a problem with the manual override not allowing it to fully fill the tub-hers must have had that problem. The third complaint about the agitator; I took a chance on that. It does turn slowly and quietly but it thoroughly agitates the clothes, if there is enough water.

Worried about durability? - Buy the extended warranty. The price is already very competitive at most places. No machine is going to last like the old 40 year-old Maytag your grandmother used..or is still using.

I now enjoy the pleasures of fresh smelling towels and sheets, and jeans that actually get clean....and the wife not complaining because the cycle is lasting too long, and about large loads coming out with dry unwashed spots, and having to use Afresh every couple of days to keep the machine from smelling like an open sewer. Sometimes progress is stepping back a bit and finding something that works.

product_title: GE APPLIANCES GTWN4250DWS, White
review_text:
I, like so many others, was horrified when my washer finally died after 22 years. After reading all the reviews, virtually no washer available got what I considered really good marks, even those that were well over a $1,000. Consumer reports is starting to get silly on this environmental stuff so they didn't even review washers with agitators. Geesh! Amazon is starting to be more and more reliable and is quoted quite often by reviewers with the advantage of being able to read each review. After balancing reviews, costs, and using a little common sense, I decided to go with this washer.

First thing everyone needs to understand, these new style washers do not fill with water. When the wash cycle starts, the wash basket spins slowly while water is sprayed onto the garments, thus soaking the garments. You need to place the detergent in the washer before the wash starts since there is not enough water to disperse the detergent in the same manner as the old washers. I think that is what is worrying so many people...it's just different. There are also separate dispensers for bleach and fabric softener; I have used the one for bleach and it worked beautifully.

Reading the manual is a must because it really lays out what exactly the washer does and it's easy to manipulate the settings to do what you'd like. There's even a setting for just blue jeans. Or, you can override everything and just do long washes filled with as much water as the machine allows...but I doubt the wash would come out any better. Also a big plus, most regular loads have come out really, really dry. It's almost bizarre of how rung out they are and it has cut down on drying time. It is also very quiet...at least compared to our old machine.

Of course, I have no idea how long this washer will last but it has really exceeded my expectations. I honestly am very surprised at how well this washer works. My only advice for reading reviews on these new washers is realize they use much, much less water and spin really fast so complaints that are the results of those two realities, like clothes being twisted due to the fast spin, you almost have to ignore.

This is a very, very good washer and the price makes this thing a best buy, in my opinion. I honestly couldn't be happier.

We use so much less water now I am shocked. Now, for me, I'm not that big on the ecological stuff as I find most of it to be misleading. However, if you want to use less household water, this washer has made a significant difference. If water conservation is a concern, then this is a good washer for that reason alone.

review_title: The Worst Washing Machine Every Designed.
review_text:
My machine was purchased from Lowes on December 14, 2012. Lowes finally delivered it on January 4, 2013. The following comments are offered after using it for the past 2.5 months.

1. No matter what load setting is used on initial start, the machine will not put in more than a few inches of water. It requires either filling with a bucket or recycling through another start cycle. If you recycle by pushing the "Stop" knob, it will beat the clothes with inadequate water resulting in torn clothes. It is best to unplug the machine instead of pushing the "Stop" knob.

2. If using the hot water setting, the water comes in VERY slowly (water pressure is sufficient and screens are clear) and will not fill to the required setting. Again, either unplug it and fill with a bucket or cycle the timer through the start cycle about 3 times until sufficient water level is assured. The GE repairman came and stated the machine is designed to assure low hot water flow during filling. Someone should inform the designers of their incompetence.

3. Any time the machine is turned off, the agitator will whip the clothes violently. If no one is watching to assure an adequate water level is present, damage to clothes is highly likely. DON'T EVERY LEAVE THIS MACHINE UNATTENDED!

4. When water empties at the end of the wash cycle, it does not spin out the dirty water and soap. This results in retaining a large portion of the soap and dirty water. Therefore, the rinse cycle is immediately contaminated by an unnecessary amount of dirty water.

5. When the rinse cycle begins, the tub will only fill to about 20% of the required rinse water. If left unattended, this results in more clothes damaged due to agitation with very little water. The rinse cycle, again, requires either filling with a bucket or cycling the timer enough times to assure there is sufficient water in the machine.

6. Since the machine failed to spin out the dirty wash water, it is necessary to start another wash cycle in order to properly rinse the clothes. Without this step, the clothes remain dirty because they were never rinsed in clean water. This extra wash cycle requires the same monitoring and manual addition of extra water to prevent destruction of clothes.

The process of washing a load of clothes takes about 1.5 hours and the machine must be constantly monitored. If the above was the intent of the GE design team, they need to seek other employment.

A positive comment: The machine looks like a normal top-loading washer.

review_text:
After owning this horrible GE washer for 22 months, and having it repaired three times already, I bought a new Frigidaire washing machine today to replace this maddening, unreliable, horrible machine.

It doesn't matter what price you find this machine at, even if you find it on the side of the road with a "Free!" sign on it, don't take it, unless you are a GE repairman yourself, because you will not be able to depend on it.

Speaking of GE repairmen, I am on now a first-name basis with the GE repairman in our area, who was at our house four times in the 22-month lifespan of this GE washer. The control panel had to be replaced...twice. Now the transmission is dead; standing water in my machine, wet clothes, can't get it to spin. Third time in 22 months that I've been without a washing machine, even though we paid good money at the big box store for this GE washer, did I mention it was 22 MONTHS AGO??

And even when the machine is working, it does NOT clean well. Cat hair, dirt, the smell of perfume and deodorant -- all those things would still be on my "clean" clothes when I removed them from the washer.

Long story short, now that the transmission is dead, and the service people tell me it will be SEVENTEEN DAYS before a repairman could come!!!!...enough!! Enough! I'm sorry I ever bought this washer, and sorry I spent money on a useless service contract, and I'm done.

Even though I still have seven months left on the service contract for this 22-month-old GE washer, this aggravation and being without a washer is SO not worth it. I got in my car, drove to the neighborhood appliance store, not a big box store, and bought a Frigidaire washing machine. Goodbye forever, GE, and thanks for absolutely nothing but grief, piles of dirty clothes I can't wash for my family, trips to the laundromat even though I own a washing machine, tears, and tearing my hair out.

Recommendation: Absolutely not.

review_title: Easy hack to fill it 3 holes down from the top with water:
review_text:
Got this machine a few days ago via the Thanksgiving promo.

So far it seems alright, will keep my fingers crossed. It is more quiet than the previous very basic GE washer that we had. Also, the clothes are spun to a drier state, thus faster drying time.

A lot of people don't like that it never fully fills with water. While on Super the water seems to come up about 5 holes down from the rim. Now, this is not all it can do. While playing with the settings, I've figured out how to fool it to get as much water as it can, which is about 3 holes down from the rim.

The sequence is the following:
1) start some wash with the water temperature you desire, and wait for it to fill the drum a bit
2) cancel the wash by holding the button for 3 seconds
3) start the wash again by pressing the button
4) if it starts draining, press the button for 3 seconds immediately, to cancel the draining
5) start the wash, it should start filling, and this time it will fill up to how much the sensor can take

I've had the water setting on "Large", and it filled the drum to 3 holes down from the top by doing this sequence which it should not have had done for "Large".

Consider this a manual override for "special" occasions. For having to do this silliness I've taken 1 star off.

review_title: Update, good washer with a few quirks . . .
review_text:
Just bought this GE model. It seems to be washing just fine, the clothes are very clean, smell good and are spun quite dry. However, we are noticing a really odd smell coming from the machine, especially during the spin cycle. It does not seem to effect the clothes. Difficult to describe, the best I can come up with is a sort of industrial chemical smell. Also the unit makes a loud clunk when it first starts and some other odd noises throughout the cycles. It is not quiet compared to my last machine, but if I close the laundry room door, it's fine. I wonder if anyone else had the funny smell and if it is something that will "wear off" in time . . .

Update, May 2014 - the machine washes the clothes just fine, and spins them SUPER dry. The smell did eventually disappear. If it goes into spin cycle and the clothes are off-center, it makes a UBER LOUD!!! HORRIBLE NOISE!! I mean, it sounds like something just crashed into the house! I make sure to use to sheets/towels or jeans option if I'm doing a heavy load, that seems to help. I have found that I do use the automatic fill setting more than I thought I would. Even though it looks like there isn't enough water, the clothes still come out clean. I can tell by the sound now whether I need to go move the knob to add more water. I like that it still has the extra rinse option, the new machines no longer have that. Overall, very satisfied.

review_text:
I had read several bad reviews of this machine but bought it anyway because I don't like front loaders ( can't open after cycle starts ) and I wanted a simple agitator as opposed to a drum that shuffles around to balance clothes and not a machine that takes a couple of hours to run through a cycle. So far it has worked fine. When I use the auto load setting I use HE detergent since the machine uses less water - and use regular when I set the water level. Either way my clothes get clean. It's true that the water does not fill all the way up on super but it still fills with more water than my old Maytag, since the drum is bigger. The only thing I have noticed is that when I use the auto load and am washing a small amount of clothes, there is more than enough water than needed really - as opposed to when I fully fill the drum with clothes and the clothes are barely covered ( which is okay, since that's the way the HE is supposed to work ). Maybe there is just a minimum amount of water needed for the machine to run?
The spin cycle is loud and my clothes come out pretty twisted on the regular cycle - but much drier than before.
Basically I am pleased with this machine.

review_text:
It breaks my heart to say this about a GE appliance, but let me count the ways I hate this machine. First of all, let me mention that my grandparents bought GE appliances. So did my parents (my dad worked for GE for years). I continued the tradition, and my daughter’s first appliances are, you guessed it, GE. I proudly own GE stock.

First of all, the washer doesn’t use enough water. The clothes come out a tangled mess, and I have actually had some that were torn to shreds. So now I am forced to sit by the washer and wait until it stops filling. Then I add enough additional water to make sure that the clothes can move freely and won’t be destroyed.

The PerfectTemp feature obviously doesn’t work as intended. The warm water is way too hot, the “colors” setting makes it too cold, and when I use the hot setting, it apparently thinks my water is too hot and adds cold water.

Oh, and don’t make a mistake and start a load on the wrong setting. Just this morning, I started a load of colors, and forgot I hadn’t changed the setting from my previous load, which was delicates. The washer was ¾ full, I changed the setting, and the washer drained. It drained. Along with all the detergent and additives I had put in. HUGE waste of money literally down the drain.

If you accidentally lift the lid before the washer stops spinning completely, the drum comes to a screeching halt. This can’t be good. There should either be a lock on the lid to prevent it from being lifted to soon, or some sort of indicator light to let me know when it’s safe to do so.

The additional settings are on dials instead of buttons, so it makes it difficult to choose the options I want for each load. I find myself choosing one or the other for things like a second spin, auto soak, extended spin or power rinse for when I use fabric softener.

I do like the fact that the agitation is much gentler than most machines I have owned, and that it has a way of redistributing the load to avoid the spin being off balance.

The dryer it comes with has a few flaws as well. Drying large items such as blankets, sheets and quilts is a chore, as you have to stop the dryer about every 10 minutes, remove the ball of tangled items, and then redistribute them (it) to make sure the inside of the “ball” gets dry. Otherwise it works fine, and if I use the auto dry setting, it drys normal loads completely the first time, on any temperature setting.

All in all, I would return this pair if I could. As it stands, I’m stuck with them for the next 10 years or so, which is about how long any major appliance lasts these days. I’m still a fan of GE appliances, but next time I’ll be much more choosy when I shop for a washer and dryer.

product_title: GE APPLIANCES GTWN4250DWS, White
review_text:
UPDATE - FINAL REVIEW

Here is my actual review of this washer. I did go out the next day after writing the "pre-review" and bought the washer and matching dryer. Writing the pre-review convinced me to go ahead and get the set.

First, I must amend my comments about this not being a HE (High Efficiency) washer. It is a HE washer but lacks the locking lid so it can't be called HE.

The locking lid is a necessary safety feature because the tub spins at 700 rpm during the spin cycle which is really fast. The lid on HE washers locks until the spinning has stopped to avoid injury if someone were to reach in while the tub is still spinning. It would take off a finger, a hand or even an arm. It's dangerous. I'm giving it a 5 star rating with the understanding that it can be a dangerous machine. Believe me, I don't even think about opening the lid during the spin cycle. I don't even open it during the wash cycle. (Opening the lid during the wash cycle aborts the wash cycle, empties the water from the tub and you have to start all over.)

Also be sure that you use only HE detergent and use it sparingly. This washer doesn't need the usual amount of detergent.

I expected the controls and settings to be baffling at first and they were. Eventually I got the hang of them and I hardly think about the settings now. It's a moderately steep learning curve. The learning isn't helped by a poorly written instruction booklet. It's basically a generic set of instructions that cover about half a dozen models similar to this one. I've read them so often that they are dog-eared.

The controls give you a lot of choices and flexibility. What was surprising was the number of settings for water temp. There is "cold only", then you have about 2 or 3 settings of slightly warmer water, then you have warm and hot. You have many settings for wash cycles but eventually you'll mainly use the Color, White and PermaPress settings. It also has LEDs on the control panel that light up to show which cycle the washer is in. Nice touch.

The clothes are very clean and nearly dry when they come out of the washer. I can wash a very small load, I've even washed a single item on occasion. On the other end of the scale, I tried washing a comforter (single bed) and it came out beautifully with no protests from the washer. I'm doing more laundry than before and my water bill is actually a bit smaller. This really does save water.

I think the most important issue is to be sure the washer is perfectly level. My installers did a good job and I later re-balanced the washer. The high speed of the spin cycle demands that the washer be very level. If it's out of level, it will make loud noises and "walk" itself across your floor.

I've used the washer heavily in the time I've owned it and it has operated beautifully. Just beware of opening the lid while the tub is spinning. Bottom line is that this is a wonderful machine. It cleans well. You add soap and softener first, then add clothes, set the controls and push Start. Then you walk away for an hour or so and the clothes are ready for drying. Washing is almost fun.

I've not said much about the dryer. It's more conventional and does a fine job of drying quickly. Just be sure to clean the lint filter after each use. Cleaning the filter allows the dryer to dry clothes quickly and with the least amount of power. It also prevents lint buildup in the exhaust hose, which causes fires.

Thank you, Ed

====================================================

PRE-REVIEW

I'm seriously thinking about buying this machine but haven't actually purchased it yet. This is a "pre-review", not one of a washer that I own. At least I don't own it yet.

I've noted in many of the reviews that people think this is an HE (High Efficiency) washer. IT IS NOT an HE washer.
It is an Energy Star rated machine. Energy Star means that it meets certain standards to reduce energy and water used to operate the machine.

An HE washer takes energy efficiency to a much higher level. HE is much more automated, takes longer to cycle, makes noises not usually associated with washers and uses a different method of washing and cycling than a traditional machine.

Neither is it this washer the washing machine of just a few years ago. True, it does use less water. Using less water is one of the requirements of attaining an Energy Star rating. If this makes sense, then you'll see that there is a big difference in Energy Star rating and an HE rating.

Interestingly, the reviews of this model on Amazon are largely negative. In comparison, the reviews on Home Depot are just the opposite. They are mostly positive. I take both the bad and the good with a grain of salt. It's telling to me that there are 578 reviews on the Home Depot site with an overall rating of 4.0 stars of a possible 5.0 stars. There must be something good about a washer where almost 600 people agree that it's a fine washer.

I suspect that a lot of the negative reviews were related to not fully understanding how the machine operates. It has electronic controls which give you a very wide choice of settings and all of these choices can also be confusing. Also, since it has to conserve water in order to get the Energy Star rating, it "looks like" there is not enough water in the tub to wash clothes properly.

Again, I read in a number of the positive responses that the clothes came out very clean and the users were happy with the results.

As I said, I'm seriously thinking about getting this machine. One of the local dealers is offering it for under $500.00, delivered and installed through 3/26/14. This the best price I've found. It's a machine with many good selling points. For me, the stainless steel tub and the generous 3.9 cubic feet of capacity are pluses. The Energy Star rating is another big plus for me. In addition, it features lots of cycles and variations on the basic cycles and I like the 700 RPM spin speed (drier clothes out of the washer). Another selling point for me is that the cycle times are substantially less than an HE rated washer. I also like that I can customize the washer to wash just as I want it to. The bottom line is that it seems to give a lot of "bang for the buck". It's a good value at this price.

I rated the washer with only four stars because I don't yet own it and have had no experience with it. I'll return with a followup review after a good trial of how it works. I may just earn a 5 Star rating.

Thank you.

review_text:
GE Washer Agitator Tangles clothes, "catches" straps, strings, and buttons - ge hydrowave washer
Initially, I loved my new 2012 GE HydroWave quiet agitator washing machine. But, turned out, lots of things get caught on or under the agitator. Buttons get caught. Straps, like on tank tops or underwear, get caught. Strings like the ties on sweatshirts get caught. Clothes get tangled up together, and since it's deep and the clothes are wet, it's hard to remove these things from the machine. When the buttons on a jacket were caught under the agitator, thought it was going to tear the clothing. Would never have gotten that machine if I knew that would happen. I've washed clothes weekly for 40 years in all sorts of machines, and that never happened. What's wrong with this model, and how can this be corrected? Is it possible to get a new agitator part that doesn't do this? Has this machine been recalled? There are sorts of hook-llke slots at the base of the vanes that things get caught in--obviously a faulty design--and there's room under the base for buttons to slide into. Solutions, please, or I'm going to ask for a replacement model. I can be reached at ShinerFamily@earthlink.net

I not only blame myself for not doing my research before buying but also the dumb Government and the lazy GE engineers that just took a regular non HE washer and just programmed with less water on the rinse/spin cycle without thinking about the consequences to customers like me which are beginning to hate badly designed machines with poor quality, no wonder the US is loosing to foreign made machines. How sad.

review_text: I'm very happy with this washer so far. I have yet to try the "auto load sensing" feature (which may be what others are complaining about with the water levels being low?), but when choosing small, medium, large, extra large or max settings it washes our clothes just fine (even with the abundance of dog hair usually present on our clothes). I also washed our Queen sized bedspread in it and was happy with the results. We decided on this model after our front load washer died at only 2 years old (top load models seem so much more reliable because there are not so many electronic features). After some research we had it narrowed down to this model or one from Sears. This washer won due to the quicker delivery time listed. Which brings me to my reason for the 4 star rating instead of 5…. This product lists a delivery time of approximately 1 - 1.5 weeks. After you purchase it you get an email from the company stating that actual delivery time is 1 - 3 business days of processing time + 7 - 10 business days of shipping time. I was a little bit annoyed that this didn't match what Amazon said, but I thought, "that's still pretty fast." 2.5 weeks later I was emailing the company for an update, and 3.5 weeks later our washer was finally delivered. I felt very mislead, and wish the seller would update their delivery estimate to something more realistic. So if you're in need of a washer quick, don't believe the timeframe listed. product_title: GE APPLIANCES GTWN4250DWS, White
review_title: Computer programming flaw: You have to have unusually high water pressure for it to fill up
review_text:
I bought a house with this washing machine in it. It was filling with a thimbleful of water no matter what setting I put it on. I had to do tiny loads. I was freaking out over this lemon and thinking that with the "high efficiency" it was designed to not be able to wash.

Then, reading these reviews, I see half and half that it fills up great versus that it doesn't fill and uses a thimbleful of water.

I went through troubleshooting it as if it were broken. And, I got it to fill with water. Anyone who was told by a repairman or company employee that this won't fill up and that that is how high efficiency machines work had a dud repairman or General Electric employee lie to you. This washer is supposed to fill. However, it has a computer programming oddity to where you need to have high water pressure for this to happen. It allots a certain amount of time for filling up, and if the washer isn't full, the washing machine just turns water off and goes into the wash cycle without ever waiting to fill up completely. You can see in reviews, some people say it fills up great. Some people say it won't fill. That's probably a difference in their water pressure.

Anyway, here's how I fixed mine.

Mine was filling up to the bottom few dots along the side. It would fill with maybe 3 or 4 inches of water in the bottom no matter what setting I put it on.

I first started from the view that maybe the pressure sensor had gunk or build up in it, since I got the washing machine about 6 years old. The pressure sensor is something in every washing machine that has a tube and water goes up the tube and raises air pressure in a bubble at the top of the tube and when the pressure is too high, the washer knows it is full and stops filling with water. You never want to take that thing apart, because if you mess it up, then your washer can not know when it's full and can overflow. What I did is ran a load with a gallon of vinegar added. Vinegar dissolves hard water deposits. Mid load, I lifted the lid and left it open to leave the vinegar water sitting in the machine. Next I ran a load of plain water. Next I ran a load with a half gallon of bleach added. Bleach dissolves cotton and human hair. So, I figure between the two of those, that will dissolve most gunk. The plain water in between is because bleach and vinegar together will make chlorine gas, so you want to clear all the vinegar before running bleach through and vice versa. After I did that, the washer would fill up to about half way on hot water wash, but still just a few inches on cold water wash. (Both vinegar and bleach will damage rubbers, so this is not something you would want to do on a maintenance schedule. Once in a while is no big deal, but doing this regularly would be a bad idea.)

I disconnected the hoses, and tested running water through them by connecting them to the garden hose spigot outside to make sure water was flowing. The hot water hose was to where it would shoot water across the yard. The cold water hose was more like a faucet tap, so flowing freely but not spraying. This made me think that there was hard water build up inside the hoses. (You want to replace your washer hoses every 5 years anyway, to prevent risk of them popping and flooding your house.)

I got new hoses. After connecting the new hoses, the washer fills up about 3/4 of the way full if I do "Super" wash. That's the most water I can get the machine to fill with with my water pressure, and the water pressure is totally fine in the house. I know for sure that the washer is supposed to fill up to two dots from the top of the drum when it's on "Super" wash, because if I start it going, then spray a garden hose in along with the washer fill, the washer will cut off water when it gets to two dots from the top.

What is going on with this washer is this: The pressure sensor (measures how much water is in the machine) is only talking to the washer to tell the washer to turn water off at the end of the fill. The washer has some kind of timed cycle where step 1 is a combined fill and soak. If filling up takes longer than the preprogrammed allotted time for fill and soak, the washer doesn't wait until it's full. Instead, it just moves into a wash cycle with too little water. So, if you have any kind of lower pressure water at going into the washer, then it won't fill up in time. You have to increase the water flow into the washer. The washer will recognize when it's full, and cut water off to not overflow, but if the washer is mostly empty, it doesn't care and just goes "time's up, time to go to the wash cycle". For me, connecting new hoses worked to get a satisfactory wash, but I don't have enough water pressure in my house to actually fill it. (And like I said, water pressure is not at all a problem in my house.) My only option would be to use an actual garden hose (with a bigger hole in the middle) as a fill hose, and that would be risky in case of rupture since washer hook up hoses are intended to hold lots of pressure for years, but a garden hose no one cares if it pops and they aren't designed to hold pressure for years and years. My washer is in a garage where all my stuff is up on shelves with feet, so flood is not a big deal, but in a room in a house, I would have no way to get more water pressure, and even in the garage I really can't risk it. It's a really bad design flaw with the washer - that thing were it starts the cycle after a set amount of time whether or not it's full with water. Like I said, I don't have any water pressure problems, and I can't get it to fill to where it is supposed to for a "super" wash. By increasing water pressure the best I could, I wash able to get a big improvement. I hope that helps anyone wrestling with this lemon. It's not as bad as a high efficiency machine that simple won't fill, but if you don't have super high water pressure, it may as well be.

By the way, when it comes to high efficiency machines and water use, the EPA had new regulations kick in for personal use machines in both 2016 and 2018 to where now they really can't use water. This machine couldn't be sold after 2016. This machine, the GTWN4250DWS, is the "good old days". It's not a good machine, but you can't buy a new one that is better. You have to get used. The EPA allows about 1 and 1/2 times as much water to be used for commercial machines, and if I hadn't been able to get this working, I would have bought a Maytag Commercial or a Speed Queen TC5000 (reversed the changes in 2018 where Speed Queen tried to do a fast wash cycle and the machines from 2018 just weren't cleaning). If you want clean, you have to repair the older machines like this one, or else you have to get a commercial grade replacement (which the government allows to use more water). Washing machines got regulated to where even though this GE washer is a lemon for computer programming and not especially well made, it's better for cleaning than anything you can buy new for under $900.

Honestly, the house this came with - the family that lived here had 4 kids, and I have 4 kids, and this was made in 2012 and now it's 2020, and it seems to work just as it did the day it was new (ie. badly unless you have super high water pressure). I think it probably was an OK machine, but I wish that GE would have fixed the computer programming to where it would check and make sure it was full before starting the cycle, and that GE employees had not just lied to people and told them that "this is how high efficiency machines work" when the bad computer programming caused problems.

product_title: LG WM3070HRATurboWash 3.7 Cu. Ft. Wild Cherry Red Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Get ready to love doing the laundry - REALLY!
review_text:
Ok, so I didn't think I'd be so thrilled that I'd actually be writing a review for a washer, but, nonetheless, here it is! This is the first front load washer I've owned and I can say that I will never go back to a top load again. The short list consisted of this washer and a Samsung. The Samsung I was looking at had PowerFoam as a feature, but was a little over $700 more than the LG. To be fair, that washer was a 4.5 cu. ft. size as compared to the 3.7 cu. ft. size for the LG. I'm sure the Samsung washer would have been a great washer; I liked the idea of PowerFoam. However, I'm a family of three and so the 4.5 cu. ft. load capacity wasn't really something we needed. 3.7 is more than large enough for my family's needs. Also, as cool as PowerFoam sounded, I liked the idea of the Allergiene cycle that uses steam to remove 95% of common household allergens. My wife really suffers with her allergies and I really liked the fact that this wash cycle could help mitigate some of her suffering. The SpeedWash, TurboWash and ColdWash features were also big selling points. Couple that with the Direct Drive motor (as opposed to pulleys) for the movement of the drum and I was satisfied that I was getting a washing machine that would more than satisfy my needs. So in considering this machine and the Samsung, I very quickly realized that while both machines were quite good, I would be almost able to purchase both the LG washer and dryer for the price of just the one Samsung washer. As a side note, the smaller capacity Samsung washer (the one that would be more comparable to the LG I purchased) did NOT come with the PowerFoam option, so in a more apples to apples comparison, I feel the LG washer outshines it's similarly equipped/sized Samsung competitor.
With regards to performance, this machine is the best I've ever owned. I had high expectations, but I was also somewhat skeptical as to what a front load washer would really be like. I was sure it would wash clothes and that it would do a good job, but would it really be a noticeable improvement over my old top loader? YES! If you've been on the fence, time to move. I do not regret this purchase at all.
I've had the LG for about a week now and I've used it daily. First, the machine is extremely quiet during operation. Our laundry room is located in an open nook just off of the kitchen. There is no door to close to dampen the noise. Prior to this, we'd always have to adjust the TV volume accordingly when washing clothes. The only real intrusion I've noticed is during the initiation of the spin cycle. During the actual washing cycle, I don't even hear the machine. It doesn't intrude in conversation or TV viewing. It's amazingly quiet. Don't get me wrong, you can hear it if you choose to attend to the noise, but it becomes so innocuous in the background that it's easy to forget the machine is even running. Of course, once you hear it's end of cycle signal, you remember you had clothes running! Once the washer is spinning, it returns to very quiet operation, too. I just notice the difference when it moves from the wash cycle to the spin. And that's really if I'm even listening for it.
Since I'm speaking of the spin cycle, this washer does not walk all across the laundry room floor either. It's very stable and has not even vibrated the floor, house, windows, etc. even once - not even a hint of vibration. Given that front load washers can spin at some pretty impressive speeds, I was surprised by this. The TrueBalance system on this machine is definitely impressive and effective!
With regards to performance, I was thrilled at the difference between washing in the top loader and this LG. This LG replaced a Maytag that, at the time of purchase, was a top of the line washer. I nicknamed the Maytag the Washing Dead because it refused to die. It was 16 years old and still going strong. It was undoubtedly a relic. The agitator was a pain when it came to washing comforters. I can't begin to count the times that a small load would get out of balance and the machine would just stop until I manually balanced the load. Sometimes it would get out of balance and quit again within 5 minutes. This was annoying, but if I was home it wasn't a big deal. This would be a problem when I'd set clothes to wash when we were leaving. It was never a good feeling to come home only to find that the machine hadn't finished the job. Say goodbye to that problem. This machine completes the job every time.
After several loads of clothes, I can say that my clothes feel cleaner. I could tell the difference with the first load of clothes I washed. However, because I didn't want to chalk it up just being excited about a new appliance, I waited several days to make a judgment. I have no doubt that our clothes are cleaner with this machine than they have ever been. Things just "feel" cleaner and on a deeper level, too. Another plus is that my clothes are not being beaten up by the agitator any longer. That means that clothes will look newer for a longer period of time. A front loader is just going to prolong the life of any garments washed in it. Another thing that amazed me about this washer was how dry clothes came out of the washer. I'm used to jeans dripping wet coming out of the old Maytag. That's a thing of the past. This machine spins as much water out of these clothes as possible and with such effectiveness that it reduces the amount of time (and therefore energy) needed to dry the clothes. That's a win-win scenario in my book!
There are a multitude of programs and cycles available in this washer and I don't believe any of them are gratuitous. In a little over one week, I've found that I've used a great deal of them. About the only consideration I gave with my other washer was hot, warm or cold and then moving the slider to correct position for the size load of clothes I was washing. That's about it. With this machine, I can wash small loads or bulky loads. I washed two full sized comforters at the same time and still had room to spare. I've loved the ColdWash cycle and have found it to be just as effective as the warm wash cycle. I've used the Allergiene cycle and my wife commented that her sheets, pillowcases, and comforter never felt or smelled better. While there are a myriad of options available for washing, I have not found any to be gimmicky or unnecessary. I can see a use for all and have already used most.
I purchased the matching pedestal to go with this unit and I highly recommend it. It brings the machine to eye level and eliminates stooping down to load or unload the machine.
All in all, I'd buy this machine over again in a heartbeat! It's been one of the best appliance purchases I've made in years! The dryer that goes with this washer is also amazing and I have reviewed that as well. My wife and I both love the Wild Cherry color. It sounds awkward to refer to such a mundane appliance as sexy, but nonetheless the red is just that. It pops nicely against our mocha paint in the laundry/kitchen area. So not only is this unit visually stunning (again - hard to believe I'm talking about a washing machine and not an exotic car with such jargon!), but also incredibly efficient and effective. While the options are numerous, a quick read of the instructions manual or PDF online will have you up and running in no time. The automatic dispensing of HE detergent (liquid or powder, but I recommend liquid), fabric softener, pre-wash, and bleach takes all the guess work out of cleaning your clothes. I've found the pre-wash to be very effective at helping clean some of my red clay soiled jeans. I also got some dark cherry juice from cherries on a white t-shirt out without a trace. I didn't get a stain on the shirt intentionally, but I figured this would be a good litmus test for how efficaciously the washer cleaned clothes. It worked like a champ!
When they first released appliances other than TVs, I was skeptical of Samsung and LG. I once remarked, I don't want my refrigerator made by people who specialize in TVs. I can honestly say, I have been proven wrong. I would have no qualms buying a refrigerator or washer from either company. The highest compliment I can give LG is that they completely exceeded every expectation I had for this machine. Nothing feels cheap at all about this machine. It is truly a fantastic washer and, for the first time ever, everybody in the house wants to do the laundry!
