This machine completes the job every time. After several loads of clothes, I can say that my clothes feel cleaner. I could tell the difference with the first load of clothes I washed. However, because I didn't want to chalk it up just being excited about a new appliance, I waited several days to make a judgment. I have no doubt that our clothes are cleaner with this machine than they have ever been. Things just "feel" cleaner and on a deeper level, too. Another plus is that my clothes are not being beaten up by the agitator any longer. That means that clothes will look newer for a longer period of time. A front loader is just going to prolong the life of any garments washed in it. Another thing that amazed me about this washer was how dry clothes came out of the washer. I'm used to jeans dripping wet coming out of the old Maytag. That's a thing of the past. This machine spins as much water out of these clothes as possible and with such effectiveness that it reduces the amount of time (and therefore energy) needed to dry the clothes. That's a win-win scenario in my book! There are a multitude of programs and cycles available in this washer and I don't believe any of them are gratuitous. In a little over one week, I've found that I've used a great deal of them. About the only consideration I gave with my other washer was hot, warm or cold and then moving the slider to correct position for the size load of clothes I was washing. That's about it. With this machine, I can wash small loads or bulky loads. I washed two full sized comforters at the same time and still had room to spare. I've loved the ColdWash cycle and have found it to be just as effective as the warm wash cycle. I've used the Allergiene cycle and my wife commented that her sheets, pillowcases, and comforter never felt or smelled better. While there are a myriad of options available for washing, I have not found any to be gimmicky or unnecessary. I can see a use for all and have already used most. I purchased the matching pedestal to go with this unit and I highly recommend it. It brings the machine to eye level and eliminates stooping down to load or unload the machine. All in all, I'd buy this machine over again in a heartbeat! It's been one of the best appliance purchases I've made in years! The dryer that goes with this washer is also amazing and I have reviewed that as well. My wife and I both love the Wild Cherry color. It sounds awkward to refer to such a mundane appliance as sexy, but nonetheless the red is just that. It pops nicely against our mocha paint in the laundry/kitchen area. So not only is this unit visually stunning (again - hard to believe I'm talking about a washing machine and not an exotic car with such jargon!), but also incredibly efficient and effective. While the options are numerous, a quick read of the instructions manual or PDF online will have you up and running in no time. I can honestly say, I have been proven wrong. I would have no qualms buying a refrigerator or washer from either company. product_title: LG WM2650HRASteamWasher 3.6 Cu. Ft. Wild Cherry Red Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
We bought the LG Front Load two years ago - my husband's impulsive Black Friday purchase. Two years into it, here is what I can say:

1) The machine starts out by doing a test spin to determine the volume of laundry, and adjusts the water supply accordingly. However, there have been times when that machine was FULL, and it still showed only two bars for fullness (instead of three). Consequently, I have washed an entire load of clothing, only to take it out and discover that the clothing in the middle of the load was BONE DRY.

2) It leaks. It leaks little tiny river trails from the bottom of the lid. This can be annoying.

3) The spin cycle on it is RIDICULOUSLY unbalanced. We leveled the unit per the instructions, our floor is level, etc., but when the spin cycle kicks in, the entire house shakes. I've learned not to do laundry when we have people over, otherwise, our guests get scared thinking there is an earthquake.

4) Speaking of spin cycles - sometimes, for no apparent reason, it just doesn't drain all of the water. I guess that is why they have a separate "spin" you can put the setting on. The manufacturers must have known this happens.

5) This is the only washing machine I have ever owned that requires regular maintenance to keep it from getting gross. In no time at all, the inside rubber gasket rim gets full of gross crud, as does the inside of the clear lid. On a traditional top loader, I would have to clean the inside lid maybe once a year. On this thing, it really needs to be cleaned once a week or more.

6) Speaking of gross - don't make the mistake of leaving the lid closed when not in use. You will come home to a stink factory. This is particularly annoying, if, like me, you like your laundry room buttoned up and tidy. But nope, gotta keep that big old door hanging open. This leads me to wonder, if a simple closed door can breed so many organisms that the entire laundry room will smell, just how sanitary is the entire unit? You know, a unit designed to make things clean?

7) Speaking of clean - clothes come out OK, but not stellar. I was expecting stellar from all of the advertising LG had been doing on these machines. The only way for me to get clothes as clean as I prefer is to do a prewash, a stain cycle, and an extra rinse.

8) The large capacity is misleading. At full capacity, the clothes do not come out clean at all. At half capacity, the clothes come out okay.

9) Additional annoyances: The writing on the buttons started to flake off after about 6 months. Really, LG? Really? The cherry red coating on the plastic components (like the soap dispenser drawer) started melting off after about 6 months also, meaning each time I open that little drawer to pour in the laundry soap, my fingers get coated in red melted goo. Note: this drawer needs to be cleaned out regularly, too!

10) Positives: It looks nice with the red. The accompanying dryer is AWESOME and FAST.

11) Bottom Line: After noticing that my drain pan was full of water this morning, I just couldn't take it anymore. We are moving this set into the garage and buying a Kenmore or Maytag top loader set.

product_title: GE GFWH1200DWW 3.6 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
We wanted a front-loading washer because we like the performance of the front-loader in our previous house, and we like the feeling of using less water and getting cleaner clothes in the bargain.

First Impressions

I am impressed! This washing machine has a lot of button and lights and at first glance one can be intimidated by the controls. However, the "GE GFWH1200DWW" makes most of the selections for you depending on what setting you chose via the rotary dial which includes the following selection: Whites, Colors, Sanitize, Delicates, Speed Wash, Drain + Spin, and Basket Clean. There are push button controls for "Soil, Spin and Temp" with a wide range of selection, however these are made for you automatically depending on your rotary dial choice.

You are free to change them of course, but I have found that letting the washer chose the setting for me tends to work best. So controls that once looked intimidating aren't and washing a load is just a dial setting away.

GE recommends using only High Efficiency (HE) detergent with the GE GFWH1200DWW and we settled on Tide because it tends to get our cloths cleaner. The detergent dispenser is situated on the left hand side of the washer and has a compartment for detergent, fabric softener, and bleach. The compartment is removable and good thing since the fabric softener compartment tends to fill with water after each wash and needs to be emptied.

The GE GFWH1200DWW is fairly quite though you know when the door is being locked or unlocked. Speaking of which, the washer can be paused during the wash cycle to permit to adding of additional cloths; the start button is actually a Start/Pause button.

Conclusion

With its 3.6 cu. Ft. capacity, the GE GFWH1200DWW can and does swallow a lot of cloths. The average wash cycle last 1:25. We opted for the optional pedestal/ storage unit and I'm glad we did because it raises the washer off the floor to just the right height where we do not have to bend over to add and retrieve clothing.

Overall I (we) are quite pleased with the "GE GFWH1200DWW Front Load Washer"; it does what it is supposed to do with minimum fuss and at the end of the wash cycle and alarm will sound at 1 minute intervals until you come an retrieve your wash. Nice touch GE. And while I would have preferred another color, blue, or red perhaps, the white is not unattractive, and it gets the job done.

If you are looking for a sub-$1000.00 front loading washer ($839.00 at Amazon.com believe it or not; they sell everything!), the GE GFWH1200DWW should be on your list.

product_title: Frigidaire FASE7074NWAffinity 7.0 Cu. Ft. White Stackable With Steam Cycle Electric Dryer
review_text:
I purchased this electric dryer from the local appliance store. It was recommended by the staff sales associate assisting me. I had a few requests: auto sensor for moisture, large capacity for a comforter or load of towels, steel drum. The associate informed me this was an excellent machine as it has a large sensor along the back wall of the drum. I had nothing but stress with this dryer! It was inconsistent in drying-- part of the load remained damp, a load seemed crispy dry, and so on. One day to test it properly, I spent five hours doing laundry. I varied the materials-- cotton, poly blend, heavy cotton/denim-- as well as the amount of the load and the different dryer options. Each time some of the clothing remained damp. I would then place these items back in the dryer for a 2nd time. After 10-15 minutes, I stopped the cycle to check and the items were crispy dry. Yet, I was the one who stopped the cycle! So much for the auto moisture sensor!
The local appliance store did not make it easy to return. There was talk of paying for a service person to assess the problem, to assess the duct system and length of the vent run, and so on. I decided to exchange, minus the restocking fee, and try out a GE electric dryer. I am so very very happy with the GE dryer. I love it.

review_title: Most expensive mistake in a long time, purchased July 2013
review_text:
This washer (note the matching dryer is great) is one of the worst investments I have made in a long time. Aside from the delivering dealer's service being absolutely horrible, the machine has been a constant irritation from day one, and warranty service has not really improved things. The machine imbalance is terrible. Warranty service determined a "bolt" was missing from the balance assembly (it was just a large screw), which seemed to improve things somewhat. The machine has been "leveled" to death, but just the flexibility of the Samsung pedestals and the cushion of the rubber feet seems to be enough to allow for incredible vibration at high speed, and the machine literally rocks while clunking at lower spin speeds with any load size. It is so bad that I don't know if this balance part is still working or not.

The amount of water to fill is usually inadequate. Any fabrics that soak up water such as towels, sheets or jeans, the machine will only put enough water to make a damp-to-wet ball that thuds back and forth. Synthetics are the only clothes that don't abrade in enough water for more of a sloshing action. I use He detergents by the teaspoon in order to get adequate rinsing with an extra cycle, and the cold-only rinsing makes things worse. Bleach is dispensed only 7 minutes before the end of a wash cycle, why I have no idea.

If I had the chance to do it over again, I would not follow test organization ratings in choosing a washer, but get a machine where users have stated they can get around problems by having more manual settings such as load size to overcome some of these bizarre behaviors. I would never recommend this machine period, much less on any floor but concrete. I would insist on more than a 30-day return policy, no strings. I would demand being able to purchase an extended warranty after the 30 days, when you realize the machine will probably vibrate itself to oblivion. The only plus, wherever you are in your house you will know when your load is done, no need for the chime at all!

review_title: Stay away from this Samsung Product
review_text:
While we own three excellent Samsung HD TV's this is perhaps the worst appliance we've every owned by any manufacturer.
It stopped working after only five weeks of light to moderate usage. The error message displayed was NF- not filling. After trying various fixes suggested by Samsung's repair center, they agreed we needed a service call.
The technician determined that the problem was not with the product but that we had high water pressure. When questioned on the plausibility of this answer, he changed his explanation to too low pressure. Telling a consumer that the cause of a problem with a washing machine is due to water pressure is like telling someone that their TV is not working because of fluctuations in the electric grid. One can only assume that in a multiple story building, water pressure probably is different on the 1st floor as compared to the 10th floor. Stay away from this machine if there is any chance that your water pressure does not meet the standards Samsung has set for this machine. We would actually give this product a zero rating if we could.

product_title: Samsung WF457ARGSGR 4.5 Cu. Ft. Onyx Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
I read the first and only review on this product and I can almost guarantee that reviewer doesn't even own one. First, the "smell". It's a new product. I didn't notice any smell. It's probably the smell of the Home Depot he checked out this washer at. As for parts not lasting - I'm not sure where this person came up with that one. I would like to read some more details about his/her experience on these unreliable parts. Third, expensive parts. This is a premium product. It's like buying a Mercedes over a Chevy. But to be more realistic, appliance parts are expensive to begin with. I've never heard anyone say "wow, the part for my washer/dryer was dirt cheap!".

Now for the review itself: We upgraded both the washer and dryer with the Samsung products and couldn't be happier. The number of options and modes that it allows you to chose when washing clothes is just unbelievable. The touchscreens are huge and very visible. The washing/drying is extremely quiet. I actually had to go back a few times to check if the machines were even on because they were so quiet! The ability to connect the units to wifi and your smartphones is an added convenience. You have the ability to control the units via inside the house using your smartphone or in a remote location. Some people may say this is a stupid idea but realistically, it's an added "convenience" and for some, they will benefit greatly from this feature.

I plan on writing another review after a couple of weeks to see how things hold up. So far, so good. I couldn't be happier with my purchase. It's quite surprising how far washers and dryers have come even from 5 years ago.

Update (09/13/2013): Still loving the washer but discovered a big oops on my part. I threw into the washer a soaking wet towel. When I mean soaking wet, I could have squeezed about 2 cups of water from it. Anyway, I put it in the washer and just left it there for a few hours without running it and long and behold, the washer leaked the water out and onto the floor. Now, before you see this as a flaw: Front loading washers have a huge mold problem. Fortunately, this washer has not had that problem. So the keep the washer mold free, it has to "open" everything up inside to let it breath. With that said, if I were to dump a bucket of water into the washer without it actually being on or on wash mode, the washer itself wouldn't know and the water would leak right out. So this is totally not the washer's fault. It was my stupid mistake. Who leaves a soaking wet towel in a washer anyway? Right there you're already asking for mold/mildew problems.

product_title: Samsung WF457ARGSGR 4.5 Cu. Ft. Onyx Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
I bought the washer dryer pair almost 2 years ago (looks exactly the same, but slightly different model number). I have been very pleased with it. I was hesitant to purchase a more expensive high efficiency washer because I wasn't sure if the gentle motions would clean as well as a normal cheap washer. Well it has cleaned everything I have thrown at it, and the flip side is that my expensive clothes have barely faded at all. This has saved me hundreds of dollars on clothes because I work in an office and have to dress professionally. This is in addition to the noticeable drop in my electric bill (my electric company sends weekly emails with usage charts and I no longer see spikes during the hours when I do laundry).

One family member who lives on campus about 1.5 hours away will bring her clothes here just to avoid using the conventional washer at her campus apartment. The reasons she gives include the Samsung being more gentle on her school clothes, she doesn't like to hear the noise of the washer in her apartment, and she likes the "Sanitize" feature for her medical scrubs.

The only negatives I have are that I use the gentle/delicate cycle when washing the expensive clothes, but it forces me to use the low spin speed which extends the dry time slightly. At the same time, the dryer automatically shuts off when it detects no moisture so there's no extra dry time compared to my old dryer that ran until the timer finished. Also, when drying my king size sheets they sometimes ball up even with the "Bedding Plus" option. If I don't check and unwrap them, the center of the ball will still be wet when the cycle finishes.

I did have one scare in the first few weeks. The washer worked but it would accumulate a pool of water when sitting for a couple of days. I called and Samsung sent a technician. It turns out it was because the Best Buy installers barely opened the water valve. It's not intuitive, but he said it was because there was no water pressure. All he did was turn on the water valve and was on his way in a couple of minutes--it was under warranty so he didn't charge me anything. I have had ZERO problems since then. I did learn that the Samsung support was very courteous and professional, but I was left wondering why they couldn't have suggested opening the valve over the phone?

review_title: Real review of the dryer and it's great after a year of use still
review_text:
I don't think the other reviews were even for this specific product, just a general dislike of LG products. We, however, do have this exact dryer and thought we would give actual feedback on this specific product.

We've had this for a year now and we have not had any problems. We do laundry a few times a week because of a new baby, and the washer that goes with this dryer has been great for us (we wrote a more detailed review of it).

The dryer has been working just as well. My favorite features of the set are the load sensing it has, the washer can sense the load size and weight and the dryer can sense the water content and adjusts the time on how long it needs to dry. For this to work properly though, you need to choose the correct material you are drying. If you have nylon or spandex and choose the general cotton, it will not correctly sense the water content and the timer will not be right for it. If you do choose the right one, there shouldn't be a problem.

There is also an option to do a quick fresh-up dry option that I use when I'm too lazy to iron my wrinkly piece of clothing, works pretty well. And then there are other extra options galore, which are helpful when you have something very delicate or intricate. You can change the heat as well as the time manually if needed.

We make sure to check on the obvious parts if they need maintenance and haven't had any problems. Love the dryer and washer. We hope our review helps you in your decision!

product_title: LG DLEX8000W 29" Electric Steam Dryer with 9.0 cu. ft. Mega Capacity
review_text:
This review is largely in response to the previous review bashing the dryer.

I purchased this dryer based on Consumer Report's recommendation, 9 months ago. We have 2 children in the house, and it seemed to me that the larger the washer and dryer the fewer times we'd have to do the laundry. Be aware, it's _very_ large. My brother in law asked me what laundromat I stole it from. We have had absolutely no issues with the dryer - it seems to have rock solid build quality, and to be very well engineered.

It's impressively quiet for what it does. For maybe 15 seconds after starting it makes a bit of noise, but, then quiets down. I'm not sure why or how it does this.

The dryer does a good job drying clothes, and our comforters, with exception of our 1 king sized comforter. The washer will wash it, but, the dryer leaves it damp. I believe this is a limitation of dryers that are meant for residential use, there is just not enough space for the air to circulate with the dryer 80+% full.

With regard to the other reviewer's mention of the "customer service scoreboard" - I did actually look at this, and, noticed, every company that makes dryers has >94% negative reviews... You must keep in mind that people only contribute when their experience was bad - good experiences rarely seem worth praising - the device has already required a call in to customer service after all.

And, with regard to the other reviewer's dryer being broken: almost all complex devices show a U curve failure rate - a bunch of failures when they are new decreasing to few failures for most of the normal working life, increasing failures when they get old. I will agree that not having the option to have your dryer replaced is a pain, however, even local stores won't pick up big items for free - at least that's what I found buying my lawn tractor from a big box store. And, it weighs 180lbs - not exactly something you can throw in the back of your sedan and return.

review_title: Reasonably fast and large capacity dryer.
review_text:
I bought this thing from Sears to replace an old standard top loading washer and dryer after the washer developed a leak. Not very happy with Sears, due to some mixups in the delivery, but once I got the jumbo washer and dryer installed and running, it just about blew my mind. Between the extra capacity (~2 times more than my old washer) and faster drying (~1 hour instead of 1.5 hours) I think this pair processes my laundry 3 times faster. The extra options and efficiency are nice, but the speed and capacity are what really amazed me and differentiate it from the competition. I also really like the clearly audible and pleasant song it plays at the end of the cycle. Way better the *brrrrr* noise my old dryer made.

The only downside is that the drum doesn't drain away bits of hair or the occasional ball of lint as well my old washer. A quick wipe down between loads resolves the issue.

I can't speak to the customer service issue accept for the fact that JD Power put LG just below Kenmore Elite (also made by LG) in their 2013 washer and dryer rankings. The closest competitor is Samsung (also Korean BTW). There are just a couple of other brands that come even close, though Meile is absent from the list (maybe they didn't interview enough Meile owners).

product_title: Electrolux IQ Touch White Front Load Washer and ELECTRIC Dryer Laundry Set with Pedestals EIFLW50LIW_EIED50LIW_EPWD15IW
review_text:
Okay, I really hate to bash a product, but this washer is a piece of misery.

Bought a washer dryer set late November 2012. The washer developed a major leak in the first month. Given my personal circumstances at the time, I insisted that the local vendor (a nice independent store) replace the unit. They did. 7 months later the 2nd washer starts to make a loud noise whenever the drum spins, which is quite often in a front loading washer. I recorded the problem with several short movies on my cell phone, then looked for an authorized repair service.

There are only 3 authorized service repair facilities in all of Southern California for Electrolux. That should be a clue. The YELP reviews on all of them were horrible, so I picked the closest one. The first technician they sent watched my video but incorrectly diagnosed the problem. I waited a month for the part he'd ordered to arrive. It didn't. I asked the service shop to send another technician. This fellow took one look at my videos and knew immediately that the problem was with the bearings. They were failing. So he orders the two big expensive parts to effect repairs. Now the real fun starts.

The relationships between Electrolux and the authorized repair shops is best summarized as fraught. I've learned more about it then I care to or should ever have to know. Since early August, I've had at least 20 conversations, including emails and conference calls, between the repair service and manufacturer. This has gone on for over two months and is not resolved. The repair service is required to purchase the replacement parts through a vendor, usually Marcore. Marcore doesn't have the parts in stock. Electrolux does, but will not sell them directly to the authorized Electrolux repair service. Go figure. The local repair guys have to spend extra to acquire the parts from Electrolux through Marcore, and they aren't happy about that. The tub assembly that arrived was damaged in shipping so it sits in my garage until someone comes to fetch it. A second tub assembly has come and is also sitting in the garage. The box looks suspiciously bashed up but I'm not going to touch it until the repair man gets here. The other part, outer basket, has yet to make an appearance. It is supposedly in Florida, but I haven't seen it or a shipping order for it. These parts get shipped directly to me, the consumer, not the repair shop. That means being here to accept delivery and having room to store the 3 foot square boxes. The repair won't get done until both parts are on hand.

Like I said, the problem is still not fixed. But once it is done, effectively the washer will have been rebuilt. That's not encouraging. If you've ever had a car go through a major accident and repair you know it is never the same. I've got my doubts about what will result from this repair.

When I did my homework on washers, I liked the Electrolux for its size and appearance. It's still big and looks nice, but right now, that doesn't cut much slack against the miserable customer service and poor quality. Oh, and the soap dispenser dish doesn't drain (the cup is always full of water) and there is always a crust of soap in the cup after the wash cycle is complete. Yes, I use HE soap in the correct amounts.

Furthermore, both the local shop and Electrolux have chastised me for not buying an extended warranty. Call me old fashioned, but I rather thought that a washer costing over $1000 should work at least for a year or two. I certainly did not appreciate being made to feel guilty for not purchasing the extended warranty.

Maybe you will have better luck then I have, but I would still heartily recommend not buying this machine.

product_title: Electrolux IQ Touch White Front Load Washer and ELECTRIC Dryer Laundry Set with Pedestals EIFLW50LIW_EIED50LIW_EPWD15IW
review_text:
Not to discredit the first review with 1 star... but you can read 1 star reviews on literally every single washer made and the service after the sale is the key to this. I have been using a top of the line set of Maytag Neptune front loaders for the past 10 years. While they would get the job done, features were slowly failing. The sensors in the dryer quit, the tumbler bars were coming out, the washer seal was failing again, the LED panels were dying, etc.

We shopped this model from several local stores before deciding to look on Amazon. Who knew you could get large stuff like this shipped so quickly and for so much less than the store... Setup was easy if you have any skills whatsoever. Reversing the doors was not as easy as the last few machines I have done it on, as it had more steps involved, but it was straight forward. review_text:

"If it were not for the one problem that I had with this machine I would have given it 5 stars. It does an excellent job of cleaning the clothes and has a large capacity. It is also very quiet. The problem is that the dryer damaged the clothes due to a badly designed seal between the rotating dryer drum and the stationary front pannel. Small buttons (the ones on the front of button down shirts) and drawstrings (like on sweat pants and hooded sweatsherts) get caught in the unsually large gap in the front seal. The repair technition that came out and looked at my machine was VERY supprised at such a large gap. When he called back to where ever he called they told him that there had only been one official report of this type of damage to clothes. The fix for the issue was to tilt the machine backwards. He did this and so far I have not had any more damaged clothes. However, in my opnion this should only be a temporary fix and I am hoping that GE is redesigning the front seal and will issue a recall to fix the machines already in service. Tipping the machine is not a fix for a design flaw. Also, the installiation instructions state that the machine should be level for operation so I don't know if the tilting will cause damage to other parts of the machine (like the washer) over time. The loads that had damage to my clothes were a small load and a medium load so the dryer was definitely not over loaded."

This is 100% accurate, please keep in mind of this issue. I have yet to try the tilt thing, but I hope this works because I can't continue to deal with damaged clothes.

So I decided that since my 13 year old Kenmore Elite dryer finally went, I'd get the matching dryer.  I have been using it for about a week and am very happy with it.  The steam feature is great, especially if you have a tendency to not take your clothes out of the dryer immediately.  The LED touch screen is great and the cycles include anything you'd want or need in a dryer.  You can adjust temperature from high to no heat at all.  There is also an eco-boost to help save energy and an efficiency scale right on the front that tells you if you have the most energy efficient setting in use.  I am very happy with this dryer and would highly recommend it.

review_title: Worst appliance I have ever owned.
review_text: Worst appliance I have ever owned.  Where to start…  First of all, it doesn't get the clothes clean, and actually, often they come out of the dryer even dirtier with caked, dried-on lint (and yes, I clean the lint trap between loads every time).  Secondly, it is ridiculously slow (both washer and dryer).  Third--and this is one of the most annoying things--the presets on the dryer don't every get the load all the way dry, and your only other choices are "60 minutes" and "90 minutes."  The fact that there is actually a 90 minute setting is a sign that this machine is crap--a regular load on a decent machine should take no where near that long, even a load of towels.  The washer was very quiet the first time I used it, I'll give it that, but after a few uses it now makes a horribly loud, metal-on-metal noise every time it goes into spin cycle.  OH--the spin cycle--another problem.  You cannot select just a spin cycle.  The only selection available is rinse-and-spin, so if the clothes for some reason don't get spun out well (and this happens a lot), you cannot select to just spin it again only.  Save your money!  Don't buy this awful appliance!

review_title: My washer tried to kill me tonight.
review_text:
I have this unit, it was a Christmas gift from my Dad a few years back. I had been without a washer dryer for a real long time. I was super happy to no longer have to run outta underpants. I've had this machine for a little less than 3 years. It's always made horrible noises on the spin cycle and shook my entire house but aside from that it did the job (and kept me from having to use my towns super creepy laundrymat.) I do have to pick the lint off my clothes when I fold them. I clean the trap after every cycle. I have two cats so I'm very conscious of that. Tonight after almost 3 years, my washer part just stopped doing anything productive. It melted a few items including it's self and produced a small electrical fire. Yea! My house smells horrible, my remaining clothes are sopping wet and there is 2 feet of water inside the washer that won't drain. Good news though, the dryer part still works but I've been drying the same load of clothes for 4 hour.
I'm also in the process of moving to New Orleans. This is the very worst possible time for my washer to try and murder me, my clothes and our two cats. Based on the other reviews here, going through customer service will be an all day process that I don't have time for. Super happy that I have an excellent smeller or this review would be a heck of a lot more depressing.
Edit: finished my 5 hours of drying and everything in that load is now blue. My socks are blue, my shirts are blue, my gray leggings are blue, my bras are blue. I just can't even, this is a disaster. I'm 35 years old, I know how to properly do laundry. This is not human error. Half my closet looks like I'm sheltering smurffs.

review_text:
.
We've had this about 3 years and find it a big improvement over our 1998 Kenmore washer.

- - - Energy Savings - - -

The EnergGuide label shows it to cost $15/year with a gas water heater...only a few dollars per year more than the best front loaders (see Note 1 for more EnergyGuide data). (If your water is heated by electricity, the cost difference is greater.)

In our area (San Diego) it qualified for rebates from the power company and the water company... $135.

- - - Noise - - -

It's not quieter than our old Kenmore, just different. The spin cycle does remind you of a jet engine...but a really high quality jet engine, and not an offensive sound.

- - - Controls - - -

The controls are organized and mostly sensible. You can rotate the knob to one of 7 settings, or select your exact preferences with push buttons (water temp, short/long cycle, spin speed, etc.) The pre-set selections don't quite line up with our eco-desires, so we work the buttons before each cycle. You can program (save) one custom cycle to your own wishes, which is nice.

Most of the "normal" soil level (wash time) selections result in a 52-57 minute cycle.

- - - Setting Confusion - - -

There is some confusion over settings which I find annoying and inexcusable. What's the difference between "Tap cold" and "Cold"? Between "Warm" and "Eco warm"? It says the "ColdWash" setting is for small loads only (8 lbs max), but it does not explain why. And does that also apply to manual selection of Cold or Tap Cold? Or just to the cycle enacted by the special ColdWash button? None of these reasonable questions are answered in the 32 page manual, or anywhere.

Come on, LG, it's 2013. The information age. We're supposed to care about energy efficiency, and you've spent millions of dollars engineering an efficient machine. But you can't explain what each button does, or what the trade-offs are?

The owner manual is clear and complete on many things, but they should have finished the job.

- - - Shopping Tips - - -

Our local Sears store had all the machines plugged in. Nice, if you want to check out the controls. Our salesperson at Sears knew a lot more about the machines than the reps we got at Best Buy (maybe random luck).

The 35-page owner manual can be downloaded from the LG site if you want more details.

- - - Top Load - - -

After years of front-load mania, top loaders seem to be getting more popular again. It seems much easier to load and unload. Larger door, no stooping, no hide and seek.

- - - Cleaning Effectiveness - - -

I don't know. According to Consumer Reports (August 2013) this model is "Very Good" but not as good as the best front loaders.

- - - Capacity - - -

The drum seems huge. The stainless steel part is 22" diameter x 17" high (no agitator in the middle). The total drum is 21" high (probably not all usable).

- - - Details and Overall Quality - - -

This machine feels like quality. Shock-absorber feet...beautiful stainless steel drum...dampened lid hinges (lid closes gently when you let go of it).

- - - Pricing - - -

This model goes on sale for $600 at all the major outlets every few months (free delivery, free haul-away). Check camelcamelcamel for a look at price history (hit the Best Buy tab). Amazon merchants can't quite match this, apparently.

- - - Notes - - -

Note 1: EnergyGuide label:

- Assumes 8 loads per week, 10.65 cents/kWh electricity cost, $ 1.218 per therm gas cost.
- $24 yearly operating cost with electric water heater (lowest model is $10, highest is $71)
- $15 yearly operating cost with gas water heater
- 225 kWh/year electricity use

~~~ Comments & questions welcome ~~~

product_title: LG WT4870 4.5 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity Top Load Washer Featuring Powerful StainCare Te, White
review_text:
When our 10 year old kitchen aid washer went out, I was shocked to learn that the new washers had no agitators and the door locked and they used much less water. So my husband and I started researching washers, reading dozens of reviews and asking everyone we knew about their washers. We learned a lot and decided that this LG washer/ dryer was the best value for the money. We have had it for almost 2 months now and have been very pleased.
It cleans well and is very quiet. The loudest part is when the water enters or exits the tub. We both enjoy listening to it and often leave the utility room door open so that we can. We never did this before... I know it sounds weird.......but it is just cool hearing what sounds like an airplane ( a quiet one) take off in your utility room and the melody played at the end of a cycle!!!!
A few recommendations: 1) read all installation instructions before installing and follow them. 2) make sure it is level and on a good solid floor (it does spin very fast). 3) after washing, pull the detergent dispenser out to release trapped water and leave lid open for a while to dry out and avoid smelling. We have not had this problem but some reviewers said they did and i want to avoid this. 4) place clothes around the center in a balanced formation and put in similar items per the directions, towels and sheets really don't work well together. 5) if you are buying the washer go ahead and buy the dryer because they are most efficient when used together ( and look great too).
And best of all, 6) Be sure to check with your electric company for rebates on new high efficient energy appliances. Ours offered a $100 rebate on this washer. We bought ours on sale at Sears, picked it up and installed ourselves and received the rebate. So we feel we got a great deal and a really high quality product for the money. Other washers with similar features were $300-$400 more.
Best wishes!

review_title: Bought as a set with Dryer
review_text:
I wanted to wait to review this until after I used it for a month or so. I read the reviews on this set prior to purchasing it and I'm glad that I did.

Many seem to not like the extended wash time so I was prepared for 1 1/2 hour cycle. However, I found that the increased space that this machine offers equals 2 and maybe 3 loads of my old unit. This means I'm still saving time because instead of doing laundry 3 X per week I'm only doing laundry once.

I love the direct drive and how the spin cycle really spins out the water. This equals less drying time.

One thing I used to like doing is to set my machine and let items soak and then close the lid and finish the wash. With this unit, you cannot fill the machine and let a few items soak. The machine fills the tub according to how much laundry it senses is there. So if there is only a few items it will know to only fill the tub to a certain level. I will need to experiment more with the soak option.

As an allergy sufferer I can say that my sensitivity has gone way down. Also a reason I got the direct drive. No belts to contend with! The belts emit dust.

Many have commented about the noise during spin cycle and I must say that this machine is 100% quieter than my belt driven old unit. I don't even hear this running! I have to leave my utility room door open to hear it chime when finished. And the chime is so fun to hear :))

review_title: Update: It's been 18 months or so... still runs well. Cleans, agitates, spins, pumps. So far so good.
review_text:

This is why this machine is more powerful and efficient than standard washers like whirlpool,etc. Notice in the reviews a lack of any mechanical issues? Bingo! Now if the could make a washer that could load itself, that would be something.

review_text:
This washer replaced a 12 year-old GE select that I liked very much. The GE was a workhorse and never gave us any trouble at all--until it started leaking. We chose to purchase a new washer rather than repair. Believe me, we got our money's worth out of the GE.

I read the reviews and selected this particular LG washer, mainly because of its capacity and overall ratings (especially from Consumer Reports).

I was surprised that the LG actually had a much larger capacity than the GE. It's huge. One reason is that it does not have an agitator like the old GE (which means nothing will get torn up either). The only thing preventing me from doing even larger loads now is that we still have the GE Select dryer (fingers are crossed--don't want another large expense!), and even though I thought its capacity was quite large it turns out it doesn't come close to the LG.

I wasn't looking forward to the digital display (everything was mechanical on the GE), but after getting used to it, it's not that big a deal. It is a bit intimidating at first though.

We had a pro deliver and install the washer, and we're glad we did because I can see that it does need to be balanced just right. Speaking of that, the only complaint I have so far is that we get the Unbalanced signal when we have larger items like blankets in the washer.

Overall, the washer has cool sounds and does a great job of washing the clothes. No regrets.

review_title: Took me awhile, but it grew on me
review_text:
My experience with this washer was rough going for the first month or so. Many of those first loads had a horrible odor...the clothes and the tub.

I like the function of the settings. I like that it's programmed to a 'normal' setting that we typically use. One of my children thinks every load should be on quick wash (which I don't like). On our old machine, I wouldn't notice that he had turned the knob until I had done a load or two. On this machine, he can put it on quick cycle and it will automatically return to the 'normal' setting that I like for the next load. After I run whites set on bright white with hot water, the next load automatically goes back to the preset program.

I like that it's top load. That's one less bending stress that my back doesn't need. I've never liked the front load. I like the see-through top. It's interesting to me to see just what's going on in there. I guess it's the child in me. Even though the barrel is deep, I have no problem reaching in to unload. I'm 5'6", but two of my children are several inches shorter. They have no problem removing clothes as well. The child in me also likes the tune it plays when a load is finished. It does take longer to run through the cycles, but that's okay with m because the clothes come out much dryer. The spin cycle really gets the water out, which takes less time to dry.

Initially I gave this a 3 star rating. That was completely based on the 'stink'. The only problem is that I simply could not believe how bad they smelled at first. I've done a lot of research on this and have found that this is often a problem with high efficiency machines because they don't use as much water. My previous high efficiency washer never left clothes smelling at all...never ever. To manage that, I sometimes add vinegar to the bleach compartment. I know sounds crazy right? Vinegar has a million uses. This is annoying to be sure. Were it not for that, it would be a 5 star for sure. I gave it a 4 star, however, because of its rocky start.

I should finally add that now, after a couple of months, I haven't had any loads that were unbalance or smell at all. I've also washed tennis shoes a couple of times and it was not a problem at all.

So all in all, its' turned out to a great washer.

review_text:
Pros-washes medium sized loads with minimal water (avg 13 gallons per load according to the manufacturer vs. avg 60 gallons of water per load for my previous model), looks nice, able to use your phone to diagnose problems, access to local repair man when needed.

Cons-clothes clump together and when washing really dirty clothes I get deposits of lint/dirt in the wrinkles, takes much longer than my old washer, limited preset wash cycles that don't let you have many wash options. It takes me over 3 hours to wash my cloth diapers (using the manufacturers recommend wash cycles!) and I often have to wash my toddlers clothes twice if I fail to get every scrap of food off the garnet before washing. The average wash using normal cycles takes almost an hour. I use HE detergent as recommended by the manufacturer and it's the same soap I used in my old washer without problem. The wash cycles are preset with only limited options to change the settings. There is no way to soak clothes for more than 30 minutes. The delay wash feature only works sometimes.

Bottom line-if you do medium loads of clothes having minimal soil in a drought area it is a great buy. It takes over 3 hours to wash my cloth diapers and does a poor job getting my toddlers clothes clean.

product_title: Samsung WF365BTBGWR 3.6 Cu. Ft. White Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
We bought this washer and its matching dryer in December of 2012. I immediately loved them as they are such an enormous upgrade to the terrible, cheap top loaders I was using before. The sanitize and steam settings are fantastic for a family with three children and a husband who sometimes forgets to switch the laundry before going to bed.

The unit is also pretty quiet, it doesn't rattle or make any annoying noises like I've read about in other product reviews for other machines. I especially like the "singing" alarms which are a far cry from the noxious buzzer sound I'm used to hearing.

All that being said, I give this machine a 3 star rating because of one very odd problem : the lettering wipes off when one tries to clean it after the control panel has had fabric softener or detergent dripped on it. I discovered this when I tried to clean some Downy off of it, using a plain white washcloth dampened with water. Some light researching yielded many complaints about this issue, and I'm concerned Samsung will not be able to do anything so I'll have to use my extended warranty where I bought it to get a new washer (which seems silly). Apparently they didn't bother to put a clear coat over the lettering on the washers so exposure to certain chemicals -- particularly the ones used to clean laundry -- will cause the markings to wipe away. This wouldn't be so terrible if the control dial and buttons didn't add up to 20+ individual words and setting combinations. If they expect me to happily print off a picture of what it looked like "before", just so I can use the darn thing properly, they're wrong.

I will try to come back with an update on how my email to Samsung turns out. If they actually have a solution that doesn't involve putting another of the same in my house (with the same problem), I will bump this up to a 4 star but leave the warning. No one should have to worry about their machine being ruined by a liquid that is used *in* the product on a near-daily basis. And doing returns/exchanges is always a pain I like to avoid.

UPDATE, 1/16/14 : As of today, they continued to blame the control panel wiping off on me and refuse to admit fault. One rep did say they would pay for it, then the next guy who spoke to me after I emailed my model number decided they wouldn't do it after all. I saw another reviewer say going on Facebook and Twitter helped, so I will be trying that and come back with another update. Highly recommend getting a clearcoat if you buy any of their products and promptly treat the control panels as Google searches found problems with Samsung dishwasher and refrigerator panel lettering wiping away with water as well.

product_title: Samsung WF365BTBGWR 3.6 Cu. Ft. White Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Consider your needs v. your wants.
review_text:
We have had this set for more than a year now -

First of all it looks and operates really nice. People have commented on how nice it looks (on the pedestal. Looks are good, but operation is important, as well as cleaning (for which you buy this type of machine). We bought the combination washer and dryer, so they would look nice. It would be a mistake to buy a front loader without buying the Pedestal to elevate it high enough to avoid bending over to take out and put in laundry. After a number of months of use, we found out that you should not overload the machine (too much) because the belt will come off in it's operation. That was a dumb move on my part. The energy and water you save is nice (although it's not a huge amount), and we like the different selections of operation (which gives us a huge amount of choices when doing our wash). One important note; this machine will not clean your cloths better than a "tub" washing machine. You can also load a larger amount of clothing in a "tub" machine. Cleaning is very important to me, so if I had to do it again, I'd find a nice looking "large tub" machine and go in that direction. But if your sold on the front loader - I'd recommend this product. I mean, good looks, and doing the job is important, but looks aren't everything to me.... but doing large loads and getting them clean is.

review_title: Quiet, Energy Saving, Cleans Very Well!!
review_text:
I purchased this washer from Home Depot and received it with no scratches.
It is a very gorgeous washer (and dryer combo). I did not purchase the pedestals
because I am only 26 years old and I just can't see the extra money for nothing
more than convenience.

Pros- VERY quiet (at full spin speed I really had to verify it was on), cleans thoroughly,
empties the detergent tray every load (easier cleanup). So many wash choices for various
situations (most of which I'm sure I'll use frequently), including PureCycle. PureCycle
allows you to sanitize the washing machine, killing any mold spores inside.

Cons- It seems like the wash cycles take quite some time, my average load runs about
57 minutes (the sanitize cycle of the washer requests around 2 hours 27 minutes).
My son loves to put his face to them and smudge the chrome.

This is a very versatile washing machine; at this point I do not think I could have made
a better choice. ALSO: The music is pleasant; functionality is not nearly as complicated
as it looks at first glance.

UPDATE - (1 MONTH OF USE) While the sanitize cycle takes quite a long time, the rest do not. The additional time spent in the washer is saved during drying. I realized this after a few loads as the clothes are hardly even damp when the wash cycle is complete. I have had no issues thus far. Be careful when you pull the filter (you should do this often) for cleaning, make sure you pull the hose first and have some kind of bowl nearby to catch water.

review_title: Junk - Threw away after 16 months and 3 repairs
review_text:
I purchased mine as part of a set from Lowe's in October 2012. We had been happy with our Maytag Neptune set for 11 years but our new home required stackable units so we purchased this set. We were excited b/c of the features and it being a newer and prettier set than our 11 year old Neptunes. We had them delivered and installed by Lowe's.

We were initially happy b/c the sensor functions worked better than our Neptune set and the capacity was slightly better. The washer worked ok although this dryer does take longer than our old Neptune.

We started having issues in June 2013 when we opened the dryer and a 3 inch wide by 6 inch long gash appeared in the drum. It was very sharp and very dangerous. It completely shredded a pair of my basketball shorts. Fortunately, it did not damage other clothes. The dryer was completely unusable. This is where the fun began. We contacted Samsung and could not secure an appointment for TWO WEEKs. We had already had a service appointment once on the washer (less serious issue but still a warranty issue) that had taken nearly a month to resolve with 4 different trips. Samsung, the global conglomerate that makes mobile phones, many makes of video monitors / televisions, countless other consumer electronics, hundreds of consumer electronics such as watches-phones-music devices-etc used a sub contractor to work on their appliances that was nearly 4 hours away from our home despite us living within 1 hour of two 800K person cities and 45 minutes from a 250K person city. They would send a tech from Columbia, SC to Beaufort, SC but not from Charleston, SC or Savannah, GA, or Hilton Head, SC....this led to many long lead times and trips back and forth when the techs could not figure out what to do. To add insult to injury, there was a 1 month back order on the drum (they had to replace the entire drum to address this). After 68 days, they finally addressed this with a new drum and we were able to dry clothes again.

Now (February 2014), only 17 months later, we have a dryer that shuts off after about 2-3 minutes running. No matter what setting we use; it just turns off after about 2-3 minutes. If we stand there long enough re-starting it it may run 10 minutes. Drying one load can take 5-6 hours and require you to start and re-start over and over. We contacted Samsung and were told we would wait about two weeks to see a tech, again from Columbia, SC; and we would have to pay for this honor.

So long Samsung; your equipment was picked up by our recycling folks in Beaufort. We have learned our lesson...no more Samsung equipment period. We even wrote letters to your office of the president and to customer care people who helped us before and got NO RESPONSE after two weeks. We called both 800 numbers and got nothing but "we are sorry" and run arounds. So, we bought new electrolux equipment and we will never ever buy Samsung anything again. Shame on you for building junk and then not supporting it...and finally for not even acknowledging our communications with you.

Buyer beware. I would not buy Samsung unless you buy some type of long term warranty or have the energy and time to do your own work on their equipment. They clearly do not care enough to support their products in market by having anyone able to respond to emails or letters and dispatching sub contractors from 200 miles away. Unbelievable.

review_title: If you are coming from a conventional, top-loading washer, be aware of the following.
review_text:
So I got this top-loading LG HE washer as a replacement for my 14-year-old top-loading Kenmore washer that eventually failed. This LG was the highest rated washer by a leading consumer reports magazine, and that's why I bought it.

Can't say that I am thrilled with this new machine :(

Pros:
Supposedly uses less water and electricity.
Higher spin speed gets more water out, resulting in shorter drying times in dryer.
Quieter, and less vibrations at high RPM.
No need to manually set water level; it supposedly figures the right amount of water to use.
Glass window on top, to see what the washer is actually doing.
No back panel like other washers; easier access to front controls.
Electronic controls (not mechanical dials and knobs).
Clothes look and smell clean after wash, but are they really cleaner? (see cons below).
Larger capacity.
Gentler on clothes.
Gives you an indication of remaing wash time in minutes, that could increase during the cycle depending on certain conditions.
Soft-closing lid (doesn't slam).

Cons:
Takes twice the time for a wash. (So where's the energy savings?)
Does all kinds of rotations with the clothes, without water, to try to balance the load before water-intake.
And still gets out of balance during spin (uE code), and does an unnecessary rinse again (during spin cycle), lengthening wash time, to try to re-balance the load.
The Owner's Manual states" "Always try to wash articles of somewhat similar weight to allow the washer to evenly distribute the weight of the load for spinning" (page 30). Really? What BS! All this because of the higher spin RPM? How do I find something similar in weight to my white bathrobe, as my other whites? It was very, very rare for my old washer to ever go out of balance.
Don't watch the clothes too long via the top glass window, or you might get dizzy.
Absolutely needs HE only detergent.
I've seen the same bathrobe pocket on the top of the other clothes at the beginning of the wash, and at the end of the wash. Sometimes smaller items get enclosed in the bathrobe. Are these indications that the clothes are not moving around properly in the water? Never had this problem in my old, agitator-based washer with sufficient water.

Update:
After a couple of months of use, I called the LG Tech Support to look at why I was getting so many uE (unbalanced load warnings). The technician came by and immediately replaced the rotor (with magnets around it), saying that there was a batch of them that had magnets that were not exactly identical in power causing some issues. Well, I still see uE warnings today. He did not indicate that my machine was not level or anything like that. He did say to avoid the default (cotton/normal) cycle because it uses very little water (to qualify for the washer HE rating), and that tends to cause more instances of unbalanced loads. Use Bright Whites, Pure Color and Bulky/Bedding is what he said.

2nd Update:
The washer is ripping our clothes in a different way than my previous agitator-based washer did.
If I use medium or high spin speed, the wet clothes can occasionally get stretched/pulled during the spin cycle, and this causes rips in strange places. I have to manually switch to use low spin speed with every wash load now, and that negates any energy savings of getting the clothes a little more dry by the higher spin speeds.

3rd Update:
I have figured out a way to get more water in the Pure Colors wash: simply pause the washer once it begins washing, open the lid and push/pull/move the clothes around manually, maybe add an extra item to wash. Then close the lid and resume the wash cycle. In a short while, it will intake more water until the max limit, and continue the wash cycle.
It is a pain to have to do this with every wash, but clothes move more freely and tend to wash better this way, I think.

product_title: LG WT1101 4.3 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity High Efficiency Top Load Washer with SlamProof, White
review_text:
I waited a few months before I wrote a review on this product. I wanted to have time to come to understand how this washer performs and what it's challenges were before I wrote down my thoughts. I think this is a very good washing machine, not worthy of five stars, but surely worth a solid four stars.

This machine has several cycles ranging from 35 minutes to over an hour. However, the actual time is longer than the 35 minutes if the load goes into imbalance and the machine resets itself. This might be frustrating to some but the technology wants the machine to correct itself. Aside from the wash cycles there are rinse and spin or spin only cycles. Do not put waterproof items in the washer as it will damage it.

The most prominent thing you will immediately recognize is how quiet this washer is. Standing next to it you can barely hear it washing. Spin cycles are a little louder, but if your laundry is on the main floor of your house, the machine will not disrupt your activities. The machine advertises that it saves water and energy which may be true, but without submetering your water or electricity, it would be tricky to come at a firm number. The fact that it spins at a high rate of speed (there are four spin settings: high, medium, low, and none) removes a lot of water meaning that your dry times will be faster than a conventional washer with agitator.

To operate the machine simply place your items in the drum and add detergent to the dispenser and select a cycle. The machine will determine load size and the amount of water needed. Note that if you fill the machine plumb full, it will likely go into imbalance mode. If the machine cannot correct the imbalance, it will shut down. This may lead some people to criticize the design, but keep in mind it is not a commercial washer at a laundromat. Think through how much you put in the machine and do two loads if necessary. Again, some will say this will not save as much, but overfilling a conventional washer will not get the clothes clean and cause excessive wear on the motor. Save yourself the hassle and do not fill the machine barrel more than half way. It has a large capacity, 4.3 cu. ft. so you can get a lot of clothes in it.

When I was considering a new washer I knew I wanted something different than the old standard agitator machine. Front loaders seemed too low to the ground if I didn't want to buy the base for an additional $200+ so the choice came down to Samsung or LG. I settled on LG and have been generally pleased thus far. I say I'm generally pleased as I have overloaded my machine and had it stop. I've selected lengthy cycles that seemed to take forever to finish. I've loaded only towels and had the machine go into imbalance. I've learned from my earlier mistakes and am not displeased with my choice. I did purchase a warranty plan from my local appliance dealer because this technology is still relatively new. I may have wasted my money but it seemed like a good idea at the time.

So four or five months into my ownership of this washer I feel like I've gotten to know this machine relatively well. Would I buy it again? Yes. Would I switch to a different brand? Not necessarily. As I said at the start of this review, it is a very good machine, but it's not perfect. I did not buy this from Amazon as I felt more comfortable buying it from a local dealer who can also service my machine should it need repairs. I like this machine a lot and do not regret my selection.

product_title: LG WT1101 4.3 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity High Efficiency Top Load Washer with SlamProof, White
review_text:
We purchased this LG top load front panel washer and matching gas dryer to replace old Kenmore units. We needed them to fit in the same space. The new front loads would not fit and sit higher. This design was perfect for our space. The lid opens to stay below the wall cabinets. The front panel controls are really convenient.

We were concerned about several reviews that criticized the long cycles and "balancing" at the start of the wash cycle. Some said this step would result in the cycle stopping and forced a reset while you manually re-distributed the load. After 6 weeks of operations including whites, colors, large bed comforters, small loads, etc. we have not had any problems. The washer goes through "dance" at the beginning as it senses the load size and weight. This does take time but seems to work well.

This is a HE washer. So it uses less water .. no center spindle to beat up your clothes. A large load of white underwear with bleach and "soak" cycle can take over one hour. But the closes come out clean and white and the spin cycle can be set on high and they are de-watered completely .. taking less load off the dryer.

We did wash a king bed comforter on cold water, gentle. Looking through the top window you can see how the washer uses little water and the comforter is sitting above the water line. But it works and works on it until it seem happy. The comforter cam out clean and spun dry.

The matching dryer has also worked well. Like the washer there are many combinations of settings. Large loads have come out dry .. if you figure out the right settings.

We have no idea if the warranty service is any good. We purchased our set from Pacific Sales and they say to call them if we need service.

So far we are very pleased with our new washer dryer pair. They also look cool!

My money is down the drain - don't follow with yours.

review_text: I have had this washer for about 7 wks.  It takes an hour to wash even a tiny load.  You have two options.  Clothes come out wet, looking and smelling exactly as they went in.  Or you get clothes that are coated with detergent and need to be re-rinsed.  The washer "balances" and flattens the clothes to the outside of the drum.  Then the water and the detergent spill into the CENTER of the drum, avoid the actual clothes.  There is only at best a  50/50 chance your clothes will get enough water and/or detergent to get clean.  The efficiency then goes out the window, since you are continually re-rinsing, re-spining, and yes, at times re-washing all of your clothes.  I now have a service call in, since Lowes won't accept return after 30 days. Unless you LOVE to stand guard over your washer, pause it, mash the clothes around with a stick to make sure they are all wet and soapy, then triple check to make sure the thing actually rinses the clothes, DO NOT BUY THIS WASHER.  If you STILL think this is the machine for you, I will sell you mine, it is only 7 weeks old....I am FLABBERGASTED by any positive reviews for this machine.  DON'T BELIEVE THEM!!!.  I am sorely regretting that I did, and I may be out $700 because of it.  Look at the GE Model GTWN4250WS.  That is what I am KICKING myself for not buying.

review_title: Yes, you must think and plan ahead before you use it.
review_text: The many poor reviews of this genius piece of engineering seem to have the same common thread running through them.  Given its auto-leveling function (to prevent unbalanced loads) the machine requires the user to separate heavy items from lighter ones; bigger items - like bedding - from smaller items.  This may not be an ideal machine for someone with a large family and limited time, but it is an excellent machine for those that invest the minimal amount of time and effort to maximize its efficiency.  Like its front loader cousins, the spin cycle of this machine reaches very high rpms, which wrings out a tremendous amount of water and significantly reduces drying time.  Finally, the front positioned keypad control panel was a major selling point for me, as my hot water heater is mounted on a platform above my W/D, which made accessing controls on a standard model a challenge, to say the least.

UPDATE #1: I have now had this machine for two months and it is not performing any better. I tried the green scrubbie and the vinegar that LG recommended to other reviewers on their website. I've already had one here that threatened to charge me if he came out again for a false alarm. He hooked his computer up to it which indicated that it is still within factory specs and is working as manufactured....go figure!

UPDATE #2: The new service man tested my machine and it is again working within factory specs with no repairs needed. I now have figured out that if I do two extra rinses (hit the extra rinse button twice) the clothes come out 90% "clean". The soap residue is mostly gone, but the pet hair is not. I can't wait to see my new water bill. This is using a lot more water than my old dinosaur. I watched it fill up three times to do three complete rinses! So my tub fills up four times now instead of two. How is this energy efficient? I also had a soiled item I washed twice in hot water that was pre-treated with an Oxy Clean Stain stick and it did not come clean as it would have with our old machine. This one also still winds things up, like bra straps even though it has the new agitator design. I'm concerned about trying to find a new one. All of them that I've looked at have issues. I can't imagine any machine working worse than this one though. You also can't soak items for any length of time. The water drains out of the washer within a very short amount of time. You end up with clothes that now have a mildew smell that you thought were soaking in water!!

UPDATE #3: LG has told me that they will not authorize a return since my machine does not have an actual defect that is easy to repair. The supervisor accused me of having buyers remorse. The company where I bought it has since fired that salesman due to the promises that he was making to customers that did not follow company policy. review_text:
AVOID AT ALL COST! Oh my gosh, can a washer be considered a nightmare? YES...this washer qualifies. First LG appliance, and I can definately say it will be our last. Purchased last December, and it has been an endless hassle. Looks pretty,functions terribly.
I always do a lot of research prior to purchasing an appliance, somehow this got very good ratings on a major "Consumer" site,along with Big Box electronic store ratings, but I cannot fathom how! Kind of makes me lose my faith in the validity of ratings.

Where to start?
1) As many others have mentioned, endless BALANCE issues. I can't remember the last wash cycle that actually managed to get completed on its own without having to go in and redistribute the clothes 2, 3, 4 or more times. This washer will indicate "Ue" (uneven) while running,which them prompts the washer to try to rebalance itself using loads more water and electricity, the progress to "UE", which means the wash cycle has been interrupted and it has shut itself down. Go in, redistribute the clothes, try again.., more water/power. A wash load that should be completed in 35 minutes can stretch on for 3-4 hours!!! Yes, I have followed all the guidelines: keep loads with similiar weight/type fabrics, don't only wash one or two items at a time. It does not make any difference.
2) Can not wash anything remotely water resistant, ie jackets, kids baseball uniform hoodies as it messes up the sensors somehow. Forget washing sneakers in this washer, forbidden item as well. So, if you have school age kids and sports gear to wash, this is not the washer for you.

Give me my old, plain, reliable Kenmore washer ANY day...you could throw anything in there, not all the crazy limitations, and it NEVER stopped in a wash cycle.

Bottom line: looks pretty, plays a nice tune at the end of the cycle (if you can ever get to that point, it's like the movie "Groundhog Day") but is an epic fail in the land of washers, keep away if you don't want to drive yourself crazy in the laundry room!

review_title: So far, I'm bummed I bought this machine.
review_text:
I plan to give this washer a chance, but after my first couple loads, I'm not happy.

1) Detergent type. I've got bad MCS allergies and can't use most laundry detergents; BioKleen works for me. What I didn't realize is that this washer wants you to only use particular brands of detergent. The BioKleen label says to use 1/2 a capful for high-efficiency washers, so I assume BioKleen is OK for high-efficiency washers. The instructions to the LG say I'm supposed to be looking for a certain, HE logo on every detergent product. Similary, LG's instructions say nothing about using white vinegar (against odors, mold, and for softening) or Borax. They just say "Oh only use our products, because other stuff might affect the sensors in this machine." I guess this is fine for people who are willing to use nasty, smelly chemicals like Tide. For me and my kids, it's not ideal.

2) Following instructions as best I could -- the half-capful of BioKleen detergent put in the little drawer, and I did add a very small amount of vinegar and some pre-dissolved Borax straight in with the clothes -- I selected the "heavy duty" cycle for clothes after we'd been camping in them. I filled the washer fairly lightly, because I'd read that this washer comes unbalanced easily. The load was pretty quiet and everything seemed fine... until I got the clothes out of the dryer later. They have a peculiar set of wrinkles, and they smell like campfire. Some are stained. Heavy duty? Hardly.

3) Trying to pre-soak clothes the way *I* want to wash them seems surprisingly difficult. If I want to soak a bunch of clothes in a tub of water with some BioKleen oxygen bleach or Borax or whatever, for 20 minutes, and then have the washing machine rinse it down, with old-fashioned washers I was used to being able to do that. Then I could add normal detergent, add some more clothes that didn't need the pre-soak, and run a normal load. This washer doesn't seem to want me to presoak at all! LG says on Bestbuy's site, replying to similar customer confusion, that the "Soak" cycle includes a 30-minute soak -- as part of its mysterious high efficiency cycle.

4) I asked the salespeople multiple times about LG's famed "Allergeine" allergy cycle, and supposedly it's in this machine, but there's no button or indicator that says allergy. Haven't sorted that out yet.

For what it's worth, I did a lot of research before purchasing. I'm unable to use front loaders because they tend to become mildewy more easily than top loaders, and I have a Severe Mold Allergy. product_title: LG WT1101 4.3 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity High Efficiency Top Load Washer with SlamProof, White
review_title: Kinda wishing it would break so we can replace it with something else. Anything else.
review_text:
First off, I purchased this machine at an actual store and not through Amazon. It is, however, the same model. As I know people check the reviews on Amazon as they research products, I wanted to pass on the knowledge we've gleaned after owning this thing for about a year now. We're a family of 4 and seem to accumulate a rather startling amount of laundry on a weekly basis. This machine has a few "Pros", but some major "Cons". Be aware before you buy.

Pros:
Huge capacity is great. This machine can eat through our Mount Laundry Hamper in just 2 loads, compared to our previous machine's 4 or 5.
Cleans well. Cold cycle is a plus. I've never had anything go in dirty that didn't come out completely clean. No complaints there.
Very quiet. Our L.R is right off our kitchen so a quiet machine was important to us.
Smooth running. No "jumping" or "walking" issues. It doesn't even shake the floor during high speed spins. No complaints there either.

BUT.......
Cons:
Nearly impossible to keep loads balanced: machine runs on computerized wizardry that is heck-bent on keeping the machine in balance. If a load shifts during one of the (many) spin and "back and forth" cycles (which is a common occurrence), it will throw a "uE" code and start refilling with water. Even if you're wash time is down to the final 10 minutes, it may suddenly go off balance and start refilling again, adding an additional 10 to 15 minutes while it attempts to shift the load and balance again. If the "uE" attempts to re balance the load fail, you'll get a "UE" code which will stop the machine. It will wait patiently for you to come and toss the contents (salad, anyone?) and get it going again.

Once a load starts to throw codes at you, you are in for a long laundry day: seriously, no matter what you do, it will keep throwing the stupid "UE" and stopping, or you'll be dealing with constant refilling. I once spent a full 4 hours washing a load of whites. One load. Seriously, true story.

Loads need to be large: That whole Large Capacity thing sure sounds great. However, it's less of a perk and more of a requirement if you want this machine to run well. Too small of a load? Sorry, it won't stay balanced. (Codes galore). Too large of a load? Sorry, won't stay balanced. (Codes galore). I feel like I spend a LOT of my time attempting to find the sweet spot between too small and too big. It's a time wasting endeavor that makes me hate doing the laundry.

Some things refuse to cooperate in there. I can wash quilts. I can wash comforters. But blankets? Forget it. Not gonna happen. Whether I put the blankets in the machine alone or with other "similar weight items", ( per the manual's tips), I can anticipate a few hours of good old fashioned code throwing fun.

Manual tips are ridiculous. The manual suggests loading the machine with materials of the same weight; however, in our family, and I would suspect in many families, that makes the load size too small for this demented machine. If you try to mix the fabric weights, you may get the invite to the dreaded Code Party. Some loads go through without a hitch, others are like the ghost of some awful cooking smell that you just can't get rid of. No rhyme or reason to it.

LG Customer Support is no help. I've tried telling them what I'm dealing with. Their response is a chipper "I can help you with that! Be sure all the loads are of the same weight!" Thanks. Helpful.

In short, this is the first washing machine that we've owned that I find myself hoping will break. And believe me, we will not attempt to fix it when it does. If I had known how impractical it was at the time we bought it....if I had read the reviews a little more thoroughly, this beastly thing would not be taking up space in my home, or on our credit card, right now.
