product_title: LG WT1101 4.3 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity High Efficiency Top Load Washer with SlamProof, White
review_title: Intentionally designed for SMALL loads. . . (unwritten advice from LG technician)
review_text:
UPDATE: I returned my LG Wt1101 and am returning to a conventional washer with a central agitator. The fact that this huge washer is DESIGNED for small loads and has no effective setting for more typical medium-sized loads was central to my decision. The first thing I did with my new machine was to re-wash many of the clothes I'd done with this LG HE washer because they reeked of soap and fabric softener.

ORIGINAL POST I've had this washer for two weeks and am still deciding whether to keep it. My complaint, like many other people, is that the water level is so low that clothes are not pulled down into the wash water. After an hour on the phone with a LG technician, I learned this: the different cycles are designed to use different amounts of water. Ignore the given names (e.g. Cotton, Heavy Duty) and think of the cycles in terms water levels.

He said that two cycles, Cotton/Normal and Heavy Duty, are designed to add water only up to 1" above the silver knob in the center bottom of the tub. That equals 5" of water measured from the deepest pockets in the bottom of the tub, but an average of only 4" throughout most of the tub. If you put in more clothes than this, the clothes on top might not get pulled into the water. I put in six long-sleeved t-shirts and the top one did not get pulled down into the water in the Cotton/Normal cycle. Apparently this [stupid] design helps LG qualify for the low water/high efficiency rating on this machine. It would take 54 minutes to wash those six shirts.

Two other cycles, Bright Whites and Pure Color, are designed to add a bit more water. I measured it as 2" from the top of the silver knob and 6" from the deepest pockets in the bottom of the tub, averaging about 5" deep throughout the tub. In addition to the six long-sleeved t-shirts, there was enough water to add three lightweight sweat shirts using the Bright Whites cycle. Together, this load was smaller than what I could do in my old-fashioned 2.4 cubic foot washer with a central agitator. The was cycle was longer than an hour.

One cycle, Bulky Items, is designed to fill the tub and it does. It works well for large loads.

The technician recommended always using small loads and selecting Bright Whites, or using very large loads and selecting Bulky Items, and then manually setting the water temperature, agitation, and spin speed to create the wash I want. There are buttons for water temperature and spin speed; the Soil Level button sets the agitation (more "soil" adds more time and uses a stronger agitation; it does not add more water like I thought). There is no easy way to wash a medium-sized load on this machine because the cycles provide too little or too much water.

He also said it's important to use the Fabric Softener button if softener is used in the Cotton/Normal or Heavy Duty cycle (the manual also mentions this). In those cycles, the default setting uses a spray rinse that will not remove fabric softener from the clothes. Again, this is a trick to reduce water consumption in order to qualify for ratings; it does not provide an effective rinse. By pressing the Fabric Softener button, you override that default and the rinse will "fill" the tub with water in normal rinse fashion. Apparently the other cycles always "fill" the tub during rinse so the Fabric Softener button is not needed for them.

The last thing he said is that the Load Sensing period that occurs before the wash begins is simply an attempt to distribute the clothes evenly; it has nothing to do with judging the weight of the load or assessing how much water will be required. By the way, I've washed some heavy items and have never encountered the unbalanced load problem that others report. I think the trick is to load the clothes as if there were a central agitator in the middle, spreading items around the edges of the tub.

So the bottom line is this: this huge capacity washer works best for very small or very large loads, and the "smart" specialty cycles need to be overridden for almost every load of laundry. I'll try a few more loads now that I have this information but I'm not pleased.

One last word of advice: the washer does not have a way to filter and remove lint or dog hair from the water. I washed a load of dog bedding and then, as I explored this topic of water level, I ran several loads of just water (no clothes) to see how much water entered the tub. Even after filling, spinning, and draining several cycles of water, there still was dog hair floating in the water. The only way to remove it seems to be doing another load of laundry and having it stick to clothes, and then being removed by the dryer. The matching dryer, however, is great at removing lint and dog hair as the clothes tumble dry.

I think the trick is to load the clothes as if there were a central agitator in the middle, spreading items around the edges of the tub. So the bottom line is this: this huge capacity washer works best for very small or very large loads, and the "smart" specialty cycles need to be overridden for almost every load of laundry. I'll try a few more loads now that I have this information but I'm not pleased. One last word of advice: the washer does not have a way to filter and remove lint or dog hair from the water. I washed a load of dog bedding and then, as I explored this topic of water level, I ran several loads of just water (no clothes) to see how much water entered the tub. Even after filling, spinning, and draining several cycles of water, there still was dog hair floating in the water. The only way to remove it seems to be doing another load of laundry and having it stick to clothes, and then being removed by the dryer. review_text:
Picked this up a year and a half ago and have generally been pretty happy with it. Sure there was the occasional UE error code, but these were for genuinely unbalanced loads that would have shaken the washer to pieces if we hadn't remedied the situation. Things started going downhill a month or two ago, though, with the washer getting progressively worse on the UE codes. It was getting so bad that I was told to make my current pair of underwear last, because there was going to be no more washing until the washer was fixed. Something had to be done!

After giving the washer a top-to-bottom dressing down including removing the top, removing the agitator plate, checking the suspension, and checking for loose wires, I found a giant nut on the bottom of the washer that could easily be turned by hand. Since this nut looked to hold the motor onto the bottom of the drum, I figured it was kind of important and tightened it. The good news is that the problem now seems to be solved! We've since done 5 loads of laundry and not a single error code. Best of all, since this washer is so lightweight (especially in comparison to our brick-loaded Adora), tipping it back to check the tightness of the screw is pretty easy to do. Just make sure to have some way to lock the drum/motor in place so that you can really get that thing on tight.

review_text:
We bought this washer at Home Depot based on the insanely high number of good reviews, and it was a huge mistake. At least the truth is out here on Amazon! Please listen to all the 1 Star reviews and do not buy this washer. It cannot stay balanced to save its life. I wash a very normal amount of clothes, and it gets to the end of the cycle end with no problems about 1/4 of the time. It very easily goes off balance and cannot spin the clothes dry. But it doesn't simply stop and wait for you to balance things. It quickly re-fills with water to balance the clothes itself. It's trying to save you the effort, but in doing so, the energy efficiency goes down the drain. How is it using less water if almost every load gets an extra rinse? Even if you catch it re-filling, and start again with a "spin only" cycle, you have a problem. Spin only means "spin until I get unbalanced, and start that extra rinse thing again." I basically have to babysit this washer when I do laundry, and I hate it.

UPDATE: After months and months of hating my washer, my hubby was basically offering to buy something and start over. I said how about you just call LG and bug them until they help us (we should not have to spend hundreds on a new washer!), and he did. After a couple calls where they told him to call a repair man (he tried, no one was reasonable and most didn't even want to look at this washer), they finally offered him an LG repairman for $200 flat rate with a guarantee that it would be fixed. Finally, something worth trying. On his first visit, he replaced the "brain," the computer panel and the button panel at the top of the machine. Supposedly the software was out of date which could be causing all the UE codes, extra rinses and loads that could never spin. The load he did worked, but the problem was just the same for the 2 weeks following. So we called again - we want our guaranteed fix! This time he replaced the motor which also contains the sensors. Finally we have a working washing machine!!!!!!! It has not gone UE since. My husband is convinced it was bad sensors this whole time. The wash was never unbalanced or unable to spin, the sensors were going nuts and causing all the problems. I agree, and I think LG should contact EVERYONE complaining of this problem and replace their motor/sensors. If they did that, I would change my star rating, since my washer does work now. However, I think they have a glaring problem in manufacturing somewhere, and they don't care. I would warn people away from buying this washer until that gets fixed.

Honestly, this machine worked flawlessly for 8 months. It cleaned the clothes very well regardless of load size. I have no idea why so many people are having trouble with unbalanced load errors; I only had it happen once in 8 months and I reset the clothing, restarted the machine, and it finished without further issue.

Now comes the "warning" for potential purchasers. When we finally got a technician out to check out why, he determined that the plastic "outer basket" was leaking. Not a hose, but the outer basket itself. Upon checking his parts listing, he found no listing for a replacement part. He called LG who told him that they "discontinued making replacement outer baskets" for these machines and the technician stated LG would call me on Monday or Tuesday (this was on a Saturday) with an authorization to get a new washing machine because my machine (this same identical model listed) was "unrepairable" according to LG and the service technician. Before the technician left he recommended I DO NOT get the same model because some parts for this particular machine are "obsolete" rendering the machine "unrepairable". It is now Friday of the same week and no call from LG as of yet.

My recommendation: DO NOT buy this machine! review_title: I loved this machine for the first couple of years of ...
review_text:
Persistent Mold and Constant Unbalanced Signal.

I loved this machine for the first couple of years of ownership. I use it once or twice a week at most, so it hasn't had anywhere near heavy use.

Two big things have shown up recently. The machine frequently throws an Unbalanced code, despite my always-careful loading. Given that I'm out of earshot when the machine is running, this results in unfinished loads and, when I catch it, having to run and rerun loads. It probably happens more often than I know, so I getting loads that look like they are done, but they are not.

The bigger problem is with mold. All was perfectly well for the first few months, but now there is a persistent mold smell, despite having routinely kept the door open from day one. I have tried many things: running tub cleaner three times in a row using the Tub Clean cycle; running tub cleaner three weeks in a row; and running Tub Clean cycles using bleach, vinegar, and baking soda (separately, of course). Nothing keeps the smell from returning within a day or two.

My guess is that there is a design problem with the machine that allows mold to grow in places where the cleaning products can't reach.

LG's response to both problems is to say that the machine is out of warranty and that there is nothing they will do beyond charging me for a $125 service call and, if the technician finds that the problem(s) are LGs, refund the charge. We'll see what happens when the technician is here. Bottom line: save yourself this kind of trouble and buy from another manufacturer!

I was very excited to get this washer after looking up reviews all over the internet on it, but it really hasn't lived up to what I thought it would be like. If I did this over again, I would probably go to an actual appliance store and look at them in person and do much more research and get something else.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text:
I did not purchase this unit from Amazon, I purchased from Living Direct.
I came with all the necessary attachments and tools. (did not have to pay extra)
I also purchased the extended warranty considering how expensive the unit was.

If you are hard core hot air dryer addict, then you probably won't like this unit.
Vent-less drying means it dries clothes like an air-conditioner via dehumidifying / condensing.
Clothes will have a slight "damp" feeling when you first pull them out, but in a minute or two they are dry.

Pros - keeps your home cool because it does not radiate heat
- it is extremely cost efficient.
- clothes come out incredibly clean and NO soap residue
- you don't have to move laundry from the washer to a dryer YAY
- uses extremely small amount of water! Incredibly environmentally friendly!
- it's great for limited space, or apartment living where washer/dryer hook-ups are lacking
- no risk of a dryer fire breaking out!
- perfect for delicate fabrics that are easily damaged by heat
- much less shrinkage of clothes
- colors do not fade like they do from heat drying
- clothes still come out soft without using fabric softener, but even more so if you do.
- no more dryer sheets to control static cling! OH YEAH!
- clothes do NOT come out wrinkled if you remove them within an hour or so of finishing
- the powerful spin cycle means clothes hung to dry will dry fast even when indoors
- only need space for ONE UNIT.. instead of 2
- does not require exterior venting (huge plus factor!)
- say goodbye to public laundry mat
- it sings an adorable tune to let you know your laundry is done =) Not annoying.

Cons - no.. you cannot throw something in and have it come out dry 10 minutes later.
- it can take double the time to dry items than a conventional dryer (but sill less $$$)
- lint.. you must manually remove the lint or do a load w/o drying to wash out lint
- you cannot leave the laundry in the machine for an excessive amount of time.
.. of course.. even with a regular dryer leaving laundry sit is bad news...

NOTE: YOU NEED TO FOLLOW MANUFACTURER INSTRUCTIONS AND RUN THE CLEANING CYCLE EVERY MONTH!
If you don't then problems can and probably will arise. (I have not had a single problem)

I recommend leaving the door open after use to completely dry out the interior.
Remember that it is based on a wet system so just use some common sense.

DIRECT DRIVE means a turbine engine on steroids. It spins hard and fast.
YOU MUST MAKE SURE THE UNIT IS PERFECTLY LEVELED or it will bounce and get damaged.
When leveled, it functions smoothly and quietly. Some vibration on highest spin cycles.

Yes, it will wash comforters and quilts up to double/queen but won't let you dry them.
You must hang them to dry but due to the spin cycle they dry in no time when hung.

There is an incredible array of features and options that are easy to use except for one.
The setting for washers on wooden floors to suppress vibrations (it works fantastic), but it
requires holding the stain button down for a couple of seconds and listening for beeps.
It's hard to know when it's on. That's my only pet peeve.
They really should have created a separate button for this function.

I've had it 8 months now and never had a problem.
Customer service was great when I called in for assistance with the vibrations suppressor.

Pros - keeps your home cool because it does not radiate heat - it is extremely cost efficient. - clothes come out incredibly clean and NO soap residue - you don't have to move laundry from the washer to a dryer YAY - uses extremely small amount of water! Incredibly environmentally friendly! - it's great for limited space, or apartment living where washer/dryer hook-ups are lacking - no risk of a dryer fire breaking out! - perfect for delicate fabrics that are easily damaged by heat - much less shrinkage of clothes - colors do not fade like they do from heat drying - clothes still come out soft without using fabric softener, but even more so if you do. - no more dryer sheets to control static cling! OH YEAH! - clothes do NOT come out wrinkled if you remove them within an hour or so of finishing - the powerful spin cycle means clothes hung to dry will dry fast even when indoors - only need space for ONE UNIT.. instead of 2 - does not require exterior venting (huge plus factor!) - say goodbye to public laundry mat - it sings an adorable tune to let you know your laundry is done =) Not annoying. Cons - no.. you cannot throw something in and have it come out dry 10 minutes later. - it can take double the time to dry items than a conventional dryer (but sill less $$$) - lint.. you must manually remove the lint or do a load w/o drying to wash out lint - you cannot leave the laundry in the machine for an excessive amount of time. .. of course.. even with a regular dryer leaving laundry sit is bad news... NOTE: YOU NEED TO FOLLOW MANUFACTURER INSTRUCTIONS AND RUN THE CLEANING CYCLE EVERY MONTH! If you don't then problems can and probably will arise. (I have not had a single problem) I recommend leaving the door open after use to completely dry out the interior. Remember that it is based on a wet system so just use some common sense. DIRECT DRIVE means a turbine engine on steroids. It spins hard and fast. YOU MUST MAKE SURE THE UNIT IS PERFECTLY LEVELED or it will bounce and get damaged. When leveled, it functions smoothly and quietly. Some vibration on highest spin cycles. Yes, it will wash comforters and quilts up to double/queen but won't let you dry them. You must hang them to dry but due to the spin cycle they dry in no time when hung. There is an incredible array of features and options that are easy to use except for one. The setting for washers on wooden floors to suppress vibrations (it works fantastic), but it requires holding the stain button down for a couple of seconds and listening for beeps. It's hard to know when it's on. That's my only pet peeve. They really should have created a separate button for this function. I've had it 8 months now and never had a problem. Customer service was great when I called in for assistance with the vibrations suppressor.

review_title: Great if you like wet clothes
review_text:
I've had many different driers over the years, and they've all dried clothes. The only differences were capacity, heat source, and features. It didn't matter the capacity, the heat source (gas or electric), or the features, they all had one thing in common, they dried your clothes. The permanent press cycles are nice, the cool down cycles are nice, infinite temperature settings are nice, but they are all worthless if it doesn't ultimately dry your clothes in a reasonable amount of time.

Then there's this drier. It is the absolute worst drier I have ever used. It will not dry a load of clothes on one dry cycle. Doesn't matter how many clothes are in the drier, how long the cycle is, the temperature of the cycle, items never come out dry. And I don't mean a little dampness or slight cool-to-the-touch around the waist line, I mean wet. It always takes at least 2 cycles, and often more, to get them dry. Especially towels. I will be up half the night restarting the drier every 75 minutes or so just to get one load dry! It must have 15 different drying cycle types, and it doesn't matter which one you use, everything is still is wet on completion.

This is the only computerized drier I've ever purchased, and it will be the last. Give me a good old mechanical dial for the amount of time and a 3-position switch for setting the temperature any day.

review_text:
I had an old whirlpool washer from 2001. The last 7 yrs it's had really heavy use especially since that model had a smaller tub. I have a tight laundry space that only allows certain dimensions, so this was the most important factor when picking out a replacement. I went to Best Buy and bought a new set that was still a manual model for approx. $1100. The very next day I happened to stumble upon this machine at Menards for only $400. It was an upgrade from what I originally selected and let me tell you how happy I am. I've had this machine about a week so far so please keep that in mind. What I love:
-Set Up: It's very easy. In fact, I don't think there really was a "set-up" to say. Basically the technician installed it and said it was ready to go.
-The tub: It's Stainless steel and for a smaller machine, the tub seems huge.
-The panel: VERY VERY easy to select your wash cycle. I also LOVE that you can override the pre-set selections to customize your wash which is not possible on a lot of more expensive models.
-Agitator: Really love that there is an agitator. I read a ton of reviews prior to getting this machine and it seemed a lot of complaints on the ones that don't have an agitator were due to clothes not getting clean and severe wrinkling.

The things that I wish were a little different are very minor but in fairness feel they should be pointed out.
-Detergent cup: this may or may not apply. I have the laundry soap where it has a spicket. On my old machine I would pour in the detergent and rinse out the detergent cup in the water so it was always clean, then add clothes. You can't do this on any of the newer machines (not just this model). Once you start the water, you can still add clothes but the water stops filling immediately making it so you can't rinse out the cup. Small annoyance. I will switch to a different method of detergent to avoid this or deal with a messy cup.

-Noise: It is a small tad louder and more noticeable than I'd like. Don't get me wrong, my last machine sounded like Air Force One was landing so this is a huge improvement, but you can hear the water splashing around and spinning. In a way this is a blessing because most negative reviews complain about the low water level so the fact that I can hear this splashing against the lid is reassuring that the tub is filled with water.

Again these are small annoyances and because they are pretty common on all machines I won't deduct for it. I haven't tried the delayed start yet which is a feature I was excited about, nor the bleach dispenser so those weren't factored into the review. I would highly recommend this washer.

product_title: Whirlpool WFW86HEBW Duet 4.1 Cu. Ft. White With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
This review is for those who are accustomed to seeing your washer fill up with water, agitate, drain, spin and repeat. This front-loader does more of a tumble, tumble, drain and spin but the big surprise is how little water it uses.

Your laundry will be soaked, but there is no extra water sloshing around in the tub. Just wet laundry being tumbled, making you think that it cannot be working. However, we have discovered that our clothes come out looking and smelling great, the towel setting produces great results, and we are pleased. The only negative is that we usually do an extra rinse to make sure the soap is out, but that is more a personal preference.

A big positive is that the machine spins so much water out of our laundry that our old dryer runs for a little less than half the time it did before. This translates into big electricity savings for us. We are also enjoying the fact that we can wash 12 pairs of jeans and jean shorts in a single load, maybe an hour or so, and then dry them in 20 minutes. This machine is easy to use.

I take away a star because I think it does a good job, and I reserve the extra star for products that are spectacular.

10/3/2013 As a follow-up, we've been using this machine for several months now, and still like it. Points of interest: It has not broken. It has a lot of buttons and lights and does a lot of work, so i won't be surprised when it does, but so far no problems. We've never seen a sock get stuck, never seen it leak, none of those things. It does have very sesitive controls. If you lean against the machine, or sometimes throw a towel on the machine it can touch the power button and stop the machine in mid-cycle. Also, we run the "Clean" cycle less than is recommended by the soap-selling manufacturer and still have never once smelled mold or mildew or anything except soap - a pleasant surprise.

review_title: Love this washer. Just don't close washer door after use
review_text:
We've had the same washer for 12+ years. We have two children, now in their mid to late teens, who play a lot of sports. We've probably done an average of 20 loads of laundry per week. The washer finally broke down this week, which is why I'm looking for a replacement. We love this washer and will definitely replace it with the latest version.

We understand that a front loader has to have a water tight seal so that water does not spill when washing. When we're done with laundry, we just leave the door open to allow the interior to dry. We've never had any issue with mold or mildew. It is sad that in our litigious society, the cost of this appliance will go up because consumers will sue for mold/mildew as a manufacturer defect rather than use common sense. If you can't leave the washer door open after use, it's best not to buy a front loader.

I like that this washer uses very little water. I use an eco-friendly detergent, Mrs Meyers Clean Day - Lemon. It leaves clothes looking and smelling clean. When I need to use bleach, I use it as instructed, and always do the white load last, prior to washing cleaning rags. This is not something I do just because of the low water use; I've always done it to avoid any bleach residue getting on dark / colored clothes. Unlike other reviewers, I've never had an issue with clothes not getting clean or with bleach ruining our clothes.

review_title: Looks great, but doesn't wash the clothes
review_text:
I bought this washer, locally not online, about 4 months ago after our old maytag gave up. After reading many positive reviews both by other owners and by appliance "experts" I decided this was the one.

First let me start with the good. I love the look of the washer. It really looks like it's stainless steel and the front panel controls give it a really clean look. It has a huge capacity, way more than our older dryer can handle. It is super easy to operate and is really quiet, almost silent. It also spins the clothes really dry. I've read some reviews from people complaining about unbalance errors, UE, but I have only had that happen once and it was with a large bulky comforter so it's a non-issue for me.

Now for what I don't like about it. My biggest complaint with this washer is it doesn't wash the clothes. I mean come on, it's called a washing machine for a reason right? We have people in our household that are out in the dirt and grease daily and their clothes get very dirty. It doesn't matter how much spot treatment or presoaking is done, the clothes don't come out even remotely clean. They are literally just as dirty after they are "washed" as they were when I put them in. Any money that you save from the reduced water and energy usage is more than offset with the cost of spot treatment and new clothes. The wash cycles also seem to be excessively long, especially for the pitiful amount of cleaning that is done. Lastly, and not a big issue, but the tub is very deep and I had to make a step for the ladies so they could reach the bottom.

To be fair, this is the first "high efficiency" washer that we've had and also the first without an agitator, so the poor cleaning performance might not be exclusive to this machine, but it doesn't do a very good job of cleaning that's for sure. If I could have given it 2.5 stars I would have. It is very nice looking, quiet, and has a lot of different cycles and options with a huge capacity, so if you're someone who doesn't get their clothes very dirty, it might work just fine for you. I will be buying a simple "cheapie" washer with an agitator to wash the dirty clothes and use this for the less dirty clothes and bulky items like bedding and towels.

Hopefully this review was helpful

review_title: Great washer, only gripe is "uneven load" error
review_text:
It's a shame that everyone is having bad experiences with this washer. I bought a lower version of these about 2 years ago from Best Buy but had leaking issues with them, so they replaced and upgraded the washer/dryer for us to these models at no additional charge (awesome!).

We do not have children, just my boyfriend and I and our zoo of animals, so we probably don't wash as many loads of laundry as the average household. That having been said, the clothes always come out clean, it is quiet, efficient, plenty of cycles to choose from (I usually run it on the "cold wash" cycle to save more on energy, unless something is heavily soiled then I'll run it on "normal"), and sings you a tune when the load is finished. :)

My ONLY gripe about this machine is that nearly every other load it will give me an "uneven load/UE" error. This has happened on large loads, small loads, medium loads, you name it. I will go down and re-distribute the clothes to re-balance it... sometimes this will fix it and the cycle will continue, other times I get several more UE errors until I give up and just toss them in the dryer (having no idea where it is in the process). I feel like this would be solved if the washer did have an agitator.

Another gripe is that, when I do experience the UE error, if I know that it was in the final "rinse" cycle of the wash, I will manually set the cycle to "spin only". If I get another UE error, the washer reverts back to "rinse and spin", filling it with more water in an attempt to redistribute clothing evenly...

All in all, this really is a great washer/dryer combo. No gripes, looks nice, easy to use, cleans clothes, quiet... just have to deal with that pesky UE error and walk down into my cold basement every time... ugh.

product_title: LG WT1201CV 4.5 Cu. Ft. Ultra-Large Capacity Front-Control Top-Load Washer with SlamProof Lid Â– Graphite Steel
review_text:
I have owned this washer (and the dryer that matches) for about 3 months now. I LOVE it. Some background:
Household Occupants: 6 + a dog, cats and other sundry animals.
Location: Rural hobby farm
Usual Cleaning Needs: Outdoor dirt, farm dirt, average amount of cat hair and women hair (shoulder length or longer)
Usual Load Size: Large
Child ages: 8-23 no, we are not the Duggars ;)
Replaced Washer Brand: Maytag Neptune (Worst machine I ever owned - did not clean well and twisted the clothes terribly when spinning out - but after 10 years with no mechanical issues I give Maytag credit)

I did try the Samsung almost top of the line model but it shook like crazy when spinning out and made weird rubbing noises when washing. I sent it back and a replacement was dented so I just figured it was a sign I needed to go with a different brand.

Enter the LG. I LOVE, LOVE, LOVE this washer and the matching dryer (my old dryer did not have enough cubic ft. to match the washer so I sold it and installed the LG. Make sure you think about that before you replace your washer alone)

Negative Issues:
Cleanliness: NONE
Unbalanced load: RARE (seems to happen with smaller loads so if you usually do smaller loads don't buy this machine. It's a waste of your money. If you do occasional smaller loads, just be cognizant of when the load is running and check on it to see if it gets unbalanced in the spin cycle. Not all my smaller loads do it.)
Tub Reachability: If you are 5' 6" or taller - NONE

Other Points to Consider:
Ease of Use: Very easy to operate. Some might not like that you have to push the Power On button every time you do a load but it's a non-issue for me. Everything is self explanatory and for all other things there is the manual.
Noise level: AVERAGE TO MINIMAL - This machine does make some noise when ramping up for a spin but really nothing that I wouldn't expect from any other washer and it is definitely quieter than my Maytag was (everyone though a rocket was lifting off for space). We have 2nd floor laundry with our bedrooms very close to the laundry area and we have no issues if the washer is working when we go to bed. When washing it is very quiet. It also does not have that annoying buzzer when the load is done, it plays a very nice little song. I don't think you can change the song (my friend has a front loader that has song options - this one does not) You can choose to turn it off completely.
Water amount needed for load: Good to Great (I like more water as the clothes do get cleaner and rinsed better)
Amount of space needed: A bit more than my last washer but worth it
Recommended Cleaning Detergent: I have used all natural powder soap as well as tide liquid soap and have had no issues. I did have an issue with the powder PODS. They don't like to break down in the detergent tray. They also don't like to break down when placed directly in the washer. So I would recommend you get loose powder if you are going to use powder.
Load Timing: Varies from 35 min (speed load) to 1hr 20min (soaking load)
Effectiveness of Spin: PHENOMENAL

Other things to consider would be if you do a lot of waterproof items or rugs with rubber backing. Check with the manufacturer to see if their product allows this. Some do not at all and some say ok if you low spin your items. This one is ok as long as it is not a lot of items in a load and you low spin them.

Also love the feature that lets the tub breathe without having to have the lid up. I have family that have front loaders and they stink to high heaven. ugh! You don't have to worry about that with this washer. Very well thought out.

Only drawback I have had so far is that you cannot choose every option for every load type. Some loads you cannot choose hot water for and some you cannot choose low spin for.

Otherwise I love the washer. Love the look, love the performance and love the pair. If you get this washer do seriously consider the matching dryer. It used to take 70 minutes in my Maytag gas dryer to dry my loads, now with this gas LG it takes half that time or LESS. Seriously, that much less. I am saving a ton of money on gas and electricity usage here. I NEVER have a load of wet clothes waiting for the dryer to finish anymore.

We purchased this at a local retailer.

Feel free to ask any questions - I would have no problem answering them.

product_title: GE GTDP200EFWS 6.8 Cu. Ft. White Electric Dryer
review_title: It has operated fine for me
review_text:
I have owned this model for 10 months. It has operated fine for me. I only use the timed setting, but there are also options for Permanent Press and Cottons. 60 minutes gets clothes dry, but you can run it up to 80 for larger/thicker loads.

I never wash extra large loads of clothes, so I'd probably be safe putting two washer loads in this dryer at the same time without exceeding the rating. My washing machine is only designed to handle 3.9 Cu. Ft., and this dryer is rated at 6.8 Cu. Ft.

The nicest feature of this dryer is the light inside the tub that is triggered to come on when I open the door. A light is such a simple, but thoughtful addition. That extra illumination ensures I don't leave a sock or some other small article of clothing behind.

The biggest design flaw of this dryer is location of the lint filter. It's positioned just below the access to the tub with no screen between the filter and the door. Whenever I open the door, the suction from the door causes bits of loose lint to come flying out all over the floor. Thankfully, I have a separate wash room. If this dryer was in a hallway, I'd need to vacuum after every load to keep the lint from getting all over the house. Having the filter inside the door like that might be a good reminder to clean out the lint after every load, but that's about the only advantage. If I were buying a dryer today, I'd go with another model due to this particular flaw in the design.

I purchased this dryer from Lowes when they had it on sale for $399. I bought the extended 3-year warranty, so the total was approximately $460. This model is currently priced $440 at Lowes without the warranty.

UPDATE 7/31/16: I am updating this review and reducing the rating from 3-stars to 2-stars. I have now owned this dryer for two years. About six months ago, the On switch became finicky and would not start the dryer. I finally figured out I can get it to start if I twist the button counterclockwise. I will be calling Lowes to see if they will repair this problem under the extended warranty I purchased at some point. All in all, my impression of this dryer is that it's not the greatest design, and the parts are cheap.

review_title: Steam sanitize cycle not what i thought
review_text: I have had this dryer for almost 6 months and am mostly satisfied.  I bought it based on reviews and features.  I like the anti-wrinkle and steam refresh cycles.  The dry-sensor is more accurate than on older models.  What I don't like is the manual.  It is not helpful.  I was having a problem with the refresh cycle. Following the manual exactly, the clothes were still coming out with big wet spots.  I called Samsung and a technician told me that the manual was wrong, I needed to put more items in the load.  Problem solved and those steam cycles work great.  But when I first used the steam sanitize cycle, it shut off after a few minutes.  The manual does not tell exactly how to use this cycle.  I was under the assumption, and so are many people judging by online comments, that this cycle was intended for dry items, just as the other 2 steam cycles are.  I wanted to steam some pillows. Luckily I have an extended warranty, so a technician came. He said it needed a new panel.  When this didn't fix it, he talked to his supervisor who said the items need to be WET.  This makes no sense to me. This cycle simply dries at a very high temp, then shoots out some water at the end.  I don't see how the result is any different from the regular sanitize cycle.  The moisture from the load plus the high heat would make steam.  I am very disappointed. I am writing this review mainly to make people aware that the steam sanitize cycle is not what one might expect.

product_title: Frigidaire Electric Washer/Dryer Laundry Center – White
review_text:
Purchased this item brand new from Lowe's, end of January 2013. This is my first washer/dryer combo with no center wash agitator.

When the machine is running properly, it's fantastic. The wash cycle is significantly quieter than other machines I've used. The knob selections leave you with very limited options as far as being able to influence the actual wash duration. I've noticed that the "normal" wash cycle typically takes up to an hour, which is significantly longer than other machines I've used.

The spin cycle on this machine is another story... It may very well be that I have a faulty machine, but when doing larger, heavier loads (i.e. towels, blankets) the machine gets extremely finicky. Sometimes it will run smoothly, but the majority of the time, it makes horrific clanging noises as if the wash bin is loose and thrashing around inside the machine, and the entire unit shakes and rattles wildly. Doing "normal" loads (shirts, pants etc.), I can load the machine to 80% capacity and it usually runs okay. But with heavier loads, if it's not under 50% capacity, the machine goes berserk.

I even had an authorized repairman take a look at the machine. He opened up the front panel and examined the machine under load and could not locate the source of the clanging noise.

Another limitation of the machine are the knob selections. For example, "rinse" and "spin" are a single selection. You can't just run the spin cycle to wring wet clothes, you are forced to run the clothes through a rinse cycle as well. This of course caused problems for myself and the repairman trying to trouble shoot the spin cycle because now we had to wait 10 minutes for the rinse cycle to complete...

Pausing the machine mid-cycle for any reason is also a no-no. Pushing the button to halt machine operation (for example, if the machine is banging around during spin cycle) will pause the machine, shortly after which it "resets" the cycle. So for example, if you pause the machine with 10 minutes remaining in the wash cycle, and you let it sit too long (3-5 minutes?), when you "resume" the wash cycle, it will just start all over again.

Regarding the lint trap itself is very small and clogs quickly. Is this a limitation of the dryer or are my clothes just linty? :p If the trap gets fully clogged, I would recommend clearing it and running the dryer cycle for a few more minutes or so in order to catch remaining lint.
Also, the dryer door has a spring in it which causes the door to close slowly when opened. This is extremely irritating when trying to put clothes into or take clothes out of the dryer.

PROS: Quiet operation (when it's working properly)
CONS: Noisy spin cycle (when it' not working properly), lack of options on the knob turn dials, small lint trap, dryer door automatically closes.

I will try to post a video shortly.

review_title: LG WT1201CW top-load-washer: very happy with it
review_text:
I read alot of reviews (on Amazon and elsewhere) on many makes and models, which led me to buying this washer (LG WT1201CW). In reviews I read people's most frequent complaint about High Efficiency (HE) washers seems to be they don't add enough water to cover the clothes. I found this to be true, seeing about 1/4 to 1/5 the height of the clothes being left exposed when beginning the wash cycle in a 'normal' mode. It seems strange especially when coming from a traditional non-HE washer (my old one broke down) that fills the tub enough to leave the clothes swimming in it. So for this new HE washer, what could I do to get more water in the wash cycle if I wanted it? I learned of a few tricks from others and from reading the manual/guides:

1. The quick reference guide that comes with the washer says to hold the Extra Rinse button for 3 seconds and it will add more water. I'm not sure if this added more water up front (seemed like it didn't) in the wash cycle, but tapping the Extra Rinse button once or twice did add noticeably ore water in the Rinse cycle (it allows up to 2 increases).

2. Start the machine, let it fill with water in the wash cycle. Shut it off. Start it again and it is tricked into thinking there is a heavier load (the weight sensor is what gages how much water the machine adds).

3. Start the washer in 'bulk' mode, which is used for bulky stuff like blankets and pillows. In this mode a lot of water is added, like is done with a traditional (non-HE) washer. I did this with my usual clothes load and it was like I had my old washer back. This feature alone would make all those complaints about lack of water go away.

4. Get a bucket of water and add it in with your clothes before hitting the Start button. This is easy if you have a wash sink nearby or another tap. You can add just enough water to top the clothes but even this extra amount will still result in using much less water than what you'd have by running in 'bulk' mode. You'd be semi-HE I guess.

If you find the machine's standard water-fill adequate, then by all means leave it alone because that is where you get your savings. Maybe having more water is only a placebo for those transitioning from the old traditional water-generous units. Then again it might not be.

As far as operation goes, I really like how quiet it runs, and it runs smooth with very little vibration. When vibrating it feels damped, and this is probably due to the excellent suspension system this machine seems to have. When installing the machine it's best to make sure it is as level as possible. You can use the legs to adjust each corner. The basket should look centered. I used a level to check it and the bubbles were centered even with the basket visually slightly off center. So its good to eyeball the basket too and try to perfect the level. I found it worth the extra effort.

Another tip I was told is that in HE machines you use very little soap and fabric softener, like 1/3 of what is used for a load in traditional washers. I reduced my usage this way and the clothes came out clean and fresh.

Finally, it is very worthwhile to read the manual even though the machine can be used intuitively. The manual tells you how to optimize its performance for the various types of fabrics out there. Or, you can keep it simple and run it like your old washer by using 'bulk' mode for everything.

I gave this LG washer 5-stars because it works great and it shouldn't be penalized for annoying 'water efficiency' that is mandated by the US Government.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW5800BW 3.8 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: The Worst Washing Machine ever Manufactured...by anyone...
review_text:
This washer is defectively engineered. Whirlpool wanted to create a top loading, water sparing machine, so their idea was to come up with a tiny agitator on the bottom of the tank and allow it to "wobble" to force the water through the clothing. The water used for washing does not cover the clothing, and the agitator kind of tries to move the water through the clothing.

That does NOT happen. The clothes do NOT come out clean. I suppose it is possible to wash similar size, small items like underwear in it. But you can't mix clothing or bedding types in the same load.

Compare this pathetic machine with a modern front load washer that uses gravity to tumble the clothes against each other in two directions, as well as allowing them to soak momentarily on the bottom of the tub with each change of direction. You can't help but wash the clothes.

Cabrio runs the clothing through a very thorough rinse cycle, trying to make up for the deficiencies of washing. The clothes get all tangled and knotted up. It also unbalances easily as a washed sheet will eventually gather up smaller items into a ball and the agitator will just smash against that ball of sheet and underwear.

I submitted my review to Whirlpool and I suggested they redesign the washer and tilt the clothing tub to a 35% angle, which would start to use gravity...but that would expand the footprint of the machine. They said no-way and took my review off line.

I sent mine back after 4 days and paid the restocking fee. It is the worst washer made. You'd be better off using your great-grandmother's washer with an attached hand wringer. (Watch your fingers). There have also been technical, electrical and mechanical problems with it, even after a short term of ownership.

I got a Maytag front loader instead, and it works great.

I think the Cabrio is best used as land-fill.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW5800BW 3.8 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Do not purchase this HE washer
review_text:
I tried to post review on Whirlpool site but it never was approved. That would explain majority of the positive reviews on their site. We purchased our washer/dryer set at Costco since they have a wonderful return policy. This set is going back because of the washer. The actual washer model is 5810BW which is made specifically for Costco. It is the same as 5800 BW sold here. This washer does not rinse the detergent out of our laundry. After the first use whole family was itching because of the detergent left in the laundry. We have been using the same detergent for many years and in fact we used up most of this bottle with our old washer. I also am aware of differences between HE and regular machines and specifically checked instructions on the amount of detergent to use. It is Kirkland Signature HE detergent so it is designed for this washer. After the first fiasco I started using less detergent - 1/2 to 1/8 of recommended amount. The itching stopped but if our laundry had any stains they would not come out. With our old washer (also Whirlpool and also from Costco) I just had to pre-treat with a Shout spray and toss it in the washer. All stains would usually come out. With this washer I had to wash one t-shirt 3 times to get a stain out. How is this saving water? I also use additional rinse cycle for all of the loads because I have no desire to itch again. How is this helping with the water use?
I took a video of the washing cycle since the washer has a glass lid. You can clearly see the white item sitting on top of the load throughout the whole washing cycle. Small items do circulate through detergent but larger items stay in one position and do not move. When I hand wash items I also do not submerge them in to the water and rub. I use a little detergent and rub the item against itself, but this is not what this washer does. The washer just moves its "washplate" back and forth and wet items just vibrate on it.
I use dress shirts from Costco which are treated with water repellent. This washer cannot get this shirt wet on normal cycle. I have to use deep water cycle to even get the shirt wet. First time I did not believe my eyes - had to open the lid and make sure that part of the shirt was dry at the end of the wash cycle! The heavier items like bath towels do not get clean and stink after the first use. This rarely happened with our old washer. And don't get me started on the "spray rinse". I am not sure who came up with this concept and what it actually rinses. If you watch videos of Samsung or LG HE top loaders, these washers have a nozzle which sprays water ON your laundry that is stuck to the sides of the drum after a spin cycle. I can see how this can do something like rinse. This washer just pours water at the center of the drum from where it happily drains in to the holes in the bottom. How this can possibly rinse anything is way past my understanding. There is no way to overwrite any of the settings or add a little water.
The sensing process is unreliable. If I put few small items, the washer will add a lot of water, 5 inches or more, and the items would be swimming. It I put larger item, like a towel, it will absorb all the water and there would be almost no water in the tub. Ether this technology is bad or Whirlpool's implementation is bad.
The only good thing I can say about this washer is that it spins laundry very well. The laundry comes out much drier and therefore dryer does finishes much faster. This is well compensated by washer taking more that twice as long as our old "inefficient" washer did. I should have fixed our old washer instead of buying this new one, more so since I already diagnosed what the problem was. We thought to update our 14 year old set with the new one - what a mistake.

As I understand it is the government that is mandating these water and energy savings. How about starting from the government itself? On my way to work I see on-ramps being watered every morning, being that it is drought in California and all. How about saving water there? Also mandate more water efficient landscapes instead of planting grass everywhere. I wish the government would stay the heck out of my laundry room.

You can clearly see the white item sitting on top of the load throughout the whole washing cycle. Small items do circulate through detergent but larger items stay in one position and do not move. When I hand wash items I also do not submerge them in to the water and rub. I use a little detergent and rub the item against itself, but this is not what this washer does. The washer just moves its washplate back and forth and wet items just vibrate on it. I use dress shirts from Costco which are treated with water repellent. This washer cannot get this shirt wet on normal cycle. I have to use deep water cycle to even get the shirt wet. First time I did not believe my eyes - had to open the lid and make sure that part of the shirt was dry at the end of the wash cycle! The heavier items like bath towels do not get clean and stink after the first use. This rarely happened with our old washer. And don't get me started on the spray rinse . I am not sure who came up with this concept and what it actually rinses. If you watch videos of Samsung or LG HE top loaders, these washers have a nozzle which sprays water ON your laundry that is stuck to the sides of the drum after a spin cycle. I can see how this can do something like rinse. This washer just pours water at the center of the drum from where it happily drains in to the holes in the bottom. How this can possibly rinse anything is way past my understanding. There is no way to overwrite any of the settings or add a little water. The sensing process is unreliable. If I put few small items, the washer will add a lot of water, 5 inches or more, and the items would be swimming. It I put larger item, like a towel, it will absorb all the water and there would be almost no water in the tub. Ether this technology is bad or Whirlpool's implementation is bad. The only good thing I can say about this washer is that it spins laundry very well. The laundry comes out much drier and therefore dryer does finishes much faster. This is well compensated by washer taking more that twice as long as our old inefficient washer did. I should have fixed our old washer instead of buying this new one, more so since I already diagnosed what the problem was. We thought to update our 14 year old set with the new one - what a mistake. As I understand it is the government that is mandating these water and energy savings. How about starting from the government itself? On my way to work I see on-ramps being watered every morning, being that it is drought in California and all. How about saving water there? Also mandate more water efficient landscapes instead of planting grass everywhere. I wish the government would stay the heck out of my laundry room.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW5800BW 3.8 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Wonderful results if you can unlearn what you “Know” about washing
review_text:
It has only been a short while, but I love this washing machine. It uses fewer resources (water and soap) and my clothes are cleaner.

I have read the critics of this machine. I want to respond to some of the complaints. First, it IS louder than my traditional washer. This is not a big deal to me. Is it really a big deal? Next, each load may take longer. What is your rush?
I may get flamed for this, but my guess is that the folks that have an issue with this dryer are not following the directions and/or are clinging to lessons that were true with earlier washing machine technology. In many cases, they return perfectly good machines. This drives up the cost of all of us. I would like to see folks study the manual and call for help before demanding the retailer take back a perfectly good product.

Some people claim it leaves soapy residue. My guess is that they were using up their non-HE soap. In general, HE likes liquid detergent. Powders, which have traditionally been more effective, struggle to dissolve properly in this environment. Try skipping all the powders and see if you are happy. (Sorry Oxi Clean). Also, it is important to use LESS soap. This is hard for some of us that were brought up on MORE soap=CLEANER clothes. This was true. It is not true with HE washing machines.

Other people complain that their clothes were still wet after the spin dry. My guess is that they used the wrong cycle. I have not seen any evidence of this problem, although it was mentioned by reviewers on other boards.

All in, this washing machine is a great, entry level HE washing machine.

Buying these was a serious mistake. It won't be repeated.

The "timer" that tells you how much time remains actually ADDS time....so if you think it will be 59 minutes to wash your clothes and then you look 10 minutes later...it will say 56 minutes.

This thing is such an amazing piece of junk that LG should get out of the appliance business.

I don't write many reviews, but I wrote this to warn others.

DO NOT BUY this.

The electronics and smart features slow your wash down to a crawl...it is just junk.

Stink to a tried and true brand like Kenmore or Whirlpool -- and skip the ridiculous electronics.

I literally despise this product. IF YOU WASH YOUR CLOTHES WITH this even once, you will be full of anger.

It truly stinks that bad.

...and they dryer can't handle the load that you might put in the dryer....and the dryer is as slow as molasses.

These LG products absolutely stink.

They LOOK cool...and the nice bells and whistles are fun and interesting for about 1 day....and then when you are left with a slow as molasses washer that does a horrendous job -- a "load" balance system that takes forever and forever to analyze, re-analyze, analyze again....before it does a half-a**ed job of attempting to wash your clothes....OH MY GOD.

YOU WILL DEEPLY REGRET THIS PURCHASE.

What you want in a washer is speed, capacity, vigorous washing and not endless whirring about doing nothing.

...and a dryer needs at least as large a capacity as the wash....a large enough tumble space to aerate the clothes (so they don't just end up in a damp heap) and speed.

THESE PRODUCTS ARE TRULY HORRENDOUS.

Stick to simple, powerful, heavy duty and fast....

The electronic locking lid on the Washer will drive you absolutely insane.

If you think this experience is a unique one, be sure to do you own research.

http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/lg_washing_machine.html

There are even videos describing how bad these machines are.

I have no axe to grind with LG, but these products are truly terrible.

I grew up with Kenmore, Maytag and Whirlpool. They were built like tanks, were fast and got out all the dirt without fuss or muss....

These "modern" applicances are so aggravating, I'd rather a stone and a puddle.

product_title: LG WT5680HWA TurboWash 5.2 Cu. Ft. White With Steam Cycle Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
After our front load washer broke 4 times in 8 years, I decided it was time for a change. Now I can only wonder why we didn't do this sooner!

After pouring over reviews and consumer ratings on multiple sites/sources for days, I finally decided to purchase this machine for several reasons. Hopefully, the amount of research I did prior to our purchase can help someone else limit theirs. ;)

The first reason I chose this machine is because it's a top loader. I never loved our front loading machine because of the maintenance requirements, and consistent stale smell from wet lint, dog hair etc. that would be left behind in the rubber gasket.

The next reason was because this model has a soak cycle available. When I gave up 'soaking' at the time we purchased our front loading machine, I had no idea how much I would miss having it. With active kids, sports stains, etc, it was a must-have for us.

The last reasons I selected this machine was it's huge capacity (for handling our king size bedding) and warranty.

I admittedly was concerned by the 'out of balance' reviews and comments indicating the lack of water used in these top loading HE machines... I just couldn't help but wonder if it would be enough to get items truly clean. So much so, I almost opted for another front loader but ultimately decided since this model offered a 'water plus' feature (essentially allowing you add additional water) coupled with Best Buy's 14 day return policy, I would give it a shot. After muliple loads of wash, including several very large loads, I can honestly say I have no concerns whatsoever by the amount of water being used and am thrilled with how clean the clothes have come out.

All in all, I'm very happy with the purchase. Although it was expensive and I haven't gotten to use all the cycles yet, this machine appears to be a keeper. We did purchase an extended warranty, which for us, is uncommon. But, based on the track record of appliances these days, especially our prior washer, it's piece of mind if nothing else.

Good luck!

product_title: LG WT5680HWA TurboWash 5.2 Cu. Ft. White With Steam Cycle Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
This review encompasses both the LG Washer/Dryer I purchased. I have been shopping for a larger capacity and QUIETER (main requirement) washer/dryer combination. Was replacing a pair of 6-yr old Maytag appliances and although they still worked well, the noise was annoying. After a couple of months shopping, comparing, and watching prices fall I settled on the LG DLEX5680W (Dryer) and WT5680HWA (washer).

Recommendations: Read the manuals (LOL) and you will find them quite easy to operate.

Washer: EXCEPTIONALLY QUIET! Have only done a few loads so far but with the door to the laundry room open and me sitting in the living room (30’ away) I only hear the bells telling me the load is done. Seems to clean clothes as good as any other washers, will be trying comforters soon.

Dryer: EXCEPTIONALLY QUIET! Seems like my drying time has been reduced by about 20% and am looking forward to the larger drying capacities.

Tip: This set is SMALLER than my older Maytag’s (both width and depth) but slightly higher. I made allowances for the dimensions EXCEPT for the washer height with the lid raised (DUH). The lid hits my storage cabinets above the washer by 1/4 of an inch. A minor pain and does not interfere with the lid being open @ 98% of the way. So watch the height dimensions too.

product_title: LG WT5680HWA TurboWash 5.2 Cu. Ft. White With Steam Cycle Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
My (Front Load) Whirlpool Duett broke down after 8 good years of great service. I was told it would be too costly to repair and that all front loaders stink. So in good faith I started to look at the alternative...a top loader! I did my research online, looked at different machines in the store and came up with a favs list of the things my 'new baby' had to have. I decided on this LG. I read alot of the reviews, too! Once it was delivered, I read the manual, loaded it just like they say in the book (because ppl online kept complaining about the wastefullness of water to balance the load and how long it would take to wash one load due to that fact), then I started washing different types of loads..big and bulky, sanitary, heavy duty and of course the normal. People were right, it is very deep. I am not a short person, just average 5'7, but I really had to stretch to pick up the stuff from the bottom of the drum. I stood there and watched this thing do its job... making a long story short, I don't like to use the word hate, so I will say I VERY MUCH DISLIKE this machine! While in sanitary, my clothes just floated in water while the tub was sloooowly going around and around and around. That went on for quiet a while until I got borred and walked away, came back to watch it float some more and left again lol
Then I washed my sons cheap, very thin and lite nylon/polyester full size summer comforter, fitted queen sheet and 2 std sized pillow cases. This water wasting beast required THE WHOLE TUB being filled with water. I mean come on now...5.2 cu. Ft of water for just a small little maybe half size load? I am sure my Utility Co would love me for using all this water, but my pockets aren't that deep! The manual says it weighs the load in the beginning? Well I guess the scale was incorrect in my case!? The rest of the other loads I washed came up short too. Most of my clothes were barely moved during the cycles. Coming from a front loader, I am used to see my clothes being tumbled around, all equally being swooshed and turned in the water. If I wanted my clothes washed gently and barely wet, I would have used the delicate cycle. So neatless to say this machine has its water usage all mixed up and I am exchanging it today for another front loader. So happy about my 30 day exchange policy!
When the sales man that sold me this machine saw me and I told him how much I 'disliked' the LG, he told me "Once a front loader, always a front loader" I just wish he would have told me that before, not after the fact!

review_title: You had one job, Bosch dryer...  One job!
review_text: I didn't buy this from Amazon, but I felt I needed to provide a public review after purchasing one of these units at our local Lowe's store and losing our minds trying to get a small batch of kids clothing dry.  This thing has a bunch of sensors in it that automatically shut it off when it thinks the load is dry.  The problem is that we normally will wash socks, poly blend shirts, cotton tees, and cargo shorts all in the same load.  It seems some of these fabrics dry quicker than others and trip the sensors before things like cotton cargo shorts are anywhere near dry.  It was super frustrating, and we are returning the unit two days after purchasing it in favor of repairing our old Meile Novotronic which never left us trying to trick the unit into running long enough to get all the clothes dry.  Bosch really missed the mark on understanding the use patterns for dryers in the US market.  This is a pricy unit, with low capacity, and isn't effective at completing it's sole purpose for existing.  It failed us only slightly less spectacularly than the Viking dishwasher we purchased several years ago that ultimately led To us placing our faith in the Bosch appliance brand, as Bosch does manufacture a stellar dishwasher.  I wouldn't recommend this to anyone, though it does meet a specific niche market for compact ventless dryers.

A Bosch compact pair (each 24 inches wide) has been great for 15 years, and the dryer just died, and I replaced it with this unit so I could still plug the old Bosch washer into the dryer for power. Bosch is only making ventless dryers now, and I bought this against my better judgment because the reviews of the ventless dryers have been terrible. Bosch apparently went to ventless because of new regulations about lint fires in ducted dryers.

This dryer is great! The automatic sensor is adjustable for different levels of dryness. It is faster than the previous vented Bosch dryer, and the clothes come out perfect. The fact that the washer spins to 1200 means the clothes are already pretty dry. If your washer does not spin at 1200, that might explain why clothes would take a long time to dry in this dryer. The condensation unit at the bottom of the dryer drains into a hose which empties into the same drain as the washer. (If you have a 3 prong outlet, the manual shows how you can rewire the dryer for a 3 plug cord, or you can replace the outlet) . Some warm dry air is emitted from the dryer and we use it to help heat the house when it is cold.Why waste this source of heat? In the summer I will direct the warm air into the garage or turn on the exhaust fan in the laundry room.

In short, we are thrilled with this dryer. We have only had it a short time, and hope it will last as long as its predecessor.

review_text:

There is one MAJOR advantage to this dryer. Living in a drought-prone area, I put the drain hose into a bucket and recover one to two gallons of water from each load that I use to irrigate my garden. Clean clothes, happy tomatoes. What's not to love?

product_title: Samsung DV50F9A6EVW Electric Front Load Dryer with Steam Dry, 7.4 Cubic Feet, Neat White
review_text: We bought a $1000 Samsung model #DV52J8700EP/A2 dryer just over a year ago.  The dryer comes with a 1 year warranty, but naturally, things start going wrong after the warranty expires.  The dryer was making a squealing noise that sounded like metal grinding on metal.  It would make the noise periodically, but got worse over the course of a couple of weeks.  All of a sudden, there was a loud bang and the drum wouldn’t turn any more.  First thing I thought of was that the drive belt had broken.  When I removed the back panel to inspect it, the belt was fine – it was the tension pulley that had broken.  I should say, rather melted.  A cheap plastic pulley was what kept the belt tension tight.  It had been melted by the friction on the bracket it is mounted to.  Even more scary was the fact that there was a wiring harness directly beneath it.  Had the pulley melted and gotten hot enough, it could have burned through the insulation on the wires and caused a short or possibly a fire.  I called Samsung to explain the situation and how dangerous it was, and all they said they would have to send a technician (about $150) to inspect it (they direct you to another website to schedule service instead of talking to you).  The whole bracket assembly is held together with 1 screw and 1 spring.  I managed to locate the part at an appliance store, but had to spend $40 for the whole bracket assembly for a $1 plastic pulley.  The person at the appliance store said that they were cheaply made and he had people buying them all the time for the same reason.  It took about 10 minutes for me to replace using only a screwdriver and a pair of pliers.  I would have been really upset to pay a technician that kind of money to remove a screw and spring and then put it back on. The whole situation could have been avoided had Samsung spent a couple of dollars more and used a metal pulley instead of a plastic one.  All of the parts are cheaply made, and I expect more repairs in the future.  The pulley will last about a year under normal circumstances, so I expect to spend another $40 in about a year, provided I will be able to find the bracket again.  Their customer service was a joke.  All they did was constantly apologize that there was nothing they could do but send a technician and offered no help whatsoever.  In my opinion, spending $1000 on a dryer that is made in China with cheap parts – I’ll never buy a Samsung product again.  Don’t waste your time or money on them.

First, let me say that I rarely write a review unless the purchase/product is exceptionally good or exceptionally bad. Happily, this purchase falls in the "exceptionally good" category. So, let me run down the reasons that I have been pleased so far with this purchase:

1. Shipping speed. We ordered this set around noon on a Tuesday. Within an hour or so, I received the shipping confirmation. The next day, Wednesday, I received a call from the trucking company to set up a delivery time for the following day, Thursday. The washer/dryer set was delivered before noon on Thursday. That totally blew me away!

2. Packaging. The washer, dryer and two pedestals were, as I expected, packaged separately. What I didn't expect was the quality of the engineered packaging. It was pretty amazing and, as a result, these heavy units came out of the packaging completely unscathed.

3. Installation instructions. They were clear, fairly concise, and not cluttered up with pages and pages of "lawyer speak" safety instructions which often seem to be designed not to make the product installation safer but, rather, to limit the manufacturer's liability in case of an accident.

4. Energy efficiency. Yes, I knew that these were HE appliances but when I read on the Energy Guide that the total cost to operate the washer for a year was only $12, I was in disbelief. Honestly, I'm still somewhat skeptical but that's what it said.

5. Operation. I would never have believed that a washer/dryer could be so quiet if I had not heard it (barely) with my own ears. They are amazingly quiet. Our wash room contains the washer, dryer and a large upright freezer. Honest to goodness, I can hear the freezer running over the washer and dryer. review_text:
My 30-year-old Kenmore dryer (wow!) was on its last legs, so I researched on line reviews and Consumer Reports. The Samsung DV56H9100GG was well-regarded, but CR listed it as #1 which sealed the deal for me. I bought mine at Home Depot and they delivered it within the week.

I've been using my new dryer for several months and it is quite a step up over the old Kenmore. It is very quiet and energy efficient. Plus there are a variety of spiffy drying options that weren't there in the old days: a "Wrinkle Prevent" to keep clothes looking good if you can't get back to the dryer in time; "Wrinkle Away" for clean stuff that just needs a spritzing and tumble dry; a variety of settings for anything from light blouses to heavy towels and bedding, and an illuminated drum so you can see what you are doing. They even include a drying rack for tennis shoes, toys, etc., though I usually just stick stuff like that out on the back porch to dry.

The Samsung dryer is several inches taller than my old Kenmore, which makes me glad I didn't buy the pedestal that raises it off the floor; I don't think it would have fit in my available space and I certainly couldn't fold stuff on the top surface. In any case, check the dimensions of your laundry area before buying.

This Samsung dryer looks O.K. (shrug, it IS basically a big box) and appears well made. It sounds cute soft musical tones and tunes to signal different features. The "load finished" tune is rather long and resembles (to me) an 8-bit version of a "Pirates of the Caribbean" drinking song. ;) The lint trap is tucked on the door edge for easy access. Unfortunately, my new dryer door opens to the right and it appears to be a tremendous hassle--possibly impossible--to change the hinge direction.

This is a pricey critter and if I ever have a problem I'll post an update immediately. I doubt I'll get 30 years like I did with my old Kenmore, but this is a really nice clothes dryer. Five stars.

product_title: Samsung WF42H5200AW Energy Star 4.2 Cu. Ft. Front-Load Steam Washer with SelfClean, White
review_text: Perhaps the reason for all the negative reviews is a front load learning curve problem... this is my first front loader, and the transition from water-soaked top load agitator washing is apples and oranges.  No, it doesn't use a tub full of water, float the clothes and beat them to death.  On my first front load, my clothes and towels smelled dirty and felt like cardboard after the washer/dryer cycle.  Here's what will give you front load success.  Switch to powder detergent (HE only) for a short time -buy a small box- and don't use more than line 1 on the scoop for any load.  The powder is more forgiving if you use too much detergent, which is exactly what I was doing.  You CANNOT use the amount recommended on the detergent container.  Less water = less detergent.  DO use fabric softener, half capful.  Don't be afraid of gumming up your machine or other horror stories.  The high spin speeds render clothing less than desirably soft, although dramatically cut down drying time!  In the dryer, use MEDIUM heat and your MOISTURE SENSOR, which works very well (I have the matching dryer).  The towels I thought I had ruined by blasting them dry on high heat and a timed cycle are now soft and fluffy again.  My whites have NEVER been so white, and I do not use bleach.  I also do not use vinegar that so many seem to swear by in the rinse cycle.  I use the Normal cycle for most loads and use HOT for whites, STEAM for extremely nasty items (anything sweat or dirt-soaked), and WARM for everything else.  Cycle time is around an hour except for steam, about 1.5 hours.  Dry time is 45-55 minutes for HUGE loads.  My laundry is sweet-smelling, clean, fresh and soft again.  I'm never going back.  My water bill is down $10 a month and I've reduced my loads from 10 a week to 6.  I've run the clean cycle once and just got the reminder to do it again, which I do while I'm sleeping. I clean the detergent drawer and leave the washer door open when I'm done for the day.  Bottom line - if your stuff stinks, you're using way too much detergent. Be patient - it's going to take several powder loads to get rid of all the excess that's stuck in your clothes, but you will win in the end : )

review_title: You will repair this washer every 2-4 years
review_text:
I bought this on Amazon around four years ago. I am repairing this machine for a second time for the same problem. It has a defective design on the central drum bearning. That's the part that allows the drum to fit in the motor/drive housing and spin. Over a two to three year period of running normally these bearings will go out and they will need to be replaced.

You can buy a new bearning kit for around $80 and repair it yourself if you're VERY good at repairing things. You will need to:
1) Completely dismantle the machine.
2) Lift the drum assembly which is very heavy. You must use a pully or have other people help. You will likely get hurt if you try this without ample help or equipment.
3) Dismantle the drum assembly and remove the bearings. This requires a machine press or a hammer and pin and lots of patience.
4) Insert the new bearing with the same amount of equipment and patience.
5) Reassemble the entire machine (all of it... the gaskets, hoses, shock absorbers, wiring harnesses, control panel, etc.).

Or, you can do 90% of the disassembly noted above and spend $300+ on an entirely new drum assembly.

Or, you can spend even more than that to have a professional repair it or buy a new machine.

I would advise against buying this machine.

If you have this machine already and hear it sounding like an airplane taking off then chances are this problem is happening to you. If you have the persistence to fix this as I've mentioned above then I suggest you look online for a video on how to do this repair. I bought the service manual from Samsung (which is a horror story all by itself) but it didn't help as much as the videos online.

review_text: My problem with this set is not so much function, but form and fit. They are HUGE, and have negatively impacted the utility of our small laundry room. The curved tops make them worthless as a work surface. They scratch easily (and I'm not even putting anything on top, due to the curving). You have to bend over the washer control panel to retrieve the laundry, so if you have to open it mid cycle, to adjust the load (which happens frequently), you will probably zero out the setting and need to start the load over. You will have to soak your clothes (a hint I found online) AND hit the water + function every single time to maybe have enough water for the clothes to move freely and have a chance in hell of getting clean. If you throw a folded handkerchief in this washer, it will still be folded when it comes out - all that does is rehydrate the boogers. The dryer at least does its job without special care and handling, but I can't recommend it because of its curved top, excessive size and excessive price.
