review_title: My issue is it is so easy to be unbalanced
review_text:
Bought this from a chain store to replace my front load machine. This fit the space in the laundry room with a larger capacity.
After a few months of use I am dissatisfied with the purchase. It does clean clothes as well as a front loader. My issue is it is so easy to be unbalanced. I installed it as directed but almost every load shows an uneven error message.
I find myself playing Tetris to place clothes in just right so the spin cycle doesn't go to an "UE" uneven load error message.
This machine was bought to handle large loads with minimal water. When UE happens the machine fills the tub to near capacity to even the load. A 1 hour wash cycle lasts for hours.
I would never buy this again and would re-buy a front load.
I only gave this a 2 star because it does clean clothes.

review_title: Once the water loads it splish-splashes like someone is in there taking a bath in it
review_text: This washer has too many cycles to choose from and too many options within each cycle.  You may desire a certain cycle and certain options but for that cycle but you cannot select the option you want because it is pre-set. If I were to use Manual Speed wash for every cycle which allows you the freedom to select more options, what's the use in having purchased this high end machine?  This washer is very noisy and makes an array of strange sounds.  Once the water loads it splish-splashes like someone is in there taking a bath in it. Then it spins so hard it sounds out of control (literally shakes but the balance indicator does not come on so I figure it's what it's supposed to do), but it sounds like it is ready to take off for the moon; it's actually scary.  When your cycle is complete it plays a little dainty little sing-song tune that lasts maybe 3 seconds.  If you are not near you will not hear it and that is the only indictor you get.  No mechanical or washing performance problems have been encountered since my purchase date of October 2014 from Lowes.  It was supposed to take 2 weeks to get it, that got pushed to 4 weeks, 6 weeks later we got it.  It came over on a ship from Korea thus I was not able to get a look at it at time of purchase but trusted the LG brand.  I do love the no agitator feature of this top loader, and the very large capacity drum for easily washing blankets and sheets, and doubling up some loads.  But because I am 5' tall I must hoist myself up, over and in a little to reach to the very bottom of the drum to retrieve small items like socks and underware.  I rated this washer a 3 because it is new technology, energy saving, and I respect all that, and, it does do the job.  My message to the manufacturer would be to get back to basics and make this chore more simplified with less cycle options.  All we need is a normal wash cycle, delicates cycle, and the ability to dial in the amount of time we desire for the load so we can get going on other things instead of trying to select a correct cycle for each type of load we are washing.  I literally made a chart for myself to refer to for doing each type of load - lights, darks, bleach, towels, delicates etc and which cycle and options it allows me to select.  A 2 might be a more accurate rating but I am hopeful I will get more accustomed to the machine as time goes on and like it at least as a 3 star rating.  Same goes for its complimentary dryer.  Too many cycles and the end alert plays a 3 second sing-song tune that you cannot hear unless you are nearby.  I prefer the annoying ding-ding-ding of my old dryer that went on and on but I surely heard it at some point and retrieved my clothing promptly.

review_title: love it 90% of the time, hate the fatal flaw 10% of the time
review_text: We've had a model similar to this, the Cabrio WTW8040 for about 4 months now.  We've been really happy with it but we just discovered a problem which is a real deal breaker on this thing.  While we like all the features and size and new user interface it turns out there isn't a drain & spin setting on any of these Cabrio washers.  The least you can do is rinse & spin.  The problem is with a large and bulky item in the washer it will be out of balance during a rinse cycle and then it will fail to spin, stop, and leave you with a soaking dripping item.  The washer gives up, stops, and wont resume the cycle.  You can sort it out where it's in balance again but there isn't a way to just make it spin - you have to rinse and spin again so it will become unbalanced again during the rinse cycle.  It's maddening.  You effectively can't wash anything big.  We won't be buying one of these again.

I am returning this set tomorrow, but I am back to square one without a washer and dryer. Thanks, Whirlpool 😡

review_text:
I am EXTREMELY disappointed in this purchase.

First of all, the shipper you used to send this product to me is based in Brooklyn, NY, and used a third party shipper here in Illinois. The third party shipper that made final delivery was not very flexible to my work schedule, and therefore was unable to deliver the washer and dryer until today, 14 full days after the originally promised delivery date. Even if I was unemployed and sitting at home 24/7/365, the earliest attempt they made at delivering the items was a full WEEK after the promised date.

Secondly, and MOST IMPORTANTLY....the dryer is not working.

Although there was no visible shipping damage, the dryer is NOT operating. There is a problem with the electric motor being seized, or being held in position so that it cant move when electrical power is applied to the circuit. I am extremely mechanically inclined and re read the install instructions multiple times. There are no shipping bolts holding the drum from moving. But it is clear that when the motor is electrically energized, something is preventing it from being able to turn the drum.

Troubleshooting with Samsung has been underwhelming to say the least.

Less than 4 hours into ownership of this premium top of the line product, a warranty repair has already been scheduled.

Pretty pathetic if you ask me!

review_text: I bought this because it was the best price, I saved at least 600 bucks buying from Amazon vs in store at Best Buy/Lowes/etc. The washer was delivered about a week after I ordered it, and the delivery company was good and put the washer in the garage. The delivery company charges another 100 dollars for installation, so instead I called a local handy man who did it for about 20. The washer and dryer is VERY large, so I will take measurements of doorways and hallways before purchasing. I didn't do so and we just barely got it inside, and we had to remove a door to do so. In the laundry room the unit is big and deep, but the loss of space is so worth it. It washes so much better than anything I've ever used. I love that I can throw in my comforter and it will wash it fully. I was even able to throw in a 3x5 rug that I couldn't get clean for the life of me, and now its like brand new! The dryer is also very good, and I noticed our clothes no longer shrink in the dryer like it used to. Do note that you will need a way to get water into the dryer as well as the washer, since the dryer has the steam function. Also, VERY IMPORTANT, remember to remove the shipping bolts on the back of the washer once you get it into place. Our installer didn't do this, and when I tried to run a load, it was shaking so violently that it came forward about 5 to 6 inches. Once I removed them, it worked like a charm.

product_title: LG WM4270HWA TurboWash 4.5 Cu. Ft. White Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
This washing machine is a bit of an enigma. It is one of the few front loading washing machines within my price point that has three, yes three, additional rinse cycles and this alone was critical in my decision making process as I have severe allergies. So LG won major points here! And while it throughly cleans clothes extremely well (as with all new HE washers), it has one major flaw....if you home has high water pressure you will have the infamous "water hammer"! This is a major design flaw with many new HE front loaders and if you purchase this one, you must also purchase a water hammer resister to keep you pipes from thumping when the machine is cycling. Water hammer resisters are only $10.00 each but it's the principle that matters. I would have given this machine 5 stars as it cleans like none other, can accept a large volume of clothing articles; will save on water, electricity, and offers a myriad of wash cycle options to include its on onboard water heater, but it's the need to purchase additional equipment that influenced my decision.

Update 5.8.2017: I am updating this as a forewarning to potential LG customers. I've had this washer now for a less than 2 years of time and the design flaw reported which did not properly address those with high water pressure finally gave way. Thank God I purchased the extended warranty as my "intake cold water valve" gave way several weeks ago. It's amazing that LG's replacement part was redesigned. Hmm imagine that! I believe that LG redesigned this part due to a plethora of issues with this washer. The kicker is that my infamous "water hammer" issue has been minimized by the replacement part. This machine cleans very well and I really like the customized wash settings but before you even think about purchasing any LG (or other brand for that matter) do your homework! Hope this helps!

review_title: Water hammer is an absolute must buy with it.
review_text:
When LG washer & gas dryer set was installed, I didn't know why there was a huge knocking and banging sound from the washer and the hot & cold water pipes were shaking violently. Thanks to TJORD, I saw that I was missing two $10 water hammer units that takes the sudden decrease in pressure from the HE washing machine. Don't expect Home Depot to tell you that you need these water hammer unit before the connection to the water hoses.

I went with the white color since it was $100 cheaper than the gray version. So far, it is working great as it gets my cloths clean like from commercial laundry mats and the matching gas dryer works great at drying my clothes. These are at least 8 inches longer in depth than traditional washers and dryers, but it saves much more in water and electricity use. The top and side covers are made of steel with paint coating which address a complaint I saw on Samsung washers and dryers that use plastic and it discolored from laundry detergent landing on it. When the washer is in use, a red icon lights up and you can't open the washer door until you pause it or turn it off.

review_text:
Best machines on the market at this price bracket.

Before I go in to my own review, I want to point out (as per the comments on both his reviews) that Amazon reviewer "Steve" who has posted two identical negative reviews actually own a DIFFERENT MODEL (WM2650HRA, a cheaper and older unit). It seems he's cluster bombing any LG models on Amazon with this review and posting it twice - While he may be frustrated with his models, it's completely misleading for anyone looking at these machines because they are incredible.

My review: We needed new machines for home and I just wnated the best of the best. Sadly, since Maytag flooded the market with cheap machiens the high end of the market has narrowed considerably. I was advised by my local appliance store to buy Electrolux units (EIFLS60LT Washer & EIMED60LT dryer). It turned out to be the single worst purchase of any device in my lifetime; I won't go it in to here but after a year long battle with ElectroSUXS, 11 technician visits and 60+ hours of my life I'll never get back, they finally and begrudgingly sent replacements....which turned out to be BROKEN.

Thankfully the silver lining of this was the opportunity to get my money back from them! After a lot of research, which firstly involved talking to the various technicians that were coming to attempt to fix the Electrosuxs units, every single one said "LG", without even hesitating "easy and cheap to fix, if they ever need it" was the same response from each one.

So I got these units from LG (WM4270 range) and after 4 months of use, I could not be happier. So much, that I just ordered a second pair for my business, even though the warranty doesn't cover commercial use. I don't care - they're that good.

Firstly, HUGE drum size, yet small overall unit footprint. I can do 15-20 large, soaking wet towels without them even flinching. They also have a ton of of programs but they keep it simple on the dial. If you want to customize the programs then you can easily, using the little matrix buttons for each setting (temp, soil, spin speed etc) and a nice touch is that if you try to go outside what is sensible for that setting it won't let you (i.e. you're trying to to go max temp on a delicates setting). Simple things like this make it a real breeze to use if you just want it for basic functions but then you can also get really advanced with completely customized programs if you need (I haven't bothered yet).

These units are also really fast. Sub 20 min wash cycle and the paired dryer unit will dry a huge load of heavy clothes in around 45 mins.

I could go on and on, but honestly, these are incredibly machines, period.

The only single issue that these have (the entire LG range have it) is that the internal valves for the hot and cold water feeds open and close very quickly. This can lead to water hammering (google it) in older houses where pipes aren't strapped or very long pipe runs, but this doesn't bother me as I have strapped pipes and hammer arrestors installed.

review_text: I've had it for about 2 months now.  Overall, I really like the machine.  Thus far it has done a really good job cleaning.  A couple of quirks:  The preset cycles are just that - preset, w/o a lot of ability to change things.  Depending on cycle, you may not be able to change the soil level to lowest or increase water temperature to highest, etc.  The machine is highly automated and does a lot of sensing, it uses very little water and spins the clothes so fast they come out almost dry!  Because it spins so fast it can vibrate and be a bit noisy if the load is unbalanced (like a bath towel mixed in with a bunch of underwear).  My only major complaint is due to it's design and energy star rating, it won't do a true hot water wash - it always mixes in cold water and unless you select the SANITARY cycle (which activates the internal heater), the water will be quite cool even on the hot setting.  I use liquid HE detergent so this hasn't been a problem, but I wonder if powders or pods would completely dissolve in such cool/cold water.

product_title: LG WM1388HW 2.3 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text: I needed a washer and dryer that would fit into a space of about 28 inches deep and 25 inches wide.  This is hands down one of the best units I could have purchased.  I have a family of 5 and the laundry is constantly going.  I needed something that would handle everything I could throw at it.  This unit does exactly that.  I am a second floor condo unit.  I do not have a dryer vent pipe and really didn't want to deal with putting one in.  The unit is stacked (the stacking kit comes with the dryer) and we drain the dryer condensation through the drain pipe.  Some people are concerned the drying time is longer with these condensation units however I find the drying time very comparable to a full-size unit.  With the exception of drawing water, the washer is very quiet.  Regular size washing pods are too much for these little guys.  I have done a few loads and find it's simply too much detergent.  Now, I place a tablespoon of H.E. detergent in the plastic cup that comes with the laundry soap, and I throw the whole cup in the washing machine. Cup comes out clean and it's the right amount of detergent for this unit.  It works perfectly!  I don't have the doors back on the closet yet and I can barely hear either the washer or dryer.  They are very pretty to look at.  My previous GE Unified washer/dryer leaked while we were away and caused significant damage to the unit below us.  So we placed the new LG units into a compact metal drip pan made specifically for this size (found on Amazon).  We also added Flood Stop to the faucets to ensure there is never an accidental flooding issue if we are away.  Accidents happen.  I try and be prepared.  The units are expensive, however, if you are looking for a small unit for a small space, these are the units for you.

review_title: We have been very happy with the one we had and had no hesitation ...
review_text: We just ordered this from a local Home Improvement store.  With a sale price and 10% off coupon the price was considerably lower than on Amazon. I am basing this review off our prior LG washer a WM2277 model that we bought in 2004.  We have been very happy with the one we had and had no hesitation getting this one.  We run a massage business and would do 3-6 loads a day in this, throwing in 6-8 twin sheets each time plus our other laundry.  I would say we gave this machine a good 40 years of normal use.  It needed a few repairs which I did myself, the drain pump and gasket were replaced late last year.  The bearings finally gave out and I tried to replace but ran into some issues disassembling it and decided it was not worth the extra work.  Considering the use it got I was really impressed with how it held up.  Also by doing my own repairs and watching videos on these, I saw that the mechanics were pretty much that same and differences between models are pretty much cosmetic.  Will update if we run into problems down the road.

product_title: LG WM3370HWA 4.3 cu. ft. Front-Load Washer with 9 Wash Cycles in White
review_text:
I did not purchase this machine from Amazon. I have owned it for three months.

The door seal has leaked on my unit since brand new. LG sent a repair technician around to address the seal but was unable to replace it as the units are stacked and LG does not permit service personnel to assist in unstacking the washer and dryer.

The washer will not begin to address the soil that accumulates in a mechanic's laundry. It does not seem capable of completely removing the wash cycle residue even if the operator selects the second rinse option.

The LG washer seems to clean bed linens along with bath linens well enough so long as you remember that a little bleach might be necessary at times.

The performance overall is certainly sub par in comparison with the competition.

This morning, the unit completely fails to operate. Nothing. Not even an indicator light. I suspect that three months of average use is just about all this LG washer is capable of supplying. A disappointment that I suppose will require a legal remedy to resolve.

One week later...
LG does not acknowledge my demand for a replacement washer or a suggestion that the firm repurchase the defective washer. In fact, I have received no response. My conclusion is that my particular washer is worthless and so is LG's warranty, implied or express. A clear violation of the Uniform Commercial Code which covers product merchantability in all US states.

product_title: LG WM3370HWA 4.3 cu. ft. Front-Load Washer with 9 Wash Cycles in White
review_text:
Did not buy this machine from Amazon (Lowes on sale). I love everything about this washer except that the control panel was designed by an idiot: the level indication LEDs are so blindingly bright that they completely obliterate the legends on the option pushbuttons (which are not illuminated). See attached photo. There is also only one Custom setting, so different family members won't be able to have their individual wash options. This is puzzling, because since the option is in software, I can't see how LG is saving any money in production by limiting it thus.
The filter is very low on this unit, so I like it to be a bit off the floor to facilitate cleaning it. Although the instructions indicate to not put the unit on struts, I placed it on 2 lumber 2x4s, making sure to drill shallow wells for the feet so the washer could not walk off, and that has worked well. The unit gives an error if it is not perfectly levelled on installation, but once level there are no balancing or shaking problems at all. I recommend a concrete slab under it!

review_title: DEAD After Only 14 Months! -- More Expensive To Fix Than Replace.
review_text:
My previous machine was a KENMORE Top-Loader that lasted an incredible 18 years. Then, when it was necessary to replace this antiquated laundry hero, I considered a newer high efficiency machine, and ultimately settled on a not-so-cheap LG WM3370HWA, which lured me in with its advanced features. I felt it might provide an edge cleaning set-in stains, and handling sizeable loads, while reducing impact on the environment.

After four months, problems began, with the washing machine and matching dryer, so I called LG support, and they had me place my telephone against the machine and push some buttons so they could listen to tones the machine produced, to find out what was wrong. Okay, so it told them I needed to change detergent amount and settings. Problem solved. Temporarilly. Another 10 months... right after the washing machine was off warranty, it began screaming, as loud as an abnoxious high-pitched piercing siren every time it spun the clothes! I contacted SEARS, where I purchased the LG Washer and they callously informed me... "Well, these machines don't last forever, seems to me, you were just unlucky with the machine you bought, and you just got a bad one, there's nothing we,re going to do about it!." They refused to help me further, refusing to accept any additional calls I placed to SEARS.

I then tried to contact LG directly, and found their support line required that I input a cell phone number where I was willing to receive regular text messages (advertising?) from LG. The automated LG system then announced if I refused to leave a phone number where I was willing to receive text messages, the call would then end. I did not respond, and the LG voice responded in a very abrupt, loud tone, GOOD BYE---...

I then checked with a local repair center and duscovered bearings go bad, with corresponding cost equal to what I paid for the washer new. Unfortunately, since the machine was still fairly new, many of the parts are not yet available on the market and I would have to wait another 3-6 months, for them to be made available by the manufacturer, according to this repair shop. This simply emphasized the mistake I made in purchasing an LG Washer.

I strongly advise against anyone considering either an LG WM3370HWA, or any LG product, period, due to observed inability to assure quality, poor longevity and value for the price paid, and for inadequate or non-existent customer support to enable post-sale repair problems. It concerned me with the WM3370HWA, that following my initial contact, I was not able to locate a single LG Customer Support center, other than the one described.

For these reasons I will not recommend LG under any circumstance.

review_title: Not the Quality I Expected from LG
review_text:
I purchased this dryer as part of a set from another supplier several months ago. I had not had a new dryer in 20 years and was excited to have something large enough to handle the large loads the washer could handle. NOT. Even with permanent press loads, I have to split my washer loads in half, or the clothes come out more wrinkled than they are at the bottom of my laundry hamper.

Additionally, the moisture sensor doesn't work at all. If I'm drying a load of towels, it cycles off while they're still wet, and worse still, if I'm drying something lightweight, like a fleece throw, it cycles off after just a couple minutes. The only way I can get clothes dry is to use the timed dry mode. I may as well have stuck with my 20 year old dryer!

To add insult to injury, the only way to have warranty service, is to first test the dryer by unhooking the vent hose from the dryer and drying a load of wet laundry for 30 minutes. With the dryer VENTING INTO MY HOUSE! If the problem (which has existed since I purchased the dryer) persists after that, I can submit a request for service. This is the first LG product I've purchased, and it will be the last.

review_text:
My typical use is to dump the clothes in, select "cotton/normal," select start, and come back in 75 minutes or so to unload the dry clothes.

5 months after purchase, I performed the same operation, and when I came back, the clothes were still wet. I restarted the same cycle, and could feel no heat at the vent. I started a support chat with LG, who told me that when the "energy saver" mode is operational, which is the default and cannot be permanently disabled, the dryer will not apply heat to the load. Now, I've used this dryer for 5 months, and I have never experienced this behavior, so either she is incorrect, or the machine was not working as designed for 5 months, but suddenly as of today it is. The user manual says use of the energy saver mode will increase drying times (from minutes, to days or weeks, apparently), but nowhere does it say heat will not be part of the cycle.

To add insult to injury, the support person told me that if a service call was created, I would be charged, even though the machine is under warranty, as it's an end-user issue.

Summary: if you wish to use heat in your drying cycle with this machine (apparently not a normal situation, per LG), you have to manually disable the energy saver mode each and every time you run the dryer on one of the default cycles. Basically, take the behavior of every other dryer ever made, and do the opposite of what you'd do on those, and you'll be in good shape. I can only guess that their washing machines may have a "water saver" mode as the default, where you have to manually specify each time that you want the load to use water in the wash cycle.

6 months after purchase, and now it's showing error code TE1 on the display and refusing to finish a cycle, so I have to call for service. 6 months! Is there anyone in the world that thinks this passes for quality? Not that I think any other manufacturer is any better - the mechanicals on all of these appliances are fine, it's the super cheap electronics, which serve no functional purpose other than make it look fancy, that are the Achilles' heel.

review_title: Just spent ~$700 on this horrible, very bad
review_text:
Save yourself! Just spent ~$700 on this horrible, very bad, no good washer to match the O.K. dryer. Hate it, hate it, hate it! (Don't tell my husband.) Uses so little water that there's no point in the drum rotating; it does not agitate the clothes, it soaks them. I can do a better job in my laundry tub by hand. It takes 84 minutes to run a "Normal" load; 120 minutes--TWO HOURS! to run a "Heavily Soiled" load. You're not allowed to wash bulky items on "Extra Hot," which is one thing you'll need to get ANY kind of load clean. There is a "water plus" feature but you are not allowed to use it with the "Extra Rinse" feature, which is necessary--your clothes need all the help they can get. You're not allowed to set the washer for a hot rinse. This is all stuff it's not easy to find out in the showroom when you're under the gun for a new washer, quick.

Essentially this washer "works" by soaking the clothes in a minimum of water, and using the spin cycle to remove the (somewhat) dirty water. I'll have to start my loads of "Heavy Soil" loads before I go to bed, and run an extra 15 minute "Speed Wash" first thing in the morning. EVERY night. Or maybe get up in the night to run an entire extra cycle. I know the "Energy Star" people think they'e doing us and the environment a favor by mandating standards of minimum water and energy usage, but if you have to run your clothes twice in boiling hot water, that's not really a savings, is it? Stinks, stinks, sticks! Zero stars!

product_title: LG DLHX4072V 7.3 Cu. Ft. Graphite Steel Stackable With Steam Cycle Electric Dryer
review_text:
This machine has many nice features, and as green folks we love the concept- but it has one serious design flaw which causes it to leak water onto the floor after a few month's worth of use. We've seen over a half cup of leakage with heavier loads. In short: this machine may ruin your floors and require frequent visits from LG technicians and a lot of frustrating time on the line with customer support affirming that yes, indeed you do clean your lint trap, (we do, religiously), and no, the vent is not clogged.

So here's the issue: In a conventional dryer, most of the lint gets trapped in the lint trap, with the remainder going out the air vent (this is why you need to clean your dryer vent periodically). In this machine, the residual lint that evades the trap clogs the evaporator (a component of the hybrid system) and never makes it to the air vent. After the evaporator gets clogged with lint every few months, moisture gets trapped and condenses inside the machine and water droplets blow out through the back of machine where the air vent attaches.

We had a technician out, who discovered the cause of the problem. After he cleaned the evaporator, the machine functioned without leaking for a couple of months and then started leaking again. The technician came out again and found the evaporator clogged again. We suspect that the cleaning will become less effective over time as there are areas in the fins and inner surfaces of the evaporator that are hard to get to.

LG has yet to come up with a solution other than sending the tech again. Our warranty expires soon, and we have gotten uncertain information on whether LG will continue to service this design flaw without charge. In any case, it does not seem like a viable long term solution.

We appreciate that LG is trying to adopt a greener technology that has been available for many years in Europe. However, this is a new technology for LG . We did not realize that we were such early adopters of the LG product, and as such have learned the hard way that this early model has a major design flaw. We'll update again if we get a satisfactory solution.

review_title: Avoid at all costs!  You've been warned.
review_text:
Our old Whirlpool washing machine lasted for almost 25 years. Top loader and it was as reliable as a sunrise. Long story short, we were sold on Whirlpool. We purchased a High Efficiency model on Black Friday, got a great deal, and were never happy with it (clothes were spun so hard the wrinkles wouldn't come out and the water level was laughable and the clothes didn't seem clean and powder was often left on the clothes) but we soldiered on with it and after only 5 years, yup 5 years, it went completely haywire. We had it recalibrated and reset..etc...but to no avail. ___ Well, I guess we were slow learners, five months ago we replaced it with a Whirlpool agitator model (the one listed here) and now, ONLY FIVE (5) MONTHS, YES MONTHS, LATER, the agitator has seized up. Everything works but the agitator is just locked in place and won't budge. It was working perfectly, and BAM! ___ something seized up. We are only two people in this household and do laundry only about twice a week and only usual small loads of shirts, socks, pants..etc. I can't imagine this machine would have lasted a week for a normal family of 4 with children where the machine is used daily. I don't know what's happened to Whirlpool, but they have completely collapsed in quality. These new machines are junk and the repair bills will quickly equal the price of a new machine, so don't bother. And even though this one is under warranty for a year, the Customer Service folk at Whirlpool are useless. They will basically tell you to contact the place where you bought it. Oh...they will be soooo' sorry and sympathetic and they will do NOTHING. I can only tell any prospective buyer to AVOID THESE PRODUCTS LIKE THE PLAGUE THEY ARE. We've gone through two machines and this one has lasted 5 MONTHS. Never again, never, never, never.
If this is indicative of Whirlpool quality today, they are doomed as a company. It's truly sad to see this happen to a once very reliable American company. ~sigh!~
I can only end by saying that I wish it were possible to give this appliance and company a negative rathing.

review_text: Okay, I worked for Sears as an appliance repair man for 8 years so I know washers and dryers very well.  To everyone out there, if you’re going to by a top load washer make damn sure you get one with a full action agitator.  Otherwise you will be very disappointed unless you only wash delicate non-dirty cloths.  Front load washers do pretty good, but leak and just break down too much, and the cost to keep them up can be heartbreaking.  If you just don't want a washer with an agitator, then your best bet is a front load washer, just do your homework and checkout the reviews and feedback before buying.  Best wishes: Rick Warton

review_title: Buyer Beware (Cracked drum after limited use, Company says you’re on your own)
review_text:
Bought a Samsung washer and dryer unit in this series 4 years ago after buying a home. My home which needed renovation took me two years to move into, thereby leaving the washer and dryer unit sitting wrapped in the original packing/shipping boxes even some time after moving in. Please note I also have a smaller Frigidaire unit located on a different floor in my home which is used mostly because of its proximity to the bedrooms. There are only three adults within my home and NO children, so washer and dryers are not used as frequently.

We started hearing a loud pounding noise with the dryer mid to late October 2018. We discovered the issue yesterday; a cracked drum. Since we NEVER allow shoes of any kind in our units and the heaviest items to go in the units are blankets, we were dumbfounded to find this issue. We’ve since done some research and found other customers complaining about a cracked drum as well as a current class-action lawsuit against the manufacturer (Samsung) for this known issue.

Samsung refuses to fix the drum and will only set-up an appointment if I pay for it. They’ve advised me that even if my dryer was still under warranty, that they wouldn’t cover it regardless because it’s considered a cosmetic issue.
I’ve had many washers and dryers over my lifetime, including the “work horse” Frigidaire washer and dryer on my second floor, yet I’ve never encountered this issue. This is a defect with the manufacturing of this product and Samsung absolutely refuses to make it right.
This will be my last Samsung washer and dryer unit. Other than that I very much enjoy my Samsung TVs and tablet. Samsung gets an A for electronics in my book, but not so much for their washer and dryer units.

product_title: Samsung DV40J3000EW 7.2 Cu. Ft. White Electric Dryer
review_text:
This purchase was a regrettable mistake that I made. I bought the Samsung clothes dryer because I had such a good experience with their TV. It does dry clothes, but what a pain to use, and a risk to my clothes.

The sensor dry in my opinion has only been useful when drying towels or large loads. It doesn’t work nearly as well as my sensor on my 40 year old kenmore that I got rid of.

I have used this machine for over four months now and am totally dissatisfied with it. It’s a hassle to use because the sensor dry feature in my experience is super sensitive to fabric weight and load size. I mean SUPER SENSITIVE, and if you don’t get it right you have to fiddle around trying to finish drying, or worse it may just shrink the clothes by frying them. Mine is biased to over drying the clothes big time and Samsung advises that is my fault for not getting the load size figured out correctly. And,I can not envision myself ever needing to use “very dry” or “more dry”.

The thing that makes it worse is that the manual timer is extremely limited. It’s called manual, but the only four choices you have are 20, 40, 60, or 80 minutes. So, I tried using damp dry so as not to shrink my long sleeve shirt sleeves. I’ve had a lot of experience washing and drying over a thousand loads of laundry and I’m pretty good at estimating the amount of time a “not dry enough yet” load will take to finish drying without shrinking my shirt sleeves, but there is no way to select anything less than 20 minutes with this machine.

When I first started using it (before I knew I had to be careful) the dryer shrunk a load of my long sleeve shirts, and fried a load of my underwear. I always wash my shirts separately and my underwear separately.

In summary, The automatic sensor dry is not something that can be relied on to take the effort out of drying your clothes, and the manual timer is very limited. It’s a real hassle to dry anything other than towels or a big load of rugged clothing. My poor experience with Samsung service will be considered when deciding on whether to purchase other Samsung products.

For those who are interested there are more details below:

I am very dissatisfied with the performance of the automatic sensor dry. I tried to return or exchange it with “Best Buy” right away but they would not do an exchange, and referred me to the manufacturer who I promptly called. Samsung quickly sent a repair tech out, and the only thing he did was start the empty dryer…watch as it ran for a brief time and shut off. Then he said it was operating normally and there was nothing wrong. That was it. He did not test anything more, and never even brought a tool box or any instrument in. I continued to call Samsung and was eventually, after much time on the phone, placed in contact with a supervisor, who continued to tell me it was operating as designed and they also denied my request for an exchange.

A minor annoyance that was not noticeable until I began to use the machine is that when it’s leveled properly nothing will stay on top of it while it is running. The top tappers off quite a bit at about 9 inches from the from of the unit and there is no lip at the edge. Anything set on top will fall off the front. The paint durability of the top from a scratch perspective is poor. It is really very soft and the top of the machine scratches so easily. I bought a rubber mat with enough friction on the bottom of it to stay put, as well as to protect the paint from scratching and that issue is solved. Samsung obviously doesn’t want me to set anything on top of the machine.

On the positive side, the filter size is generous and is easy to clean, the machine is an attractive design, the wrinkle prevent is a convenient feature and works well, and the paint color is a pleasing modern white.

review_title: Now if you are in the same situation I am in here is what I have found out and recommend. ----- problem history and details ----
review_text:
Alright I get to leave the first review to tell everyone how much I loathe this washer.

I have been going back and fourth with support for over a month now. The washer doesn't properly wash the clothes.
Now that is past the 30 day return policy I cannot return the waster and I'm stuck with it.

My recommendation to everyone here is if there is a problem,

--->>> DON'T CALL FACTORY SERVICE! <<<---
(seriously the dumbest thing I did)

Instead quickly return it within the 30 day window to save yourself time and money!

TRUST ME! I'm stuck with a washer that hardly works and will have to throw away money to get a properly working one.
I even tried contacting customer service and corporate with no luck.

Now if you are in the same situation I am in here is what I have found out and recommend.

----- problem history and details -------

It all started when I first noticed random stains on my clothes after washing them. I watched the wash cycle closely by pausing and watching it.
Clothes aren't moving from bottom to top and back down again. Any clothes on the top would never get submerged to get washed. It's supposed to be an high efficiency washer

(see image. the sample sock and my undies never went under water and just floated)

(I recommend anyone try the same test themselves. Put a white sock on top and pause the wash every couple of minutes to see if it moves.)
Now the "tech line" said that this was normal opperation. I watched quite a few videos online and how high efficency washers work and them in action.
All the videos I saw did rotate closes from the bottom up.

Now the workaround.
Always use the deep water (half load) or heavy load (3/4 load) wash. This will make sure there is enough water to cover the clothes.
What I do and recommend to give you clean clothes is pause the wash cycle every 5 minutes or so and pull the clothes on the bottom to the top and unpause the cycle.

I hope this helps any of those who bought this washer having the same issue I am.

review_text:
I had my whirlpool cabrio for 5 painful years. I finally, celebratory, took it out to the curb today. First of all when we first got it the thing would finish a load and then start the load again after 2 minutes. So if you started a load and left the house (not uncommon) it would wash the load OVER AND OVER again until you got home. It gave you about 30 seconds before restarting. We called Whirlpool customer service and gave them the code it was showing "LE" on the display and they told us we needed to call an appliance repair man. We did. We called 5, in fact. Each of them told us that they did not work on Whirlpool Cabrio machines because they were either too hard to work on or they were "pieces of ****." Mind you we paid $799 for this machine.

Finally a friend of ours came over and found out that the only problem was that it was still on Demo mode. There was NOTHING in the manual about this, nor could Whirlpool tell us this. The friend fixed it.

2 weeks later the lid lock broke making the machine completely inoperable. Knowing that no one would work on it, I ordered a new lid lock mechanism and replaced it myself, which took me about 6 hours. That was a fun Saturday. I did get it working again tho, to the extent that it ever did work.

The basic function of a washing machine is to take dirty clothes and make them clean. I'd say about 50% of the time the machine left the clothes smelling musty, even if we removed them IMMEDIATELY after the cycle was done.

Recently the machine stopped filling with water. It would pour water in, and the water would immediately drain out, and it would wash our clothes completely dry. We'd have been better off putting them in a big bucket, pouring some detergent in there, shaking it around a while, and throwing them into the dryer. We again called several washing machine repair men and all of them said that either they don't work on those machines, or that it's better to just go get a different machine.

We did. We went online and found a nice used GE machine for $160 and I can not tell you how far superior this used apartment complex style machine is at the basic function of washing clothes. PLEASE save your money. Stay away from the Whirlpool Cabrio, and Whirlpool in general.

review_title: The model we bought was a few years older (discontinued) but these GE all in one units are terrible: a repair person explained t
review_text:
Do NOT buy this product from GE. The model we bought was a few years older (discontinued) but these GE all in one units are terrible: a repair person explained to me that these used to be maid by Frigidaire for GE and they were fine, but when GE took over the manufacturing they are lemons.

Our experience: 13 months after purchasing the product, every time we tried to wash clothes with warm or hot water, washer would freeze mid cycle and shut down and wouldn't reboot for a day. A repairman came and said the motherboard needed to be replaced (after 13 months?! Nice product GE), and they tried FOR SIX MONTHS to order it but couldn't get the part. We went on for another year just using cold water, and now you can't run water without a massive leak. Our repair person said while it could be a hose, it's likely a bearing issue which is so unfixable on these units he does't fix them any more, and it could also be the transmission which would be a 600 to 800 dollar part, plus labor.

I would expect a GE washer dryer to go at least 3 years without any issues, but ours lasted 13 months. Stay away from GE, and from these all in one units especially.

What is she insinuating...that we broke the machine on purpose because we want to sit on the phone waiting for over half an hour to speak with someone? After weeks, the dealer was finally able to exchange the broken machine for a new one. The second new machine came today and was installed. Guess what! It is still broken. This time it is the dryer. During the dry cycle, when the drum is rotating, a rhythmic loud noise comes out of the side of the machine, like a hammer banging. We will be contacting GE AGAIN! What happened to quality control? GE should compensate us for time spent waiting on the phone to speak to a GE rep, time away from work waiting for their service person, and frustration and angst from this entire experience.

review_title: Not perfect, but pretty darn good
review_text:
We're on our THIRD attempt at compact laundry that works for our condo. We first bought the LG combo washer/dryer. We must have gotten a lemon--it was really a disaster in terms of vibration. I thought it was going to take out the whole floor! The thing was terrifying, even though we had the service department come out to level it twice (and yes, the shipping bolts were removed!) The drying cycle also took an incredibly long time, and it smelled as if our clothes were getting cooked. In reviews people seem to either love or hate this machine.

We replaced this with a stackable compact Bosch set, which is great, but still has some vibration. It's WORLDS, even whole UNIVERSES better than the LG combo, but it's noticable to my downstairs neighbor. With some loads the pans hanging from her ceiling and the paintings on her wall vibrate, and we can't figure out which load-type will cause it. You should expect that the dryer will off-load heat into the space, but that was true of the LG as well. I think that's the case with all non-vented condenser dryers. The Bosch set has seemed well-made, and were it not for the slight vibration bothering our neighbor, would suit our needs perfectly as a family of 3.

We're having the Electrolux compact stackable set installed this weekend, primarily because it has a second floor noise and vibration guarantee. I was surprised to see that it's rated the same as the Bosch set in terms of vibration by CR, though. If it has the same level of vibration as the Bosch set, it's going back for sure. But if it's better, out of consideration for our neighbor, we'll keep it and eat the cost.

review_title: Lots of improvement over the old model
review_text: This is my 2nd Bosch washer. The new one is better than my old model AXIII bought 10 years ago. The washer comes with hoses, but it was originally designed to be used in conjunction with the tab water which is closed most of the time.  But in United State, our washer hoses will be pressurized all the time.  To reduce the risk or burst, we recommended to replace it with a SS shielded durable hoses which costs about $30 from Home Depot or Lows.

product_title: GE GTW680BSJWS Top Loading Washer with Stainless Steel Basket, 4.6 Cu. Ft. Capacity, 14 Cycles, White
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:f9a2157e17c48b37e50ecc27d718202a]] [[VIDEOID:6caf2c673cad178681f5b192e0fd969d]] The troubleshooting section of the manual states that if the problem is 'Washer seems too quiet', then the possible cause is 'Quiet by design'. Clearly, these are not technical writers, but comedians.

The sounds generated by this machine are perturbing and loud. How loud? At 1 meter in a tiled hallway, the sound pressure levels I measured were:: wash: 77 dBA, spin: 72 dBA. That's as loud as my cyclone vacuum cleaner at full power. The difference is that the GE sounds like power lawn equipment. My prior 4 washers were much quieter. My LG spins at a much higher speed than this GE, and it stays relatively steady. During spin, the GE, even with no load, shakes excessively and rattles. The machine is leveled along 2 axes, and all 4 feet are in contact with a hard floor. I attached a short video of the GE washer during wash and spin cycles.

This washer has a tendancy to go off balance with small loads. There is no sensor to stop the motor when this happens. The basket continues to spin, and bangs against the side panels. The GE technician told me this was not a defect, just the design. It is inconvenient being on standby when doing laundry. Other washers I've used hardly ever have this problem, and in addition they have a sensor to detect the off balance condition.

This machine does have some features that many new HE machines do not, such as deep fill and warm rinse. But I consider them non-features since they negate the energy efficiency of an HE machine, and other top rated machines clean clothes just fine without them.

Based on professional reviews, the top scoring washers were from Samsung and LG. However, actual consumers, having long-term experiences, reported issues with those brands, ranging from machines getting stuck trying to balance the load, to machines that exploded. I settled on this GE as a compromise, since it has pretty good reviews from professionals and pretty good reviews from consumers.

Thus far, this GE looks like a loser. It's not as good as my LG washer, and not as good as my retired "real" Maytags made in Newton, Iowa. In summary, the various symptoms of this machine point to larger design flaws, and I don't expect it will be as durable as my previous machines.

review_text:
After reading many reviews about washing machines before making a decision, I decided to purchase this GE washer. I've always liked GE products, but after owning one of their previous HE models for about four years and being terribly disappointed with it's performance I almost purchased a competitor's product. I'm happy that I didn't.

Note that this is not a paid review.

Now for the review:

Cleaning - 4 stars. This top load HE washer gets clothes clean. I would rate my previous GE HE at two stars, so a great improvement. I considered going back to an agitator washer but worried about capacity and the detrimental effect that an agitator has on clothing. The only reason I didn't rate a 5 is that I haven't tried to clean grass stains yet. It's winter time here so I have no grass stains to work with.

Capacity - 5 stars. The 4.6 Cu. Ft tub has plenty of room for larger articles, including a king size quilt that I recently washed. The last load washed consisted of 4 pairs of jeans, a pair of work pants, 6 shirts, including a 2X flannel shirt and a 2X sweatshirt, and a few pairs of socks. There are settings on the washer for washing jeans separately from other colored articles, but that isn't the way we wash laundry in our household.

Features - 5 stars. As mentioned above, there are plenty of settings for your laundry, 13 total, including one to sanitize with Oxy. There six water temp settings, four levels of cleaning (light through extra heavy), and four levels of spin cycle from no spin through max. All are controlled with easy touch buttons. If that seems like a lot of choices, no worry. You can set the "my cycle" button to remember your settings. I especially like the slide out detergent and softener dispenser tray located at the top of the tub that mixes the detergent with the load as the washer fills. This also makes cleaning easy, although I've washed more than 30 loads and there is no residue showing yet. If you've experienced clothing stains in the past from fabric softener dispenser build-up, worry no more. For those who remember warm water rinse, that feature has also returned with this model. There is also a "deep fill" button, which I use frequently. Press that button and 5-6 more gallons of water are added. I like to see my clothes bathing in water. Also included is a "deep rinse" button, recommended for use with fabric softener. This uses a bit more water and increases cycle times over the 34 minutes they boast about, but I feel more at ease. The glass top makes it easy to see what is going on in there.

Noise - 3 stars. This compares to 1 star on my previous washer. I don't worry a lot about noise as my washer isn't setting next to the television. It does make some odd noises during the wash, also not a bother to me.

One drawback is the dreaded walk that washers sometimes do. The only time I've experienced this issue is when the load became unbalanced on the king size quilt. If this happens, press the pause button and wait about 30 seconds for the lid to unlock to situate the items in the tub.

The washer "walk" and the fact that I haven't tried to clean grass stains yet is my reason for rating at 4 stars instead of 5. I could have spent up to $200 more for another competitor's top load or twice as much for a larger capacity front load but I'm happy that I didn't. We aren't a large family and the 4.6 capacity is plenty enough for us. If you fall into that category, do some shopping for the lowest price and I think you'll also be pleased.

review_title: Not enough water to clean thoroughly
review_text:
I have had this washing machine a little over a year. I did not purchase the extra warranty. My feelings on this washer have varied--sometimes I think it is okay, but more often than not, I am displeased with it.

I am using it correctly, the right settings for the types of laundry, but the clothes don't come out as clean as they did in my old Maytag which had manual settings.

The dog blankets and rugs come out still smelly, with dirty patches. I wash them at least once every two weeks so they don't have a chance to get filthy. I often have to rewash them.

If I only wash a smaller load of clothes (the amount that would fit into a 3.2cf washer), it works alright, but if I do a really large load, no way! How can it work, with the clothes sitting in a small puddle of water?? This washer supposedly will wash 4.6cf. Really?? Forget washing pillows. There simply isn't enough water to do the job.

I can see how a front loader would be better, but then they, too, have their issues.

I am now looking at going back to a normal top loader, biting the bullet and getting a Speed Queen with manual controls. I would not recommend this GTW680BSJ5WS at all to anyone who asks.

review_title: This machine does not live up to its name or function
review_text: In the stores and reviews, this appeared to be the best machine for saving water and energy within a moderate income.  I've have the machine for over a year and regret the purchase almost everytime I use it for more than a small load of shirts and delicates.  On the regular cycles, water only sprays on the clothes....the ones at the bottom get wet; those on top may get wet or stay dry.  The clothes only swish back and forth so the material on top never gets close to the water with the detergent.  When doing sheets and towel or any larger item, I always use the deep fill cycle so that there is sufficient water to cover and clean.  It is also necessary to use the additional, second rinse function since the detergent does not seem to dissipate in the normal rinse cycle.  Due to its design, any larger load, such as one set of sheets or two towels will cause the machine to go off balance during the spin cycle and either "walk" or clunk frantically and stop.  At the end of the spin cycle, the sheets and towels are too damp and are usually hung to air dry for an hour or more prior to being added to the dryer.  The multiple functions appear to be a selling point, but it is not possible to reset any dials to lengthen the wash cycle or add a second spin.  It is programmed to do only what it does and will not allow for human intervention to lengthen a cycle once the sequence has begun.  I thought I was being a wise and ecologically mindful consumer when purchasing this machine, but have discovered that it does not live up to its function of adequately washing larger items or loads.

review_text:
I Purchased this machine for the DEEP FILL FEATURE. We are a farming family so I wanted the choice of ENOUGH WATER to clean dirty work cloths if necessary. The biggest fill that was ever achieved on Any Setting using DEEP FILL was about 1/3 tub of water - that would not cover dirty coveralls or Carhart Heavy Winter Jackets. I was forced to add additional water by bucket -- then be available for rinsing to add buckets of water so the dirt & soap would rinse out. The agitator of this machine was so rough that it tore sleeves & pocket flaps off new shirts, twisted sheets into ropes & knots so that it was impossible for them to get clean & agitated the edges & hems from towels to shreds. This machine was definitely good for the garment & towel industry--needed replacements in about 1/4 the normal life of the garment. Family clothing became grey, stained & shredded.
I complained to the GE Dealer who proceeded to send out repairmen to educate me on the proper setting for this machine (their Best Machine) while totally ignoring the poor design -- assuring me that all machines operate this way. Also, the Spin was SOOOOO fast & loud that we COULD NOT decipher a low flying helicopter from the sound of this machine spinning down our basement as it walked about over the concrete floor and rubbed the paint from the side of my dryer. I agree all of THIS GE Model washer work similar( my son's family had one identical to mine and It worked the same but additionally failed to spin the water out of his family,s laundry. I can not believe that I spent nearly $750 for a new modern machine that was worse to operate than the Wringer Washer that I helped my Mother carry & fill with 5 gallon buckets -- 50 years ago. My Sons Family and I finally gave up trying 'to adjust to new technology' -- and junked these machines after 1 year while still being covered by 4 year Extended Warranty-- GOT new Maytag Deep Fill Washers and are now Quietly suffering thru LOOOOONG Gentle Water-Covered wash cycles--our clothing is steadily getting BRIGHTER with each wash.
SHOP BEFORE YOU BUY A NEW WASHER -- CONSIDER REPAIRING YOUR OLD WASHER.

review_title: If I could rate this lower than 1 star I would!!!!  Waste of money.
review_text: First, I live alone so I don't have tons of laundry as with kids.  Was delivered Nov 23, 2016.  Washer worked fine for 6 months,  then gear box broke, leaked oil all over my floor, and a valve had to be replaced too.  GE did give me another year warranty as a courtesy for the oil on my floor.  Worked fine till Oct 2018.  It sometimes stopped spinning .  Drain and spin would put it through another complete wash cycle and maybe spin, maybe not.  After about 4 visits from Warranty repair places, and calling GE technical support, a little piece of plastic had to be drilled.  That was supposed to take care of the problem.  Not so.  Worked a few times, stopped spinning almost every load.  I had to take my dripping wet clothes to my son's to spin them.  They replaced the faulty lock.  Didn't work. Then it started filling to a large load, even if I had it on small.  Replaced the main control board.  Worked a few times, then stopped spinning again.  Just had the 10th repairman and everything tested working properly.  His conclusion:  I AM DOING LAUNDRY WRONG AND NEED TO REREAD MY MANUAL BECAUSE THERE IS NOTHING WRONG WITH THE WASHER!!!!!  Are you kidding me???? He said it gets off balance, so I am doing something wrong.  It didn't get off balance before October.  Suddenly every load is off balance?  I'd like to know why every load is now off balance.  That answer is not logical.  GE says they will deliver a new washer for $400 that the warranty is for repairs only.  If I have to buy another washer, it will not be a GE.  I actually will never buy another GE product.

review_text: Whoever wrote the software for this machine should probably  be in jail. Initially, we had someone come in and do a software update. They told us we were good to go. It didn't take more than a coupe of weeks, when it started acting up again. Besides the software freezing up like Windows ME, mechanically it isn't robust enough to compensate when a load becomes off balance. One problem might be the water saver features they put in new machines. Because they have so little water in them, they don't really have enough mass to compensate for an unbalanced load. The load inevitably goes off balance and the machine has to be stopped to adjust the laundry. As soon as this is done, the fussy software becomes an issue and it doesn't remember where it is in the cycle. Do yourself a favor; take a pass on this one. The only good thing about it is that it's made in the US. Sorry GE, you failed.

product_title: GE GTW460ASJWW Top Loading Washer with Stainless Steel Basket, 4.2 Cu. Ft. Capacity, 14 Cycles, White
review_text:
Don't believe the hype on Lowe's website where this washer gets nearly 5 stars. In fact, this washer may be the worst purchase of my adult life. The reason I feel this way is the false advertising. GE advertises this washer as 4.2 cu. ft., however on the largest load size setting ("Super") with the "Deep Fill" and "Deep Rinse" options selected, the washer only fills up about 2/3 of the way. This makes the washer approximately a 2.8 cu. ft. capacity (small) in reality. While, GE boasts the washer has “innovative wash action” and that “it can operate with high-efficiency, using less water while still getting the load clean”, I assure you this is completely FALSE. Yes, front load washers can clean clothes effectively with a lower water level, but this top load washer DOES NOT.

This is a big deal for me because I intentionally purchased a “large capacity” washer so I could clean my king size bedding and wash large loads of laundry at end of week. What is the point of owning a full-size washer that can’t handle large loads? For instance, the water level is so low I can't wash a king size comforter effectively. When I try washing a king size comforter (on the largest load setting & and deepest fill option), portions of the comforter barely get wet so they certainly aren't being cleaned. In the attached picture you can observe that portions of the bedding are still dry!

However, king size comforters are not the only problem. The washer can't handle large loads of clothes either so I end up doing multiple small loads so my clothes actually come out clean. Lastly, the super low water level makes using fabric softener totally impractical. Even on the "Deep Rinse" setting, fabric softener just dumps onto your clothes (staining them) and doesn't mix into the water.

My final thought is that I do not recommend this product and strongly suggest you look for a better brand. Even though this washer is rather new I'll likely leave it behind when I move and buy a real one.

product_title: GE GTW460ASJWW Top Loading Washer with Stainless Steel Basket, 4.2 Cu. Ft. Capacity, 14 Cycles, White
review_title: Owned for 3 years and did some repairs
review_text:
I actually like this washer. I find the new High Efficiency (HE) front loading washers do not clean as well as an agitator does. This was the only HE agitator washer we could find. I had my doubts at first, but it slowly won me over. Things I like
1) HUGE tub
2) Fast wash cycle (< 0.5 hours)
3) The numerous settings for laundry type, level of soiling, water temperature, and options (delay wash, 2nd rinse)
4) They used screws to assemble this thing! That means a tinkerer like me can actually fix things as they break.

Things I don't like.
1) it tends to twist our king size sheets which causes an unbalanced load. I have to untwist the sheets mid-spin cycle about a third of the time. This occurs even when using the Towel/Sheets setting
2) The Precise Fill setting. To me, it always looks like too little water. Never really did a test, just a gut feeling.

About repairs. Over the 3 year period, the washer didn't drain two times. The first time, I downloaded the Technical Service Guide (a MUST have), and went through the Diagnostics (which actually worked like they described). It said the drain pump wasn't working. The TSG also lists a series of tests for many of the washer components. I ran the drain pump test, and guess what, it failed. Before ordering a new part, drained the washer (unplug it and just take the drain hose and place the end in a bucket, it pretty much drains itself). I flipped the thing on its side and the innards are relatively simple and look just like the diagrams in the TSG. The drain pump is held to the drum with 3 3/8" bolts. I removed those puppies and then popped the motor from the pump (2 plastic side clips). Turns out sand got into the pump. I washed the sand out, re-assembled it, and worked like a charm. Took me nearly all day the first time (didn't want to break anything). The second time it happened, it took about 3 hours to drain, dis-assemble the pump, clean and re-assemble.
Should this happen? NO!!! But I AM grateful that they built this thing in such a way that this kind of simple repair doesn't require a $200 service call. The way most things are built these days, they're not repairable (open up a large screen TV; there are like 4 parts, including the screen). This washer is repairable. And since I had it on its side, I checked the motor belt each time. After 3 years, still looks like new.

Call me old-fashioned, but overall, I'm very happy to have a HE agitator washer. I've heard nothing but complaints about cycle time and mildew from my friends with the latest front-loaders. Thanks GE, for still building the agitators.

review_text: Bought the machine in May 2018.  Initially it worked fine, however, within 6 months we started having trouble.  When agitating, the house lights would dim.  I examined the fill hoses (I was using hoses with metal braiding on the outside) and the hose were fused together.  After extensive troubleshooting by the authorized warranty repair center, it was determined that the motor had a short.  The part was on back order.  We were without our washer for almost two months.  Now, it's just over two years, I luckily had purchased an extended warranty when I purchased the machine.  Just over a week ago, the machine stopped spinning.  The machine also began malfunctioning in other manners (when we changed the setting, the machine did not do what we had selected but instead did something totally different and not the same thing twice in a row).  Warranty authorized repair tech diagnosed the problem as a bad controller.  The controller was replaced and the machine ran fine for three days.  Last night it started making gear grinding noises and didn't work properly at all.  I used to be a Whirlpool, Kenmore, Roper guy (my grandfather and uncles use to own a Whirlpool sales and service business).  If I survive this GE, I'm going back to the Whirlpool family.  I have no beef with the techs who are trying to support this machine, you can only do so much with a piece of junk.

If I could rate this one negative 5 I
would.
I don't hate many things in life and am generally forgiving and happy. I've never hated anything as much as this machine. Have had it for 2 years now and I hate it! I've spent more money on water, detergent and electricity than this machine cost. It washes great for about the first five loads. Then when it's time to clean the inside of your agitator you can't get it out without a repairman. $$ GE in all their wisdom decided not to put a wing nut in the agitator to easily remove for cleaning underneath. I've never had a more energy sucking and water sucking machine in my entire life. Dirt dosent leave the machine, it just evenly distributes it among all your clothes. It has to be run only on the super size deep fill bulky item cycle just for a small load of daily clothes. Then use the extra rinse cycle, and hope you don't have to run a second full cycle. Keep fingers crossed that it dosent destroy anything in the meantime.
You can't soak clean the tub and just drain it. It take tons of electricity to spin an entire cycle just to drain water. This was their rough draft and they charged people unfairly for an inferior product.
At 60 years old this is the one of the only things I hate!
Save yourself money and frustration, spend a little more on a better machine and a better brand. It will otherwise cost you tons more in the long run. Avoid this machine! Did I mention that I hate it more than anything? Am buying a side load and throwing this one in the recycle dump.
If you see five stars on the reviews , it's because they have only had the machine for a few days. Just wait, they will wish they had waited to leave a review.

review_title: Too smart for its own good
review_text:
Infuriating. It has a double interlocked lid and tries to be smart, losing all control over the wash cycle like those old school machines you could turn the knob to the part of the cycle you wanted and it would do it.

Had to:
Defeat the interlock because one retard let their kid play in the washing machine, so I can redistribute the load mid cycle when it twists the sheets. It's so complicated to defeat, it was easier to detach it and place the lock/interlock outside the machine and plug it in. Where there's a will there's a way. This method also keeps it relatively "stock", the switches and sensors are just moved externally.

Smart fill does not fill enough water to let the clothes move about, so you add more and then it triggers some mode to drain all the water. Unplug/reset won't fix it. Plug it in and it continues draining. It then keeps draining wasting water and soap. You'll find the clothes sopping wet because it just drained randomly without completing the cycle. It takes a few to get it out of this state if triggered. If somehow unnoticed, the clothes will likely be too heavy for your drier and break that too (ask how I know). I don't know how I would have figured this out if I could not open the lid mid cycle.

Hate these computers and safety features. Wastes more water than it supposedly saves. At least it still spins and seems to have great load balancing capability (but still capable of twisting sheets into unbalance which you can't easily fix without disabling the lid control nonsense.

review_title: LG RESPONSE: ONLY DESIGNED TO DRY 80%
review_text:
TERRIFIC Dryer--- If your purpose is to have damp clothes when you take them out-- on ANY cycle!!! LG & repair (yes, FINALLY got repair to come out), responded that dryer is designed to dry items @ 80%.

That means, when you take your clothes out of the dryer and put them on, expect damp collars and waistbands. It means even AFTER you've dried your comforter 3-4+ times, you can expect areas of it to still be damp when you put it on your bed. That means, when you put your towels in your linen closet, you might want to put a fan or a heater in the linen closet as well so that they don't mold or mildew when you shut the door.

That means, you've used More energy than your OLD dryer because LG has a cooling cycle. Dryer heats up, doesn't dry your clothes, cools down, and start the dryer over again -- and again. We are absolutely FURIOUS!!!!! and that's the meat of my review.

Additional comments:
Repairman prior to service call: I'm going to educate you about your dryer... I'm going to tell you what LG doesn't tell you...

My husband and I both work in service/ public positions. We know what Quality & Customer Service is. LG ISN'T.

Our purchase was based on reading reviews from several websites. Good to Great Reviews. Didn't mean a thing!!!

And incidentally, our dryer tested fine & service man stated that he gets "these complaints all the time."

product_title: LG WM9000HWA TurboWash 5.2 Cu. Ft. White With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
Remember that you are not just purchasing the product itself, you have to deal with the company when things go wrong.

I purchased this product back in late March of this year. In July, the washer started to spill water all over my floor. Called LG who scheduled a service appointment for the next day - which was great. No show. No call. After I spent a week calling LG, the service provider's tech showed up randomly. He said that it was just a clog and could be easily fixed. He told us we needed to use less softener than the lines on the machine showed. He also advised us to fix the issue the next time by unscrewing the top of the machine adn fiddling with it ourselves. Obviously this would not be advisable. Fast forward to October and yet again the same issue with leaking everywhere, even though we have been following the instructions. This time LG scheduled the same tech, who did not show up yet again on the date provided by LG. Called LG and they wanted to send me to their scheduling department. That meant a 3 to 5 day turn around time for them to find someone to set up an appointment...unacceptable! I called around and found that Sears would send someone, so I scheduled them myself thinking that I could just pay them out of pocket. At this point, we have been without a washer for almost 2 weeks now (not including the week and a half in July).

Luckily Sears is a provider that can contract with LG, so it didn't cost me anything. Funny how I found someone in two hours when they said would take them 3 to 5 business days to potentially locate a service provider. I have spent a total of 3 1/2 hours on the phone with LG in the last 36 hours trying to get some type of escalated assistance. The only thing they do is spout off company policy and procedure and have done nothing toward solving the problem.

Now I am waiting on parts to be ordered, which is going to take another 3 to 5 days. The tech that I arranged to come out today isn't even sure that this will 100% fix it. I dropped over $3700 on appliances at home depot cause these were the latest and greatest. I have had these units for a total of 7 months and have not been able to do laundry in my own home a total of one month and counting.

When it works, it's great. But overall I haven't had the best experience.
I have emails out to some LG executives so will update this review if and when there are steps made by the company toward fixing this issue.

I don't know about you, but I don't agree with LG when they say it's perfectly acceptable to be unable to do laundry with brand-new machines I purchased from them for 3 weeks or so!

review_title: Dryer had an internal short.  GE doesn't care.
review_text:
I received this unit two hours ago and am really regretting this purchase. After the install guys left, I reached behind the dryer to check that the air discharge duct was properly attached and received a strong electrical shock when I touched the unpainted metal on the back. I put a multi meter between the casing and a common ground and measured 122 volts passing through the case.

This is an incredibly dangerous production error, and could easily have resulted in fatality if my body had been grounded (this is in a laundry room with water and plumbing), I would have had the current pass through me with no GFI protection. The dryer plugs into a 220-volt outlet on a 30-amp breaker.

I am completely stunned that GE would allow this to happen to a major $600 appliance. To add insult to injury, I am now being told that GE won't send a tech out to look at the issue for another 5 days. I have a family of four - we generate a ton of laundry, and I have a wet load in the washer as I type this.

The fact that this dangerous situation occurred is one thing. I get that errors happen regardless of best efforts to prevent them. GE's handling of the situation is unforgivable. They obviously don't care about the customer once the sale is made.

review_title: Impressive, and my clothes are clean.. faster.
review_text:
Both are working great three weeks in.

The washer had a little rattle on the back panel but I was able to bend it slightly in so it fit snug enough on the back to not rattle.

Oh yeah.. the other reviews might say it made a bad sound when they first started it. Pretty sure those folks didn't read the instructions. There are four nylon screw bolts on the back of the washer to support the drum in shipping. They MUST MUST be removed before you use the washer. You even have to unscrew one at the bottom just to free the electrical plug.

I have not owned any front loading washer / dryers before this so i'm new to the game. They are the quietest set I have ever owned. Some people said I might need water arresters to help stop the pipes banging, but I have not heard any thuds or annoying sounds. The washer definitely turns the water off and on more times than my old washer. It sounds like it runs some water in, then drains some, then runs more in. Anyways so if your pipes bang when your current washer finishes filling, you might want to look into a set of water arresters for this.

The washer spins fast enough that it has become my cat's new obsession. He sits in front of it and just watches it go around. It does have a very good balance too.

I have heard about front loaders smelling bad from the buildup in the door and seals. Mine isn't smelling bad. I dry the door seal and glass with a towel and then leave the door open. This one does have a little notch where the door isn't closed but it isn't open enough that your pets can get in it.
The manual says to run washing machine cleaner though it once every two months, so we picked up some at the store, have not used that yet.

The dryer seems impressive too. You can just set it to normal and it will estimate the time remaining. It will increase or decrease the time based on how dry the clothes are.. pretty cool. And it has not made our laundry room humid or anything like that.

Both sing songs when they complete their tasks. I can see how some might get annoyed by it but for me it just reminds me to get the clothes out of the dryer.

We purchased this model less than a year ago through Home Depot and a few weeks ago it started making a terrible grinding noise. We had purchased the extended warranty through Home Depot, but because the washer was less than a year old Home Depot's warranty is useless (manufacturer warranty only). Whirlpool sent a technician who diagnosed a failed bearing, requiring an all-new drum assembly.

So now we are waiting for the parts to arrive (a week waiting for parts as of today), and only after they arrive can we schedule the actual repair. At this point we are looking at going a full month without a working washing machine. Taking our clothes to the next town over to borrow someone else's washing machine is not exactly how we imagined spending our weekends less than a year after spending a thousand dollars on a new washer.

All the features in the world aren't worth a thing if a washer can't fulfill its most basic function.
