review_title: pretty good other than the washer gasket
review_text: I've been pretty happy with this washer-dryer pair.  I've had them for 1.5 years now and no serious problems.  They clean the clothes efficiently and the LED readout that tells you how long the load will take is very handy.  These have larger capacity than normal, which is helpful for bedding.  The downside is that the washer is too big for the standard drain pans.  I had to find an outfit online that makes metal drain pans to order.  On the other hand, a metal drain pan is more likely to still be serviceable when you need it so not unhappy about the extra cost and trouble.  It did hold up the installation waiting for the pan since I didn't realize ahead of time it would be needed.  My only substantial niggle (which brought it down a star) is that the water tends to accumulate in the rubber gasket of the washer, resulting in mildew and gunk.  I think you need to just dry it out with a towel after every usage and to leave the door open to dry.  There doesn't seem to be any fix for this.  It's also very quiet and reasonably vibration free.

product_title: LG DLGX7601WE 27" Gas Dryer with 7.3 cu. ft. Capacity, in White
review_text: The LG DLGX7601WE is the highest rated dryer by Consumer's Report which is why we purchased it.  I remember reading a review online where someone said it didn't dry the clothes well and I thought, well...that can't be true, they must have just gotten a lemon.  Our experience after owning if for a month is that the sensor does not work well. Our clothes come out partially dry on numerous cycles.  The thin easy to dry clothes are dry the thicker clothes are damp. In the case of drying socks the dryer kept turning off after 5 minutes because we were told we didn't have enough in the dryer.  We found LG after running through tests telling us that it was just fine if we took it off energy savor. That is not the case.  The clothes still do not dry on sensor mode.  The only sure way to get the clothes dry it to use time dry.  We are stuck using only the Timed drying mode which is a bit like going back to our dryer 30 years ago after paying heavily for "up to date" technology.  After spending that much money we are surprised at the bad design and lack of support by LG to address the core issue: a sensor design that is ineffective. Put in a load of socks to dry and you will be very disappointed. Consumer's Report got this one wrong to our experience.

review_title: Takes 2.5 hours to dry a load and some items are still damp
review_text:
Pros: can control and monitor remaining drying time in the LG ThinQ app. 2 way door is somewhat useful.
Cons: takes too long to dry even half a load, the app will tell you 12 minutes are remaining but 12 minutes later, it'll say 15 minutes are remaining, this will keep happening until you've waited about 2.5 hours for a load to finish and some items to still come out damp. I suspect it turns off the heat frequently in the middle of the cycle and air tumbles the load, because when I open the door to take out some quick dry items, the dryer will be lukewarm, in fact I've never had the inside of the dryer feel 'hot'. This is for a new install in the garage with a new very short vent hose to the outside.

I replaced a 2 year old Kenmore junk dryer but that one at least took about 1.5 hours or so to dry a load before it failed.

review_title: Error code because it's too cold outside
review_text: Do not buy this dryer.  It's been installed 11 months, and we got error code "TE2".  Arranged for LG Direct to repair it.  The day before the technician is scheduled to arrive, LG informs me that the error code is probably due to the cold weather in Chicago.  Let me state again - the agent confirmed on a recorded line that there is a good chance that the error code is showing because the weather outside is too cold.  To fix it, I should run a speed dry cycle before running my normal dryer sensor cycle.  Oh, and if he comes to fix it and it's not a defect, I will be charged around $100.  Poorly engineered device.

review_text:
I bought this at Nebraska Furniture Mart. I shopped around, read a gazillion reviews, etc. I've owned it for 2 years. I generally like it, but I don't think it cleans that well (sometimes). Liquid detergent works better for me than pods with this machine.

Some complain about noise. I know what they mean. But mind you, my previous washing machines have always been used. I'd buy some beat up Kenmore or Whirlpool beast off the back of a trailer for $200 bucks and they'd work fine -- until they didn't. So at 40 some years old, I said, what the heck, I'll buy a new one. This isn't as noisy as late 90's, heck, even mid 2000s, top-loader w/ agitator. But it's different.

I end up using the large (not regular or extra large) setting because I do all my colors and all my whites in two loads. And it fills up the tub. Ironically, you get better performance if the clothes are just barely covered by water -- even if you use lots of detergent. A small load is a "regular."

It works fine for me. But using the standard measures I'd say on scale of 1-5:

Washing performance: 3-4 (again depending upon the water level and detergent)
Features: 3 (there's no soak feature)
What else? Looks? 3 i guess

Mine doesn't move around on me. The spin cycle does have clicks and clunks. But whatever, I'm not annoyed by that. The spin cycle does seem to take a while.

GE Dryers? I LOVE the GE Dryer i bought with this. The GTD42. Perfect.

If you want to buy this off me, I'd sell it used. I'm considering getting that Whirlpool everyone likes.

review_title: No Low heat setting capability with sensor dry, and controls not visible when stacked on the washer.
review_text:
One of the basic settings I need is Low Heat and dry clothes using a sensor dry, this is not possible with this unit. Many of my clothes, and my kids clothes, call for Low heat. The only sensor dry option for Low heat is the Wool setting, which does NOT allow changes to the dryness level, and leaves the clothes essentially wet. The Delicates setting is actually Very Low heat, which will at least allow me to select the dryness level, but when set to Very Dry, the clothes still come out slightly damp, so I then have to put them on a timed dry for another 20 minutes. The sales person said to just use the time dry, which only allows me to set the Temp level to Low, but that seems to be defeating the purpose of having sensor dry capability in the machine. Using the Timed Dry option on Low heat does dry the clothes, but I have to guess at how long to put the clothes in for, seems really ridiculous, why cannot I have manual setting with sensor drying? The sales person said it seems all new dryers seem to have these setting that lock out what use to be basic settings.

Outside of this massive deficiency of no Low heat setting with sensor dry that actually dries the clothes, the unit can dry clothes. Have not tried the steam option yet.

I have this dryer stacked on the matching washer and it is impossible to see all of the dial settings so we have to use a stool to control the dryer. This is a bit of hassle, but hopefully we get use to hot set it and need a stool to control the unit, which by the way is a fall hazard...

review_title: A nice machine with some annoyances
review_text:
Good machine, generally. I can say that because after 18 months (now 4.5 years as of late 2020), mine hasn't required repairs, nor the matching dryer. It was a replacement for an inexpensive top-loader. I opted for the 6500-series for the aesthetics and because it was on sale; otherwise, save for a bit of extra space, I see no good reason to choose it over the 5200-series.

It cleans as well as you want it to. With shorter cycles, some synthetic garments that retain smells aren't cleaned. A three-hour steam cycle cleaned a camping item that had been sprayed with cat urine impervious to a half-dozen other remedies.

It's fairly well-balanced. Not exceptionally so; you can still get it to vibrate with an offset load, but it has a motion sensor to self-limit speeds. This can make getting the water out of something big and heavy, like a comforter, challenging. Oversized clothing loads have no such problem. Noise is audible and mostly inoffensive, though it probably would annoy a light sleeper.

Like most front-loading machines, this Samsung retains water around the rubber seal. I've left the door askew on mine from day one. No smells or buildup. I suspect this would be less true if I closed the door, though I haven't had to sop water with a cloth or apply any other prophylactics.

The little add-clothes drawer is mostly a nuisance. I once opened it frequently to air the machine out, but the plastic catch would periodically jam for no reason I could discern. The washer is vigilant about locking both doors. Chances are, if it'll let you open the small door, it'll let you open the big one too.

Digital controls are a mixed bag. You get a nifty timer that's moderately accurate for an average-sized load. However, and this is inexplicable: there's no true custom setting. You can create a saved personal wash, but it has to be based on the presets, which arbitrarily lock things out. No hot water for this one, no fast spinning for that one, too short a wash time for another. It's maddening; just let me pick what I want!

That aside, it's a capable, forgettable, stackable machine that's light on power and water. Hard to argue with that if it continues to hold up.

Noise is audible and mostly inoffensive, though it probably would annoy a light sleeper. Like most front-loading machines, this Samsung retains water around the rubber seal. I've left the door askew on mine from day one. No smells or buildup. I suspect this would be less true if I closed the door, though I haven't had to sop water with a cloth or apply any other prophylactics. The little add-clothes drawer is mostly a nuisance. I once opened it frequently to air the machine out, but the plastic catch would periodically jam for no reason I could discern. The washer is vigilant about locking both doors. Chances are, if it'll let you open the small door, it'll let you open the big one too. Digital controls are a mixed bag. You get a nifty timer that's moderately accurate for an average-sized load. No hot water for this one, no fast spinning for that one, too short a wash time for another. It's maddening; just let me pick what I want! review_title: Starts to smell like a damp locker room
review_text:
We’ve owned this washer for 6 months. Prior to this one we had a GE top-loading washer that was fairly basic, but that worked wonderfully and that we miss dearly — we left it when we moved and thought we’d give this Samsung washer a try.

Why did we try this washer? Well, it looked nice and seemed like the front-loading form would be easier to use. Big mistake.

We quickly discovered that for some reason the designers could not figure out how to keep water from pooling in this forsaken device after washes. So after each wash you have more work to do: wipe down the inside of the door, wipe the large ring interior around the door opening to soak up the remaining water, check the trap for gunk, then leave the door and the detergent module open for about 30 mins until everything air dries the rest of the way, ideally in a well-ventilated room or with a fan blowing on it. Then occasional also run the self-cleaning cycle. (Hopefully you are also using high-efficiency detergent in the right quantities.)

If you do all of that, you MAY be spared the stench, but possibly not. We haven’t been. Now as we walk past our laundry room we often smell the mildew odor while we’ve left the washer door open for it to dry... even just today and we’d run the cleaning cycle yesterday.

I’m so upset at this garbage washer. To have paid more for a machine that is more work and yet doesn’t work as well is so frustrating.

Also, this machine has turned itself off automatically on 2 occasions with no explanation. We came back the first time to find sopping wet clothes. The other time we found it full of suds still.

How does a dryer like this pass any kind of internal design review and quality assurance? Do not buy.

review_text:
I bought this expensive washer and dryer to replace ones that lasted 25 years with the hope paying up front would give me the same good service. For what these cost they are disappointing. All the bells and whistles of the washer do not seem to improve the outcome so I usually use plain vanilla. For those who want a lot of options this machine has them. The only way you get really hot water from the beginning is to use the sanitize setting. This is an EPA ruling and you will find "energy" saving features on all new machines. The max spin is great for towels, but be aware it will cause clothes to wrinkle so I use a slower spin which is fine.
The dryer is my main dislike. The clothes are thrown forward and revolve in a tight circle near the door and thus really wrinkle and take longer to dry because they are in a tight ball. I called Electrolux to ask about this. They were extremely pleasant to deal with and set up a service appointment. The service man said this was the way it was designed to keep clothes away from the heating element so they won't burn and the exhaust (where the lint screen is located) pulls the clothes forward. I don't think so! I showed the service tech with a wet load of wash what happened. He also said that was not right. What was the supposed fix, raise the front leveling legs to throw the clothes back. That helped, but did not cure the problem. In my opinion this is a design failure. I would not recommend these expensive machines.

product_title: LG WM3488HS 24" Washer/Dryer Combo with 2.3 cu. ft. Capacity, Stainless Steel Drum in Stainless Steel
review_text:
I would give this machine a zero if I could. I hate when other people use that line in a review, but i hate this washer so much that this remark is justified. I have had this machine for just under 2 years. from about the third month on, this machine has made my clean laundry smell like mildew, sulphur and rotten eggs. yes, I've tried various methods of tub cleaning methods, all to no avail. this washer's design includes a water reservoir that collects water. the manual says you should empty the reservoir every 3 months, but in actuality you will need to empty it every day if you want your clothes smelling even remotely palatable. and don't expect emptying the water to be a cake walk either. there is a 2 inch tube coming out of the Reservoir about 1 and a half inches from the ground. The water uses gravity to drain, so you will need to find a large shallow pan to stick under the hose every time it needs to be emptied. Then you will need to wait three or four minutes for the reservoir to drain completely. Then you will need to balance foul-smelling water in your shallow pan to your sink and hope it doesn't spill on anything else on the way there.

If you don't remove your clean clothes within a couple of hours, expect the load to smell like you forgot it while away on a week long vacation.

The stain removal quality of the washer is not as good as my last washer which was a whirlpool Duet.

Additionally, if your load becomes unbalanced and you need to re-spin the clothes make sure you don't miss the auto re-spin cycle. Because if your cycle times out, you will need to re-rinse your loads in order to re-spin it. There's no "spin only" cycle setting.

in conclusion: of you want a stress free laundry experience that gives you clean looking and smelling clothes, don't buy an LG washer.

product_title: LG WM3488HS 24" Washer/Dryer Combo with 2.3 cu. ft. Capacity, Stainless Steel Drum in Stainless Steel
review_text: Made for small apartments, and for those who don't want to go to the expense of adding external venting.  Works extremely well so long as it's installed properly.  I paid a professional plumber a small fortune to install this unit and have had no problems mentioned by other reviewers - excessive vibration, flooding, clothes wrinkling, not drying, etc.  Yes, the combined wash/dry cycle takes approx. 3 1/2 hours for a large load; a normal load takes about 2 hours.  But once you set it, you can forget it, without having to load a separate dryer.  Yes, the lint filter is not conveniently located, but you only really need to empty it a couple times a year.  And yes, the first 10 or so loads come out with a rubber smell, as the seals wear in, but the smell goes away entirely.  Two years in, this is a marvelous unit for those with cramped space and no desire to add venting.

First off let me say I did not purchase my machine from Amazon and the one I got was eight years ago.

I wanted to write this review because I believe anyone buying this product should be aware of LGs customer service.

My machine started displaying the LE error code so I reached out to LG about it. They told me I'd need to contact a service center and provided the number. I called the service center and was told it would cost $125 just for them to come out. I paid the $125 and had to wait five days for someone to come out. The tech came, said he fixed it and left. I tried to run a load and boom! LE error was back. I called the service center back and they said more parts was ordered but the tech could not come back out until the next week. When he came he told me that he's putting in a request for a new machine because he's not able to fix it. I was told I need to send proof of purchase, so I did. Now this machine has a motor with 10 years warranty so LG making sure it's fixed should not be an issue (tech said it was the motor). The request got put in and after a couple days of not hearing anything back, I called to find out what's going on. They said it takes up to three days to get approved. During that time no one reached out to provide any updates. I called after 3 days and was told I had already gotten a replacement five years ago. That's not the case as this is the first time I've had to interact with LG. Also, it would be quite easy to provide that wasnt the case as u have the serial number for the product I bought, not another serial number! Needless to say, they weren't interested in getting that issue sorted out and were very rude throughout the various interactions. When u finally spoke to a supervisor, he then told me it's not the motor that's the issue (bear in mind, the tech declared that was the problem onsite) and the part that was causing the problem is only under warranty for 7 years (how convenient?). At this point it's almost four weeks since I have no machine and my issue has not been resolved. The experience has been appalling to say the least, the lack of care shown by LG was mind boggling. They treated me as though I stole their product as opposed to the $3000 I spent.

Their product is solid while it is working but be aware of what might com when you need LG's customer service the most.

TO CLARIFY: I DID NOT PURCHASE FROM AMAZON, BUT REVIEW IS ABSOLUTELY NECESSARY.

LITERALLY after the year mark, 12mo exactly, the unit started throwing out error codes. The first was an error code indicating the heating was "abnormal", so I gave it a rest and only used the unit to wash for about a weeks time before trying the dryer again.. it didn't continue displaying the abnormal drying error as long as I kept the drying for intervals of 30min MAX.

THEN, at the 15mo mark, MID WASH CYCLE - mind you - the damn unit just stops. Starts giving off this terrible beeping noise and prompting an error code fc. We looked it up and the error code states: "FC. No feedback signal from driver unit - Service Required." We spoke to a gentleman initially who stated he could place us in the warranty, as it was only a few months past the year mark; He asked we call him back at a later date, to confirm the correct serial #, which we did. This time, 2nd call, we got another representative - WHO REFUSED to place us into the warranty regardless of the notes that were placed on our account. Not only were we on our own for the servicing of the unit, they were no longer going to honor the "paying for parts, even after 1 yr warranty" that was initially presented to us.

We are now at 10+ days, and I'm on Amazon leaving this really crummy review for this REALLY CRUMMY product and company & YES, our clothes are still trapped probably moldy and unsalvageable. DO NOT BUY. We gave it an honest try, and as soon as the 12mo warranty is up, this machine will just start falling apart.

review_title: Our LG Dryer caught fire during the warranty period!
review_text:
Our LG dryer caught fire 10.5 months after we bought it new from an authorized dealer. There was extensive smoke damage and, obviously, our home and the safety of my family (wife, two daughters and a dog) were imperiled. Luckily, in the end, only the dryer was dryer was ruined. Who knows what chemicals we were exposed to from the smoke?! The WORST part of it all was how LG ducked and weaved and finally turned their backs on us completely. The only thing they would offer to do was repair this faulty, dangerous unit. I told them I don't care if 10 NASA scientists came to our house, fully disassembled and put the unit back together again, it will NEVER be used in our home EVER AGAIN. Who knows if it will catch fire again?! Who knows what chemicals are in the smoke that was created?! LG was completely unsympathetic. They said we were refusing their help and washed their hands of us. And we were contacted by someone in the "Presidential Liaison Office" who said she was the ultimate authority. One of the most unhelpful, unfriendly customer service people I've ever talked to. A heart of ice. And, for the record we're adults and we know how to use a dryer properly, clean the lint filter, etc. The technician who LG sent used a special airflow meter to confirm that the vent and duct were clean.

LG refused to help us in any kind of meaningful way when its appliance caught fire under warranty in our home, putting our safety and possessions at grave risk. It took days for them to address the issue and I spent hours begging and pleaded various customer support agents in Manilla to escalate this. Finally, someone from the highest levels of the support organization, a "Presidential Liaison" contacted me. She was unfriendly, unsympathetic and utterly unhelpful. The only thing she would offer to do was to give me 20% of the value of the unit or have it repaired. I'm not crazy. NO ONE wants a faulty dryer that has caught fire repaired! Who knows what was burning in that unit (plastic, wiring, etc) and what dangerous chemicals were created?! Who knows whether it will catch fire again?!.The idea that we would keep this appliance in our house, given the fact that it put my entire family and home at risk, is completely ludicrous. But the Presidential Liaison was like a robot, just repeating the same thing over and over. I asked her if she was OK with me leaving our interaction furious with LG and ready to yell this story from the mountaintops (ie. social media, review sites, BBB, Consumer Affairs, UL, etc.) and she said she was fine with it. What kind of liaison is that?! What is clear is that the culture of LG and LG Support is completely unsympathetic, completely focused on the bottom line instead of the customer, perhaps even jaded and uninterested in the reputation of LG itself. It is the reflection of a sick company and a cynical corporate culture. For such a widely praised company, it was shocking and hugely disappointing. Needless to say, we will NEVER use LG products again and we will make sure to tell this sad story to everyone we know and care about.

review_title: Critical flaw -no battery backup for cycle settings
review_text:
LG went to great lengths to design elegant digital controls with many cycle options. Too bad they never considered what happens when the power goes out mid wash cycle. The machine “forgets” it was even running when power is restored. You can be left with a washer full of water, not sure how far along it wash, is it in the way cycle or rinse? The only option is to run a spin only cycle to empty it then start all over and hope the power stays on for the compete cycle.

Unlike some other reviews, the washer cleans my clothes well and the high speed spin cycle removes as much water as possible which reduces dry time. I suspect some of the reviews are from people with very dirty clothes. If you have such issues frequently you need the front load washer style.

Took every towel I owned to try to soak up the sopping carpeting (and lots of washing/drying of towels afterwards) and a fan that ran nonstop for 4 days to dry the areas.

A kitchen redo forced us to relocate the washer and dryer and stack them. Not sure if all new stackable washers and dryers require all this extra maintenance? Anyone know?
Just want to alert anyone interested in purchasing these machines that they require more maintenance!

Be extremely weary, LG does not stand behind its products, and you can easily end up where we are, living in a very expensive house with a very expensive washer, hauling your clothes to the local laundry mat. My strong advice is to avoid LG at all cost.

review_text:
I’m not terribly impressed with this washer in comparison to my last one (Samsung front-load). Consumer Reports gives this one very high ratings, but I’ve only had the thing about 2 months, and it’s honestly not as nice as my former washer.

Basically, I can only use this thing on one cycle, normal. Anything other than normal and the drum bangs against the unit casing really loudly until it auto-retries to do a spin cycle, over and over and over. I’ve checked, and the unit is level... and the feet don’t wobble, so I’m not really sure what’s going on there.

It’s hard to judge, but I don’t really feel like it’s getting my clothes as clean either. I mean, for the most part it does the job, but occasionally you do have to wash something twice.

I’m not a big fan of how the cycles don’t remember when you make a change to something like water temp, etc. Normal defaults to warm, but I usually do either hot or cold. That said, I think there may be one cycle you can customize, but... with it banging so badly, I’m afraid to leave the normal cycle.

Now, I’m not saying Samsung is a better brand... my old washer almost caught fire when it finally broke (hence the switch to a new brand), but when it was working it was nicer than this machine.

review_text:
Just moved to a new apartment temporarily and this is the washer they provided in the unit. Take my advice and do NOT buy this washer or any top loader of this tub design. You will regret it if you like clean clothes from just one wash cycle.

There is no real agitator and it underfills so clothes never get fully wet. The agitator is just a bottom spin plate with humps on it. If you do manage to get it to fill enough then the clothes do not circulate. Nothing gets properly clean. The only way to get clean items is to never put more than 3 inches worth of clothes in it. If washing sheets you have to wash them one at a time or they balloon up and never circulate.

If you try to change the setting during the wash it then goes through a re-sense mode to judge the weight which now includes wet clothes. That causes it to fill to the maximum level regardless of many clothes are in the machine. When that happens you have to reset it to spin only and start over which results in the machine being the biggest waster of water ever.

If you pay for water usage expect your water bill to at least double.

After about a year, the cycle times started getting longer and longer. When you start the load it tells you how long the cycle should take, about an hour. SO I would set an alarm on my cell phone for whatever time was on the washer. All went well for about a year. Then upon returning to change the load, there would still be 10 minutes left on the timer. Next week, there would be 25 minutes. Soon, a load was taking over two and a half hours. SO I watched what was happening. It would try to spin and it would go off center, stop, go slowly for a minute, back and forth, then try to spin again, and go off balance. Bad thing was that he wouldn't guarantee it because it was a design flaw. The same thing would probably happen again. He recommended that I scrap the machine. So I lose the purchase price. I lost the cost of two repair visits, over $200. and I've been without a washer for over a month while we tried to diagnose the problem.

Called Samsung. They refused to do anything because the washer is more than 12 months old.

review_title: BOSCH is luxury lifetime quality and technology that the industry will one day catch upto
review_text:
I am a previous BOSCH owner of washer/dryer and dishwasher.

I owned all three and over a period of 10 years I never had a single service call so I am a Bosch customer for life.

I was hesitant when I read the review here on Amazon on these. I went to Bosch-home.com and read that these were the latest technology that was being manufactured and called customer service to ask questions about what I read here on the dryer.

I have used for three loads of laundry both washing and drying.

I found the washer to be outstanding and was very quiet.

I found the dryer to be incredible technology and had no issues with jeans, socks, linen, t-shirts and synthetics and drying times were as expected in any dryer and perhaps a little quicker.

For anyone questioning why the mixed review and how is my review any more valid.. Here are a few items to consider:

1) Yes, there is a learning curve associated with Bosch because these are so technologically advanced that there are programs that are necessary when you use various articles of clothing.

You cannot just throw a bunch of laundry in and press a button, you need to be aware of what your washing and what program is the best to use.

2) The dryer is absolutely incredible and I agree with Bosch that this is the future technology for drying because of the incredible savings and efficiency!

With that being said, it is high maintenance in the sense that you cannot just clean a screen every once and a while.

You MUST clean the screen, but EVERY LOAD and once a month need to clean a heat exchanger as well. If you don't mind and are capable of making sure you screen is clean each load and clean the exchanger once a month you will be EXTREMELY HAPPY with your electric bill and insane technology used and how much better your clothes will come out and be protected!

Here is the link to copy and paste for going directly to Bosch to read about both waster and dryer technology and quality:

review_title: Buyer Beware (Cracked Drum after limited usage)
review_text:
Bought a Samsung washer and dryer unit in this series 4 years ago after buying a home. My home which needed renovation took me two years to move into, thereby leaving the washer and dryer unit sitting wrapped in the original packing/shipping boxes even some time after moving in. Please note I also have a smaller Frigidaire unit located on a different floor in my home which is used mostly because of its proximity to the bedrooms. There are only three adults within my home and NO children, so washer and dryers are not used as frequently.

We started hearing a loud pounding noise with the dryer mid to late October 2018. We discovered the issue yesterday; a cracked drum. Since we NEVER allow shoes of any kind in our units and the heaviest items to go in the units are blankets, we were dumbfounded to find this issue. We’ve since done some research and found other customers complaining about a cracked drum as well as a current class-action lawsuit against the manufacturer (Samsung) for this known issue.

Samsung refuses to fix the drum and will only set-up an appointment if I pay for it. They’ve advised me that even if my dryer was still under warranty, that they wouldn’t cover it regardless because it’s considered a cosmetic issue.
I’ve had many washers and dryers over my lifetime, including the “work horse” Frigidaire washer and dryer on my second floor, yet I’ve never encountered this issue. This is a defect with the manufacturing of this product and Samsung absolutely refuses to make it right.
This will be my last Samsung washer and dryer unit. Other than that I very much enjoy my Samsung TVs and tablet. Samsung gets an A for electronics in my book, but not so much for their washer and dryer units.

review_title: While this washer seems to wash clothes just fine, there are several things about it that are ...
review_text:
While this washer seems to wash clothes just fine, there are several things about it that are so annoying, it downgrades everything. First, the good stuff... It's capacity is huge, like the largest I've ever seen, cuts your laundry load time in roughly half. Comforters, rugs, no problem! It has a sink feature that allows you to presoak stained clothes...ok, neat, but not required. My wife loves that feature though.

Now for the bad...The sounds on this thing are just insane. Like I think the person who designed it might be insane. The "sound off" button does literally nothing. And when this finishes a cycle, it plays a 20 second song that is loud, obnoxious and super annoying. Especially with small kids sleeping in the house, it's woken them up on multiple occasions. And also the actual sound of the washer is the loudest I've ever heard when it's loading water in there - it sounds like a fireman crew is outside the house spraying at the walls, ridiculous. On several occasions I ran down to it to see if a hose was busted and spraying all over, but nope, just the "niagra falls" sound of this thing loading water. On the plus side, the spin cycle is actually quite silent.

Overall we regret this purchase, but I guess we are stuck with it for the next decade or so :(

The black stainless is nice but there's a white one available and it's a tad cheaper.

review_title: High tech is not always better
review_text:
We bought a house with this washer/dryer combo in the laundry room. So far the experience has been one problem after another. When it comes to washers, I value simplicity and reliability above all else. This washer has neither. If you put in even a tiny amount of HE soap or softener more than recommended, the machine will leak, setting off an LC1 or LC2 error code. Samsung service was called since the washer was leaking duration purchase inspection. The tech did nothing to correct the problem, which was caused by dried up soap and softener in the upper and lower filling cups. It is VERY sensitive to oversudsing, so get out your chemistry flasks and measure carefully!

Other wonderful "features" are:

It weighs a freakin' ton. Can be moved by one person if you're a gym rat.
It throws codes that are not intuitive - you need a manual or Google.
The loading height is very low. I have to get on my knees to move clothes from the washer to the dryer.
It's noisy.
When it finishes, it plays a little tune. My wife thinks that's cute. I think a loud buzzer would serve the purpose better.

This machine is an example of technology gone over the top. The techies at Samsung have evidently never washed their own clothes. They have no understanding of the end user's needs. As soon as the opportunity presents itself, these machines will go on Craig's list or to Goodwill. I will replace them with what has worked for us for nearly 20 years without a problem - a Maytag top loader and matching dryer.

Call me a Luddite, but simple and well made works for me.

product_title: Samsung activewash White Top Load Steam Washer
review_text:
While this washer seems to wash clothes ok, there are several things about it that are so annoying, it downgrades everything. First, the good stuff... It's capacity is huge, like the largest I've ever seen, cuts your laundry load time in roughly half. Comforters, rugs, no problem! It has a sink feature that allows you to presoak stained clothes...neat, but superfluous. My wife loves that feature though.

Now for the bad...The sounds on this thing are just insane, so loud, and impossible to turn off. I think the person who designed it might actually have screws loose. The "sound off" button is useless, it does literally nothing. And when a cycle finishes, it plays a 20 second song that is loud, obnoxious and super annoying and also impossible to deactivate...possibly the worst idea in the history of home appliances! Especially with small kids sleeping in the house, it's woken them up on multiple occasions.

And also the actual sound of the washer is the loudest I've ever heard when it's loading water in there - it sounds like a fireman crew is outside the house spraying at the walls, ridiculous. On several occasions I ran down to it to see if a hose was busted and spraying all over, but nope, just the "niagra falls" sound of this thing loading water. On the plus side, the spin cycle is actually quite silent.

Overall we regret this purchase, but I guess we are stuck with it for the next decade or so, if it lasts, which is doubtful based on other reviews :( In addition, the first TWO, yes 2, machines they delivered had irreparable issues and they had to bring replacements. So this is our 3rd machine. Just gives you a clue into the quality control over at Samsung. A major product fail!

I not only would not recommend this product to anyone, I would advise, for health reasons, NOT to buy it. It is a lovely concept that was not tested enough, or thought through thoroughly enough to have been unleashed upon unsuspecting buyers. DO NOT BUY.

product_title: White Front Load Laundry Pair with WAT28400UC 24 Washer and WTG86400UC 24 Electric Dryer
review_title: Don’t Waste Your Money and this is not the 500 Series.
review_text:
First off I would like to say part of my disappointment is that when I was searching for what I wanted on amazon I searched specifally for this product line BUT the 500 series not the 300 which is what I got. When it’s the first things that comes up and NOTHING else about the ad itself tells you that your looking at the 300 and not the 500 it’s very hard to know. I even expanded the pics that were available but when you bring them up large enough to see the words and numbers it for to blurry to read. I feel like maybe this was a little intentionally deceptive on the sellers part and I should’ve done more research.
Bottom line these pair is an expensive disappointment. Washer claims to be a high capacity yet low profile machine that can hold up to 16 lbs of dry clothing. I challenge you to try to get that much into this washer without stuffing things so tightly they don’t get clean. The washer however otherwise works fine. It runs quietly and cleans just as well as you would expect at this price point and for a Bosch product.
The dryer....ugh what can I say that’s positive? Not a lot sadly. If you’ve watched any of the YouTube videos featuring the 300 series then you already know where I’m headed and why I was trying to avoid purchasing this in the first place. The dryer basically has two filter/lint trap areas that you need to be concerned with. The first is the typical in dryer type that you take out and clean after every use, no harm no foul it works fine. The other is this contraption on the front bottom of the dryer on the left hand side as your facing it. This thing is a giant POS. The brochures tell you this needs maintenance less often that your in dryer lint trap to keep it working but oh how untrue this is. The dryer will basically stop drying before your clothes are anywhere near ready with pretty much every load and it’s because this filter gets even the tiniest debris in it and causes the dryer to presumably over heat I’m actually not sure how the mechanism works but bottom line it just stops drying all the way. At which point you will have to take this thing out and get ready because the compartment is filled with sitting water that for some reason didn’t drain all the way and as you pull here comes the water steaming down the dryer onto you, the floor, your clothes. Sometimes as much as 3/4-1 cup of water. Then you stand there staring at this filter that for all intents and purposes looks totally clean other than dripping water everywhere. So you go through the motions of shaking it, putting your hand into the filter compartment to loosen the other little flap at the back that the manufacturer doesn’t even tell you is the actual problem in an attempt to find sometimes up to a sliver of sopping wet lint that you hope and pray is the problem but is inevitably not becaue a load and a half in your dryer isn’t drying again.
I’m giving one star because the units are nice looking, compact as promised and other than being really low capacity the washer does clean really well.
My suggestion just get one of the typical white top loading washer dryer stacking sets you use when you stay in almost any vacation condo. They’re cheaper, hold more clothes and work better.

product_title: 'LG Graphite Steel Top Load Washer'
review_text:
We purchased the LG top loader 5.0 washer in November 2019 and had issues with it from first use. The soap/rinse dispenser was not draining or flushing the soap through to adequately clean the clothes. It was overflowing with water after use, but the clothes were often no clean. Often they were not even wet in the middle where they often twisted into knots. We contacted LG and were told that we had a water pressure issue and to hire a plumber. $300 later the plumber and a contractor tell us our water pressure is still fine.
We call LG to request an exchange or return and are told that we could only get a service call. 3 months later, 5 service calls (only two actually show up with a 5 hour window on week days!), countless phone calls without ever getting a return call, two new parts replaced, the issue still exists and LG still refuses to take back or replace the washer! We were very frustrated-stuck with a $900 washer that does not work and LG will not take responsibility. It was under warrantee and we purchased the 3 year extended warrantee. They instead insist on repairing a brand new appliance until it works.
Finally, after threatening legal action and at least 100 phone calls with numerous unsupportive staff, very poor customer service and recording of the issues, we got Home Depot to pick up the defective product. It was a poor experience with both companies, so beware that if you are part of the 20% of LG washers that do not work properly (as stated to me) you will be stuck with it! I highly suggest you consider another company with better product and customer service. Fingers crossed you do not need it and do not have to waste your time with this experience or 4 months without clean clothes.
Also note, the drawer dispensers are poor quality and flimsy, they do not drain water well. I was told by multiple sales people that there is often water left over in the drawer system which can contribute to mold issues. Several appliance stores in Seattle have even stopped carrying LG due to issues with service and need for 'repairs.'

review_title: Loud annoying grinding sound during agitation cycle - perfectly normal, though
review_text:
I've had this a week and done half a dozen loads. This is a nice looking and well-operating machine. There is one significant problem.

The agitation cycle is annoyingly loud and jarring. The washer makes this grinding noise as it swishes back and forth. I've been around washing machines for half a century and I've never heard a washer make a noise like this. Normally, the washing machine sounds kind of blend away into the background and become like white noise. With this machine, you definitely know it when the machine starts agitating. And it does this agitation more than once per washing cycle, so it becomes very distracting.

At first, I thought that there was something wrong with my washer. But no, GE has on its website (accessible through a QR code that you scan) audio of the washer making this noise. I'm sure they do this precisely to reduce the number of customer service complaints they get about it.

I find a few things about this interesting. First, that GE obviously knows that this noise is a problem. However, instead of doing some actual engineering to try to fix it, they direct you to their website to listen to it, to avoid the inevitable customer service calls. Second, this unit is a replacement for a previous stacked GE unit that must have been around 15-20 years old. The old unit didn't make this sound - no other washer I've ever heard during my entire life ever did. This is progress?

That being said, the washer and dryer work just fine. Clothes come out clean and dry. Speaking of actual engineering, they did a couple of nice things to improve the dryer in the 15-20 years since my last unit. The old unit could only be set to dry for 50 minutes, which was never enough to get the clothes fully dry. You can set the new one to 90, which is enough.

When the old dryer was done with its cycle, it used to make this very loud annoying buzz - EHNNNNNNT - like on a game show, but only if the game show really wanted to make fun of a loser. The new dryer doesn't make any noise when it stops. Also, they've moved the lint collector to the front of the dryer instead of being waaay in the back. This makes removing lint much easier.

The only reason I've dinged the rating by a star, from 5 down to 4, is because of this annoying grinding sound. This noise cannot and will not blend into the background the way other washer sounds do. If you live in a place where the W/D is out of earshot, I would give this the full 5 stars for you.

review_title: Don't Buy!  Failed after 13 months.  JUNK
review_text:
After about a year, the cycle times started getting longer and longer. When you start the load it tells you how long the cycle should take, about an hour. SO I would set an alarm on my cell phone for whatever time was on the washer. All went well for about a year. Then upon returning to change the load, there would still be 10 minutes left on the timer. Next week, there would be 25 minutes. Soon, a load was taking over two and a half hours. SO I watched what was happening. It would try to spin and it would go off center, stop, go slowly for a minute, back and forth, then try to spin again, and go off balance. I tried opening it up and rearranging the clothes inside. Same result. I tried it with an empty machine. Still same routine. SO I called in a certified repairman. He couldn't figure out how to fix it. I paid him. I called in another professional repairman. After an hour of diagnosis, he said he would have to research the problem. Got a call. He said that there are two fluid containing ballast weights on the front of the machine that had probably leaked and would have to be replaced. Estimate, $500. Bad thing was that he wouldn't guarantee it because it was a design flaw. The same thing would probably happen again. He recommended that I scrap the machine. So I lose the purchase price. I lost the cost of two repair visits, over $200. and I've been without a washer for over a month while we tried to diagnose the problem.

Called Samsung. They refused to do anything because the washer is more than 12 months old.

review_title: Complete junk. Huge waste of money.
review_text:
We have had this washer for a bit over 2 years. Started out needing 3?, 4? service calls just to make it STOP LEAKING water all over the floor. The lack of an agitator and large tub is a nice idea, but a complete fail in application. Not only does it not clean clothes nearly as well as a machine with an agitator, but the extra space this allows is intentionally not used by the washing machine. It simply will not fill up high enough with water to wash blankets, or anything else relatively large that still easily fits inside this huge and beautiful looking tub.
This is all about looks, not function. Lots of bells and whistles... oh, and beeps. Pretty little sing-song beeps. This is what the engineers at Samsung think cleans clothes. They spent their time on pretty little beeping noises. I would rather have an ugly, 20 year old washer that actually works.

review_text:
First and foremost this was not the dryer of my choice. My partner wanted us to get a dryer to replace the 30yr old one I had and left it up to me to pick but once I did pick, he seemed a bit disappointed that what I picked was half the price of this dryer, and he gave me a spending limit which was more than this dryer. He decided to pick this one due to what I would consider bells and whistles which I know I would never use and I am the one who does the laundry. As to why my first choice was something a bit simpler but still a large dryer.

The first one we received sadly has an issue. The panel behind the buttons must of been slightly off because the start button only worked 10-20% of the time. Every other button worked 100% to the lightest touch but the start button would not even work if I covered it will all my fingers. The few times it randomly ran it worked perfectly. It never gave me the error for the flint and it dried everything all the way through without stopping way too early. But not being able to get it to ruin 80-90% of the time made it impossible for me.

Luckily the seller was quick and kind enough to help us with the situation, and was happy to get a new one out to use once the one we had was picked up. The seller made the transaction easy, simple and was very quick to respond. So majority of the good review on this is the seller.

We got our new one and all the buttons work. But....now I have to deal with the flint error. I decided to wash a fluffy queen bed cover and the dryer kept alerting it was the filter about every 10 minutes, and the blanket was still damp. I felt like i was stuck babysitting the dryer to make sure it dried this one blanket. I still had 2 bed covers, 3 sheets and another queen blanket ready to start drying in my washer. My work desk isnt far from my garage so I hear it as soon as the warning lets off and I work from home, so for me its irritating but I can work with it. For someone who has to trust a dryer running while they leave home for work or etc, you cant trust to leave this dryer going cause you might come home to linen still damp.

I Just put in a load of clothes and I have to run everything on the heavy cycle because I feel it will never get dry after repeat restarts. I even check the filter and clean out what little if any is in there. I had just checked the time at 10:23 as I walked into the kitchen and by 10:29 it was beeping saying flint build up. I cleaned it out and started it again. 10:40 it is beeping again and I know it hasnt past 60 minutes from when i start it the first time. From what I felt the clothes feel mostly dry, and the issue is when they get slightly dry the move around a whole lot more so more of it begins to pile in the front over the filter region. But at times there may still be damp clothes towards the rear. Due to this bad design it causes the dryer to turn off and sound the alarms. Had the company designed the glass to slightly go in at a slant a bit, not causing heat build up over the flint compartment but to at least keep buildup from happening over it, im sure these dryers would work amazing. Sadly I am not sure as to why they chose the design they did. So even if the tub might seem huge, its not really worth putting a large amount or even one single large blanket in it which really is sad.

Pros: If you have cats &/or dogs that shed a lot, this dryer is amazing. I retired a very well kept 30 yr old dryer that was handed down to me but I had no idea what I was missing out on with a newer dryer. This thing gets all the fine hairs out and one dryer sheet does the job at making everything smell amazing.

Con: The design causes a huge annoyance with larger blankets or larger mix loads due to its fidgety flint sensor. If the company created an item that could easy snap or rest into place above the filter which would keep air circulating and keep clothes off of it, I would be happy to buy it in the heart beat. But sadly dont think anything like that exists yet. Here is hoping

product_title: GE GNW128SSMWW Top Loading Washer, 2.8 Cu. Ft Capacity, White
review_title: Bought And Returned This Compact Washer For NOT Being Compact
review_text:
The most important piece of information concerning this washing machine was misquoted, by the vendor specifications, at the store where I bought this unit. A 2.1 cubic foot washer is the best compact available, and of course is unavailable so, given no other option for something that could fill enough to properly wash a Queen comforter, I purchased the new, GE 2.8 cubit Foot top loading washing machine, thinking it was the next innovation. I assumed, based on specs, that the washer was slightly taller, with a slightly deeper basket, resulting in a 2.8 instead of a 2.1 cubic foot load capacity, as widening the machine would be madness.

Given that the width of door frames in the average bathroom in the 1960s, 1970s and 1980s built apartments, condos and houses was between 24 and 28 inches with the 24 inch door size in very common use, more common than the other two options, it would make no sense to produce a compact or portable machine that had a width precluding use. This unit is 24 inches by 24. 5 inches, with no wiggle room. Even with the door to our bathrooms off their hinges, this machine would never fit in any of them, so back in the box and back to the store this went.

The specifications have been updated, where I purchased this, again, 24 x 24.5, and hopefully the same thing won't happen to anyone else, however, for anyone looking at this machine, please be advised that it is too large to fit through any bathroom door in our house, built in the 1970s and, after measuring at a friend's 1960s home we found their doors also measured exactly 24 inches, with about 23.3 between the door frame stops on either side.

Given that a 23 inch machine is the maximum that can fit through what was, for decades, the standard bathroom door size, this machine is simply not workable unless you are using it in a large, standard size washing machine slot in a garage or laundry closet and, if you can fit a 24 inch machine with a low 2.8 cubic foot capacity, you can probably fit a standard 27 inch machine, why bother with a machine that washes so much less and doesn't fill enough to wash a large comforter? It just makes no sense.

I can't recommend this for anyone seeking a compact washer, as a 23 inch width is about as wide as it could be in order to be considered compact, for use in a bathroom with a sink hookup. I also don't recommend this for anyone seeking a washing machine who can accommodate a larger size washer, such as a 27 inch, because the capacity on the 27 inch GE washer far exceeds this and that washer comes with a functioning Deep Fill button, as of 2019. With any luck, someone will design a 2.5 or even a 2.8 cubic foot washer that utilizes a slightly taller tub in a housing of 22 to a maximum of 23 inches, so that I can finally replace my dead Haier 2.1, which was so useful for so many years.

I hope this helps you in your search. I must continue mine for a good 2.1 cubic foot portable. If Ge ever considers a redesign on this, making it a bit taller and thinner, to make it workable for anyone living in an older home, I will post the information on that new machine in this review and will recommend the machine.

review_title: Here is my anecdotal experience with Electrolux front load washers
review_text:
I spent a day and a half trying to fix my 6-year-old Electrolux model EIFLS60JIW1 which we inherited with our new home 3 months ago. To summarize quickly, I am now in the market for a new washer because I was unable to fix it and may have hastened its demise. So if you are curious, continue reading for details.

Also, let me say I think getting 6 years of this unit seems ok but I googled around to try to get a sense of how long these units should last and came up with estimates between 10-14 years, but to be fair I think in my case I probably went about the repair wrong in the end and this is one of those regrettable times where I may have actually caused my unit's demise too which is why I am conflicted about how many stars to give. Also, since they no longer make this version I am listing it with the new models above, not so much to warn other consumers like me but maybe to just inform everyone of my anecdotal experience. Besides, from what I can tell looking around on the internet, the Electrolux brand seems to still be highly rated or at least advertised strategically very well because I am no longer sure what to make of all of those "consumer report" websites which seem more and more biased lately after you google, "best front load washer to buy."

Ok so back to focusing on the washer; so it was apparently purchased by the previous owners in July 2015 and appears to have worked fine until now as far as I can tell basically for 6 years. I noticed there was a very small pool of water under and in front of it over the past few days doing 1-2 loads per day. On closer inspection, I saw the door seal had a small part missing portion of rubber where the glass door presses into, spanning about 2 inches in the lower-left portion of the seal so ordered the part from Amazon and replaced it (more on that later). What really prompted us to act was after the small leak got bigger and I noticed at the same time the clothes were still soaked at the end of a cycle. After watching a full 14 min rinse spin cycle finally determined that the thing was not agitating or spinning at all but towards the end of the cycle could hear the motor kick on and sounded like it turning at full speed but still not spinning. Using a very helpful, I have to admit set of videos from repair clinic and appliance parts.com on youtube as a guide, I took back panel off and saw belt had fallen off. After inspecting the belt for cracks I decided to re-install the belt back onto the rotor wheel (mistake perhaps?..should have ordered a new belt, and wheel probably) which was finally feasible after attaching a zip tie to hold a portion of the belt onto the wheel and stretching the rest on. Of note, the wheel itself was also wobbling so found the bolt had loosened and assumed this was responsible for belt eventually falling off in the first place. After tightening the bolt, put back panel on and it worked great again for 4-5 loads then the same problem occured again.

As an aside, while working on this portion of the washer, the door boot seal also came in the mail so I also took off the old rubber seal and reinstalled the new seal. To my disappointment, it still seemed to leak even with the new seal. I do not know if this was due to a defective seal or leaking from a different portion of the washer underneath (related to the stuff going on in the back) where I can't see but I did a double-take and re-inspected my installation for what its worth to confirm that the seal and springs holding it on appeared snug. Anyway, for this reason, I am recusing myself from writing a review on the boot seal since I am not sure on the cause of the leak.

Fast-forwarding backs up to the back of the washer with the belt falling off. So reading online the most common causes seemed to be worn chewed-up belts, a loose wheel (despite re-tightening), or bearings going within the tub itself. I found the wheel itself was loose again and this time there was a lot more black powder-rubber dust stuff all over the back of the tub. Looked like the belt had been rubbing against the back of the plastic tub and the metal wheel itself had actually cut deeply and completely through the tub like a blade near the top portions of the tub. There was now evidence of water dripping out of where the cuts were and pooling in the tray in the back of the washer! I think in retrospect, I should have probably tried to replace the wheel itself and the belt too because thinking back, the wheel was difficult to wrench back on, and even after tightening there was ever so slight bit of play where the wheel attached to the nut.

In conclusion, I like to do my own repairs when there is time to learn more and tinker, and admittedly I sometimes struggle with "repair guy trust issues" (my own demons I am working through), but looking back this was a "penny-wise" move on my part not getting an appliance professional in to do the repair because now the cost of fixing this will approach just replacing the unit.

Also, I want to apologize to the Michigan-based repair clinic and appliance parts .com. I used their youtube videos to do the repairs which were excellent. I thought about it and SHOULD have bought the parts from them as well and not gotten cheap and got the less expensive part from Amazon (97$ vs 140 + 27 one day ship). My laziness is why Amazon is getting too powerful so maybe need to suck it up and pay a little more to support other US companies more often. Again though I have a tough time when I can click once vs type in my address... find credit card... enter card number each time there is a new website but Karma has burned me this time for sure in this case.

I went all the way to a corporate supervisor and was told they totally understand how I felt but they would not fix a defective from the start machine. I wonder how they would reply if the tech would have died because of their neglect?

review_title: You absolutely must level it perfectly... otherwise great so far.
review_text: I bought this washer and dryer so that it could be stacked in an upstairs master closet. The only reason I bought an Electrolux was because the washer and dryer doors can be reversed. It is the only brand that allows that feature in a front loader washing machine. It is actually quite easy to reverse the door, but you must be sure to rotate the glass inside the washer door as illustrated in the instruction manual. The  washer is also extremely difficult to level because it does not come with any tool to be able to do it and it is critical that it is fully level otherwise it will shake like crazy and rattle the dryer on top of the washer. Very very annoying. The tool that they suggest you use to level it  is not provided and you cannot find it online anywhere. Therefore I Purchased an excellent set of thin wrenches available on Amazon. The 30 mm size is perfect for the task of leveling the legs. You don’t have to lift up the washer with this  wrench. You can adjust the feet by turning the wrench underneath the washer even if it is already stacked with the dryer. I was very happy with the wrenches.  After leveling it works wonderfully. It is loud at first but the sound gets much better over time. Apparently it takes some time to warm up. The delivery people warned me about that. They were right, but they did a terrible job of leveling my machine! I did not buy from this particular company....  but I wanted to give this advice because overall I’m quite pleased with the machine and how it cleans. I really like the pods dispenser.  I used to have problems with the pods getting stuck to my clothes and not dissolving completely in my old washer which was only 10 years old. This machine flawlessly dissolves them in  the Dispenser.

product_title: GE APPLIANCES GTW465ASNWW, White
review_text:
Purchased during Covid quarantine with few choices to chose from. Installed easily, and pleasantly surprised at the capacity of the tub. What I'm not crazy about is the lid locking feature (I suppose it's on all the current models) where one can't physically see the amount of water vs clothes during a wash cycle. But, the biggest problem: while washing a bathmat, a few towels or any small load, the machine always gets off balance in the spin cycle, begins violently knocking against the outer cabinet, and then, STARTS TRAVELING! After 25% of the washes, the washer needs to be pushed back into position after traveling 6-12 inches away from the wall. THIS IS INSANE! It weighs 160lbs and still travels freely like my self-propelled lawn mower!
I've already wedged it in, taped it to an adjoining cabinet, and tied it to the dryer. The next attempt will be to tie it to the rear wall, e.g. Ikea dressers. Others have commented on the lack of a dedicated SPIN ONLY cycle, which I concur. When put in SPIN ONLY mode, it goes into a cycle of adding water, spinning, and adding more water. Again, highly counter-productive. In short, this machine seems to have a mind of its own. I don't think I'll be returning it. I don't think it will last the 12+ years my last Whirlpool lasted. And, I cannot recommend others to buy this GE model. Please, take this review seriously. I have nothing against GE, but am just passing on my experiences with this washer.

product_title: GE APPLIANCES GTW465ASNWW, White
review_text: I work for an appliance repair company. I deal with washing machine problems every day. This is by far the best washer I've ever owned. NO problems with being off balance (bulky loads will cause the tub to wobble a little but it's designed to do that so it doesn't have to stop the cycle with and off-balance error code like many washers). Loading the washer properly is the key to having it work well.  I love that I can set the water depth and the extra rinse feature is a bonus. A complete cycle of laundry done in less than 20 min. If I have to find something negative I'd say it's not "whisper" quiet like the description states. It sounds like a normal washer. Behind the door of the laundry room I barely hear it. People complaining about the washer being off balance are likely wrapping their blankets, jeans, towels, etc around the agitator (which is the wrong way to load a washer) or they're stuffing it like a commercial washer at a laundry mat. They probably didn't read the manual which explains how to use the washer and recommendations for load size and water levels for each cycle selection. I recommend this washer to our customers who want more control over the water level, want to be able to lift the lid to add an item mid-cycle, and who don't want to wait all day for a load to finish.

review_title: I'm kind of stunned by all the bad reviews...
review_text:
I didn't purchase this off of Amazon, but what I got was reasonably priced unit with some cool features that I will definitely use.

Pros:

Big capacity, it can handle a lot of clothes
Precise-fill mode takes away any guess work and is awesome
Auto-soak mode does a good job of going after heavy stains
Extra spin and rinse modes also help out big time
Not exactly intuitive interface, but easy to operate once you sit with the manual for a bit
The price is low for what you get. A very good value IMO.
Because it is HE it uses barely any detergent for a normal load. Like a couple of tablespoons max.

Cons:

It's pretty loud. Not ridiculously so, but noisier than I expected. Ours is in the basement so no biggie.
It makes alarmingly odd noises when "precise-fill" mode starts. The noises are normal. Don't freak out.
The big capacity is a double-edged sword. If you are below 5' tall getting that last sock will be a strain.
The locking mechanism is a small annoyance, but as long as it continues to clean my clothes efficiently I don't really care if I can't open the lid at a given time.

All-in-all I found this to be a perfectly good machine and the price was on point.

review_title: Lives up to Consumers Reports Best Buy
review_text:
Read every review on Amazon, bought locally with 5 year extended warranty because I was nervous about the negative reviews. Don't think I needed the extra warranty since I am not having any real problems.

I am very happy with performance and cleaning but had to adjust to a little different setup and use:

1. The unit must be mis-leveled. When your level says level front to back/left to right the drum wasn't centered and that's what had to be perfectly centered by un-leveling or it will sound like it will explode. (Just like the manual describes in leveling) You can NOT trust leveling the cabinet for the drum to be centered.

Edit: Hey LG - put a dot or cross hair in the center of the see through top to make the drum centering operation take minutes instead of hours with level, test with heavy load, listen for banging, repeat this until it runs quiet. (Took me 4 repeats)

2. With old agitator washer you could throw everything in a load- towels, sheets, jeans, shirts etc - Now, you really must seperate loads by fabric density/size or the machine will be out of balance, generate more noise, and most likely wear faster. If you do throw everything together - use the bedding cycle - fills tub more.

3. If you don't like the water saving cycles the bedding cycle fills the tub completely- I use this a lot on loads that are heavily soiled or very large loads - not just bedding.

4. I think consumers reports got it right - very good washer and a best buy (2021). It takes a few changes in how you sort loads - but worth that small adjustment.

This model is the lowest priced model with slightly less features but has everything I need.

LG may have some good products, but this machine is not one of them.

product_title: LG WM3500CW 4.5 Cu. Ft. White Front Load Washer
review_text:
We are rough on our clothes washers. We seem to burn them out every 6 years. This was our first LG appliance.
Bought it at Lowes during COVID and brought it home in our SUV.

Total pain to get thru the laundry room door, even after pulling the box off. Remember to buy new water lines with the stainless steel mesh jacket (to prevent massive water leak). Washer came with a discharge tube but we needed to add two additional zip ties to keep it secured without fear of a leak. Use teflon tape on the pipe screw threads to get a water tight seal.

You'll need two 11/16 or 17mm wrenches and a magnetic bubble level to adjust the legs. Spend a lot of time on this to minimize vibration issues.

We stacked our old Samsung Gas Dryer on top and the brackets did not fit like they did on the previous Samsung and Whirlpool washers. Going to have to build a custom wood bracket to secure the dryer to the washer so it won't slide off.

The washer has two cold settings: cold (it brings super cold water up to some determined temperature) and tap cold (it just takes the cold water as is from the pipe. Probably useful in colder climates to get a consistent wash, but meh for here in California.

There is a power button that you have to use to turn on the washer before you can use the dial to choose your program. The screen to the right of the dial is a PAIN to read in low light. I printed stickers next to it for the key settings of OXY (presoak), Delay, Temperature and Cold Wash (darks).

There is a dial setting for "download" that uses your iphone or Android to download LG's ThinQ app. It basically hooks your washer up to WiFi to let you know when the washer is done and lets you create your own preset to make a custom washer setting. Used it a few times but never sure who set it last and what settings it has so I avoid using it. Did not like that the app REQUIRES you to give your location and birthdate info to use. Should be better privacy laws.

The Washer is a lot louder than our whirlpool when filling with water. The hoses move around. I'm guessing it has a smaller intake or too sudden of a shut off. There hasn't been much of a vibration issue so far. All in all a good washer. Will see how long it lasts...

review_title: Ding, Ding! Annoying ear pain! PLUS, Deep Narrow Drum rolls blankets & sheets into tight burritos!!!
review_text:
This dryer makes incessant noise, so I'm too annoyed to decide whether it works well or not.
The drum is deeper than 3 other large capacity dryers I've owned; this is very useful feature if you're trying to put it in a narrow space. If you're under 5'7", have short arms, or a bad back, the longer reach may take getting used to.
I don't know if this dryer can be stacked, but that would help the reach.
My manual, for dve(g)45r6300/dve(g)45r6100, shows how to turn off the end-of-cycle musical tune, but says this: "However, the other sounds stay active." It doesn't divulge how active those other sounds are!
If you have sensitive ears, you need to be prepared. This dryer causes me ear pain with its incessant ding, ding, dinging, to set it, open the door, turn on, turn it off...
I'll try to describe it; I've already turned off the end-of-cycle musical alarm, and the following is what remains! I may be off a ding here or there, but I'm pretty close:
Turn it on: 6 dings
Turn dial from Normal to Time dry: 5 dings (and it always resets to normal after each load).
Press the buttons from high heat to medium heat: 3 dings
Press start: 3-4 dings rolled together
I'm at over 15 musical notes just to dry a few t-shirts.
But wait, there's more!
Leave the door open while getting items out: two dings, repeating. They sort of reminded me of European police sirens. I suspect they'll continue dinging for as long as the door remains open, so I slam it shut as fast as I can!
Close the door but fail to press start! Oh, yeah, I'm just asking for punishment!
8 dings in sets of 2 quick EU police sirens.
These dings may also repeat, but, again, I press start as quickly as humanly possible to avoid additional high-pitched ear-pain! I'm thinking Havana Syndrome!
I've now jammed my fingers several times rushing to stop the dinging! My poor button pushing knuckles may eventually develop arthritis if I can't disconnect the dinging.
I will say that it's a very attractive dryer; if you wear headphones, it might be perfect.

Update: I contacted Samsung customer service via online chat for help with my now loathed new dryer.
I thought Samsung might sell a silent mechanism replacement for their obnoxious buttons/dials, or full silencing instructions; I even asked if there were actually speakers to cover with duct tape, or wires I could cut! Nobody could tell me anything!
I was transferred through two polite Samsung representatives (who only knew how to turn off the end-of-cycle jingle which I'd already done).
A third representative promised to escalate my grievance and arrange for a technician to visit my home. That was a week ago; I'm not aware of missing any calls, but I don't really expect one. So, I will try to return it, but it's been over 30 days and I'll be losing hundreds of dollars.

I think Samsung is rude to force people to hear unnecessary sounds, whether they're annoying or not.
This model number should include a prominent warning label about unnecessary sound-effects; Samsung needs to alert families with babies, light sleepers, students studying & trying to concentrate, musicians, writers, thinkers...
"Warning: This Device Dings/Pings Repeatedly & Can NEVER Be Turned Off!"
However, for people who enjoy the machine noise in casino lobbies played at a much higher pitch, or listening to cheap video games on a transistor radio, they should be fine drying laundry with this model.
Wow! I genuinely hate this product. Where's my hammer?

!!!!! UPDATE!!!!! The deep narrow drum rolls my blankets & sheets into tight burritos that remain wet in the center; we must repeatedly pull them out to unroll them & then stuff them back in to continue to dry. It's an exceptional amount of work.
Considering the expertise & experience of Samsung's amazing engineers & designers, it's almost like this dryer is some kind of bad practical joke! I genuinely loathe it with the intensity of a red dragon. I've never had an inanimate object cause me angst, so this is indeed an unusual experience; however, I wish this dryer would just go wherever missing socks go, never to be seen again. Maybe I'll just take an ax to it and carve up all that wasted money spent. Grrrrrr.

review_title: Do not buy this machine anywhere
review_text:
There are several issues with this machine, this is just a few of them. Must position clothes in a certain way to avoid unbalanced load error. I’m not talking about putting in a blanket and a pair of socks and the load become unbalanced, I’m talking about five t-shirts, five pairs of socks and five undershorts. I’m loading this washing machine like I’m decorating a cake sprinkling the dirty clothes around the machine to avoid potential unbalanced load error. Also, I know if I put in a load of towels not to leave the general vicinity of my home as the load will certainly become unbalanced even if I practice the “decorating a cake” method of loading the machine with the towels. So that means I need to reach in and rearrange several soaking wet bath towels and ask the laundry gods to assist in completing the load. I’m not sure how anyone who is either shorter than 5’5” could reach into this washing machine to do this or anyone who has arthritis or any other mobility issues.

Even allowing for user error while getting used to a new washing machine after using a front loader and growing up with an agitator washer, the idea that (1) clothes come out covered in dog hair or lint, while the mesh cover we have on the discharge hose that drains into the utility tub remains clean; (2) having to use an additional spin cycle after the load is completed still resulting in soggy, wet clothes; (3) untangling long sleeve shirts from anything else you might have washed as the shirts twist themselves into wet spaghetti; (4) inconvenient placement of detergent dispenser which unless you have an elongated spout on your container of detergent/softener means you are spilling detergent/softener on your hands and on the actual dispenser drawer, generally; (4) inadequate bleach dispenser – one drop too much sends it spilling out sooner than necessary.

This machine is advertised as being high efficiency but I would not agree.

review_title: I Didn't Know It Was Possible to Hate a Washing Machine
review_text:
We don't buy major appliances without doing some research. Three years ago, Samsung was supposedly a good brand. What a joke.

This washer claims to be high efficiency and is supposed to conserve water. Yes, when the top section of a load of laundry remains completely dry, I suppose that would conserve water. It won't clean clothes, but in theory it saves water. To ensure that clothes have a chance of getting clean, they have to be soaking wet before the washer is started. Failing to manually add water to the machine results in clothes that are dirtier coming out when they went in. Forget throwing a quick load in before heading to work unless you wake up early enough to walk between the nearest sink and the washer at least three times with a very large container of water. I'm confident that I use far more water to wash clothes with this "high efficiency" machine than I ever did with a standard washer.

This washer has to be continually babysat. It cannot complete a single cycle without stopping, emitting an incredibly annoying beeping sound, and issuing an "unbalanced" message.
