review_text:
This review is partially complaining about all of the modern washing machine choices because of unrealistic regulations that focus too much on "saving water" ...

I LOVED my previous (1999) Twin sets of Stackable Laundry Centers by Kenmore - Whirlpool. Fast-forward to 2021- it's nice to save water when you can, - to me that's what the choices for high, medium, & low water levels are for. I always used the "low" water setting with my older units whenever it made sense.

but when saving water renders unacceptably dirty laundry & an inability to "soak" -- I am sooo miserable doing laundry ...!

The total cost for my new GE gas dryer laundry center with installation & removal of those 2 older Laundry Centers that I LOVED - was $1,850 - & since there's essentially no way to "soak" with modern Laundry Centers, GE or other brands - I say switch to ANY other good name brand NON LAUNDRY CENTER SINGLETON washing machine that allows a soak cycle, & hopefully indicates a way to direct the machine to provide more water ( I prefer top load - washing machines). The Maytag non-stack top load we ordered for our mountain home around 2017 does allow the basin to fill fuller, if you call the help line & ask them for the ( secret ? ) way to do that -- maybe you put the setting on "bulky item"...? But, Covid-19 caused many "good brands" to have severely back-logged delivery dates at the precise time I needed my machine. Who can bear to wait weeks or months, or "unknown" delivery estimations, when they need new washer / dryer units yesterday...?

Who wants to blow nearly $2 thousand dollars - on a washer with new fangled short washing cycles that you can't even begin to understand how to control...?

I think at least some of these newer machines help you keep doing laundry in User-Friendly ways that you can feel more confident will actually clean your clothing in gentle, yet thorough ways. We Consumers should fight hard for our rights to have clean laundry, & washing machines that are user-friendly - we are smart enough to put water levels on "low" - if the job calls for it..! So this is fight we need to take-up with our Legislators and water-usage Regulators.

When 21 years passed while my 2 previous laundry centers sat side-by-side working VERY WELL, ... I knew the newer technology would take some adjustments on my part - but, I feel like if we can send people to outer-space ; then we ought to be able to offer Consumers washing machines that can conserve water when possible - but that also allow Consumers to elect to use more water, if that's what the job requires, & to allow the Consumer to SOAK certain loads when they want to, whether that's during the wash cycle, or during the rinse cycle.

product_title: LG WT7800CV 5.5 cu.ft. Graphite Smart wi-fi Enabled Top Load Washer with TurboWash3D0153 Technology
review_text:
Purchased this washing machine and the matching dryer. Got them installed and running last night. I was very disappointed with my initial wash.

Do not wash your clothes on the normal setting. The water does not fill up far enough to completely submerge the clothes and the agitator will shred your clothes. I was told that you can remove the agitator but I am not finding any information in the manual or on YouTube about doing so. I bought it with the intent to remove the agitator because of how it can damage clothing.

If you use powder detergent the normal cycle does not provide enough water to dissolve powder detergent and fully rinse it from your clothes. You must wash your clothes on one of the other settings which will take much longer.

The app is an absolute joke. And LG is so proud of it and certainly does propel them into the standards of technology 5 to 7 years ago. Seems a little late to join the game. But once you use the app you can see that they have no innovative twist or even basic knowledge on how to provide a customer with an easily navigatable and useful app. It's quite complex and not of the modern simplistic design. The features are in reality very few. You cannot remote start a washing machine, the notifications are out of sync with the cycle and there are no other features that are worthwhile. The app does not sync well with the machine. And the machine must be on and Wi-Fi activated each time you wish to use it. All it does is add a frustrating useless step to your normal washing routine.

Six features that need to be added: allow the owner to add more water to the washing bin during a cycle. Add a warm rinse. redesign the detergent bin. It is very difficult to add powder detergent. They haven't located in a very awkward place. allow the owner to remove the agitator. Allow the owner to unlock the lid during a cycle to add more clothes. Fire the team you have working on the app and hire a competent team who is forward thinking. (Or maybe LG is just too heavy handed to allow for any useful innovation?)

Not all of us have kids, or even have kids over to our homes. There's no reason to have the lid locked the entire cycle. Reminder to you overly safety conscious folks out there: not everything in reality is for children.

review_title: Do not buy!  This washer is a finicky piece of crap that doesn't wash and gets easily unbalanced.
review_text:
I am writing this here and publishing it to every site that will take a comment this long. I want you all to avoid getting ripped off. This machine will not make your life easier. It will make a daily/weekly chore far more time-consuming. I hate this thing so much that I'd go so far as to say it's actively anti-woman. (We all know who is still doing most of the laundry all over the world.)

Now, the capacity on this thing is huge. This is one of the reasons I bought it, as we have an incontinent adult child and a lot of bedding to wash when she visits. One problem: You can't put loads of bedding in the washer indiscriminately. Even if it everything fits in a couple of loads.

This machine has a serious issue with becoming easily unbalanced. Sheets hold more water than mattress pads. The sheets get wadded up and you are constantly pausing the cycle and re-distributing things. If you do not, the machine attempts to address the problem itself BY ADDING MORE WATER and swirling things around. If you are offended by wasting water, or your water bill, this is NOT the machine for you.

The same problem occurs for lightweight twin comforters versus a cotton blanket. Cotton blanket gets heavy and unbalances the load. So I am learning what bedding goes best together and babysitting loads of bedding through the washing cycle. This is going to be a problem any time you time you try to run different types of clothing all at once. If you're not a laundry sorter, this is definitely not the machine for you, because you have to be.

And forget about washing just a couple items you really want to wear. Same reason.

Second major issue? The machine fails in its basic job: Washing clothes. Recently, I realized that an unusual number of shirts (our most commonly stained items) were not coming clean with our standard stain treater and same old laundry detergent we've always used. So I'd spray them with more stain treater and rub them together and run them in the next load. I've never had to do more than this with any other machine. But they were still coming out stained.

review_title: Our LG Dryer caught fire during the warranty period!
review_text:
Our LG dryer caught fire 10.5 months after we bought it new from an authorized dealer. There was extensive smoke damage and, obviously, our home and the safety of my family (wife, two daughters and a dog) were imperiled. Luckily, in the end, only the dryer was dryer was ruined. Who knows what chemicals we were exposed to from the smoke?! The WORST part of it all was how LG ducked and weaved and finally turned their backs on us completely. The only thing they would offer to do was repair this faulty, dangerous unit. I told them I don't care if 10 NASA scientists came to our house, fully disassembled and put the unit back together again, it will NEVER be used in our home EVER AGAIN. Who knows if it will catch fire again?! Who knows what chemicals are in the smoke that was created?! LG was completely unsympathetic. They said we were refusing their help and washed their hands of us. And we were contacted by someone in the "Presidential Liaison Office" who said she was the ultimate authority. One of the most unhelpful, unfriendly customer service people I've ever talked to. A heart of ice. And, for the record we're adults and we know how to use a dryer properly, clean the lint filter, etc. The technician who LG sent used a special airflow meter to confirm that the vent and duct were clean.

LG refused to help us in any kind of meaningful way when its appliance caught fire under warranty in our home, putting our safety and possessions at grave risk. It took days for them to address the issue and I spent hours begging and pleaded various customer support agents in Manilla to escalate this. Finally, someone from the highest levels of the support organization, a "Presidential Liaison" contacted me. She was unfriendly, unsympathetic and utterly unhelpful. The only thing she would offer to do was to give me 20% of the value of the unit or have it repaired. I'm not crazy. NO ONE wants a faulty dryer that has caught fire repaired! Who knows what was burning in that unit (plastic, wiring, etc) and what dangerous chemicals were created?! Who knows whether it will catch fire again?!.The idea that we would keep this appliance in our house, given the fact that it put my entire family and home at risk, is completely ludicrous. But the Presidential Liaison was like a robot, just repeating the same thing over and over. I asked her if she was OK with me leaving our interaction furious with LG and ready to yell this story from the mountaintops (ie. social media, review sites, BBB, Consumer Affairs, UL, etc.) and she said she was fine with it. What kind of liaison is that?! What is clear is that the culture of LG and LG Support is completely unsympathetic, completely focused on the bottom line instead of the customer, perhaps even jaded and uninterested in the reputation of LG itself. It is the reflection of a sick company and a cynical corporate culture. For such a widely praised company, it was shocking and hugely disappointing. Needless to say, we will NEVER use LG products again and we will make sure to tell this sad story to everyone we know and care about.

review_title: Very loud and annoying dryer, LG said that's normal
review_text:
Last year I purchased several LG products. In the past, I've also purchased LG products. I like their products. However, I finally had an issue with my dryer, purchased about ten months ago.

The dryer makes a loud and annoying grinding noise. My other LG dryer, a model down from this one, does not make this noise.

So I called LG for warranty service and a technician came and worked on it. The repair didn't work. So I called LG back and they made another appointment for the technician to come and fix it. I got the appointment, took a 1/2 day off work, drove 20 minutes to meet the technician, and no one came. This happened four different times. I was given appointments from LG and I took 1/2 day off work and drove 20 minutes home and no one showed up.

Finally, the fifth time a technician showed up with parts and worked on the dryer, then said the dryer was fixed. However, it still wasn't fixed. It still makes the same loud noise.

So I called LG and talked with a Presidential Liaison person. They told me that the noise was normal and they couldn't do anything more. I would have to live with the noisy dryer. I explained this wasn't normal. My other dryer doesn't make this noise. If it is normal LG needs to re-engineer this product because their competitors would have much better products. The person I talked to just said policy states if I have someone else comes out I will be charged, and nothing can be done. They said it is a noisy dryer. They had little patience talking with me, although I was calm and kind.

After this incident, I will no longer purchase LG products. I was getting ready to purchase a large TV and LG was my number one choice, but I will go with a different company. I'm sad because I like LG, but their customer service was subpar, and the missed appointments cost me time and money.

review_text:
I love LG products and I want to love this washer but I just can't. We have had our washer for two weeks. It seems to get clothes clean, although because of such small water usage, they come out very wrinkled. The instruction manual is the WORST I have ever seen for a major appliance. It has 14 pages of installation, one-fourth of a page on how to use a top loader washer--not kidding--and 6 pages of trouble shooting. Nothing on the cycles, nothing on the extra options. Even trying to find the information online is hit and miss. The washer is worth 4 stars, but the manual is worth zero. I'm not sure I would buy this model again.

Note added November 2021: We have had this washer for 9 months, and every time I use it, I say "I hate this washer." It is without question the worst major appliance I have ever owned. The water level is ALWAYS inadequate to get the clothes clean; there is a Water Plus button to add more water, but it is always a guess as to how much to add. Also, without an agitator, there is a dead zone in the middle: if a large item gets trapped in there, it never moves with the rest of the clothes. I may make it 12 months before replacing it with a new washer, but my frustration level increases every time I use it. I like other LG products, but this one is horrible.

review_text:
Brand new LG WT7300CW Washer. All the advertisements say that it works with Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant. You have to install the LG ThinQ app on your phone and then link Alexa and Google Home. Siri or the Apple Home app does not support washers at this time apparently. The LG ThinQ app can send a notification to your phone when the washer is finished. Neither Alexa or Google Home can notify us when the washer is finished. At least Google Home can tell me how much time is left on the washer. But Alexa can only tell me if the washer is on or off. LG built a terrible skill for Alexa. They need to hire a good programming team and fix it.

Here are Alexa commands that work and don't work.

Me: "Alexa, is the washer running?"
Alexa: "The top load washer is on."

Me: "Alexa, what's the status of the washer?"
Alexa: "That's not supported yet."

Me: "Alexa, how much time is left on the washer?"
Alexa: "That's not supported yet."

Me: "Alexa, is the washer finished?"
Alexa: "That's not supported yet."

Me: "Alexa, ask LG for the status of the washer."
Alexa: "Sorry, I didn't find a group or device named L G Washer"

Me: "Alexa, ask LG how much time is left on the washer."
Alexa: "That's not supported yet."

Me: "Alexa, what mode is the washer in?"
Alexa: "Top load washer doesn't support that."

Google Home commands that work and don't work:

Me: "Hey Google, what's the status of the washer?"
Google: "The top load washer is on washing cycle and will be done in 53 minutes."

Me: "Hey Google, how much time is left on the washer?"
Google: "The top load washer will be done in 47 minutes."

Me: "Hey Google, tell me when the washer is finished."
Google: "In Greek, that's: εμένα όταν σταματήσει το πλυντήριο."

Me: "Hey Google, tell me when the washer is off."
Google: "Got it, stopping the Top Load Washer." (Oops! Now I need to restart it!)

review_title: Such a bad product and customer support experince
review_text:
Please don’t buy this washer or dryer from GE. You will need service and the process will be very painful.

I purchased this washer and dryer set with pedestals in January 2021 to be installed in my new house. About a month after installation the washer wouldn’t turn on. I scheduled service with GE and a week later they sent out a local 3rd party technician. They diagnosed the issue as the main board and ordered the part. Another week later the replacement part arrived. I informed the tech and after three weeks he came back and installed the board. The washer would finally turn on but after a week it started to only go through the first few steps in its start up cycle but would never actually start the wash cycle. We called again for service and over the next 4 months and several service calls, the technicians replaced several parts, including the door assembly but the problem still persisted. During this time we had to swap between using the washer when it would work or going to the laundromat when it wouldn't.

Finally in June, after 5 months of living with the constant issues, GE agreed to replace the washer. The washer arrived and a local installer came to install it. When they saw that the old washer was on a pedestal he informed me that they could not put a new washer on an old pedestal. The GE customer relations person had forgotten to ask if the washer was on a pedestal so a replacement one was never shipped. The installer said they would take the washer back and hold it in their warehouse until GE ordered the pedestal. I called the customer relations person back again (each call takes over an hour on hold to get through). They informed me that they would order the pedestal and email me with an ETA. Ater another week, which put us in July, GE customer relations emailed to tell me it would be the end of July before the pedestal would arrive. They offered to refund the pedestal. I explained that without the pedestal the washer would sit almost two feet lower that the dryer right next to it which was not an option for me.

After several email exchanges I was informed that the pedestal was back ordered and would not arrive until mid August. I called customer relations again on a Friday afternoon to discuss a plan. I asked if I could simply go buy the pedestal (new in a box and GE branded). They say that would work and told me that they would schedule the washer again to be delivered. I went and bought the pedestal that same day. On the following Monday I was informed by GE customer relations that they had spoken to the installer and the installer said the pedestal I purchased would not work and gave no other information about how this would be resolved. I”m on hold again with GE as we speak to try again to get some kind of resolution. My next call will be the Better Business Bureau and Consumer Affairs in my state. Bottom line, do not buy a GE appliance.

review_text:
After three years, my GE Ultrafresh Vent washer (GFW850) refuses to fill with water unless I touch the pause button three times in succession. The pause button should only be touched once to start the cycle. I've had a GE Technician to my home twice to repair the washer. He replaced a part that did not repair the washer. Now, I must wait for a third GE repair visit to determine if the washer is repairable.

If the washer is not repairable, I will probably continue to press the pause button three times in succession until the washer stops working altogether. Beware, this machine is too expensive to replace so soon because it’s unrepairable. Once it stops working, I will steer clear of GE Washers in the future.

To be clear, I understand some parts will wear out and need to be replaced. However, I don't understand why GE can't diagnose the problem and repair the washer. Prior to this issue, I've had no issues with the washer. This can't be the first time this issue has occurred for a customer.

review_title: Undoubtedly the worst product I have ever owned.
review_text: The GE Sensor-dry dryer fails miserably at its basic mission: to dry clothes.  We bought one new and after about six frustrating months had a GE repair person out to fix it because it wouldn't run a full dry cycle without either stopping or finishing with semi-dry clothes.  He explained that sensors in the dryer are spaced so that only clothes in either the front or back are measured for dryness....yet the action of the dryer moves larger items to the rear.  This means that you positively cannot dry jeans with shirts (shirts may be dry, jeans will be damp) or towels with clothes (same issue) in the same load.  In addition, the slightest amount of lint with cause the dryer to beep about once every 45 seconds for an eternity...until you get so tired of listening to it that you come to turn it off or clean out the tiny amount of lint that set off the sensor. The only way to get what you expect is to put every single load on Heavy Duty and pray that whatever you're drying doesn't throw off any lint.  Our guest house has a dryer from a competitor that works like a charm.  The GE dryer is so frustrating that I won't ever buy another GE appliance.

product_title: 4.5 cu. ft. Ultra Large Front Load Washer
review_text:
This washer is terrible. The washer is frequently unable to begin its spin cycle because starting to spin the wet clothes makes the washer shake with a huge banging. It must pause, try to adjust the wet clothes with a slow rotation, and start again. This inability to progress to spin happens rarely with small loads (~5 pounds of kids clothes), often with medium sized loads (~10 pounds of adult clothes including a sweater or two), and always if anything bulky is included (towels, bed sheets, throw blankets). When the washer has a hard time starting the spin cycle, the best case is that the washer will attempt to rebalance the wet clothes over and over again, not making any progress for ~20-60 minutes before the stars align and spin occurs. Rebalancing by hand does not help. The bad scenario is that among all of the failed spin attempts, the washer will begin to leak water on the floor. It's hard to tell exactly where the water is coming from, but after some experimentation, it seems to come from the overflow vent in the back.

We have called LG service multiple times, but they had no solution for the inability to progress to spin cycle ("try rebalancing by hand" is not useful when gravity inevitably pulls the wet clothes back to the bottom of the drum) and we didn't have the leaking problem until we had owned the washer for 13 months, which is one month more than the warranty. It was professionally installed and balanced, and I have personally confirmed the balance and level installation multiple times.

I wish I had bought something else.

review_title: Horrible - my space heater could dry clothes faster
review_text:
I sometimes have to dry our clothes twice to get them dry enough after following instructions and not overloading the machine. There are other reason this machine is a waste of money. We have the extra capacity dryer as we have larger blankets and comforters that we wash regularly. Ha! Those items, which usually don’t spin dry very well (see my review of the companion Samsung washing machine) turn themselves into cocoons of wet fabric after five minutes even with the use of tennis balls to help keep things moving in the dryer. So every five to ten minutes I need to go to the dryer, take out the blanket, give it a good shake and return it. If you have mobility issues, arthritis or are an older individual with weak strength, this is not the dryer for you. Along those same lines, I have dryed three or four throw size blankets, again with tennis balls to keep things moving around, and usually one of them remains stuck in the back of the dryer, also in a cocoon of wetness that somehow just never wanted to join the party with the rest of the throws in the dryer. This is after I shook them out from the washer before carefully placing them into the dryer so as not to load the dryer with a bunch of lumpy throw blankets.

Also, I use the fluff or air only cycle on our dryer to dislodge dog hair from the crib size flat sheets I use to cover our dog’s various beds throughout the house during shedding season prior to putting those items into the wash. The first time I used this Samsung dryer to do this, I used blind confidence and after the fluff cycle in the dryer, put them into the Samsung washer. Big mistake: first the washer threw the unbalalnced loand error (again, see washer review) and when I opened the washer to relocate the soaking wet crib size flat sheets, my hand came out covered in wet dog fur. After a look around the wet sheets in the washer, I pulled out at least five clumps of wet dog fur which the washing machine kindly formed for me in the wet sheets. The second time I tried to fluff the dog hair off the sheets before washing, I checked the lint trap which remained clean after a 20 minute fluff (with tennis balls) and for fun, I took these crib size flat sheets outside to give them a good shake and ended up completely covered in dog hair (note to self: stand up wind in the future). Our previous dryer removed 80% of all fur which I could determine by pulling out the lint trap. This dryer might remove eight strands of dog fur.

review_text:
I had this machine in two different apartments. Unfortunately it is very delicate and prone to glitches. A common problem in both apartments is "balance load" issue. It is very common that multiple times during a load, the washer will stop while your clothes are completely submerged in water for a "balance load" issue. You have to pick up the soaking wet clothes and rearrange them to "balance the load" and the sensors seem to be very sensitive to imbalances, so at times a load will stop 5, 6, 7 times asking you to rebalance the items. Very frustrating and gets in the way of a good clean.

They're also just janky. On delivery the first attempt, the machine was severely dented right off the truck. On the second attempt, the machine appeared fine from the outside, but when I turned it on, the washer gave me the "balance load" issue 5-6 times and on drying, the dryer smelled like gas (I have the gas dryer version). Lint gets everywhere in the holes of the dryer, too.

It's a cheaply made machine, I think it is useful for developers who want to purchase a large amount of washer/dryers at a cheap price. But they break so easily so I wouldn't recommend them at all.

product_title: LG WM4000HBA / WM4000HBA / WM4000HBA 4.5 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity Smart wi-fi Enabled Front Load Washer with TurboWash 360 and Built-in Intelligence
review_title: ONLY a First Day review... all is good though.
review_text:
We chose this and its dryer mate because the NY Times reviewed it as best for the year model for cleaning cloths, gentleness on cloths, and expected durability and longevity of the product line. This is a DAY1 review.

First the Bad:

1. the manuals are terrible. There is so much missing about how to use the controls it is pitiful. Consider for example that there is NOTHING in the dryer manual to tell you how to use all the potential button settings. None of the buttons worked, until I figured out hours later that you must use the MANUAL selection on the dial before you can change stuff.. If you go to the LG web site, there are other documents you can read but I mean really. As a Software Engineer, if my QA and DOCUMENTATION people wrote manuals this bad about what I build, I would fire them.

2. availability is spotty on both the appliances and their accessories. We had trouble finding the matching dryer, and could not get the pedestal add ones because none were available. Chalk this up to COVID I guess but one outfit said we would need to wait five weeks to the matching dryer. So do some research and shop around to see who has what in stock. If your current washer/dryer are on their last leg, maybe don't wait for them to fail before you but new ones? Just a thought.

3. the washer is louder that both the wife and I expected. OK in fairness, there was never any claim made about how loud or quiet these machines were supposed to be. And the door is still off the laundry room and the room is empty... so there is nothing to muffle the sound. I expect this to reduce significantly once the crap is put back into the laundry room and the door hung. So maybe I am over stating this negative.

4. 4.5 cubic feet ain't as big as it sounds. Compared to our old top loader, it seems the size of loads we are putting in the washer is smaller. It is hard to judge without a side-by-side comparison, and maybe we over stuffed to old guy whish is why it had some problems, and I could in fact stuff more into the new machine if I wanted. But it does seem like the load size smaller.

The GOOD:

1. new looking cloths, fast. I kid you not when I say the stuff that comes out of washer and dryer looks brand new. I am a work-from-home IT guy so I am mostly a sweats and t-shirt man. All my cloths so far look brand new and soft out of the dryer. And the "seemingly" smaller load sizes get done in 30 minutes in the washer unless I pick one of the longer running cycles. We did upholstery covers, blankets and bedding, pillows, towels, slippers, and lots of cloths (yeah they delivered the machines @9:30am and I did 10 loads today) and ALL of it looked NEW after being cleaned by this pair of machines. The dryer takes about 54 minutes to dry whatever you put in it. I used the manual setting for a lot of it which allowed me to reduce heat and dry time to 40 minutes.

2. no-brainer operation. If you are not into all the options worry not, you don't really need them. There are so many presets on the dial, you almost can't fail to find a setting that works for whatever you are cleaning. You just turn the machine on, put a detergent plug into the drum, load, dial up your clothing match, and press the run button. The washer appears to have some AI that checks the washer load to see if any timing adjustment is needed off the baseline you dialed in, but maybe that is my imagination. Point is anyone can use these with great precision without any effort. Kind of makes up for the crappy manuals. Only thing I add is "extra rinse" at the end of the wash cycle.

3. has less expensive versions in the model line if you do not want to spend the money on these. I am guessing of course but I would think "lower end" models in the same product line are really just fewer features but same washing and drying ability and reliability of product. So if you need to save money on your set look at those instead.

Tomorrow is the Wife's turn. If she has any major comments I will add them to this review later. Kevin

review_title: Takes some time to tweak, a pain to maintain. Drys well
review_text:
This is the only washer dryer combo that stacks in the front. If you are putting them on a pedestal you don’t have to assemble both together and lift both up. The ventless is good if you don’t have an existing vent. I preferred my old vented Axxis to this one but Bosch stopped making vented ones.
If you have pets regular maintenance is needed. You have the regular lint trap to clean and since the mesh is so fine and you use dryer sheets you have to scrub it periodically to get rid of the wax build up or it will, clog, overheat, and shut down—requiring a maintenance call to pay someone a lot of money to take off a back panel and push a button. Then you have to periodically clean the condenser which builds up hair and lint. If you don’t, the dryer becomes inefficient and eventually stops drying. Washing the condenser in your sink or tub will wash a bunch of hair down the drain leading to potential clogs. Finally you have to clean the sump—where the moisture from you condenser goes. If not, the pump clogs and the water pools and your clothes don’t dry. This is the trickiest one to clean as it is in the way back and the sump cover is a pain in the butt to open. If you are not handy and own this dryer, you will be regularly paying someone a lot of money to do basic maintenance.
Note: the default dry setting are a bit damp for someone like me who has dust allergies. You can make it dry more by using the “dry level” button. Be careful because your laundry can get hot and synthetics will off gas and cottons can smell burnt.

product_title: LG STUDIO Single Unit Front Load WashTower™ with Center Control™ 5.0 cu. ft. Washer and 7.4 cu. ft. Electric Dryer
review_text:
Very disappointed, especially for the very high price of this unit.
The unit lacks an air only/no heat setting, even though the manual recommends a no heat setting for some fabrics. The heat setting only goes to “low heat” but does not have an air/no heat setting.
There is nothing intuitive about this set. The controls are complicated and opaque in function. Some options are unavailable at times, for no discernible reason. The wi-fi connection is not well explained in the manual and I initially had trouble connecting to wi-fi.
The manual refers to additional cycles/settings that can be downloaded via the app. Why? The whole idea of settings and cycles that can be accessed only by download seems to be a gimmick; why not have these settings/cycles available via the unit’s controls?
The washer seems to do a good job and is very quiet. The washer drum is very deep and I need to get down on my knees to reach smaller items, like socks, in the back (and my arms are fairly long). The dryer seems very slow and never fully dries my clothes without multiple cycles, even at the highest dry setting.
The buttons are supposedly touch-sensitive, but they often do not respond until I touch them several times.
One of the selling points of the stacked unit is that the dryer is designed to select appropriate drying settings based on the selected wash settings. However, if you don’t get to the dryer very soon after the wash cycle ends, the unit shuts down and the programmed dry settings are no longer available.
Overall this unit is frustrating and definitely not worth the very high price. I am very disappointed.

review_title: Our LG Dryer caught fire during the warranty period!
review_text:
Our LG dryer caught fire 10.5 months after we bought it new from an authorized dealer. There was extensive smoke damage and, obviously, our home and the safety of my family (wife, two daughters and a dog) were imperiled. Luckily, in the end, only the dryer was dryer was ruined. Who knows what chemicals we were exposed to from the smoke?! The WORST part of it all was how LG ducked and weaved and finally turned their backs on us completely. The only thing they would offer to do was repair this faulty, dangerous unit. I told them I don't care if 10 NASA scientists came to our house, fully disassembled and put the unit back together again, it will NEVER be used in our home EVER AGAIN. Who knows if it will catch fire again?! Who knows what chemicals are in the smoke that was created?! LG was completely unsympathetic. They said we were refusing their help and washed their hands of us. And we were contacted by someone in the "Presidential Liaison Office" who said she was the ultimate authority. One of the most unhelpful, unfriendly customer service people I've ever talked to. A heart of ice. And, for the record we're adults and we know how to use a dryer properly, clean the lint filter, etc. The technician who LG sent used a special airflow meter to confirm that the vent and duct were clean.

LG refused to help us in any kind of meaningful way when its appliance caught fire under warranty in our home, putting our safety and possessions at grave risk. It took days for them to address the issue and I spent hours begging and pleaded various customer support agents in Manilla to escalate this. Finally, someone from the highest levels of the support organization, a "Presidential Liaison" contacted me. She was unfriendly, unsympathetic and utterly unhelpful. The only thing she would offer to do was to give me 20% of the value of the unit or have it repaired. I'm not crazy. NO ONE wants a faulty dryer that has caught fire repaired! Who knows what was burning in that unit (plastic, wiring, etc) and what dangerous chemicals were created?! Who knows whether it will catch fire again?!.The idea that we would keep this appliance in our house, given the fact that it put my entire family and home at risk, is completely ludicrous. But the Presidential Liaison was like a robot, just repeating the same thing over and over. I asked her if she was OK with me leaving our interaction furious with LG and ready to yell this story from the mountaintops (ie. social media, review sites, BBB, Consumer Affairs, UL, etc.) and she said she was fine with it. What kind of liaison is that?! What is clear is that the culture of LG and LG Support is completely unsympathetic, completely focused on the bottom line instead of the customer, perhaps even jaded and uninterested in the reputation of LG itself. It is the reflection of a sick company and a cynical corporate culture. For such a widely praised company, it was shocking and hugely disappointing. Needless to say, we will NEVER use LG products again and we will make sure to tell this sad story to everyone we know and care about.

review_text:
We were given a phone call about 30 minutes after placing the order, to verify that we understood that we were getting one machine that could do both wash and dry, as well as to set up expectations on how and when my machine would be delivered. This alone I would recommend this purchase.
Delivery was smooth and went as planned, the delivery company called about 3 days before delivery, and the driver called the morning of as well as about 1/2 hour out. Once the driver was here and we got the machine off the truck he did help cut the packaging open as it was damaged, so we verified the machine itself wasn't damaged. Which it wasn't just.
We live in a 5th wheel toy hauler, so space is very limited. This machine fits perfectly in the space we have for it in our garage. This machine is not vented, so when its drying, the "vented" goes down the drain to the gray tank, and the lint is collected around the door and seal, which makes it easy to clean.
Things to know is that with a unvented combo unit, your clothes are supposed to be slightly damp, take them out and give them a shake, this does 2 things, instantly dries and gets the wrinkles out. It does take about 3 or 4 hours to do a load of laundry that is from start to finish. So yes it does take a bit longer, but you don't have to remember to swap machines. I usually do 2 loads of laundry a day, one in the morning before leaving and one at night as we're going to bed. I come home to clean, dry clothes and wake up to clean, dry clothes. the loads do need to be smaller, but I can still wash a queen sheet set in one load, or 4 pairs of jeans or 2 heavy bath towels with a few hand towels.
This is a normal 110 unit, so no special wiring or anything, just plug it in and connect the water and drain.
I was surprised that this machine could connect to the internet, I haven't done it yet, I don't see a need for it, but it's great that I have that option. The manual was written in very good English, that was easy to read and understand, I don't know about the translations.
I would recommend this machine if you are limited on space, water and time. It has lots of washing and drying features including steam and sanitize.

If you're OK with the door opening to the right, it's a fine buy. review_text: This washer came brand new in the place I'm staying at and it is the absolute worst.  I don't understand the good reviews here.  The machine starts agitating with no clothes in it.  Then unbalances itself, then adds water to try to fix the imbalance and goes through this endless loop of adding more water, getting unbalanced.  It doesn't have this problem on all loads, it is just inconsistent enough to be a headache.  It twists the clothes into knots. It doesn't add enough water for clothes to be clean since it is "efficient" and it has gotten worse over time.  The cycles take forever (>1 hour). You have to turn it off completely to adjust any settings. It has been approx 9 months since it was first used.  It appears to be a design flaw with the way the machine works not that it is malfunctioning.  We've had to wring out clothes by hand because waiting for it to be balanced enough to complete the cycle takes forever. It is the worst. I've never had these sort of problems with a washing machine.  This is a rant based on how much time in my life this machine has wasted.  Do not buy this machine.
